in writing. ‒ the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) is the authority that takes decisions for the conservation and management of fisheries in its area of competence. those acts are binding and need to be transposed into union law. in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual plan for the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks, which will end in 2022. this plan has been successively amended by iccat at its annual meetings. the aim of transposing the iccat recommendations is to ensure uniform application throughout the eu, which should aim at ensuring a level playing field for all tuna fishermen, and in particular third country operators. otherwise, if different rules are applied to foreign fleets, all the efforts and restrictions on eu fishermen will be fruitless. i voted in favour of this report because we need to ensure that the latest measures in the multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan adopted by iccat are applied uniformly and effectively throughout the european union.
in writing. ‒ when dealing with this fishing sustainability, we must safe-guard long term productivity, promote local employment opportunities, encourage the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and a responsible exploitation of fisheries resources. unfortunately, the current bluefin tuna fishing quota system penalises small-scale fishermen, and needs to be reviewed. large vessels owners are too dominant and might harm the fishing sustainability. i therefore support transposal into union law of the measures of the multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) at its annual meetings between 2012 and 2014. i believe that the technical measures included in the multiannual recovery plan will lead to positive developments for environment, nature and local employment.

in writing. ‒ catches of bluefin tuna are one of the significant components of the fishing activity of the member states in the waters of the atlantic ocean and the mediterranean sea. their uniform regulation at european union level contributes to the recovery of stocks and to the maintenance of an appropriate level of economic use. the eu is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), the regional fisheries management organisation for tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas, and as such has to apply its decisions. in view of the positive evolution of stocks in recent years, iccat decided in 2013 to increase the quota allocated to member states slightly. however, it needs to be properly transposed by the commission in order to guarantee a level playing field for all operators involved in tuna fishing and in particular third country operators. the quotas established should encourage small-scale fishermen, who are currently disadvantaged, and provide an additional guarantee for keeping stocks at an acceptable level. the european parliament must be involved in the international negotiation of these quotas, on the basis of its powers given by the european citizens it represents. the adoption of this document is a first step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean aims to ensure uniform and effective application of the measures recently adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas to restore bluefin tuna stocks. the eu is part of iccat, which has the authority to adopt decisions for the conservation and management of fisheries in its area of competence. as regards the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks, iccat has taken measures such as the gradual reduction of the level of total allowable catches, restrictions on fishing in certain zones and periods, measures relating to sport and recreational fishing activities, measures relating to spawning and fishing capacity, and the setting of quotas at european union level. the decisions taken in iccat so far have led to a spectacular recovery of bluefin tuna stocks and in this regard these measures should be continued for a full recovery. i therefore voted in favour of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean.

in writing. ‒ free and fair competition is one of the fundamental values of the european construction, which has been the basis for the realisation of the huge economic potential of the member states and the common market. its protection by the european institutions must therefore be one of our main objectives. unfortunately, the european parliament does not yet have the necessary powers to determine the situation decisively. however, as direct representatives of the european citizens, we can ask the commission to respect certain principles. one of these is to avoid abuses of dominant positions in order to allow all players, large and small, to be present on the market through anti-trust policies. state aid can also affect free competition, but in some cases it is necessary to avoid the collapse of certain sectors of the member states that employ a considerable workforce. at the same time, the level of charges may constitute an element of imbalance between member states, which is why their harmonisation at an optimal level is necessary. all these provisions must have the best interests of european citizens and the highest possible standard of living at their core. otherwise, competition for the sake of competition cannot produce a prosperous and balanced society.

in writing. i voted for the own-initiative report on the annual report on eu competition policy. the rapporteur welcomes the concern shown by the rapporteur for the sme sector, criticising taxation models which distort competition, creating considerable problems for medium-sized enterprises in particular. the report calls on the commission to ensure that member states implement in a timely manner the new public procurement legislation, as well as the new provisions on the consideration of social and environmental criteria and the division of contracts into lots, in order to stimulate innovation and fair competition and to support smes in public procurement markets, ensuring the best value for money in the use of public funds.

in writing. ‒ the digital agenda scoreboard shows that eu regions have very different levels of digital connectivity, internet use, human capital, business integration of digital technology and digital public services. regions that score low on these five indicators risk missing out on the benefits of the digital age. current policies and incentives have failed to ensure adequate digital infrastructure, especially in rural areas, with 44.8% of eu households lacking access to high-speed internet. i support the ep motion for a resolution on the preparation of a legislative act on the digital single market, as i believe that the achievement of a digital single market, based on a common set of rules, can boost eu competitiveness with positive effects on jobs, relaunch the single market and reinforce inclusiveness, providing citizens and businesses with new opportunities, in particular through the exchange of innovations. i also mention that the digital revolution is affecting every aspect of our societies, bringing with it opportunities and challenges, and having the potential to further empower citizens, consumers and entrepreneurs in new ways, different from the way this could be done before.

in writing. ‒ today, we will be able to guarantee better access for consumers and businesses across europe to the digital single market, creating the right conditions and a level playing field for advanced digital networks and innovative services, and maximising the growth potential of the digital economy. it is very important to have a clear stand on topics such as consumer protection, data protection, big data, infrastructure and investment, media, digital skills and copyright. i welcome the fact that the report goes beyond the commission strategy addressing issues which the commission has neglected, such as platforms, structural changes in society and the impact of digitalisation on the employment world. i am especially satisfied that the issues of workers’ rights in the sharing economy and the parcel delivery sector were included in the report. finally, i believe we must make more efforts on standardisation, patents and on social protection.
in writing. ‒ the digital single market is of utmost importance to the eu. the strategies addressed for the development of the digital single market can lead to effective economic development. the internet increases the speed of commercial exchanges, but also the speed of information exchange between citizens and public administration. the digital single market needs to be developed taking into account social inclusion and the different levels of education in the european area. therefore, i believe that the development of the digital single market must be directly linked to the investments of the cohesion funds. at the same time, the commission must ensure that there is a clear legal framework for the fight against cybercrime and the protection of personal data. the development of technology must not infringe the rights of consumers.
in writing. ‒ the report underlines consumer protection, data protection, infrastructure and investment, media, digital skills and copyright. it goes beyond the commission strategy addressing issues such as platforms, structural changes in society and the impact of digitalisation on the employment world. we have to maximise the growth potential of the digital economy. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the digital single market because europe urgently needs a legislative framework and clear criteria to create a functioning market in this area. the fragmentation of the single market, the fact that all 28 member states have their own digital rules, are major obstacles to development, especially for smes and start-ups. only 1.7% of eu enterprises use digital technologies and only 14% of smes use the internet for sales. to increase global competitiveness, europe needs to build a digital economy, a common set of digital rules, free and open internet access for all smes and eliminate geo-blocking and price discrimination based on geographical location or nationality. i stress the importance of developing european satellite radio navigation systems, investing in fast communications networks and in the digitalisation of the energy sector, meters and smart grids. future digital single market legislation should also create the necessary conditions for type-approval for the installation of ecall in vehicles and the extension of access to 112 emergency services to all european users.
in writing. ‒ this resolution represents parliament’s position on commission’s action plan for achieving a digital single market. specifically this refers to tackling issues such as geo-blocking, the reform of the copyright regime, the faster roll-out of both mobile and wired broadband internet and to incentivising the use of e-commerce services throughout europe. these elements are essential for the eu’s economic competitiveness, growth and more job opportunities for its citizens. it is a balanced resolution that i believe to correctly identify the means to create a single market for digital services and therefore it has my vote.
in writing. – i have voted for this report that will not only improve citizens’ access to information, but will also maximise the growth potential of the digital economy and will improve governance and transparency in the eu and its member states, within a single market.
in writing. ‒ a digital single market must ensure quality services and facilitate the everyday lives of end consumers, encourage innovation and create new opportunities for businesses and citizens. the resolution on the preparation of a legislative act on the digital single market develops aspects related to the actions to be taken to complete the digital single market and the consequences it will have on society and the economy as a whole. as itre s&d coordinator, i support the importance of investments in infrastructure and fast and ultra-fast communications networks, efficient spectrum allocation and management and the rapid deployment of 5g technology and ultra-fast broadband services, high standards of data protection and security of international data transfers, the removal of geo-blocking and improved consumer access to content. in order to reduce the digital divide, we ask the commission to consider a series of measures and legislative revisions: the revision of eu telecoms rules, the revision of the interoperability framework, including the commission's mandates within the european standardisation organisations, and a long-term strategy on the future uses of the different frequency bands that are particularly needed for the deployment of 5g-based networks.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has made the eu's regulation of the digital single market a priority in recent years. in this context, 16 initiatives were launched on various sectoral aspects of the european digital market. these are grouped under three main headings, namely better access for european consumers and businesses to the digital single market, creating the right conditions for advanced digital networks and new services, and maximising the growth potential of the digital economy. the main issues facing member states in these areas are consumer protection, protection of personal data and sensitive information, infrastructure and investment, digital media, digital education, copyright, e-commerce, geolocation, illegal content, interoperability and standardisation, e-government. we must be aware that the process of digitalisation is bringing about structural changes in society and in the employment model. in this context, the eu and the member states need to adapt to the requirements of the current situation. our priority must be, however, first and foremost, to ensure that this process is carried out in the interests of our citizens, creates all the potential benefits for them and does not adversely affect the workforce. only then will the digital single market fulfil its purpose.
in writing. ‒ the rapid evolution of the internet and mobile communications has changed the way users communicate, access information and knowledge, innovate and consume, leading to the expansion and change of the economy, facilitating access for small businesses to a potential customer base of 500 million consumers in the eu as well as to global markets, and giving people the opportunity to develop new entrepreneurial business ideas and models. digital infrastructure is the backbone of the digital single market, therefore it is necessary to develop a digital transformation plan for industry, with a view to increasing the competitiveness of the european economy, to increase efficiency and to unlock untapped potential. building trust in digital technologies is also essential for the development of the data-driven economy, by clarifying rules on data ownership and data portability, and by giving citizens control over their own data. i welcome the achievement of a digital single market, based on a common set of rules, which could boost eu competitiveness, have positive effects on growth and jobs, relaunch the single market and strengthen the inclusive nature of society, offering new opportunities to citizens and businesses, in particular through the exchange of innovations.
in writing. i voted for the own-initiative report on the preparation of a legislative act on the digital single market, which is parliament's response to the digital strategy for europe adopted by the european commission on 6 may 2015. the alignment of the european digital market with the single market represents a huge opportunity for eu entrepreneurs and businesses to thrive, but also for the eu labour market to fully recover from the economic crisis and its aftermath. the report responds to the 16 proposals put forward by the commission and develops the issues related to the actions to be taken to complete the digital single market and the consequences that the completion of the digital single market will have on society and the economy as a whole.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, before i get into the details of this topic, let me say a few words on what happened in vienna on saturday, where we showed that, exactly six months after having reached an agreement with iran on their nuclear programme, iran fulfilled the commitments we had agreed on. the iaea verified this compliance and the international community, through the e3+3, the joint commission that i coordinate and that i, and my successor after me, will continue to coordinate for the whole duration of the agreement, verified that this has been done and therefore that the deal has been implemented. let me reiterate that six months ago there were many people, in europe, the region and the world, who were deeply sceptical as to whether we would ever manage to implement this agreement. they were betting on the possibility that iran would not follow up the agreement with concrete deeds. let me say that most of all it is a nuclear negotiation, a nuclear agreement, and this is the core of our satisfaction: the fact that we have prevented a major risk of nuclear proliferation and maybe even the possibility of a conflict in the region. this is the first reason for satisfaction, but there is another element of satisfaction linked to the fact that we have shown that multilateralism and diplomacy can work. as we saw in the previous debate, not only can it work in terms of reaching an agreement, it can also deliver in terms of implementation. so, in these difficult times there is good reason for hope. and let me also say, as i get to the real issue of our debate, though the two are closely connect, that there are two other elements for hope. one is the door that now opens for relations between iran with the rest of the world – starting with the europeans – and for us europeans to engage in iran in different ways and in different sectors. finally, last but not least – and perhaps most importantly – this agreement could open the way to a different kind of relationship in the region. here we come to the issue of tonight because, after managing to hold negotiations for 13 years, with difficulties and ups and downs and a lot of scepticism, and achieving that historic result against all odds, we now have to invest in the possibility of a different kind of cooperation in the region. we are not naïve; we know very well that this will not be easy, that this will not happen overnight and that we will face obstacles and setbacks. the willingness of iran to further cooperate on regional matters will have to be tested. but the fact that they have stated this willingness is already a step forward in respect to the past. their will to implement the agreement they signed in july will also be tested. but just think back one year ago. many believed we would never manage to agree on a strong deal with iran, a verifiable and implementable deal, and we proved them wrong. if we keep working hard and together – united as europeans and with the rest of the international community – i am sure we can keep surprising the sceptics somehow. dialogue among all regional powers, starting with saudi arabia and iran is – we are united in believing – the only way out of the current turmoil in the middle east. in the past few years, a struggle for regional hegemony has mixed with revamped ethnic and confessional tensions. terrorist groups such as daesh are fostering sectarianism to throw the region into even greater chaos and bolster their own power. international disputes between saudi arabia and iran can easily play into the narrative of a war of religion between sunni and shia muslims, and we know this very well. the risks of this are huge. new frictions can block the difficult path towards peace in syria, as we have just discussed, but also in yemen. we did not discuss that this time, but i think we will tomorrow. these frictions can destabilise iraq and lebanon, the two countries in the region that are most exposed to sectarian tensions. they can destabilise entire muslim communities worldwide, from asia to africa, in the horn and in the sahel. bilateral tensions can, in this way, potentially inflame the region even more, prevent political processes from either starting or yielding results, and potentially inflame the war. this is why we are trying to contain and de-escalate these tensions in close coordination among ourselves as europeans, with all the member states. we are ensuring that we, our international partners, including the united states and, to mention just one, the foreign minister of indonesia – whom i had on the phone just before her trip to tehran and saudi arabia a few days ago – send a similar message to try and facilitate the containment and the de-escalation of the conflict. this shows how important this issue is in at least three continents, if not four, because potentially this could inflame communities around the world. as you may know, we reacted immediately on 2 january 2015 to the execution by the authorities of the shia cleric, sheikh nimr al-nimr, and 46 other individuals, most of whom had been convicted on terrorism charges in relation to their links to al-qaeda. as i expressed in the statement that i issued on the same day, the death penalty can in no way be sustainable or an efficient response to crime or terrorism. the eu opposes capital punishment under any circumstances, and we shall continue to consistently advocate for the universal abolition of the death penalty. this also refers to iran, whose human rights record is worrying. this is the message that i conveyed, not only to the foreign minister of saudi arabia, but also to the foreign minister of iran, whom i contacted at that time. the specific case of sheikh nimr al-nimr raises very serious concerns regarding issues such as freedom of expression and the respect of basic civil and political rights. these should be safeguarded in all cases. also let me stress that, in the framework of the fight against terrorism, we have also taken an immediate position on the reactions in iran because nothing can justify an attack on embassies or consulates, as happened with the saudi embassy in tehran and the consulate in mashhad. in the conversations i had with both the iranian and the saudi foreign ministers in the wake of these events, i stressed the need for iran to abide by its international obligations. this also means ensuring the protection of diplomatic premises in all circumstances. in my phone call with both sides and in the contacts we had afterwards (we met with mr zarif over the weekend, among other people) the main message i passed on was to try to manage the bilateral tensions without inflaming the risk of spill-overs, especially in the region, to preserve our efforts for peace in syria and yemen and to avoid further destabilisation in the area, especially with regard to iraq and lebanon. i was given reassurances by both sides on the need to find a way of preserving this process. as we have said, for the syria process to begin and have some chance of succeeding, it must be supported by all the regional players. for the same reason, to try to find common ways of protecting the process, early this year i discussed the situation, and the risks of it degenerating, with the un special envoy for syria, staffan de mistura, the secretary-general of the arab league, ministers of many arab and african countries, and with some asian ministers. we are also coordinating messages and actions, not only with our partners, but first and foremost among europeans. this was the case yesterday at the foreign affairs council, where we discussed and agreed on common lines in this regard. finding a negotiated solution to the current conflicts in the middle east is in everybody’s interest, especially everyone in the region. protracted war can only benefit terrorists of all kinds, and it can only let instability spread further well beyond the borders of the middle east; we in europe know that very well. this is not a zero-sum game, and this is the other strong message we are passing on to our iranian and saudi friends. if the wars in syria and in yemen and the tensions in the region do not stop, everybody will lose. there is not a single place in the region that can benefit from the escalation of tensions. the only alternative to a win-win solution, where everybody sees their interests recognised, is chaos and further chaos. it took us months to gather all regional powers around the same table to discuss peace in syria. as we said, the same goes for libya, a country from which we had encouraging news today since we managed to unite the region’s international actors in a process along similar lines to that which we put together for syria. we cannot afford to waste any of these positive trends and we cannot afford to expose them to tensions that need to stay contained – if possible at a bilateral level. the european union will keep doing all that we can to promote dialogue, and fight sectarianism. this is because we have learned our own eu lesson. i said this in the previous debate, about colombia. this is the eu lesson. it is only regional cooperation that brings peace and prosperity, and we have experienced this for 60 years now. only through this kind of regional understanding, cooperation and partnership did we manage to overcome centuries of war and conflict and experience peace in our region. this is our way. we believe it is regional cooperation – and never confrontation or competition – that is beneficial for all. this is particularly true for an area of the world like the middle east.

madam president, the european union, through its institutions, has always been concerned with respect for the fundamental rights and values enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights. the presumption of innocence is a right, but also a value, which has received increased attention from both the member states and the european institutions. strengthening it, and identifying mechanisms to guarantee it throughout the criminal process, has been a serious challenge in highly complex and at the same time diverse judicial systems. on the basis of the premise that judicial decisions must be considered equivalent, regardless of the member state in which they were taken, we understand the need to develop judicial cooperation in this field between the member states of the european union. to this end, it is necessary to establish common minimum standards on the right to a fair trial throughout the criminal proceedings. we therefore consider it extremely important that any person accused of a crime should have access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings, but not least that he should be given the opportunity to communicate with third parties and in particular with consular authorities during his deprivation of liberty. the adoption of this directive constitutes an additional guarantee of respect for the right to a fair trial, so that a person is not considered guilty by a public authority before the conviction is established by a final judgment.
madam president, as rapporteur for the epp group on mrs stihler's report, i would like to thank and congratulate the three rapporteurs, mrs ford, mrs stihler and mr antonio lópez, for all the work they have done over the past few months. the new gas appliances regulation is an example of union harmonisation legislation, ensuring both the free movement of gas appliances and the placing on the market or putting into service of gas appliances that meet higher consumer safety standards, thereby also reducing gas safety risks and ensuring, at the same time, a more rational use of energy. from simple portable stoves to large power plants for very large buildings, the current stock of gas-consuming appliances in the european union is 470 million and growing, with over 30 million units sold each year. i am pleased and very grateful that the rapporteur, mrs stihler, has embraced the idea of introducing and amending the text from the point of view of consumer safety, adding amendments relating to the precautions that should have been and must be taken to avoid and prevent the poisoning of people with gases, including carbon monoxide, and the leakage of any substances that could cause health and safety problems, carbon monoxide poisoning being a major cause of death associated with the use of gas appliances. the new legislation will clearly benefit european citizens.

in writing. the dutch presidency must take concrete steps to create the digital single market and to implement the energy union projects. these two markets will have a positive effect on growth and job creation in innovative fields. the dutch presidency must actively engage in achieving the union's energy union objectives by promoting common energy market rules. the eu must take decisive steps to strengthen its energy policy based on competitiveness, sustainability and security of supply. the european investment fund is a tool in the hands of the dutch presidency to encourage the promotion of investment projects in the modernisation of energy infrastructure, cross-border network connectivity and to promote technologies that promote energy efficiency. simplification and harmonisation of european digital rules and standards must be the top priority for building the digital market. the dutch presidency should focus on the rights of consumers and cross-border digital workers. further integration of the internet single market and strengthening consumer confidence in digital technologies, ensuring security, transparency and privacy are issues to be taken into account. consumers should be informed about the use of their data, in particular in the case of services provided in exchange for data.
in writing. the dutch eu presidency has the opportunity to tackle a number of impactful energy and telecommunications proposals during its term. in the field of telecommunications, a modern regulatory framework for telecommunications companies is needed to strengthen competition, competitiveness and investment in this sector. it is also necessary to review the wholesale market for roaming services and to propose a harmonised framework for spectrum allocation, and for egovernment we need an ambitious and comprehensive action plan. the dutch presidency also set out to contribute to the energy union objectives of reducing energy dependency and ensuring affordable energy. the commission will also be presenting a report on the implementation of the energy union strategy, which will be presented in the next few months. another legislative proposal with an impact on european industry is the revision of the ets. i stress that we must ensure that the proposed objectives and targets are not met to the detriment of european industry and jobs.
in writing. the dutch eu presidency has a crucial role to play in harmonising member states' positions on the refugee issue, with the primary aim of safeguarding the schengen area. today, the schengen area is in danger, and its collapse means the collapse of the union. the dutch presidency takes up its mandate at a time of unprecedented challenges for the eu. its top priority, the integrated approach to migration and international security, is well-defined but does not sufficiently reflect the urgency of the measures needed. we need more ambition. we have to acknowledge the eu's failure to address the refugee crisis. we have failed to formulate a common european response to the refugee crisis. we must say it loud and clear: not all migrants who come to europe can stay in europe. we need a clear rule to distinguish between refugees and economic migrants. we have a moral duty to provide protection to refugees from syria, but we also have to identify economic migrants who need to be directed back to their home countries. the dublin mechanism needs to be reviewed as a matter of urgency on the basis of the ec proposal expected in march. a radical reform of frontex is needed to ensure effective protection of the eu's external borders. in this way, by preserving the area of free movement, we prevent the disintegration of our union.

in writing. ‒ the development of crossborder cooperation aims to support the fight against terrorism and international crime. we must remember that europe is also attractive to investors because of the legislative framework that preserves and promotes data exchange to guarantee increased security for citizens. in order to achieve this objective of cooperation and to continue development in all sectors in a secure framework, the union needs to support a system of exchange of information as effective as possible, which, in the case of latvia, has also developed on the basis of decision 2008/615/jha. given that this country has already fully implemented the fundamental principles of data protection in its legal system, completed the vehicle registration questionnaires and, moreover, in a pilot test, obtained a successful assessment, i consider that it can now provide personal data in accordance with decision 2008/615/jha on the automatic exchange of data. i support the european objective of cooperation and security and that is why i voted in favour of this report on the launch of automatic exchange of vehicle registration data in latvia.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on automated data exchange with regard to vehicle registration data (vrd) in latvia, as it will strengthen cross-border law-enforcement cooperation in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report that will step up cross-border cooperation in combating terrorism and cross-border crime through the launch of automated data exchange with regard to vehicle registration data.

in writing. ‒ a viable european union cannot exist without an effective judiciary. the ongoing legislative work of the european union supports the functioning of the procedural framework, and the legal pillars need to be strengthened and applied uniformly in order to recognise the freedoms of citizens on which the union is built. the presumption of innocence is a fundamental right and an essential principle for avoiding arbitrariness and any abuse in criminal proceedings, as well as a principle underpinning the protection of the right to a fair trial. this proposal for a directive is all the more important as there is currently in many member states a reduction in the rights of suspects and accused persons and an erosion of the principle of the presumption of innocence, with the violation also occurring in the media. both the presumption and the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings are intended to guarantee a certain minimum level of protection in all member states and to strengthen the rights of accused persons. i therefore conclude that we need to ensure that member states have adequate legislation to prevent such harm, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the removal of a specific reference to presumption of facts or law concerning criminal liability (reversal of the burden of proof) from the operative part of the text: this was a key achievement. similarly, the agreement on the text of the right to remain silent represents a significant improvement on the commission proposal and the council’s general approach. with regard to public references to guilt undermining the presumption of innocence and the role of the media, the result is satisfactory. the same goes for the text agreed upon in relation to in absentia trials. effective procedural safeguards in criminal proceedings at eu level remain crucial to establish the appropriate balance in the eu between repressive measures and the individual’s right to a fair trial. the adoption of rules governing the presumption of innocence is an important step in establishing that balance.
in writing. ‒ the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings is a highly important issue and concerns the life and dignity of persons. i voted for the report because i believe that there is a need for better implementation in all member states of article 11 (1) of the universal declaration of human rights adopted by the un in 1948. i believe in the need for suspects or accused persons to enjoy adequate protection against incriminating public statements prior to final conviction. member states should ensure that suspects or accused persons appear or are presented in the courtroom before and during the trial in an appropriate manner, as handcuffing or holding in a glass box creates the impression of guilt before being tried. i also believe in the report's provision regarding the defendant's right to remain silent. this right shall not prejudice the right to a fair trial. the right to remain silent cannot be used against the person in any way.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this report that guarantees a minimum level of protection for the principle of presumption of innocence in all member states. this is a fundamental right that represents the key to preventing arbitrary judgments and any abuse of process in criminal proceedings.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that aims to set a common set of regulations across member states in order to enforce the presumption of innocence and further rights in criminal procedure trials.
in writing. ‒ the presumption of innocence is one of the concepts underlying the legal systems of the eu member states. however, its application in practice faces a number of difficulties linked to possible infringements, sometimes unintentional, of this right. one of the main issues that arise is the violation of the right to remain silent in the context of which it can lead to the indictment of a suspect. another issue concerns ensuring that punitive measures are proportionate to the amount of damage caused. problems also arise when excessive media exposure of a suspect, sometimes produced with a significant contribution from public authorities, unduly infringes the right of defence of the suspect. in any event, the burden of proof in a trial must remain with the prosecution, in accordance with the principles of law existing at european level. the use of coercive measures to obtain evidence directly from the accused is not compatible with european practices and should lead to the invalidation of that evidence. at the same time, the right to be present at one's own trial, under criminal proceedings, must be guaranteed, except where the accused person waives this right. the adoption of this report is an additional guarantee of respect for the rights of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ the functioning of the european union's single market for distribution is intrinsically linked to the strengthening of cooperation between the various parties involved and could be optimized by introducing common definitions for the harmonisation and simplification of regulations on goods across the market, as proposed in this regulation. recent developments in the field of communications and the need to adapt personal protective equipment (ppe) to its end-users require the implementation of specific tools to enable end-users to have a correct understanding of how ppe is used, in particular to protect themselves against workplace risks. if workers are aware of these issues and are properly and appropriately informed, they will not only be protected but also involved in matters that directly concern them. the safety of workers can only be guaranteed by means of instruments of undeniable effectiveness, since accidents at work are often caused not only by the non-use of adequate protection systems but also by their incorrect use. i voted in favour of the proposed measures, which ensure that the existing directive cannot give rise to interpretations which undermine its effectiveness and legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ the regulation aligns the current legislation to the provisions of the goods package adopted in 2008 and in particular to the decision 768/2008/ec on a common framework for the marketing of products. this concerns requirements for the design and manufacture of personal protective equipment (ppe) which is being made available on the market in order to ensure the protection of users and rules on its free movement in the union. it includes rules on market surveillance and obligations for economic operators as well as employers. the committee vote was uncontroversial. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this report that provides technical clarifications for the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on personal protective equipment.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this report on ppe (personal protective equipment) according to which all member states should improve their current regulations, taking into consideration that health and safety protection is extremely important for all eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ i am voting today in favour of the report on personal protective equipment, as i believe it is extremely important that legislation in this area is clear and comprehensive. the legislation in this area is based on an eec directive from 1989 which has been supplemented over the years, which has left this legislation with gaps and provisions that make the bureaucratic process difficult. in this context, the completion, clarification and simplification of the legislation will bring major benefits to both the manufacturers and the beneficiaries of such protective equipment.
in writing. ‒ the way in which consumer products are marketed in the member states must be a matter of permanent concern to the european institutions. in this respect, european legislation needs to be aligned with the provisions of the legislative package adopted in 2008, in particular decision (ec) no 768/2008 on the common framework for the marketing of products. it concerns in particular the requirements for the design and production of personal protective equipment which is being placed on the european market for the first time, as well as the rules on free movement within the union. they include provisions relating to the supervision of marketing and compliance with the obligations of the economic operators and companies involved. not included are products for self-defence, a number of household products for personal use, some decorative or craft products. the main issue is the implementation of these rules in practice, which the commission must actively monitor. however, the adoption of the current report is an important step forward in this area and supports citizens by enriching the range of safe and certified products they can choose from. the same applies to the report on appliances consuming gaseous fuels.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on personal protective equipment (ppe), which is the european parliament's opinion on directive 89/686/eec, which has fully harmonised the placing of personal protective equipment on the eu market since 1989. the report adopted by parliament contributes to the updating of the legislation on ipr and clarifies the role of economic operators and the powers of market surveillance authorities to track and return unsafe goods entering the single market.
in writing. ‒ the gas sector plays an important role in the eu economy and creates 476 000 jobs in the gas appliance sector alone. the european union aims to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market for appliances consuming gaseous fuels. it requires clear and detailed rules which will become uniformly applicable at the same time throughout the union. the mandatory essential requirements and the conformity assessment procedures to be followed by manufacturers should be identical in all member states. the text, which is in line with the single market act, will be strengthened from the point of view of consumer safety by adding amendments related to the precautions to be taken to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning in people, which is the main cause of deaths associated with the use of gas appliances in europe. all the measures proposed in the report are appropriate means to achieve transparency of european union legislation and to ensure the free movement of gas-consuming appliances, which is why i voted in favour of replacing the directive.
in writing. ‒ the regulation aligns current legislation to the provisions of the goods package adopted in 2008 and in particular to decision 768/2008/ec on a common framework for the marketing of products. it applies to domestic and non-domestic appliances intended for a number of specified applications burning gaseous fuels and to fittings designed to be incorporated into such appliances. it concerns the placing on the market of these products and protection of consumers while using the products concerned. our main achievements concern rules to prevent gas poisoning and the leakage of any substances harmful to health and safety. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this report with regard to appliances that use gaseous fuels taking into consideration that the gas sector is an important sector in the eu economy. the current eu stock of gas appliances is at 470 million and growing, with more than 30 million units being sold annually.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will regulate the gas appliances sector by creating a single market which will have a positive impact on the european union in terms of businesses and consumers.
in writing. i voted for the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on appliances burning gaseous fuels which will replace directive 2009/142/ec. this directive is an example of union harmonisation legislation ensuring the free movement of gas-consuming appliances. the gas sector plays an important role in the eu economy and creates 476 000 jobs in the gas appliance sector alone.
in writing. ‒ the conditions for placing on the market of subsystems and safety components for cableway installations and ensuring the free movement of these products in the eu are an example of the need to harmonise european legislation. the union is working towards better regulation to ensure the free movement of these products. all safety components and subsystems will have to be designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements set out in this regulation, which will enhance product quality and human safety. it is noted that member states still retain their competence to regulate other aspects of cable installations such as land use, regional planning and environmental protection, although they opt for regulation. the choice is welcome as it will eliminate unnecessary transposition costs and impose clear and detailed rules that will be uniformly applicable throughout the union. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that both for these proposed measures and for the change of the legal instrument from a directive to a regulation, it is appropriate to simplify the regulatory framework substantially and avoid the risk of divergent transposition.
in writing. ‒ the regulation aligns current legislation to the provisions to the goods package adopted in 2008 and in particular to decision 768/2008/ec on a common framework for the marketing of products. it applies to new cableway installations and covers subsystems and safety components which are new to the union market when they are placed on the market. the regulation does not apply to cableway installations of historical construction, installations intended for agricultural or forestry purposes, cableway installations for the service of mountain shelters and huts intended only for the transport of goods and specifically authorised persons and on-site or mobile equipment exclusively designed for leisure and amusement purposes and not as a means for transporting persons. the new regulation improves market surveillance and safety for consumers and other users of cableway installations. a main achievement is the inclusion of the explicit mentioning of the precautionary principle, as well as enhanced safety for consumers and other users. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this report as it sets out to harmonise the conditions of placing on the market of subsystems and safety components for cable installations and to ensure the free movement of these products in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will facilitate free movement of cable installations and will increase efficiency in the market of subsystems.
in writing. ‒ cable installations for passenger transport are no longer an image that belongs exclusively to tourist resorts or mountain areas with limited access. lift systems such as funiculars, cable cars, cable cars, gondolas and chairlifts contribute to citizens' mobility by tackling the challenges normally associated with traditional urban transport such as congestion and poor air quality. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to harmonise the arrangements for placing on the internal market subsystems and safety components for cableway installations and the conditions under which they can move freely within the european union. personally, i can only welcome such a measure, which will facilitate the adoption of this mode of transport in the urban environment, where we are faced on a small scale with the most serious pollution problems, which have serious implications for the health of european citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on cable installations, which is an example of harmonisation of union legislation. the regulation adopted by the ep aims to harmonise the conditions for placing on the market of safety components and subsystems for cableway installations and to ensure the free movement of these products within the eu.
in writing. ‒ granting a requesting country the benefit of the special incentive arrangement for sustainable development and good governance by adding it to the list of gsp+ countries is an important step in that country's development, which is why the union wants to ensure that it supports the strengthening of a democratic system and that all the measures that follow from this are geared towards the safety of citizens and the respect of their fundamental rights. however, in the kyrgyz republic, assessments by several bodies, including the committee against torture (cat), the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination (cerd), the international labour organisation committee on the application of standards (ilo cas), the committee on the rights of the child, have made it clear that this country still has substantial processes to demonstrate that it wants to improve the lives of its citizens and strengthen a system of law. the presence of torture, the exploitation of children, the violation of the right to defence and the discrimination against ethnic minorities cannot be accepted. i therefore voted in favour of this report on the objection to the application of a generalised system of tariff preferences to kyrgyzstan.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against this motion for a resolution on generalised tariff preferences taking into consideration that the kyrgyz republic has ignored the european parliament’s resolution of 15 january 2015 on the country’s homosexual propaganda bill.

in writing. ‒ the application of a generalised system of tariff preferences (gsp) by the european union is a useful tool for developing trade relations with third countries. such agreements between the eu and other states are likely to remove barriers to free trade and increase the union's influence worldwide. the conclusion of such agreements implies that third states respect certain european values and rules, including in the area of democratic governance. the commission is now proposing to promote such an agreement, from the gsp to gsp+ in relation to kyrgyzstan. despite the clear benefits of such a measure, a number of internal problems persist, calling into question the timeliness of this important step. in concrete terms, this is the continuation of reprehensible practices such as torture and imprisonment, corruption in the judicial sector, high death rates in detention, ethnic conflicts, discrimination against minorities (including sexual), poor treatment of minors. in these circumstances, the present resolution rightly notes that there is a need to reconsider the measure envisaged by the commission and to support the remediation of the areas of shortcomings in this country. for this reason, the resolution is timely and should be supported.
in writing. ‒ poor nutrition is currently the leading cause of disease and mortality worldwide, while global food security is an important objective of the union and action in this regard, given the impact on this segment of the population, should be taken in consultation with global research bodies, taking into account in particular the questioning of breastfeeding and the worsening of childhood obesity. in addition to the fact that labelling and marketing of products should be reviewed in line with the world health assembly's recommendations on foods for infants and young children, it cannot be overstated that transparency is needed in the eu decision-making process by providing public access to commission meeting documents during the process of drafting the delegated regulation. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union needs to clarify and adapt these aspects of the health and optimal nutrition of its citizens, especially of categories such as infants and young children, who are a particularly vulnerable population with regard to endocrine disruptors and other contaminants.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the specific compositional and information requirements for processed cereal-based food and baby food. the world health organization clarifies that healthy food is a primary step in the good and healthy development of a baby. a primordially negative factor of obesity for children is sugar added in the early stages of developing, thus the amount of sugar added to baby foods should be reduced.
in writing. ‒ according to a report created by the commission, one in three children aged between 6-9 years old in eu is overweighed or obese. consequently, i voted for this motion as it is necessary to implement a set of rules in order to diminish these risks.
in writing. ‒ there is a childhood obesity crisis affecting a large number of children in europe and storing up health problems for tomorrow’s adults. infant and childhood diet profoundly affects child health and future eating habits. too much sugar in baby foods can lead to over-consumption of sugar and inappropriate calorie intake in the long term, causing obesity and increasing the risk factor for conditions such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and some cancers. the sugar limits set for baby foods can have major consequences, so we need to get them right. we cannot ignore the big discrepancy between the recent who recommendations and the commission’s proposal. i am delighted a majority of colleagues joined me in backing this resolution and look forward to the commission’s revised proposal.
in writing. ‒ food safety of products traded within eu member states is one of the main objectives of the european institutions. regulation in the food sector should take into account the highest standards in the field. moreover, regulations on baby food must take special safety standards into account to the fullest extent possible, because any escape can cause unimaginable tragedies. to this end, the labelling of baby food marketed at european level should be as detailed as possible in order to avoid the use of certain substances by infants and young children. more stringent control of sugar intake by infants and young children, which can lead to obesity, is also needed. a zero tolerance for pesticides in food is required. all food safety decisions must be taken in a transparent manner, to allow all stakeholders to participate in the decision-making process. in order to support these wishes and to improve the commission delegated regulation in this area, it is necessary to adopt this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the political and cooperation agreement between the european union and the andean community has also resulted in this welcome resolution on the promotion of peace-building in colombia. maintaining stability is a complex process that needs to be worked on in several stages, from addressing the problems of illegal armed groups and drug trafficking to transitional justice, then alternative and rural development and, of course, demobilization and reintegration of former combatants, including through psychosocial programmes for child soldiers and female combatants who have suffered sexual abuse. all forms of suffering caused by such conflicts must be condemned and it is important to take into account in particular the right of victims of the conflict to full, genuine and fair reparation for the physical, moral and material damage suffered. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union must support the full and complete implementation of the peace agreement and the efforts of the colombian government and the farc to reach the agreements signed so far on political participation and democratic openness, thereby providing a positive example of a conflict resolution process.
in writing. ‒ after more than one year and a half of negotiations, the colombian government and the revolutionary armed forces of colombia have finally reached a ground-breaking agreement on transitional justice, which is a definitive step forward to a conclusive peace in the long-lasting armed conflict in latin america. the transitional justice agreement has resolved some of the most serious sticking points and makes any derailment of the peace process highly unlikely. i strongly support the call for a bilateral and definitive ceasefire agreement and for starting a similar process with the eln (national liberation army) guerrillas in order to have a complete and lasting peace in colombia. the eu cannot let this historic moment get away. we must give full support to the talks that will put an end to 50 years of armed conflict.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that supporting the peace process for the benefit of the eu's political, economic and trade partners is and will be one of the most important foreign policies of the european union. in this regard, today's report presents the current unstable situation in colombia, the measures taken by the colombian government to improve it and the importance of colombia in its relationship with the eu. i also welcome the intention of european states to create a trust fund to serve the post-conflict phase, which is open to participation by communities and civil society organisations and which takes into account the priorities expressed by victims in terms of truth, justice, reparations and guarantees of non-recurrence.
in writing. ‒ the recent events in colombia represent a new hope for the peaceful internal development of this country. the agreement signed by the colombian government with the revolutionary armed forces of colombia (farc) on the provision of transitional justice provides the basis for a lasting solution to this internal armed conflict after more than 50 years. this agreement involves a series of amnesties for farc members, aimed at ensuring increased trust between the two parties, which is considered essential for the conclusion of a peace agreement in the near future. the european union has consistently supported the peace process in colombia, one of its important partners in latin america. we are witnessing a historic moment that could lead to the end of one of the world's longest and bloodiest civil conflicts. we must therefore welcome this positive development and encourage a final ceasefire. at the same time, however, we must not forget the similar conflict between the colombian government and the national liberation army, for which a similar agreement is needed. only under these conditions will colombia and its citizens be able to move towards a normal situation in which they can reach their real development potential.
that concludes the explanations of vote.
the european union is also a key player in the fight against climate change. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you very much for your comments, your questions. i thank those who have spoken, those who have not spoken. i was going to tell you, mr president, that having heard what i heard, i am prepared to come every day, because it was a real bed of roses. more seriously, i would like to return to the compliments you have paid to commissioner cañete: they are justified. with regard to french diplomacy, i will be a little more nuanced, but i will save that for the end. but first, many of you have returned to the question of 1.5 and 2 degrees and the ambition which i believe is remarkable and which is, moreover, recognised by everyone in this agreement. i admit that we might have disagreed, because after all, the previous conferences had not yet given an example of perfect success, as they say at the quai d'orsay. but the main risk, at least the risk i identified, was that we agreed, but on a minimum ambition and we talked about it often, you remember. but let's be honest, not everything is settled. that said, the success of paris, in essence, is to have reached an agreement between 195 countries without any opposition and people were free on a content that is very ambitious. and that's where the two and one-and-a-half degrees come in. you have seen, and this has given rise to long discussions, that the writing is not exactly the same for 2 and 1.5 degrees. for the 2 degrees, it was already not easy to obtain; i remember, having replaced president hollande at the g20, that i had already had a lot of trouble getting the 2 degrees. and then what happened? there has been a kind of dynamic in international conferences that advocates multilateralism. there have been very strong interventions from, in particular, the small islands, from their representatives, who have said that, of course, 2 degrees is very good, but if you don't write 1.5 degrees and if you don't make arrangements to go to 1.5 degrees, you are implicitly saying that we, we no longer exist. it's not just a question of whether we can live well or not: we'll be covered, we won't be able to exist anymore. this argument was so strong that it convinced countries that were not spontaneously in favour of 1.5 degrees. i'll use my hands. today, when we add up all the cpdns, we're pretty much on the 3-degree trajectory, to be honest. what is at stake, through the paris agreement and now the subsequent decisions, since all this is on a fairly long horizon, is to move from a 3 degree trajectory to a 2 degree and 1.5 degree trajectory. and this requires a whole series of concrete actions and a point that many of you have highlighted, namely technological innovation and major investments. at first, i wasn't the world's leading expert on these issues, i have to admit, but i'm a hard worker, so i dug into the subject. i'm absolutely convinced that there's going to be major technological changes that will make the financial hierarchy of energy quite different from what it is today. as many of you have already pointed out, in some cases renewable energy is already much cheaper, when you add up the direct and indirect costs, than highly polluting energy such as coal. we shall be going more and more in that direction. the ambition of the agreement and its universality were not contradictory but complementary, and this is one of the great successes of paris. secondly, several of you have rightly commented on the air and sea sectors in international transport. so, i'll be square then, too. there were several parties, including the european union, who wanted us to include international transport in the agreement. but you know the mechanism, which is the mechanism of consensus. it became apparent quite quickly that this point was met with strong opposition - let's call it what it is - from several emerging economies and gulf countries, and therefore consensus was not possible. this does not in any way prevent icao and imo, the two international organisations responsible for this matter, from taking action in this respect. europe, the cop 21 presidency and all those of good will will be mobilizing this year. the icao has set itself the objective of reaching an agreement by september 2016 to stabilise aviation emissions after 2020, and why not to reduce them. the european union, if i may put it that way, must be at the forefront of this issue and promote compromises well in advance. as regards the maritime sector, the discussions are admittedly less advanced, but compliance with the objectives set out in the paris agreement implies that negotiations should be opened without delay in the case of the imo. first of all, it seems to me that the eu should encourage the recognition of emissions levels from the maritime sector and the establishment of a system for measuring global emissions from the maritime sector. but you are absolutely right, because this represents considerable greenhouse gas emissions, that this year, significant progress must be made in both these areas. thirdly, many of you have spoken, and you are quite right, about low carbon, high carbon, competitiveness and so on. it's absolutely central. there is no contradiction between greenhouse gas emissions on the one hand and the requirements of competitiveness or employment on the other. of course, we need changes, we need accompanying measures, but i am absolutely convinced that competitiveness, not only for countries like ours but also at world level, must go hand in hand with a move towards low-carbon production, and this is where we come to the question - i believe mr jadot asked it - of divestment or investment. yes, you have already seen that outside of the very public investment, which is very important and essential, in the private sector, there is a shift that is taking place, and that's good; we need to be able to speed it up. first, i think that countries should gradually reduce subsidies for fossil fuels. this principle, i remind you, was set by the european council in may 2013 and france had advocated an ambitious position, for example, in the framework of export credits for coal-fired power stations. we need to make this movement global and, as i was going to say, take advantage of the fact that oil prices are low. you know the numbers: we're talking about 100 billion that we rich countries have to allocate to poor countries for climate, but the money that goes into fossil fuel subsidies is over 500 billion a year; so we have orders of magnitude in mind. secondly, to answer mr jadot, we must encourage private sector actors not to invest, or even to divest, in the high carbon sectors and, as far back as cop 21, we are seeing a movement: the first sovereign wealth fund, which is a norwegian fund, has instructed that there should be divestments in this sector, to the extent that the governor of the bank of england believes that the next financial bubble could well occur in the carbon sector, because we will see that this sector, of course, will have difficulties, whereas massive investments have been made in it. i think that in the private sector, we can ask central bankers and rating agencies to now systematically take climate risk into account and make the disclosure of carbon footprints mandatory. these are not out of our reach and would be extremely useful. however, in parallel with this trend towards divestment, there is a need to maintain a constant effort in favour of investments in renewable energy; the needs are immense. the european union has instruments - the juncker plan, the structural funds, eib projects, etc. - which, in my view, can and must be mobilised. you have a european council in march and i believe that the commission will take stock of the evaluation of the implementation of the paris agreement. these are really directions that we quite remarkable alignment of the planets. the first planet was the planet itself. 2015 was the warmest year on record, with significant disasters and a public awareness, and this disastrous situation has, if i may say so, a positive side: it made even more clear that there had to be an agreement, and it fostered awareness. so the first planet, which is our planet, is an alignment element. the second planet -- i really want to pay tribute to him -- is the science planet. i would like to pay tribute here to the remarkable work of scientists, and in particular to the work of the ipcc, which has established the undeniable nature of warming and quantified the threats. when we had public meetings, five, 10 years ago, etc., half the meeting was devoted to whether or not there was climate change, and the second half of the meeting was devoted to whether it was due to human action. now, i'm not saying that these debates have completely disappeared, but they have largely disappeared, at least in many of our countries, and that's thanks to the work of scientists. this science planet has been a great help. the third planet is the planet that i'll call the socio-political planet. there have been major greenhouse gas emitters that have taken very strong positions: china, the leading emitter, which for obvious reasons, which are practical, economic, societal and social reasons, has played a very important role, president obama, who has been very committed and, of course, the european union, and other countries, but this has allowed for there to be, in parallel, a very strong evolution of the economic circles, the involvement of the communes, the involvement of the regions, the involvement of the ngos, the involvement of the great spiritual and religious voices, and all of this, this planet that i call the political-social, which is a new element, which has obviously made the paris conference in very different circumstances from the famous copenhagen conference. and finally, the diplomatic fact that this is the planet. our task has been to promote convergence with all the countries, and particularly with the european union, and to translate all this into an international agreement with its 29 articles and 140 decision points. i am often asked: but the work of a diplomat, etc. i say, with a little humor, that i don't fully understand the reasons for this success, but i would rather not understand the reasons for success, than have brilliant explanations for failure, but once i've said that, deep down, when i look back a little bit at the work we've done, it's a bit of a sculptor's work. you know, the sculptor takes blocks of clay, he takes the main blocks first, which were china, the united states, europe, india, and he had to add all these blocks together and then give them a certain shape. then there are the smaller blocks, which are also necessary because, without consensus, there is no agreement. we had to give shape to all this, but without losing any of these blocks and, finally, this is the work we have done in a spirit of transparency, trust, which has been highlighted. at the end of this show -- and i'll give a little hammer to mr. schulz, who became the most famous hammer -- and it's quite rare in international conferences, everybody kissed. but it wasn't something we agreed on; we had the feeling that in a world that was really very tough, very dangerous, very complicated and very uncertain, for one of the first times, through the work of all of us, there was really something that was going to allow not only this generation, but future generations, to live a better life. as has been pointed out, of course, these are circumstances which are not always politically encountered in one's life, so i thank you all for making this possible.

in writing. ‒ stabilising and developing the western balkans region has been a consistent policy pursued by the european union over the past two decades. through existing instruments or by creating others specifically designed for this purpose, the eu has come to the aid of the citizens of the region, with a view to normalizing their lives and the possibility of aspiring to european citizenship in the future. the main instrument that can strengthen the evolution of the states in the region towards eu membership is the stabilisation and association agreement. it creates the conditions for attracting more foreign investment, developing business environments, economic growth and good governance through the application of european standards and community legislation. for this reason, the conclusion of the agreement is an important motivating factor for the implementation and institutionalisation of the necessary reforms. such documents have been concluded with most of the states in the region. as regards kosovo, the uncertainty surrounding its international status has so far prevented the conclusion of a similar agreement. citizens living there must not, however, be deprived of the benefits enjoyed by other citizens in the region. before signing this agreement, however, it might be useful to also settle the issue of kosovo's status, in order to avoid ambiguous issues that can generate implementation problems.

in writing. ‒ the report on the appointment of members of the commission of inquiry into emission measurements in the motor vehicle sector is the result of the joint efforts of representatives of the main bodies of the european union to request an examination of allegations of irregularities and maladministration in the application of union legislation on emission measurements in the motor vehicle sector. the main objectives of this committee will be to monitor the emission test cycles carried out and to adapt them when they no longer meet the requirements so that they adequately reflect the emissions generated by real road traffic. the commission of inquiry will also carry out, within its mandate, various investigations into the implementation of the explicit prohibition on manipulation devices, the compliance with the provisions on effective, proportionate penalties for manufacturers for non-compliance with the rules for the use of manipulation devices, refusal to grant access to information and falsification of type-approval or functional conformity test results. i voted in favour of this agreement because i consider it essential to monitor compliance with the legal provisions on emission measurement in the motor vehicle sector in order to ensure a lawful framework for the functioning of this sector.
