in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of appointing the members of the committee of inquiry into emission measurements in the motor vehicle sector. the newly formed 45-member committee will investigate breaches of eu rules on car emissions testing and allegations that member states and the european commission have failed to apply eu standards. the commission of inquiry will present an interim report within 6 months and a final report within 12 months of the start of the activity. this committee will investigate the following issues related to the motor vehicle sector: the possible failure of the european commission to verify test cycles; the possible failure of the commission and member state authorities to take appropriate and effective measures to supervise enforcement; the possible failure of the commission to introduce tests that reflect real driving conditions; the possible failure of member states to take measures on effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for manufacturers who breach the law; whether the commission and member states had evidence of the use of 'protective equipment' before the outbreak of the scandal in september 2015.
in writing. ‒ the european union pursued a policy of expanding its sphere of economic and political influence in georgia, moldova and ukraine through the signing of association agreements, including deep and comprehensive free trade agreements. the three countries have therefore opted for a policy of rapprochement with the union, drawing up various ambitious reform programmes in a number of areas, such as democracy, good governance, the rule of law and human rights. the approach of georgia, moldova and ukraine to economic integration and closer policies with the european union reinforces the efforts of the three countries to approximate their national legislation to union standards. such an agreement therefore generates added value for the reform processes in these countries. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution as the in-depth association and free trade agreements are a priority in the european neighbourhood policy and also play a fundamental role in ensuring good governance, democracy, the rule of law and the promotion of human rights.
in writing. ‒ i support the implementation of the association agreements and would like to see more attention paid to the social dimension of the partnership. i believe that more efforts are needed in the area of the rule of law, in the fight against corruption, as well as in the strengthening of democracy. it is the right of these countries and their citizens to choose their own path to follow, as long as it is towards european values, towards democracy and market economy, towards respect for human rights and freedom, towards the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary and not towards an authoritarian dictatorial regime of the asian type. the republic of moldova is an entity belonging to the european culture, the south-east european space. this policy of confrontation promoted from eastern europe is neither in the interest of europe nor of that country.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the efforts made by georgia, moldova and ukraine in taking the necessary measures towards meeting eu standards for association agreements/deep and comprehensive free trade agreements (aa/dcfta). i also believe that the aa/dcfta provisions regarding energy cooperation are of great importance in order to ensure the development of competitive, transparent and non-discriminatory energy markets in line with eu rules and standards.
in writing. ‒ as rapporteur for moldova and shadow rapporteur for georgia in the inta committee, i welcome this resolution and its emphasis on our trade relations with those countries and, of course, also with ukraine. the eu is a key trading and economic partner for them, and it therefore plays an important role in their development. the dcftas, if properly implemented, will generate jobs and will bring significant improvements to the living conditions of their people. the resolution highlights the positive results in terms of exports to the eu during the first 12 months of the dcftas’ implementation for georgia and moldova. i expect the dcfta with ukraine to achieve similar results. however, the three countries must continue to pursue their reform agenda in the areas of judiciary, the rule of law and the fight against corruption and organised crime, to which i personally attach absolute priority in the institutional arena. these reforms will allow the countries to maximize and consolidate the economic benefits deriving from the full implementation of the dcftas. their economic integration through trade and investment with the eu is the only real mid-to-long—term source of social, economic, political and institutional dynamism and structural change for – hopefully – the better.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that will bring georgia, moldova and ukraine onto the path of closer political and economic integration with the european union, undergoing reforms in numerous areas such as human rights, good governance, and the rule of law and democracy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the association agreements/deep and comprehensive free trade agreements with georgia, the republic of moldova and ukraine. as s&d itre coordinator, i stress the importance of energy cooperation, security of supply and the development of competitive, transparent and non-discriminatory energy markets in line with eu rules and standards, as well as renewable energy and energy efficiency. the eu wants to strengthen the full integration of moldova, ukraine and georgia into the energy market through the energy community. the active support and solidarity in the field of energy demonstrated by the eu allowed russia to resume gas supplies to ukraine in the winter of 2015-2016. thus, member states should fully exploit the transit potential of ukraine, strengthen their cooperation to ensure energy supply to both the eu and ukraine and avoid the construction of new pipelines to deliver gas from russia to europe bypassing ukraine, which could have a negative impact on the eu's energy diversification strategy and on eu legislation. i support the eu's intention to promote the full integration of ukraine into the energy market through the energy community and to reduce energy dependence without placing an undue burden on private households.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the association agreement with georgia, the republic of moldova and ukraine because i believe it is very important for the european union to continue cooperation with these eastern partnership countries, despite pressure from the russian federation. in the context of events and progress in the three states, i support efforts to enhance cooperation with them, to encourage and support their development and stability, both economically and democratically and socially.
in writing. ‒ the european union pays particular attention to the stabilisation and development of the regions in its immediate neighbourhood and encourages the strengthening of relations with states that wish to do so. the conclusion of the association agreements, also known as the deep and comprehensive free trade agreements, represents a new step in strengthening cooperation with the countries of the region that have demonstrated that their relationship with the eu is one of their strategic objectives. as the ratification process of the agreements is almost completed and after a period of provisional application of their provisions, it is time for these documents to enter into full force. they will act as further confirmation and motivation for those countries to maintain the path of reforms they have been following in recent years. this is all the more so as there is currently political instability in the republic of moldova which must not escalate and the eu must support pro-european forces in all three countries. the eu's partnership with these states should also focus on progress in the rule of law, the fight against corruption and the strengthening of democracy, and should take into account the evolution of the social dimension in each state.
in writing. i was one of the epp initiators of the resolution on the association and/or free trade agreements with georgia, moldova and ukraine. the resolution adopted by the ep reiterates the eu's support to the three states to maintain their pro-european course and to maintain their territorial integrity. in the chapter on the republic of moldova, the ep expresses its concern about the political instability in chisinau, drawing attention to the fact that recent developments may lead to the destabilisation of the whole country, endangering the economy and thus the flow of foreign investment. the ep urges the political forces in the republic of moldova to speed up negotiations with a view to forming a government that will continue the reform processes in favour of the citizens of that state. the resolution also calls on the moldovan authorities to continue investigations and bring to justice those responsible for the theft of one million euros from the moldovan banking system.
in writing. ‒ in the wake of the terrorist attacks in paris on 13 november 2015, which claimed the lives of at least 130 people from over 26 countries, immediate action is needed to combat international terrorism. over the last decade, eu member states have been the target of several terrorist attacks, which have left hundreds dead and several thousand injured. the paris attacks led france to invoke the mutual defence clause, with the member states obliged to provide france with aid and assistance by all means at their disposal. such tragic events underline the importance of conflict prevention and the need for the union institutions to be more actively involved in security and defence policy and in promoting the transposition into practice of all the provisions in the field of security and defence policy enshrined in the treaties. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that solidarity, mutual aid and assistance between member states is imperative in such situations. at the same time, the fight against terrorism must remain a priority for the european union, with concrete measures to strengthen security policy and prevent crime.
in writing. ‒ this was the first time the mutual defence clause was invoked. the current case will serve as a precedent for the future use of the mutual defence clause and is therefore extremely relevant. unfortunately, the security and defence architecture foreseen by the treaties is not yet fully implemented. the treaty of lisbon provides the possibilities for enhanced cooperation in csdp, including the consignment of specific tasks and missions to clusters of states, as well as the concept of permanent structured cooperation in military matter, while the member states are responsible for achieving progress in the area of security and defence of the union. i strongly believe that the council and the member states should draft and adopt practical arrangements and guidelines for ensuring an effective response in the event that a member state invokes the mutual defence clause, as well as an analysis of the role of the eu institutions should that clause be invoked.
in writing. ‒ in light of the recent paris attacks, the french government has decided to invoke the mutual defence clause stipulated in the treaty of the european union. this means that member states now have an obligation to aid and assist france by all means in their power in its actions against terrorism, in this particular context. given that this is the first time that the clause has been invoked, the parliament’s resolution primarily calls for establishing a clear implementation and monitoring procedure for the clause. it is a sensible approach that can potentially lay the groundwork for an effective eu security and defence mechanism and i therefore support it.
in writing. ‒ the treaty of lisbon strengthens the solidarity between eu countries in dealing with external threats by introducing a mutual defence clause (article 42(7) of the treaty on european union). this mutual defence clause provides that if an eu country is the victim of armed aggression on its territory, the other eu countries have an obligation to aid and assist it by all means. i have voted for this resolution on the mutual defence clause.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i support the position expressed by the european parliament in this document. the fact that france invoked the mutual defence clause for the first time showed that there were no mechanisms in place to manage and coordinate such a situation. i therefore join those who support the establishment of a permanent civil-military command to plan and coordinate the eu emergency response system. in the context of increasing terrorist threats across the eu, it is essential that member states understand that only better cooperation and coordination can prevent these attacks and respond effectively in an emergency.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in france over the past year have demonstrated the need for the eu to strengthen its security and defence policy. the activation of the mutual defence clause, in accordance with article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union, was the automatic reaction of the member states, in order to defend democratic institutions and the civilian population. however, at present, the capabilities of member states to deploy troops for external intervention in syria and iraq, as requested by france, are limited. this requires, in the long term, the acceleration of the implementation of the security and defence architecture provided for in the eu treaties, through enhanced cooperation in the framework of the common security and defence policy. cooperation may also take place through groups of member states for specific missions, but also through permanent structured cooperation in the military field. the council and the member states are primarily responsible at this stage for adopting the practical arrangements to ensure a consistent response when the mutual defence clause is invoked. the role of the european institutions in this case should also be clarified. the current resolution is more than necessary, in support of improving the coordination of the various existing structures at national and european level.
in writing. ‒ respect for human rights irrespective of race, origin, religion, class, caste, sex, sexual orientation or colour has always been a priority for the european union, with the member states having an obligation to guarantee respect for the indivisibility of human rights. the un human rights council seeks to respect, promote and guarantee the universality of human rights, which is one of the cornerstones of european unity and integrity. member states therefore have a duty to take concrete action to facilitate the respect of these rights at national level, but also to cooperate internationally to remove obstacles to the enjoyment of human rights in all areas. the eu's priorities for the cdo sessions are centred around respect for social and economic rights, freedom of thought, conscience, religion and belief. the issue of migration and refugees, as well as human rights, women's and children's rights, is also a priority. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the process of mainstreaming human rights issues into eu policies needs to continue.
in writing. ‒ european lawmakers attach great importance to the issue of respect for human rights at global level, through the eu's active and constant involvement in all un human rights mechanisms. respect for human rights must be mainstreamed in all policies, such as those on peace and security, development cooperation, migration, trade and investment, humanitarian action, climate change and the fight against terrorism. the eusr for human rights should continue to enhance the effectiveness, coherence and visibility of the eu's human rights policy in the context of the un human rights council sessions and in close cooperation with the office of the un high commissioner for human rights. the eu should take the recommendations of the un universal periodic review into account in all eu policy dialogues with the countries concerned, in order to explore ways and means of implementing the recommendations through national and regional strategies. the priorities of the unhrc sessions in 2016 should include respect for civil and political rights, including individual and collective freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and association, economic and social rights, adopting a human rights-based approach to migration, the impact of climate change on human rights, and respect for the rights of women and children.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this report that will highlight our main priorities for the un human rights council sessions in 2016. i support the call on eu member states to reinforce the eu practice of speaking with one voice as it would raise the visibility and influence of the eu as a global actor. i believe this report will encourage the eeas, notably delegations in geneva and new york to increase the coherence, visibility and credibility of the eu’s action in the unhrc by further development of cross-regional outreach and cooperation and on lobbying all moderate states in the un. we must actively oppose any attempt to undermine the concept of universality, indivisibility and interdependence of human rights, underline the need to keep special procedures and to preserve the independence and the adequate funding of the office of the high commissioner for human rights, as well as sufficient funding for regional unhrc offices open.
in writing. ‒ i would first like to congratulate ambassador choi kyong-lim as president of the unhrc for 2016. i would also like to underline that it does not do the unhrc justice to support the election to the human rights council of countries which do not uphold respect for human rights. the fight against racial discrimination and xenophobia is of crucial importance and must be upheld as a central goal by the unhrc. furthermore, the eu’s position should be backed fully with respect to a zero tolerance towards the death penalty and the countries still making use of it.
in writing. ‒ the united nations human rights council has appointed ambassador choi kyong-lim as president for 2016. i have voted for this resolution that should set out the priorities of the united nations human rights council for 2016.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that respecting, promoting and guaranteeing the universality of human rights is part of the ethical and legal culture of the european union. all states have an obligation to guarantee respect for human rights regardless of race, origin, religion, class, caste, sex, sexual orientation or colour. i support the report voted today, as it presents the situation of some third countries and their problems in respect of human rights, as well as the eu's priorities and actions in this area. the eu reaffirms its zero tolerance for the death penalty, expresses its concern at the constitutional amendments undertaken in some countries to increase the limit on the number of presidential terms and stresses that minority communities must be promoted in order to achieve equality in all areas of life.
in writing. ‒ the european union's participation in the united nations human rights council is an expression of the importance that the community institutions attach to this subject. respect for human rights is a key condition for the eu in its relations with third countries. the event will address the issue of states under universal periodic review (upr), such as georgia, lebanon, mauritania, myanmar, nepal, oman and rwanda, as well as countries where the human rights situation is at a critical stage, such as syria, burundi, yemen and saudi arabia. it will also discuss specific issues that persist in various countries, including civil and political rights, social and economic rights, business rights, immigration, climate change, women's rights, children's rights, sexual minority rights, the death penalty and press freedom. what needs to be emphasized is the universality of human rights and their indivisibility. eu participation will provide an opportunity to express a common position, which will help to increase the visibility and credibility of the eu as a global actor, encouraging eu action in various parts of the world. for these reasons, this resolution deserves to be supported.
in writing. ‒ the activities of the committee on petitions in 2014 were reflected in the annual report, which provided a precise and complete picture of the work of the committee on petitions. citizens can express their concerns about the union's various policies and legislation by exercising their right to petition the european parliament. it is therefore a tool that allows citizens to raise their concerns with parliament about the impact of the various policies and legislative provisions of the european union on their daily lives. the results of this report are an important quantitative tool for evaluating the work of the committee. approximately 69,5% of the petitions received in 2014 were resolved at the beginning of the procedure, thus noting that the decision to send information to the petitioner and resolve the petition in the first phase of the procedure is a significant increase compared to 2013 (11,3%). i voted in favour of this report because i consider it extremely important to use these instruments to guarantee the right of free expression of the citizens of the member states on matters which fall within the union's fields of activity and which concern them directly, also appreciating the progress made in the work of the committee on petitions.
in writing. ‒ i believe it is very important to give a precise and full view of the work carried out in 2014 by the committee on petitions. statistics on the number of petitions received are an important quantitative tool in assessing the committee’s work. i believe we have to strongly focus on the needs of citizens, who were especially concerned by matters related to the environment, internal market or fundamental rights. it is important to explain how eu policies should be developed and to object to decisions made by national governments if the citizens ask for it. identifying the problems that organisers of european citizens’ initiatives encounter is also an issue that has to be addressed. we must ensure correct application of eu legislation by national authorities, to avoid legislation being poorly transposed or failure to apply eu legislation.
in writing. ‒ i strongly welcome the work undertaken by the committee on petitions and the right of citizens to monitor, defend and promote their rights regarding the legislative mechanism. the commission should be strongly engaged in the process of petitions. the commission should conduct investigations concerning the cases submitted to it and provide swift and accurate replies to the petitioners.
in writing. ‒ the 2014 annual report will provide an overview on the activities and work done by the petitions committee. i have voted in favour of this report, which will provide statistics on the number of petitions dealt with by the committee, the matters raised and the countries concerned.
in writing. ‒ the right of european citizens to petition on various issues of interest is one of the guarantees offered by the european institutions to ensure the widest possible participation in the decision-making process and to reduce the democratic deficit. the way in which this right is put into practice and the extent to which it is translated into concrete decisions at european level is indicative of the extent to which citizens are exercising their legitimate rights. the year 2014 marked certain trends in the european petition process which are in line with the trends of recent years. the number of petitions to the european institutions has thus decreased, but the number of petitions rejected and resolved has increased. the most common countries of origin include spain, germany, italy and romania, confirming the trend of previous years. among the favourite topics addressed by petitioners are justice, the environment, the internal market and fundamental rights, where it seems that there are the most problems at member state level. petitions sent by e-mail are also becoming more common than those sent on paper. what is worrying is the increase in the share of unresolved petitions, which indicates a certain rigidity of the european institutions. the problems identified in the report should be addressed by enhancing interinstitutional cooperation.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, the european union and its member states have a regular and frank dialogue with the government of ethiopia on issues related to democracy and human rights. our consistent message is that economic and social development must go together with political and human rights to make it sustainable. a strong civil society and freedom of expression, association, and peaceful assembly are crucial for creating a more prosperous, secure and more economically successful country. in that context, the european union is following recent unrest in oromia, triggered by the urban expansion plans for addis ababa city, closely and with concern. there were also ethnic clashes in the amhara region, which received less attention from the media but which also resulted in casualties. on 23 december 2015, the european external action service spokesperson called for a peaceful resolution of the disputes. these events show the importance of constructive dialogue to address grievances. we called for clarity on all acts of violence and abuses perpetrated against protesters, as well as accountability for such violations. we have raised these concerns with the ethiopian authorities in addis, and most recently in brussels when the minister for foreign affairs, dr tedros adhanom came to visit high representative/vice-president mogherini on 13 january. he recognised the situation and informed us that the addis ababa expansion master plan had been discarded. ethiopia is facing many other challenges, where we are also working with the government. the population has grown dramatically in recent decades, now reaching over 100 million people. this is a challenge in terms of job creation, service delivery and poverty reduction. the effects of two consecutive droughts and of el niño have left 10.2 million people in need of food assistance, in addition to eight million already benefiting from government programmes. this endangers the social and economic development of the country. in this context the european union provides, and will continue to provide, political and financial support for improving the human rights situation in ethiopia, but also for supporting, in parallel, efforts by the government in terms of poverty reduction, economic and social development and humanitarian issues. ethiopia is the biggest beneficiary of the 11th european development fund’s bilateral development envelope of eur 745 million, complemented by regional and thematic programmes and emergency trust fund operations for stability and addressing root causes of irregular migration and displaced persons in africa. despite these immense needs, ethiopia has an open door policy and is the largest refugee-hosting country in africa, with over 700 000 refugees. in the eu, we shall provide support on this issue through the regional development and protection programme for the horn of africa, as well as through the recently signed common agenda on migration and mobility. ethiopia is an important partner for the european union in many areas – migration, climate change, regional peace and stability to name but a few. we enjoy a constructive engagement on all these aspects that are important to europe, to ethiopia and to the region. in the same vein, the european union will resolutely continue to stress the importance of human rights in ethiopia and support the country in respect of the fundamental freedoms of its citizens.
question referred under the 'blue card' procedure mr. deva, you know we were together in korea and tried, you're right, to help the two koreas reconcile. i ask you directly: with your experience, do you think that we, as the european union, can really influence the unification of the two koreas? because i spoke to the unification minister of south korea, and it seemed to me that he didn't have a concrete agenda.
author. mr president, this debate on north korea is very important for several reasons. it is part of the condemnation of north korea's recent nuclear test. this test was conducted in violation of all un security council resolutions and it poses a very serious threat to the stability of the korean peninsula. the second main reason is that this year there was a korean candidate for the sakharov prize. reverend hyeon, who has devoted his life to defending human rights in north korea, has unfortunately not been officially nominated due to lack of support. the sakharov prize for a north korean human rights defender would be a major step forward in the fight for human rights. the impact of the sakharov prize on the countries concerned is not yet proven, but in the past it has helped to revive the debate on the issue of human rights and to encourage civil society to become more involved. that is why i would like to take this opportunity to invite our colleagues who really want to help north korea to support such a move this year. no one from north korea has ever been at least an official candidate for the nomination and that's absurd, because it's one of the last totalitarian countries. the prize has been given to important people, and i think we should also take this step towards north korea. it is also important that parliament sends a strong message to korea and that these human rights situations remain a priority for foreign policy. in this connection, we call in our resolution, mrs mogherini, for the situation in that country to be monitored closely and for constant pressure to be maintained on the regime. i wanted to put north korea back on the agenda of our resolutions, because i refuse to share the pessimism about the country's capacity for change. the north korean people deserve our continued commitment, and the regime will not undertake any reforms on its own. it is up to the international community to seize the opportunities for sustainable action.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, as the proliferation of nuclear, chemical, biological and technical weapons poses a threat to international peace and security, i strongly condemn the nuclear test conducted by north korea on 6 january as a serious breach of its international obligations, un security council resolutions and the non-proliferation regime. it is essential to suspend all activities related to the ballistic missile programme and to abandon completely the existing nuclear programmes. the north korean authorities should also fulfil their obligations, cooperate and provide access to their territory for humanitarian organisations and the un special rapporteur on human rights. the commission has a duty to maintain communication channels with north korea and existing humanitarian aid programmes. it is also the duty of the north korean authorities to ensure that all citizens have access to food and humanitarian assistance on the basis of need.
mr president, i would like to express my strong support for this motion for a resolution, which strongly condemns north korea’s nuclear test conducted on 6 january 2016 – another nuclear test conducted by this country, which is again posing a serious threat to regional and international peace and security. these nuclear tests violate the united nations security council resolutions. the pursuit of illegal nuclear and ballistic missile programmes constitutes a challenge to the international nuclear non-proliferation regime and risks aggravating regional tensions. north korea has increasingly isolated and impoverished its people through its pursuit of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery, and should instead return to the six-party talks without preconditions. we must continue to closely monitor developments in the north korea nuclear dossier and its regional and global implications. i expect a further strengthening of sanctions by the united nations security council, and i call on north korea to choose, in the end, a constructive path by engaging with the international community.
member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, the european union is watching with great concern the serious violations of human rights in the democratic people’s republic of korea, as documented, among others, by the un commission of inquiry’s report in early 2014. the situation calls for urgent systematic and structural changes in north korea. this is a moral and legal imperative, but also a very practical necessity. the situation as it stands is a recipe for long-term regional instability. i would like to recall that some of the findings of the commission of inquiry even point to possible crimes against humanity. for that reason, the european union has supported the recommendation that the un security council refers the situation in north korea to the international criminal court. the european union has been and will remain at the forefront of keeping this dire state of affairs at the centre of attention of the international community. our work at the un is clear testimony of that. but the eu’s goal is not securing headlines or condemnation; our prime objective is achieving concrete improvements on the ground. that is what matters the most. the european union is already financing a number of food security, health, water and sanitation projects in the democratic people’s republic of korea that are of direct benefit to some of the most vulnerable people in the country, including some children in care institutions, the elderly, people with impairments and vulnerable farming communities. the european union is ready to do more and to cooperate further with north korea, but only if it starts to address credibly and substantially its major and serious human rights deficiencies. if north korea decides to follow the path of real engagement on human rights, starting with full cooperation with the un human rights mechanisms, then it will manage to secure a real, effective security in ways that illegal nuclear weapons will never provide. but recent actions by north korea – the illegal nuclear test that it conducted on 6 january – show that we are not yet on a positive path and our ability to cooperate remains severely limited as a result. north korea should focus on the much-needed human rights reforms that its citizens require, not on destabilisation and illegal actions that create an insecure and threatening environment to the detriment of all.
in writing. i strongly condemn the fourth nuclear test conducted by north korea. north korea is in violation of 4 un security council resolutions (2006, 2009 and 2 of 2013) which strictly prohibit any nuclear or ballistic missile programme. it is regrettable, but especially dangerous, how north korea shamelessly challenges the security and peace of the world. by violating security council resolutions, north korea is violating its commitments and poses a serious threat to peace in the region. moreover, north korea is committing human rights violations at a rate 'unparalleled in the contemporary world'. the latest human rights watch report from 2015 mentions a vast network of camps where some 120,000 people are being held. these abuses can be equated with crimes against humanity. the countermeasures taken must be aimed at sanctions that are tougher than before. i call on the government of north korea to choose dialogue over nuclear testing that endangers an entire world.
mr president, i am convinced that without the decisive and professional decisions of the european central bank, the euro area economy would have remained stagnant for a long time and would have even gone into deflation. but what i think we've discussed less is the impact of cheap money policy over a long period of time on the process of saving and the process of long-term investment. we cannot help but notice that pension funds, insurance companies and especially long-term institutional investors, as well as people who save, have had a loss. so i think it's legitimate that many people are asking the european central bank: how long do you think this monetary policy of cheap money will continue?
mr president, i would like to say the following to president draghi. you have applied the right monetary policy tools towards reaching the ecb’s objective on price stability in extremely challenging economic times over the past years. the euro is a trustworthy currency; the euro area has remained attractive, and new member states have joined over the course of the past two years. what is needed to consolidate the recovery in the eurozone and the eu are economic reforms at national level. devaluing our currency cannot remain the only economic policy tool applied to increase demand for our goods on the global markets. the ecb’s policies buy time, but there is no way around reforms. member states should not lean backwards, even in good economic times. those countries that are not competitive, do not reform, do not bring their public finances in order and do not stabilise their banking systems will be heading into the next crisis, and the ecb will not be able to help them. speaking of price stability, so far core inflation is not heading upwards. the impact of the slowdown in china and other emerging markets is not to be underestimated on the european markets, as you also rightly stated. given the extension of quantitative easing, the ecb has to provide more information about how it will exit the programme again without having major consequences on inflation targets, on price stability and – most notably – on financial markets. finally, president draghi, you said that policy-makers now have a bigger challenge to think about than the euro, as the refugee crisis is more urgent. you are right, but i would also like to add that we have to learn to tackle two major challenges at a time. the fact that the refugee crisis is a bigger and more urgent crisis should not, of course, be an excuse for us not to work on further strengthening the euro in the long term.
on behalf of the ppe group.– mr president, considering the matter of the commercial relationship between the eu and china, we should not stop at stating that china has not met the five eu criteria for a market economy. there are at least three important aspects to consider: the legal aspect and the much-debated automaticity. since there is a need to amend the eu legislation, granting the mes to china is not automatic. there are economic consequences, since there are hundreds of thousands of european jobs exposed. we expect the commission to conduct and present a deep and comprehensive impact assessment. the geopolitical context, in both ways, and the eu—china strategic partnership are in need of more cooperation and less antagonism. in conclusion, a legally-sound wto-compatible solution has to be proposed by the commission. we see a clear need to keep functioning eu trade defence systems in place. the solution delivered by the commission has to allow anti-dumping cases against china in the future as well. the entire evaluation and decision-making process should be transparent and should involve the european business community. we need a level playing field in trade between eu and china so that market forces define the competition and not intervention by the state.
mr president, the subject we are debating today is a very sensitive one. it is important to understand the heart of the problem and the consequences of either one or another position. full cooperation between the commission and parliament is essential and imperative. eu-china relations, politically and economically, are extremely important for both sides, but of course so too is the competitiveness of the european economy and industries. i mentioned the cooperation between the commission and parliament because it is only the commission, with their expertise and the results of the impact assessment, which can put parliament in the best position to judge the most suitable approach in this situation. we certainly need to avoid an economic and commercial confrontation or war with china. but at the same time, it is absolutely necessary that all measures are reflected upon and put into practice to avoid any dramatic consequences on eu industries and jobs. this means new trade defence instruments.

madam president, despite its crucial budgetary competition and social implications, undeclared work has not yet received as much attention as it should have on a european level. as the 2013 eurofound report on the topic pointed out, there are no obvious explanations regarding the dynamics of undeclared work. for example, contrary to what most people would expect, undeclared work does not necessarily go up in times of austerity, and reduced taxes and increased deregulation do not automatically lead to less undeclared work. however, what is obvious from the figures presented is that there are some member states which are more efficient than others in dealing with this problem. the size of the undeclared economy in austria compared to its gdp is almost five times less than the endemic proportion reached in my country, for example. if through this platform we succeed in transferring some proven practices across sectors and member states and regularising a part of the grey economy, we would not only bolster fair competition and ensure more sustainability for public finances, we would also put an end to the exploitation of millions of undeclared workers who do not have the social protection or health and safety guarantees that others enjoy. in addition, results in dealing with undeclared work in a cross-border manner would also contribute to restoring much-needed trust in the functioning of the single market. in writing. ‒ undeclared work has extremely serious budgetary implications through low tax revenues and social security. this has a negative impact on employment, but also on productivity. it undermines the financial sustainability of social protection systems, deprives workers of adequate social benefits and generates lower pension rights and limited access to healthcare. given the negative effects of this type of activity, as well as the lack of sufficient cooperation at eu level, in the absence of a formal mechanism for cross-border cooperation between the competent authorities of the member states, i believe that the european platform for enhanced cooperation on the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work will represent a real support at eu level. i am in favour of this report because through the platform there will be an eu-wide framework to develop expertise and analysis and improve operational coordination of actions between the different national law enforcement authorities in the member states.
in writing. ‒ the constant use of undeclared work in the member states demonstrates both the demand and supply for these jobs, and thus the need to integrate them into the formal set of rules and regulations of the social market economy, rather than eliminate them. i support the draft ep resolution on the proposal for a decision of the ep and of the council establishing a european platform for enhanced cooperation on the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work, with a view to providing clear eu added value to both efforts to prevent and deter undeclared work and to efforts to regularise the jobs concerned. i believe that a clear and precise proactive policy should be developed to encourage production in order to counteract the low level of economic growth and deflation.
in writing. ‒ given that undeclared work at national and cross-border level is two distinct forms of undeclared work and that it can contribute to the phenomenon known as 'social dumping', including through wage reductions in the member states where services are provided, i consider that close and effective cooperation is necessary both at cross-border level and at union level, as the identification, analysis and resolution of practical problems related to the implementation of union law on undeclared work conditions and social protection at work falls within the competence of the member states and their national labour protection systems.
in writing. ‒ considering the fact that the undeclared economy is equivalent to over 18% of the european union’s gdp, ranging from below 8% to over 30% of gdp in the different member states, i believe we need to ensure the adoption of the agreement reached with council and commission by a large majority. the construction sector is over-proportionately affected by undeclared work; the phenomenon is also wide-spread with regard to household and care services, private security, industrial cleaning, and agriculture as well as in the hotel, restaurant and catering sector. undeclared work is often associated with unfair competition and social dumping as well as lower tax revenues and social security contributions. undeclared workers are often subject to hazardous working conditions, lower wages, lacking social security and violations of their labour rights. i strongly support the call for the involvement of european social partners as members of the platform, and the mandatory participation of all member states in the platform.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to combat undeclared work in all its forms: clandestine work, false declarations, false self-employment. the report recommends the establishment of a european platform bringing together, under the auspices of the european commission, the member states and their national bodies responsible for combating undeclared work. the platform would be a focal point for information from states and their bodies and would have the function of coordinating and exchanging best practice between its members. the problem with this platform is that it will also have a monitoring function for the action of the member states, without any guarantee of a real fight against undeclared work. for example, we know that europe has encouraged secondment, which is itself a way of circumventing social legislation. it is also known that covert work, as long as it involves illegal immigrants, is tolerated by european leaders and by some national leaders who are in favour of illegal immigration, as the migrant crisis demonstrates. the creation of this platform will therefore at most make it possible to create a new european budgetary agency.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, which combats labour law violations and tax evasion, with the aim of increasing the number of jobs in a market characterised by fair competition, social security and sustainable fiscal stability. undeclared work distorts the market, particularly affecting smes but also workers. i believe that only through cooperation between member states and a platform that works according to well-established rules can we reduce undeclared work.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report, which should establish a european platform with the goal of reducing undeclared work. in addition, the aim is to take action and reduce labour law infringements, tax avoidance and breaches of social security requirements.
in writing. ‒ in order to successfully tackle the complex issue of undeclared work, we need first to objectively consider its true nature. this consideration reveals that the avoidance of proper registration constitutes the direct cause of a broad range of extremely negative implications and consequences. i have voted for this report that will set out the establishment of a european platform that will gather and share trustworthy information on best practices and persisting problems and will cooperate in outlining and implementing effective enforcement and enabling measures.
in writing. ‒ we voted for enhanced cooperation on the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work. the decision adopted by parliament's plenary session aims to establish a european platform to encourage cooperation between member states at union level. since the situation of undeclared work differs greatly from one member state to another, the needs of the relevant authorities and other actors of the member states for cooperation also differ. close and effective cooperation between member states should be encouraged at eu level so that they can support each other and complement each other's activities in tackling undeclared work. the measures taken at national level depend on the specific context in each individual member state and the activities carried out within the platform cannot replace a national assessment of the appropriate measures to be taken. member states and their relevant authorities shall retain the competence to identify, analyse and address practical problems related to ensuring compliance with applicable union legislation on working conditions and social protection at work and to determine the measures to be taken at national level to translate into practice the results of the activities carried out within the platform.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour for establishing a european platform to directly tackle the multiplex problem of undeclared work by strict prevention and deterrence. avoiding proper registration comprises the direct cause of the various exceedingly negative implications as well as the consequences associated with it. there must be enforcement accompanied by pro-active enabling policies and certain measures directed towards the regularisation of jobs that remain undeclared. this undeclared work highlights that there is both supply and demand for the jobs involved, which further demonstrates the need to integrate them into the formal range of rules and regulations of the social market economy. overall, the new european platform should provide value-added at the union level to efforts to prevent and deter undeclared work as well as regularize the jobs involved. these pro-active policies come at a time when it is necessary to increase production to counter low growth and deflation. increased regularisation, as a result, will provide for decent livelihoods and the needed services to customers, all while fairly contributing to market competition and sustainable fiscal stabilisation.
in writing. ‒ the phenomenon of undeclared work, or so-called 'black labour', has a significant impact on the eu and member states' economies. over 18% of the union's gdp and between 8% and 30% of the member states' gdp is diverted by this negative phenomenon, which can be found mainly in the construction sector but also in the fields of care and cleaning services, private security services, agriculture and tourism. the main effect is unfair competition through tax evasion and the draining of public budgets of social security contributions. the workers involved also lack social protection and in the workplace, being vulnerable to poor wage conditions. to remedy this situation, the commission decided to set up a european platform to enhance cooperation between member states and the main actors involved in combating this phenomenon. the platform, in an advisory role, is to be a forum for the discussion of solutions to this problem, which are then proposed to the member states. the major aim of this initiative is to provide additional motivation for the 'blacklisting' of the workforce and to prevent it. cross-border cooperation is essential to achieve this. i therefore support this initiative and consider this document to be an important element in ensuring fairness at work.
in writing. at eu level, undeclared work is one of the most worrying and complex issues. i voted in favour of the report on the establishment of a european platform for enhanced cooperation on the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work. in its proposal for a decision, the commission gave priority to a coercive approach aimed at preventing and discouraging undeclared work. this implies enhanced cooperation to combat labour law violations, tax evasion and non-compliance with social security requirements. i welcome the rapporteur's view, who also stressed the need for efforts to regularise the jobs in question.
in writing. ‒ biodiversity is currently under enormous pressure, both globally and in europe. species are disappearing at an alarming rate, caused by many human activities. habitat change, pollution, over-harvesting, invasive alien species and climate change are the main causes of the decline of biodiversity. unfortunately, only 23 percent of species and 16 percent of habitats are in good condition, so in the not too distant future, we may be facing an unmanageable situation. in these circumstances, i believe that more political will is needed to effectively address the current state of biodiversity as a political priority. we need a multilateral engagement in which local and regional actors play a special role. at the same time, the worrying state of biodiversity generates devastating economic costs for society, which have so far not been sufficiently integrated into economic and other policies. in a smart, sustainable and inclusive europe, nature must be at the centre, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ as the eu's efforts to halt the decline of biodiversity in 2010 failed, a new strategy was drawn up in 2011, developed around six objectives, each with its own specific actions: (1) full implementation of the habitats and birds directives (the nature directives); (2) maintenance and restoration of ecosystems and ecosystem services; (3) increasing the contribution of agriculture and forestry to maintaining and improving biodiversity; (4) ensuring the sustainable use of fish stocks; (5) combating invasive species; and (6) contributing to the eu's contribution to avoiding the decline of global biodiversity. the mid-term review (2015) makes it clear that we are still far from halfway there and that without significant additional efforts, the eu will miss the agreed targets in 2020 as well. i support the ep motion for a resolution on the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy, believing that biodiversity and nature must be at the heart of an innovative, sustainable and inclusive europe. i also believe that a strong will from the elites is needed to address biodiversity decline as a political priority, and that it is important to involve more stakeholders and give a special role to local and regional actors.
in writing. ‒ i fully agree with the rapporteur's argument that biodiversity must be protected for its enormous intrinsic value and to keep our planet as intact as possible for future generations. i believe that investing in nature and biodiversity provides opportunities that are useful and necessary from a socioeconomic point of view, and that is why i believe that we need to change our mindset about biodiversity.
in writing. ‒ the main aim of the strategic own-initiative report on ‘the mid-term review of the eu’s biodiversity strategy’ is to respond to the state of nature in europe report, and the mid-term review of the eu’s biodiversity strategy. this strategic report will also be parliament’s contribution to the on-going fitness check of the nature legislation (birds and habitats directives). in the fruitful negotiations at committee level, the s&d colleagues managed to integrate our important point to have a holistic approach to biological diversity in agriculture and the environment as well as the conservation of genetic diversity. another important point for us was the awareness of citizens and the educational work of the member state at local and regional level. the full implementation of the nature directives is a necessary precondition to achieve the 2020 biodiversity target.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report, which reiterates the need for additional, innovative solutions in order to halt biodiversity loss. biodiversity and nature must be central in a smart, sustainable and inclusive europe.
in writing. ‒ biodiversity represents the unique variety of ecosystems, habitats, species and genes on earth, and its loss is a loss to nature, humanity and the economy. i have voted in favour of this report on the eu biodiversity strategy, which is essential for nature itself as well as for health, wellbeing and welfare of the generations to come.
in writing. ‒ i support the position of like—minded colleagues in the european parliament and voted in favour of the report. taking into consideration that the loss of biodiversity and the disintegration of the ecosystem have been found by the world economic forum, in a 2014 ‘global risk perception survey’, to be among one of the 10 biggest risks facing the global community, and that our existence is so closely intertwined with the sustainability of natural resources, it is paramount that we adopt an ambitious and consistent approach to secure a reversal of former bad trends. we need to focus more attention towards meeting the targets as set out in the eu biodiversity strategy to 2020 to avoid repeating the failure of 2010 where the targets were not met. the prevention of biodiversity loss therefore should be a top priority. to arrive at the 2020 targets it is vital to implement and enforce already established eu legislation. indeed, we know that not only does investing in biodiversity carry positive results for the natural environment it is also connected to socio-economic development. with great scope for improvement the eu therefore has an important task ahead if it is to meet the 2020 deadline.
in writing. ‒ the preservation of biodiversity is one of the eu's strategic objectives in the field of environmental protection. the european parliament shall submit an own-initiative report at mid-term to assess the situation in this area and to draw the necessary conclusions on the various problems that persist. priorities identified in this year's report include prioritising the achievement of the europe 2020 targets, providing more information to the public to raise awareness and involving all decision-makers at european, national, regional and local level. significant measures in this area include encouraging farmers through the common agricultural policy to respect biodiversity, as well as protecting the marine environment, avoiding the introduction of invasive species, protecting pollinators, combating deforestation and supporting research and innovation. the main problem, however, remains the implementation of the existing regulations. this requires better coordination of national policies and better enforcement of european law through the use of proportionate penalties. an integrated approach to all these issues is needed, with appropriate regulation in all related areas. the introduction of basic concepts into the education systems of the member states is also important for the conservation of genetic diversity. the current strategy is just the first step in the right direction.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the mid-term evaluation of the eu biodiversity strategy. biodiversity, today under enormous pressure both globally and in europe, is essential to our health and well-being, but also to our economic prosperity. european efforts to halt the decline of biodiversity in 2010 have failed. for this reason, the eu developed a new strategy in 2011. the rapporteur advocates greater political will to effectively address biodiversity decline as a political priority and believes that a multi-stakeholder approach is needed, in which local and regional actors play a special role.
