in writing. ‒ union law requires that there be temporary protection instruments in the event of an increase in imports. in particular, where such an increase would cause economic damage to the european market and where there is a need to protect its producers, the union should make use of regional surveillance measures and safeguard measures in agreements. this is the case in the implementation of the preferential trade regime with the republic of moldova, which is, since november 2014, in the deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta). the eu is moldova's largest trading partner, accounting for 46,4% of trade, and trade with moldova accounts for 0,1% of the union's total trade. i also appreciate that the anti-circumvention mechanism that will be applied provides for the possibility of reintroducing the most-favoured-nation tariff, given that imports of certain agricultural products from moldova have exceeded a certain threshold without a justification as to their exact origin. i voted in favour of this report, welcoming and supporting the commission's proposal to protect the union market and its producers by temporarily suspending the tariff preferences in the association agreement between the eaec and the republic of moldova.
in writing. ‒ this file concerns the incorporation in eu law of the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism foreseen in the eu-moldova association agreement. the legislation can lay down the rules to be followed during the procedure and how decisions under the mechanism are to be taken. a safeguard measure may be imposed where a product originating in moldova is, as a result of the reduction or the elimination of customs duties, imported into the union in such increased quantities as to cause harm to the union industry. so far, no bilateral safeguard measure has been taken under the eu’s trade agreements. a safeguard measure may take the form of a suspension of a further reduction of the tariff rate, an increase in the rate of the customs duty (following the ‘lesser duty rule’). a safeguard measure must be limited for such a period of time as is necessary to prevent or remedy the serious injury to union industry. the association agreement also includes a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism, which provides for the possibility to introduce the mfn customs duty rate when imports of certain agricultural goods from moldova exceed a given threshold without due justification of their exact origin.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. i support the rapporteur’s approach and the aim to reach a quick first-reading agreement with the council.
in writing. ‒ the eu-moldova association agreement signed in june 2014 and provisionally applied as of september 2014 includes a bilateral safeguard clause, as is the case for the majority of eu trade agreements. the clause allows both parties (therefore also moldova) to temporarily suspend preferences in case their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase of imports causing economic damage to the domestic industry of the importing party. the agreement also foresees an anti-circumvention mechanism which provides for the possibility to reintroduce the mfn customs duty rate when imports of certain agricultural goods from moldova exceed a given threshold without due justification of their exact origin. we voted today on the implementing regulation which simply incorporates the two mechanisms into eu law in order to make them applicable in the eu. therefore the provisions related to the two instruments as agreed by the parties in the agreement have not been modified.
in writing. ‒ this agreement is largely based on comparable implementing regulations like eu/korea, eu/central america, eu/ colombia and peru. i have voted for this report that spells-out the obligation of the eu to consult with the moldovan authorities before implementing such a definitive safeguard measure, and that will harmonise the terminology of the commission proposal with the association agreement.
in writing. – i vote to support the two proposed amendments to the commission’s proposal of introducing a new regulation in the eu’s trade agreement with the republic of moldova. the european parliament’s proposed amendments should ensure that the safeguard clause and an anti-circumvention mechanism proposed by the commission are in line with the association agreement between the eu and moldova signed on 24 june 2014. more precisely, this implies that prior to any introduction of the safeguard clause it is required of the eu to deliberate the matter with the appropriate moldovan authorities. further, the amendments address the need for the commission to draft the regulation in a language corresponding to the association agreement and to include, in the regulation, a paragraph explicitly concerning the anti-circumvention mechanism.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the eu-moldova association agreement: safeguard clause and the mechanism to prevent circumvention. the bilateral safeguard clause allows preferences to be temporarily suspended if their application would cause an unforeseen and significant increase in imports, causing economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing country. this agreement also includes a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism, which provides for the possibility of reintroducing the most-favoured-nation tariff rate when imports of certain agricultural products exceed a certain threshold. the eu-moldova association agreement was signed on 24 june 2014 and the ep approved its conclusion on 13 november 2014. the agreement establishes a preferential trade regime - the complex and comprehensive free trade area, introducing autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova. the eu is moldova's largest trading partner, accounting for 46.4% of trade. in 2014, imports into the union from moldova increased by 20%, and imports of agricultural goods increased particularly by 30%. however, the duty-free export quotas were used to a modest extent by the moldovan producers.
in writing. ‒ an ambitious preferential trade regime, known as the deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta), has been in place between the european union and georgia since september 2014, and the agreement was negotiated following the same approach as in the parallel negotiations with other countries in the region. the eu is currently georgia's main trading partner. the eu is responsible for 27.2% of georgia's trade with the eu, with turkey and azerbaijan in second and third place respectively. on the other hand, trade with georgia represents 0,1% of the eu's total trade, with a total value of eur 2,6 billion in 2014. the anti-circumvention mechanism provides for the possibility to reintroduce the mfn (i.e. most-favoured-nation) customs duty when imports of certain agricultural and processed agricultural products originating in georgia exceed a given threshold (annual average import volume) without a proper justification as to their exact origin, supporting such an approach. i voted in favour of this report because it sets out the procedures to ensure the effective application of the agreement in order to prevent a possible negative impact on the union market.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report concerns the incorporation in the eu law of the anti-circumvention mechanism foreseen in the eu-georgia association agreement. the agreement has been provisionally applied since 1 september 2014. no fundamentally new conditions can be introduced during the legislative procedure which have not already been agreed during the negotiations with georgia. however, the legislation can lay down the rules to be followed during the procedure and how decisions under the mechanism are to be taken. the anti-circumvention mechanism provides for the possibility to introduce the mfn customs duty rate when imports of certain agricultural goods from georgia exceed a given threshold without due justification of their exact origin. an implementing regulation of the european parliament and of the council is necessary to put the instrument in place in the eu’s internal legislation to be able to apply the anti-circumvention mechanism. in the report the committee adopted one amendment relating to the reports which the commission has to supply to parliament and council on the application of the anti-circumvention mechanism. measures adopted under the anti-circumvention mechanism are limited to a maximum of six months.
in writing. ‒ i support the rapporteur's approach and the aim to reach a quick first-reading agreement with council.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the eu and georgia was signed in june 2014 and has been provisionally applied as of september 2014. the agreement includes an anti-circumvention mechanism which provides for the possibility to reintroduce the mfn customs duty rate when imports of certain agricultural goods from georgia exceed a given threshold without due justification of their exact origin. this implementing regulation incorporates the mechanism into eu law in order to make it applicable in the eu if necessary. being an implementing regulation, the provisions related to the mechanism as negotiated by the parties in the agreement have not been modified.
in writing. ‒ this agreement is largely based on comparable implementing regulations like eu/korea, eu/central america, eu/ colombia and peru. i have voted for this report that will harmonise the terminology of the commission proposal with the association agreement between the eu and georgia.
in writing. – an important element of the eu-georgia association agreement, the anti-circumvention mechanism, enables the possibility of reintroducing the ‘most favoured nation’ customs duty rate when imports of particular agricultural goods and processed agricultural products from georgia exceed an established threshold without the needed justification of their exact origin. in order to properly apply this anti-circumvention mechanism, a regulation of the european parliament and of the council to put in place the required instrument in the eu’s internal legislation is essential. the rapporteur highlights that the suggested regulation utilises the provisions of the eu-georgia association agreement, to which the european parliament gave its consent on 14 december 2014. adopting the proposed legislation proves necessary to implement certain obligations of georgia deriving from the anti-circumvention provisions of the eu-georgia association agreement to protect the eu producers if needed. in addition, the rapporteur embraces the reporting obligation of the commission, under which the commission shall submit an annual report on the application and implementation of the regulation to the co-legislators as well as making it accessible to the public. for the reasons stated above, i have voted in favour of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council implementing the anti-circumvention mechanism.
in writing. ‒ the european union has developed a strong and consistent relationship with the georgian state over the past decade. this was driven by the tbilisi government's interest in having a predictable and globally influential strategic partner and the union's interest in stability in the south caucasus. the signing of the association agreement between the two parties in 2014 has contributed to strengthening good relations and deepening cooperation in all areas of common interest. however, european legislation provides for a number of limits in relation to countries with which the eu has signed association agreements, which concern imports of agricultural products without a justification of their exact origin. this is the anti-circumvention mechanism, which allows the temporary suspension of imports of certain products (mainly agricultural, in the case of georgia). to avoid unwanted problems on the european market, this mechanism, which allows for a flexible approach when needed, needs to be adopted. its implementation is rather subject to exceptional conditions and does not prejudice the long-term european ambitions of the georgian state. rather, it is about protecting the economies of the two sides until they are compatible for greater integration.
in writing. i voted for the eu-georgia association agreement: the mechanism to prevent circumvention. this agreement includes a so-called 'anti-circumvention mechanism' which provides for the possibility to reintroduce the most-favoured-nation tariff when imports of certain agricultural and processed agricultural products originating in georgia exceed a given threshold without a proper justification as to their exact origin. the inclusion of the 'circumvention clause' is necessary to avoid the importation into the eu of products from outside georgia through georgia by taking advantage of the provisions of the eu-georgia association agreement. the eu-georgia association agreement was signed on 27 june 2014 and approved by the european parliament on 18 december 2014. the eu is currently georgia's main trading partner, with 27.2% of georgia's trade with the eu, with trade with neighbours turkey and azerbaijan in second and third place respectively.
in writing. ‒ the european union respects the right of persons with disabilities to education and, in this respect, must also ensure that laws protecting intellectual property rights do not constitute an unreasonable or discriminatory barrier to access by persons with disabilities to cultural materials. given that the world health organisation estimated in 2010 that there were a total of 2 550 000 blind and 23 800 000 partially sighted people in europe, i believe that the union must be concerned about the rights of all its citizens, including those persons. or it means taking into account also petition no 924/2011 by dan pescod, a british national, on behalf of the european blind union (ebu) / royal national institute for the blind (rnib), on access for blind people to books and other printed products and ensuring equal opportunities. in conclusion, i believe that the european institutions and the member states must speed up the ratification process without making ratification conditional on the revision of the eu legal framework or the judgment of the court of justice of the european union; for this reason, i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ here the petitions committee is making use of rule 216, para 2 which enables it to submit a short motion for a resolution. there will be a simple vote, without amendments or debate. the short resolution is calling on the council to accelerate the ratification process of the marrakesh treaty. signed by the eu in june 2014, the treaty focuses on copyright exceptions to allow greater distribution of books, in formats accessible to visually impaired citizens, thereby preventing discrimination of visually impaired and print disabled persons, who should have access to the same books as other persons. all except seven member states have ratified the treaty and this short resolution hopes to put pressure on these remaining countries to unblock. there are more than 26 million visually impaired individuals across europe with only 5% of all published books ever produced in accessible formats (less than 1% in developing countries).
in writing. ‒ visually impaired and print disabled persons should have access to the same books as other persons. this resolution is calling on the council to accelerate the ratification process of the marrakesh treaty, which focuses on copyright exceptions in order to allow greater distribution of books, in formats accessible to visually impaired citizens.
in writing. ‒ the marrakesh treaty is the first international agreement in the field of intellectual property rights which puts the public interest, not the interests of rightholders, first. no commercial advantage should prevent blind and partially sighted persons and persons with other reading disabilities from having free access to books that are accessible to them and from sharing these publications internationally. even in developed countries, only 5 percent of all books published are currently available in accessible formats, while in europe alone there are more than 26 million blind and partially sighted people. genuine equality of opportunity can be achieved not by loud declarations but by such concrete actions, and it is therefore surprising that some member states have taken this approach.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a multidimensional political project that places particular emphasis on ensuring equal rights for its citizens. a clearly disadvantaged category in our societies is that which includes people who are blind, partially sighted or who have difficulty reading. the world health organisation estimates that there are currently a total of 2 550 000 blind and 23 800 000 partially sighted people in europe. at the same time, however, only 5% of all books published in developed countries are currently accessible to the visually impaired (braille). the eu citizens' petitions and in particular petition no 924/2011 on behalf of the european blind union highlight the problems in this area. the marrakesh treaty, signed in april 2014 by the eu and its member states, aims to facilitate access to published works for all visually impaired people. the provisions of this treaty cannot be implemented within the union unless it is ratified by all eu member states. in these circumstances, there is a need for coordinated efforts by all european decision-makers to support the elimination of this clear discrimination against visually impaired people.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the ratification of the marrakesh treaty, which provides for the right of blind and partially sighted persons to education without discrimination and on the basis of equal opportunities. the european parliament, in its resolution, notes with deep indignation that seven eu member states have formed a minority bloc which is preventing the ratification process of this treaty. according to the who, in 2010, there were a total of 2 550 000 blind and 23 800 000 partially sighted people in europe, with a total of 26 350 000 visually impaired people. only 5% of all books published in developed countries and less than 1% of books published in developing countries are produced at any one time in formats accessible to blind and visually impaired people.
in writing. ‒ the health of its citizens and the protection of the environment have always been important objectives for the european union. to guarantee them, increased attention is needed to food that ends up being produced, traded and consumed within its borders. at the production stage, the risks to be monitored are linked to the genetically modified organisms. among them, genetically modified soybean mst-fgø72-2 contains a protein that confers tolerance to glyphosate-based herbicides or this substance is classified as probably carcinogenic to humans. however, no studies confirm this, and there is no scientific evidence linking glyphosate to cancer. i support a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, environmental and consumer interests with regard to genetically modified food and feed, and believe that this can be achieved while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market. i voted against the objection to the draft commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified soybean fg72 (mst-fgø72-2).
in writing. ‒ in october parliament rejected the new commission proposal on genetically modified (gm) food and feed and asked the commission to come up with a new one. in the meantime, no new gm food/feed should therefore be authorised under the current legal framework which the commission acknowledges is not working in a satisfactory way. the soybeans which have been authorised are resistant to certain herbicides, therefore their cultivation could encourage more liberal use of herbicides, which could be harmful to the environment and/or human health. the commission must come forward with a new proposal for gmo food and feed, which more thoroughly assesses the environmental impacts of gmos.
in writing. ‒ the environmental impacts of gmos must be assessed through a new proposal from the commission for gmo food and fodder.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this motion for a resolution with regard to the authorisation of placing on the market products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified soybean fg72. the report states that the implementing decision is not consistent with parliament’s and the council’s regulation on ensuring a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, environment and consumer interests in relation to genetically modified food and feed, whilst ensuring effective operation of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because i believe that the european union must have a single point of view on the problems facing all its states. there are values that we all aspire to as a people, and i am referring here to the need to ensure a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, environmental interests and consumer interests when it comes to genetically modified food and feed. it's an area that i think we shouldn't venture into without having concrete data on the long-term implications. so asking the european commission to withdraw its draft decision authorising the use of genetically modified soybeans is, in my view, a good thing for the future of the eu.
in writing. ‒ the advances in agricultural science in recent decades have enabled contemporary societies to identify solutions to combat pests and diseases of various plants that affect their yield in producing the food they need. at the same time, experiments on certain plants have produced genetically modified varieties that are more resistant to pests and certain herbicides. the use of genetically modified organisms (gmos) has been the subject of much controversy at european level, with concerns about their alleged effects on the human body. in order not to make hasty decisions until in-depth scientific studies have been carried out in this field, the european commission has avoided adopting a transhumance position, leaving it to the member states to take the measures they deem necessary. in the case of genetically modified soybean (fg72, mon 87708 × mon 89788, mon 87705 × mon 89788) resistance to herbicides may be harmful to the environment or to the health of consumers. for this reason, the european parliament has raised this objection, which is justified and is in fact a request for a more thorough assessment of the effects of gmos, in order to avoid any risks to the environment and european consumers.
in writing. ‒ environment and food safety must be the limiting framework for the development of the internal market, without which any economic progress would in fact be an attack on the health of all consumers, who are protected by the european treaties. either that protection must become effective, and we cannot talk about effectiveness when we want to approve products with a potential carcinogenic risk. on the other hand, the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from mon 87708 × mon 89788 soybean should not be excluded in the absence of specific scientific studies confirming the hazard of this substance to consumers. in this context, i have objected to the objection under rule 106 of the rules of procedure: authorisation of genetically modified soybean mon 87708 x mon 89788.

in writing. ‒ in this century, the development of agriculture is taking place at the micro-cellular level, and the risks that the union must monitor as a guarantor of the food safety of its citizens and of the protection of the environment revolve around the safety of genetically modified organisms. furthermore, we recall that poor diet is now by far the leading cause of disease and mortality worldwide - more than tobacco, alcohol, and lack of physical activity combined. it is becoming clear that ensuring union and global food security is not only an important objective undertaken by the union but also a situation requiring attention from the actors involved. however, in the absence of scientific studies confirming the negative effects that certain substances have on those who consume them, i believe that we should not take a radical position in withdrawing them from the market. in view of the need for concrete evidence, i voted against the resolution on the objection under rule 106 of the rules of procedure: authorisation of genetically modified soybean mon 87705 x mon 89788.

in writing. ‒ air pollution from nitrogen oxides (no2) emissions causes 75 000 premature deaths in europe each year, with 93% of cases of exceeding normal concentrations occurring near roads, or this situation is of concern and requires specific measures. at the same time, addressing nox emissions from diesel engines should contribute to reducing the current high levels of no2 concentrations in ambient air. i voted against this objection because the withdrawal of the commission's draft regulation will cause the real driving emissions measures to be implemented with far too much delay, given that the current car emissions tests have been unchanged for some 30 years. in this context, i consider that the draft regulation proposed by the commission should be implemented immediately.
in writing. ‒ i supported the objection as the draft commission regulation would result in a de facto blanket derogation from applicable emissions limits, and is therefore not consistent with union law, in that it is not compatible with the aim and content of regulation (ec) no 715/2007. the commission should withdraw the draft regulation and submit a new one without delay and no later than 1 april 2016, in order to introduce a real driving emissions test for all vehicles with a view to ensuring the effectiveness of emission control systems and enabling vehicles to comply with regulation (ec) no 715/2007 and its implementing measures.
in writing. ‒ i support the commission's proposal for several reasons. first, the european commission's proposal provides for a mechanism that reduces emissions by about five times and allows the car industry to switch their manufacturing technology for the next step in reducing emissions. as i have already said, we need to strike a balance between regulations for protecting the environment in europe and supporting industry, as long as europe is not the world's biggest polluter and as long as we do not have trade defence regulations for european industry in relation to non-european. i support environmental policies, but we need to implement them rationally. according to the commission's commitment, through commissioner elżbieta bieńkowska, it will monitor both the schedule of required emission reductions and the compliance of the car industry within a reasonable time.

madam president, i voted today on the european parliament's recommendations to the european commission on the negotiations for the trade in services agreement. it is a historically unique agreement in its size, in its depth and in the broad framework of countries it includes, countries all over the world, including the european union. this resolution recommends that the commission open doors for european union enterprises, also help these enterprises to enter the public procurement, telecommunications, financial and professional markets and also ensure that the best highly qualified professionals are able to work outside the european union. reducing bureaucracy is also part of these recommendations. but the problem is that, apart from that, each country has to ensure its own entry into the services market and not rely on what the european commission does.
in writing. ‒ tisa is an opportunity for the eu to consolidate its position as the world's leading exporter of services, and the framework for the negotiations must be a high level of transparency, dialogue and accountability to be successful. any trade agreement must offer more rights and lower prices for european consumers, more jobs and a higher level of protection for workers and many other benefits that are easier to pursue when there are more actors involved, pursuing the same objectives that are beneficial for the union. in order to achieve a balanced agreement and to respect the union's fundamental treaties, the commission must take account of the european parliament's position, which plays a decisive role in eu trade policy, and i therefore consider it justified to ask for up-to-date and complete information on the negotiations. furthermore, i believe that member states should be encouraged to get involved and consult national parliaments as well as local and regional authorities, keeping them informed of the progress of the negotiations. i support the recommendations of parliament and the opinions of the committees involved and have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i have been working as shadow rapporteur for the deve opinion on tisa and i believe our opinion sent a strong message to our colleagues in the inta committee, clarifying the fact that the impact of the trade and services agreements on developing countries has to be taken into account and, consequently, calling for impact assessments on developing countries by the commission. this is fundamental in order to ensure that the principle of policy coherence is respected. we urged the commission to continue to increase transparency and democratic accountability, and to increase accessibility to all public consolidated negotiation documents, as this is the way by which concerned civil society and citizens, including of developing countries, can be informed and involved in the process. the possibility that developing countries join the agreement cannot be excluded, and, in such cases, the approach has to be flexible, in order to ensure that their access to the global service market is fair. in a multilateral framework, the criteria for admission of developing countries cannot be the same as the ones for developed countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because a proactive approach is needed to increase the transparency of the european union's trade policies. the consolidation of the tsa requires effective cooperation between the eu and international democratic bodies, taking into account the needs of civil society. ongoing efforts to improve transparency in eu trade agreements are imperative for achieving the sustainable development goals, for the interests of european companies and european consumers, and for maintaining the stability of financial markets. the importance of tisa for member states is in facilitating job creation, as the european union is the main service provider, with tens of millions of service jobs in the european area. facilitating the export of these services to other countries will help expand the labour market, which will have a positive impact on the development of the european union. at the same time, allowing non-european companies access to the eu services market will broaden the range of options and reduce prices for businesses and customers alike.
in writing. ‒ trade in services represents the new engine of the world economy. in the eu it is estimated that the services sector accounts for more than 70% of its gdp. tisa is therefore a crucial opportunity for eu service providers to have access to other markets and benefit from a level playing field. this would create new jobs in the eu and would therefore substantially contribute to our growth. however this trade agreement should not undermine our public services which should therefore be excluded from the scope of the agreement and governments’ right to regulate in the interest of their citizens from consumer protection to data privacy. i voted for a resolution that finds the right balance between these two sets of priorities.
in writing. ‒ a decisive role is played by the european parliament in the eu’s trade policy, thus the european parliament must work to ensure a good agreement is reached that should benefit european companies and consumers. i have voted for this report on the tisa negotiations that must ensure more reciprocity in market access, create a global level playing field and provide tangible benefits for consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa). this agreement represents an opportunity for the eu to consolidate its position as the world's leading exporter of services, with a share of 25% of world services exports, which allowed it to achieve a trade surplus of eur 170 billion in 2013. the services sector employs almost 70% of the eu's workforce and accounts for 40% of the value of goods exported from europe. i would stress the potential of tisa to boost job creation in the eu. citizens' trust in eu trade policy needs to be strengthened not only by ensuring positive outcomes in terms of employment and welfare for citizens and society, but also by ensuring the highest level of transparency, commitment and accountability, by maintaining a constant dialogue with social partners, civil society, local and regional authorities and any other relevant stakeholders, and by setting clear guidelines in the negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i believe it is essential that, as a result of the negotiations and the tisa agreement, european citizens get quality products at lower prices and competitive european companies can more easily access the markets of partner countries. at this point, it is clear that the eu is one of the most attractive markets for companies from other countries and it is right that through this agreement european companies should be treated equally by their partners, which will benefit all eu citizens by creating new jobs. at the same time, consideration should be given to protecting the interests and areas of interest of european states and companies such as those specialising in audiovisual, public services and data protection.
in writing. ‒ i believe that a more careful negotiation of the trade in services agreement can reduce the obstacles faced by european smes in their path towards internationalisation of the services they provide. the eu is one of the world's leading exporters of services. one third of all services are provided by smes. however, the costs of cross-border services are increased by non-tariff barriers, which affect the proper functioning of the sme sector in the field. there is still a huge untapped potential for the eu in the global services market. the commission must take a fair and firm stance in the negotiation of tisa in favour of the economic environment of all member states and in particular in favour of emerging economies that can deliver sustainable and strong long-term growth to the eu economy. at the same time, it is very important that the agreement on trade in services does not in any way prevent the proper functioning of the eu and the member states in the application of social and labour rules. the european commission must take into account the recommendations of the european parliament and the member states in developing an agreement for the benefit of all parties involved, but above all for the benefit of european citizens.
in writing. i voted on the report on the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa). in the rapporteur's view, tisa negotiations should ensure more reciprocity in market access, create a level playing field globally, deliver tangible benefits to consumers and ensure stakeholder access to discussions, in order to facilitate future multilateralisation. i welcome the attention the rapporteur has paid to the sme sector in the tisa agreement. it is also noted that this report specifies that public and cultural services, the fundamental rights to data privacy and fair working conditions, and the right to regulate are non-negotiable and must be unequivocally excluded from the scope of this agreement.

in writing. ‒ meps voted on several resolutions on the strategy to be implemented to achieve equality between men and women. i support actions aimed at ensuring equal pay, in particular, provided that it is a question of aligning women's wages with men's and not the other way around. i am opposed to all quota requirements, particularly in the boards of directors of companies. these compulsory quotas turn women into adjustment variables to satisfy legal constraints, thus negating their personal competence and aspirations. of the four motions for resolutions tabled, i finally supported the one that was most respectful of the principle of subsidiarity and the cultures of the member states, while encouraging better pay for women.

in writing. local authorities are the main actors responsible for implementing cohesion policy. they are in direct contact with citizens and always respond to their needs. however, in some member states, excessive centralisation means that the local level is less taken into account in decision-making. a step preceding legislative initiatives is the process of public consultation of citizens. unfortunately, there is a low participation of local actors in these consultations in countries with centralised systems. measures are therefore necessary to increase the involvement of those authorities and to identify ways of making public consultations as attractive as possible. moreover, i am convinced that we can contribute to decision-making accountability at these levels by encouraging participatory governance measures. we have tools such as iti and dlrc, which aim to implement local initiatives by increasing stakeholder involvement and access to finance to exploit local development potential. vertical partnerships between actors at different levels and the involvement of private sector partners guarantee the success of these initiatives.
in writing.– esif represents the eu’s main investment policy tools with a total budget of €454 billion for 2014-2020. the esif budget for romania will deliver a critical mass of investments for the following programmes: rural development programme – €8,127,996,402; aid for the most deprived operational programme €441,013,044; human capital operational programme €4,236,838,744; administrative capacity operational programme €553,191,489; european maritime and fisheries fund operational programme €168,421,371; large infrastructure operational programme €9,418,524,484, €1,329,787,234; regional operational programme €6,700,000,000; and the technical assistance operational programme €212,765,958. the allocated esif budget for my country totals €31,278,538,726 which represents approximately 13% of the total esif budget. i support the calls in this report underlining the key role played by local and regional authorities in shaping and implementing eu’s strategies and in achieving cohesion policy objectives. the report reiterates that the european code of conduct and the reinforced partnership principle will set out legal involvement of local and regional authorities providing minimum requirements for their involvement in all phases of preparation and implementation of the operational programmes. the report concludes that these funds are essential for europe’s as well as romania’s ability to address medium and long-term development challenges.
in writing. regional development cannot be achieved without the strong involvement of local public authorities. the managers of european communities, urban or rural, are best placed to decide on priorities and programmes for local and regional development. given the continuing need to bring decision-making closer to european citizens, i support increasing the role of local and regional authorities in shaping european investment policies. the appeal to the commission is justified. local authorities can play a decisive role in regional development, job creation and economic growth only if we take into account that non-federal states need procedures that bring local government closer to investment structures. the commission must come up with concrete solutions to strengthen the role of local and regional authorities in the eu. limited resources at the level of some local governments remain the main obstacle to the contracting and co-financing of massive development work, from transport and infrastructure to health or the environment. for example, how many of the projects under consideration or ongoing in the investment plan for europe are initiated and managed by european local public authorities? doubtless too few.

member of the commission.– madam president, almost two years have passed since the illegal annexation of crimea and sevastopol by the russian federation, which the european union does not recognise and continues to condemn. in addition to being a grave violation of international law, the illegal annexation has had a serious negative impact on the human rights situation. the systematic curtailment of residents’ basic human rights and fundamental freedoms is an emblematic feature of the current situation on the peninsula. the imposition of russian laws and citizenship has created a situation of legal uncertainty and discrimination. the crimean tatar community and tatar residents supporting the territorial integrity of ukraine are paying a particularly high price for the views they express. public events in simferopol to commemorate the 1944 deportation have not been allowed. tatar media outlets have been closed and the mejlis, a self-governing body of crimean tatars and its activists, has been prosecuted. the appearing cases of enforced disappearances, torture and killing of young crimean tatars have not been properly investigated so far. high representative mogherini discussed these cases when she met in person the representative of the mejlis of the crimean tatar people in ukraine in november 2015. let me also stress the eu’s concern over the detention and sentencing of oleg sentsov and alexander kolchenko. their case, which the eu has monitored, is in breach of international law and elementary standards of justice. the eu will remain vocal in demanding their immediate release and safe return to ukraine. finally, the eu has repeatedly called for full, free and unrestricted access for international human rights actors to the whole territory of ukraine, including crimea and sevastopol. we welcome those missions which have taken place so far: the mission of the council of europe’s commissioner for human rights, nils muižnieks, in autumn 2014; the unofficial mission of turkish prominent persons in spring 2015; and the continued work of the non—governmental crimean field mission on human rights. we also praise the efforts of the un and oecd, autonomous institutions which have so far been denied access to the peninsula but document human rights abuses using a wide variety of sources. we very much hope that the most recent mission, dispatched by the secretary—general of the council of europe last week and headed by ambassador gérard stoudmann, will pave the way for an improved human rights situation in the crimean peninsula.

member of the commission.– madam president, let me first stress that since the events of 2011 the eu has been closely monitoring the situation in bahrain. the eu has been consistently engaging with local authorities at all levels, maintaining constant contacts with a wide range of bahraini stakeholders and activists. bahrain is an important partner in the gulf region and has an important role to play in ensuring the stability of the gulf region, which can best be achieved by strengthening the existing framework for the protection of human rights and individual freedoms. the eu will therefore continue to maintain an active dialogue with the country and its government and support bahrain’s stability and development. we consider that this objective can be best achieved through a process of inclusive national reconciliation, leading to gradual political and socio-economic reforms based on dialogue and tolerance. like many in europe, we have been concerned by the death penalty sentence imposed on mr mohammed ramadan and mr husain ali moosa for their alleged involvement in the february 2014 bomb explosion which killed a police officer, a sentence upheld by the bahraini court of cassation on 16 november 2015. the eu is unreservedly opposed to the use of capital punishment under all circumstances, and its universal abolition will continue to remain a cornerstone of the eu’s foreign policy. allegations regarding their possible mistreatment in detention, as well as the basis for their conditions, should also be fully investigated. the eu, both in brussels and through its delegation in riyadh, accredited to bahrain, will continue to liaise with the bahraini authorities to advocate the protection and promotion of human rights and fundamental freedoms, as per bahrain’s international commitments, the recommendations set out by the bahraini independent commission of inquiry and the recommendations made during bahrain’s universal periodic review process. the eu will continue to call on the bahraini government to act proportionately in all cases to protect the rights of individuals indicted as a result of criminal charges, as was done during the second visit of the eu special representative for human rights, stavros lambrinidis, in may 2015. on this occasion, the eu conveyed again its preoccupation as to the imposition of the death penalty, recalling its principled opposition to this inhumane and degrading punishment. the eu, in close coordination with the eu member states represented in manama, has been closely following developments related to these individual cases and to the overall human rights situation in the kingdom of bahrain. the european union has expressed formally on many occasions that violence is not justified in any circumstances. in writing. ‒ serbia is the 33rd state to participate in the european union's civil protection mechanism, and is one of the countries aspiring to become eu members. serbia has made significant progress on the european integration process, making considerable efforts to align itself with the principles and values to which the union subscribes. serbia has therefore taken significant steps towards the normalisation of relations with kosovo, which resulted in the first agreement on the principles applicable to the normalisation of relations. it has also made substantial efforts to develop the business environment, reduce the budget deficit and develop the labour market, including in terms of labour law and employment policy. furthermore, it drew up the plan for the reconstruction, improvement and modernisation of some sections of the railway network. i welcome the progress made by serbia and the reforms initiated in key areas such as public administration, infrastructure, the economy, which is why i voted in favour of this report. i continue to encourage these european integration efforts and support serbia's efforts to align with the union's foreign and security policy.
in writing. ‒ i believe we need to be aware that a lot of work lies ahead for serbia: improvements are very much needed with regards to rights, freedoms and the security of minorities, the freedom of the media , the lack of transparency in funding of political parties, the equal representation of men and women. i believe that, in our talks with serbia, we must keep our european priorities and values clear in our minds: the goal of achieving stability in the region is important but we cannot forfeit our support and defence of the exercise of democratic liberties in the balkans. i expect the serbian government to refrain from anti eu rhetoric and to stop manipulating public opinion through pressure, censure and the government's massive propaganda machine. i support this process but at the same time i believe that we must take a clear political position. it is about time for us to show that no state that wishes to join the eu can avoid putting fundamental democratic values into place and can show no interest in the values that europe represents.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this resolution because i welcome the steps taken towards serbia’s ascension to the eu. i urge the serbian political leaders to continue with the reforms needed in order to reach eu standards. serbia has also made significant progress regarding economic reforms – partly due to the commission’s support. i hope serbia will remain strong on its current path.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the 2015 report on serbia. since last year, serbia has taken concrete steps to complete a good part of the community acquis. the commission has put forward a clear set of requirements to serbia regarding the need to strengthen economic governance, the rule of law and the capacity of the public administration. serbia has demonstrated that it can be a socioeconomic driver in the western balkans: it has reduced the budget deficit, improved employment policy and the investment climate. negotiations on the judiciary, fundamental rights, justice, freedom and security remain open. serbia should take further measures to implement the legal framework for the protection of minorities, in particular in the field of education, religion and culture. it is important to clarify the legal status of the national councils of minorities. all minorities must be represented in the serbian parliament in order to increase the effective involvement of minority representatives in the decision-making process. serbia shall grant access to national minorities in public administration and representative bodies at local, regional and national level, and shall respect and vigorously promote their non-discriminatory treatment. i hope that the romanian minority will enjoy in the near future this process of serbia's legal alignment with european standards.

in writing. ‒ the european union is encouraging the european perspective of the countries of the western balkans, a region considered to be fully part of the union's natural enlargement area. in this area, relations with serbia have been moving in a tortuous but steady upward direction. the eu's relations with the serbian state are currently at an excellent level, as demonstrated by the opening of accession negotiations. in the last year, the opening of negotiations on chapter 32, on financial control, and on chapter 35, on the normalisation of relations with kosovo, is to be welcomed. also, despite a rather complicated internal political life, the pro-european attitude of the majority of relevant political forces in serbia is noteworthy. progress has been made in the liberalisation of the eu visa regime for serbian citizens. the 2015 report also highlights a number of persistent domestic problems, such as media freedom, deteriorating conditions for freedom of expression, and lack of transparency in the financing of political parties and electoral campaigns. the report also notes the need to coordinate efforts to improve the situation of the roma minority and the implementation of legislation for the protection of minorities. i consider that the document reflects the situation in serbia and i support its adoption in this form.

in writing. ‒ the situation in libya is marked by strong internal conflict, instability and political dissension. this situation has been perceived favourably by various extremist forces, which threaten peace and security throughout the region. one of the most visible terrorist groups is daesh, which has launched major offensives against the extremely important oil facilities in libya. furthermore, the human rights situation continues to deteriorate throughout the country, including cases of arbitrary detention, abductions, extrajudicial executions, torture and violence against journalists, officials, political figures and human rights defenders. at the same time, multiple cases have been reported where smugglers have exploited refugees trying to reach europe. the european union is deeply concerned by the growing presence of extremist organisations and movements in libya. these groups pose a major threat to the stability and security of the entire region and also to the security of europe. the eu must therefore continue to provide humanitarian, financial and political support to enable the humanitarian crisis in libya to be resolved and to respond adequately to the suffering of people and refugees, as well as civilians facing the interruption of access to basic services, which is why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the human rights and humanitarian situation in libya has deteriorated amid escalating violence and an increasingly volatile political environment. libya hosts hundreds of thousands of refugees and asylum seekers of different nationalities, many of whom live in precarious conditions, thus becoming a transit ground for human trafficking, which has led to the deaths of thousands of people trying to cross the mediterranean sea to reach europe. it is important that the libyan political agreement is implemented in good faith, with sustained political will and inclusiveness. its implementation will provide the tools to address the urgent challenges of reforming and building state institutions, strengthening the rule of law, combating terrorism, improving the human rights situation, combating trafficking in human beings and stimulating economic growth. i strongly support the stepping up of humanitarian funding at european and international level to meet the most urgent needs of those who have been severely affected by the conflict in libya, as well as the need to provide funds to humanitarian organisations for better assessment of the situation and improved responses to needs on the ground.
in writing. ‒ i believe we must support the government of national accord and fully back the mediation efforts of the special representative of the unsg aimed at facilitating a libyan-led political solution in finding a negotiated settlement to resolve the crisis and to ensure unity, governability, stability and peace. i therefore welcome the signature of the libyan political agreement (lpa) to form a government of national accord (gna), as the sole legitimate government of libya. i invite the house of representatives and its presidency to show a spirit of compromise and convene and discuss proposed cabinet with a view of an endorsement of the government of national accord. it is crucial the libyan political agreement be implemented with inclusiveness; this will provide the necessary tool to address the urgent challenges of reforming and building state institutions, consolidating the rule of law, fighting terrorism, improving the human rights situation and the phenomenon of migrations, combating human smugglers as well as of stimulating economic growth.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support the commission and eeas – as coordinators of member states in libya – to focus on state-building and institution-building. furthermore, progress in terms economy is central to a libyan democratic transition. however, the proxy war and the presence of daesh in the region have slowed down considerably both the progress made by the economy and a clean transition to democracy.
in writing. ‒ libya has been plagued by instability, infighting and sectarianism since the fall of colonel muammar gaddafi in 2011. the lack of a stable government has been exploited by is/daesh and other extremist forces that threaten peace and security in the entire region. i have voted for this motion for a resolution that calls on libya’s un-led talks parties to work together in order to achieve national unity, stability and inclusivity.
in writing. ‒ the civil conflict in libya that has been going on for several years has generated a number of negative effects for the european union, such as increased migration, illegal trafficking in human beings and the spread of terrorism. the signing of the libyan political agreement is an important step towards normalizing the situation and bringing the various legitimate sides in the conflict to the negotiating table. the formation of a government of national accord in the following period would guarantee respect for the interests of the various libyan political groups. it is therefore very important that the libyan presidency and house of representatives support this initiative. the european union, through the high representative for foreign affairs and the vice-president of the commission, is working with the libyan authorities and the un structures to develop a coordinated package of measures to support the new libyan government. however, additional humanitarian funding is needed to rebuild the country and restore normalcy to its citizens. in this regard, the union's member states should support those measures, provided that the new government in tripoli takes measures to reform state institutions, strengthen the rule of law, combat terrorism (including isis activity in libya), respect human rights, combat trafficking in human beings and control migration. i support the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ european islands are distinctive in terms of their environmental conditions, with endemic habitats and species, but also in terms of their cultural aspects, with their architectural heritage, sites, landscapes, agricultural and non-agricultural characteristics and outstanding geographical identities. european islands have a significant role to play in strengthening sustainable development in the union, given their high potential for producing energy from renewable sources, due to their specific exposure to wind, tidal and sunlight. however, some of the union's islands also fall within peripheral regions and are vulnerable to various challenges facing europe such as globalisation, demographic trends, climate change, energy supply and, especially in the southern areas, exposure to increasing migration flows. as a result, more efficient connectivity via maritime routes, better access to ports and better air transport services are required. i believe it is particularly important to promote the accessibility of regions and links between islands so that these island areas become tourist hotspots and points of increased interest. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a strategic approach is needed to the sustainable development of european island regions by promoting innovation and competitiveness in these regions.
in writing. ‒ taking into account the permanent handicaps of island regions, due to their small size and distance from the european continental coast, which constitute obstacles to the physical development of islands and prevent them from achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion, i welcome the rapporteur's proposal to set up a homogeneous group of all island territories. in order to carry out studies and analyses on the additional costs generated by the situation of insularity, i believe that other statistical indicators, which can reflect the vulnerability of islands, and not only their gross domestic product, need to be taken into account.
in writing. ‒ island regions have common and specific characteristics and features that clearly distinguish them from mainland regions such, as certain permanent handicaps which require particular attention. this is why i believe it is very important to know which are the specific instruments and the resources of cohesion policy to tackle the handicaps arising from the insularity and how will deal the ec in the future with the permanent handicaps of these regions, as a permanent obstacle which may affect the achievement of the objectives of the cohesion policy.

in writing. ‒ european islands are peripheral regions situated on the eu’s external borders that are particularly vulnerable to challenges that europe is facing, such as demographic trends, globalisation, climate change, energy supply and, especially for southern areas, exposure to increasing migration flows. i have voted for this motion for a resolution that calls on the commission to provide a clear definition of the type of geographical, natural and demographic handicaps that insular regions suffer from in order to provide targeted support.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis has had a dramatic impact on national and regional budgets in many member states by limiting the availability of funding in many sectors, leading to a 20% decline in public investment. the crisis has also seriously damaged the development prospects of many disadvantaged regions, including those on islands, led to increased poverty and social exclusion and hampered the achievement of the union's long-term objective of economic and territorial cohesion. given the high potential of islands for the production of energy from renewable sources due to their specific exposure to wind, tidal and sunlight, european islands can become important sources of alternative energy. the islands can contribute to strengthening sustainable development in the union, guaranteeing their energy autonomy and energy at prices more accessible to the inhabitants. a key means of countering the connectivity disadvantages of island regions is digital capacity. i would stress that investment in infrastructure is needed to ensure broadband access in islands and their full participation in the digital single market.
in writing. ‒ islands are specific geographical regions which face a number of permanent natural handicaps compared to mainland areas. these generate economic, social and environmental disparities for island areas, making access for tourists and economic operators more difficult. the islands are also particularly vulnerable to the challenges facing europe today, including migration flows, demographic trends (depopulation), climate change, energy supply. at the same time, these regions have great potential for wind, solar and wave energy, as well as for tourism, in addition to the traditional sectors of agriculture, livestock and fisheries. in this context, in line with the union's objective of reducing regional disparities, the commission is invited, through this motion for a resolution, to take the necessary measures to support the balanced development of the regions concerned, in particular by supporting intermodal transport, investments in digital infrastructure, investments in education, the creation of an 'islands office' within dg regio and the development of coherent development strategies for island areas, involving local, regional and national authorities, as well as other relevant actors from civil society, the economy and the social environment. i think it's a necessary initiative and i support its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the role of local and regional authorities and a wide range of partners - from member states to community groups - is essential in the process of developing and implementing european union strategies. on the other hand, the diversity of governance at local and regional level is an asset for the european union and i consider the principle of enhanced partnership and the european code of conduct on partnership to be very important. they shall establish the legal involvement of local and regional authorities and lay down the minimum requirements for their involvement in all stages of the preparation and implementation of operational programmes in order to achieve the highest possible absorption rate of esi funds.
in writing. ‒ local and regional authorities play a very important role within the framework of the european structural and investment funds as they are close to citizens and best understand their needs. on the other hand - due to their limited means - they are in need of budgetary support for co-financement of projects. it is important to know how the ec is going to support regional and local authorities in order to strengthen their role and impact in managing esi funds, with the aim of creating economic growth and sustainable jobs. furthermore, we also need to know if the ec envisage a public consultation, followed by an initiative, on this matter.

in writing. ‒ the eu's cohesion policy for 2014-2020 is the main investment instrument covering all eu regions and an opportunity for job creation, entrepreneurship and innovation at the level of local and regional economies, improving the quality of life of citizens and ensuring solidarity and stronger development in eu regions. i voted for synergies and complementarity between the european structural and investment funds (esi funds) and other eu programmes, where local and regional authorities can play a useful role in achieving cohesion policy objectives. we stress that any reprogramming of the esi funds should be carried out in accordance with the rules of the common provisions regulation (cpr) and that new initiatives should not weaken the substance of the esi funds. we draw attention to the challenges faced by local and regional authorities, such as globalisation, climate change, energy security, migration flows and increasing urbanisation, taking into account that each region has specific needs and characteristics. we invite the commission to continue to build on past and ongoing initiatives, including public consultations, to identify measures to strengthen the role of local and regional authorities in the management and implementation of the esi funds through partnership agreements and operational programmes.
in writing. ‒ yemen is facing a critical situation characterised by conflict, tribal tensions, and heavy violence with a significant humanitarian impact on the civilian population, especially children. the current violence stems from the failure of government structures to meet the democratic, economic and social aspirations of the yemeni people, generating discontent and dividing society. the situation in yemen is thus characterised by severe instability, a regrettable humanitarian crisis exacerbated by constant bombardment and conflict. the situation in yemen must therefore be stabilised, security strengthened, and functioning government structures put in place to make a consistent effort to combat extremism and violence in the region. i believe that in this situation, all parties must respect international humanitarian law and international human rights law and urgently work with un and humanitarian aid organisations to provide assistance to those in need. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that immediate action is needed to resolve the humanitarian crisis in yemen and to restore stability and peace to the territory.
in writing. ‒ the current crisis in yemen is the result of a failure of successive governments to respond to the legitimate aspirations of the yemeni people for democracy, economic and social development, stability and security. according to the 2016 humanitarian overview released in november 2015, 21.2 million people (82% of the population) are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. currently, there are estimated to be about 2.1 million undernourished people, of which more than 1.3 million are children suffering from severe acute malnutrition. i am deeply concerned about the alarming deterioration of the humanitarian situation in yemen, which is characterised by widespread food insecurity and severe malnutrition, attacks against civilians and medical workers, and the destruction of civilian and medical infrastructure. coordinated humanitarian action under the un leadership is needed, and all countries must contribute to meeting humanitarian needs. it is important to allow the entry and delivery of urgently needed food, medical supplies and fuel to meet the urgent needs of civilians affected by the crisis, in accordance with the principles of impartiality, neutrality and independence.

in writing. ‒ i strongly condemn the proxy war that is taking place in yemen. the conflict has created a huge humanitarian crisis in terms of the displacement of men, women and children, and even loss of life. iran and saudi arabia must come to terms and end the fighting. if this conflict continues, it will give great opportunity for terrorist groups to exploit the current crisis which would not only affect yemen, but also have ramifications in the region.
in writing. ‒ the arab spring has marked a rise in hope for the democratization of societies in the middle east. sadly, in some cases, social unrest has degenerated into violent internal conflicts, which have greatly affected civilian populations and undermined the viability of states. there is also the case of yemen, where the confrontation has deepened old religious and political divisions. the fragility of the yemeni state has also been exploited by the terrorist organisation al-qaeda, which controls a significant part of its territory. the involvement of external actors in the internal conflict was not designed to de-escalate the situation, but rather led to a battle of attrition between saudi-backed government forces and iranian-backed rebel forces (houthis). this struggle has generated a dramatic humanitarian situation characterised by an exponential increase in the number of refugees, chronic poverty, destruction of civilian objects (including blind and deaf centres, schools and economic objectives) and proliferation of armaments. in this situation, the european parliament must take a firm stand against the continuation of this regrettable state of affairs and encourage the involvement of relevant international actors in the settlement of the conflict. the european union, through the council and the external action service, can be directly involved in limiting arms sales and encouraging a ceasefire.
in writing. ‒ genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes, regardless of the place and time in which they are committed, must not go unpunished, and it is a matter of concern for the union's structures to combat these acts. in the last few years, 66 churches have been attacked or blown up in the systematic bombing campaign against christian churches in iraq. also, a worrying result of the systematic mass execution of members of religious minorities by isis translates into significantly lower numbers of christians in syria and iraq. for example, in iraq, there was a drop from 1 400 000 in 2003 to around 300 000 and in syria from 1.25 million in 2011 to only 500 000 today. as a result, current extremism and persecution of christians is an increasingly significant factor in the development of mass migration and internal displacement. the inalienable right of all religious and ethnic minorities living in iraq and syria to live in equality and security and to practice their religion fully and freely must be recognised, which is why i voted in favour of this report.

member of the commission. mr president, honourable members of the european parliament, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for putting on the agenda of this plenary session a debate on the role of public services in improving rail connectivity in the danube and adriatic-ionian regions. at the beginning of last week, i had the opportunity to attend the launch event of the european union strategy for the alpine region, which took place in brdo, slovenia. this was the launch of the 4th macro-regional strategy and the enthusiastic response of the over 500 participants once again attests to the need and importance of these macro-regional strategies. by engaging in macro-regional strategies, european regions can jointly address common challenges, thus contributing to territorial, economic and social cohesion. this cooperation is particularly relevant for improving connectivity between regions, in particular through the development of railway connections. both the danube and the adriatic-ionian strategy have identified rail transport as one of their main priorities. there are indeed enormous gaps between their regions in public rail services, which undermine the common potential for economic development. for example, in what we call the 'old member states', such as italy, germany and austria, public services are generally satisfactory, although there is clearly room for improvement. in the new member states, such as the czech republic, hungary and romania, the situation is not satisfactory but is improving, mainly thanks to the support provided by european funds. in contrast, in countries outside the european union, public rail services are truly inadequate and in dire need of reform and investment. in this context, the european commission believes that it is time to take energetic measures to support public rail services in these regions. actions should focus on the following: first, we certainly need closer and better cooperation between countries. there is no other way to succeed, at the micro- and macro-regional level. second, we need the participating countries to work closely together to implement a series of railway reforms, such as the separation of infrastructure and operations, and the introduction of licences and regulations. third, we need to invest in rehabilitation projects, removing bottlenecks and missing links in traffic management systems and improving capacity. in this respect, i am pleased to say that the ten-t indicative value for the western balkans currently in force provides a useful framework for these investments. but, distinguished members of the european parliament, we all know that only through cooperation, reforms and railway investment will we be able to overcome the current challenges. we must also work to improve project preparation, create and strengthen effective governance structures and align and simplify border crossing procedures. in particular, we need all parties involved to agree on a very clear principle: all public service contracts, rail transport, must be awarded on the basis of competitiveness criteria. public resources are under severe constraints and we therefore need to ensure that the available resources are used as efficiently as possible. three years ago, the commission put forward a legislative proposal as part of the 4th railway package and we are in writing. ‒ the efficiency of justice in the european framework is intrinsically linked to the cooperation of the judicial authorities of the different member states because, in an era of exponential growth of the movement of persons, elements of extraneity in legal relations become the rule, not the exception. in strengthening this efficiency with third countries too we have the hague convention of 15 november 1965, which applies exclusively to the crossborder service of documents in or from third countries as regards crossborder service within the european union, having regulation (ec) no 1393/2007. the expression of the desire of austria and malta, the only member states that have not acceded to the convention, to join the other member states is welcome and supports the authorisation of those member states by the union to act on its behalf by ratifying this convention. the usefulness of the convention in the field of crossborder service of documents has already been proven, and it is in the interest of both the union as a whole and the two member states concerned to have a single system for the service of documents in crossborder relations with third countries, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ of the 28 member states, 26 already apply the convention. austria and malta, the only member states that have not acceded to the convention, have expressed their wish to join the other member states. i welcome this decision.
