in writing. ‒ with regard to the opinion of the court of justice from 14 october 2014 and the recommendation of the committee on legal affairs, i believe that it is in the interest of the european union to authorise the republic of austria to sign and ratify, while malta accedes to, the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters.
in writing. ‒ the convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters, also known as the hague convention of 15 november 1965 allows for ‘service of process’ of legal documents from one member state to another without use of consular diplomatic channels. i voted for this recommendation that will apply this convention in austria and malta, after they indicated their wish to join the other 26 member states that already apply it.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention has represented a turning point in the procedure for crossborder service of judicial, extrajudicial and commercial documents in or from third countries. it has enabled the decisions of the institutions of the signatory states to be applied in the territory of other signatory states, thus contributing to the strengthening of international legality. today, 26 of the eu's member states are signatories to this important convention, which also gives it a european dimension. austria and malta, the only member states that have not signed the convention, are in the process of becoming signatory members. in this respect, the consent of the european parliament, representing the will of the citizens of the union, is required to allow the accession of the two states to the convention. this step would complete the process of ratification of the convention at union level. it is therefore necessary to adopt this recommendation.
in writing. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters facilitates judicial cooperation in cross-border civil and commercial litigation by simplifying the methods of transmitting judicial and extrajudicial documents between contracting states. of the 28 member states of the union, only two, namely austria and malta, have not yet acceded to the convention. as a legal entity, the union cannot accede to the convention and must therefore exercise its competences through its member states. therefore, an authorisation of the accession of the member states is required. the proposal for a council decision was therefore drawn up, the main objective of which is to authorise the accession of the two states to the hague convention. in view of the importance and usefulness of this legal instrument and having found that all the legal conditions have been met, the european parliament, by means of a legislative resolution, gives its consent to the accession of these states and approves the draft council decision on this legal procedure.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the accession of austria and malta to the hague convention, which establishes a system whereby documents can be served in another signatory state. of the 28 member states, 26 already apply the convention. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 has proved its usefulness in the field of cross-border service of documents and it is in the interest of both the union as a whole and the two member states concerned to have a single system for the service of documents in cross-border relations with third countries.
in writing. ‒ economic developments are linked to the smoothest possible flow of information, therefore the 2015 agreement between the union and san marino on the automatic exchange of financial account information to improve tax cooperation and compliance with international tax rules is only a first step, and relations need to be continued. the next step is the unconditional exchange of information on request, which will be ensured under the new agreement in 2017, in line with the latest developments in oecd and eu work in this area. i appreciate the purpose of this, which is to deal with situations where the taxpayer is trying to hide capital that represents income or assets that have not been taxed. the agreement is an important step in the current efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion and updates the 2004 agreement, which ensures that the republic of san marino applies measures equivalent to those in the eu savings tax directive, which is why i voted in favour of this draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i consider that the agreement represents an important step in ongoing efforts to clamp down on tax fraud and tax evasion and upgrades the 2004 agreement that ensured that san marino applied measures equivalent to those in an eu directive on the taxation of savings income. under the agreement, the eu and san marino will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of each other’s residents, starting in 2017. therefore, i support its aim to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide capital representing income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. moreover, i support the agreement as it is in line with the need for more transparency on tax issues in the eu and in its relations with third countries.
in writing. ‒ in order to improve international tax cooperation and compliance, the eu and san marino signed an agreement on 8 december 2015 on the automatic exchange of financial account information. an automatic exchange of information on financial accounts will start in 2017. this should reduce the possibility for tax evasion. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european union loses €1 billion a year to tax evasion. a large part of the evasion is done in existing tax havens including in europe and other member states. today i voted in favour of the protocol amending the agreement between the commission and san marino. it enables the automatic exchange of information on residents' financial accounts. they concern those situations where potential taxpayers try to hide capital derived from proceeds for which they have not paid taxes. similar arrangements have been agreed for other countries where tax havens exist, such as switzerland or lichtenstein. andorra and monaco are next. the automatic exchange of information is an effective and rapid method of combating cross-border tax fraud and evasion, for which the oecd has received a mandate from the g20. we cannot live together in a society where some people pay taxes and others cheat us all by hiding their earnings in tax havens.
in writing. ‒ in order to improve international tax cooperation and compliance on 8 december 2015 the european union and san marino signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. i voted for this report that will bring a provisional entry into application of the agreement starting 1 january, thus tax administrations in the european union and in san marino will be able to administer and enforce their tax laws in cross-border situations, assess the likelihood of tax evasion being perpetrated, identify correctly and unequivocally the concerned taxpayers and avoid unnecessary further investigations.
in writing. ‒ the european union has recently set out to combat tax evasion effectively. in this respect, the eu has concluded a number of tax cooperation agreements with third countries that are typically used as 'tax havens' to avoid the correct taxation of income. one of these states is san marino, which has always had very good cooperation with the european institutions. the commission document referred to in the current report updates the administrative cooperation between the two parties by allowing for the automatic exchange of account information in line with the 2014 oecd global standards. the information shall relate, in addition to interest and dividends, to account balances and income from the sale of financial assets. the agreement is due to enter into force in 2017, but the parties have agreed to enter into force provisionally as of 1 january 2016. the adoption of this document without delay is therefore necessary to allow the agreement to be ratified quickly and to reduce the current transitional phase.
in writing. the eu and san marino signed the agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information at the end of last year, with the aim of improving tax cooperation and compliance at international level. i voted for the ep report on this agreement which is an important step in the current efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion and updates the 2004 agreement, which ensures that the republic of san marino applies measures equivalent to those in the eu directive on taxation of savings income.

in writing. ‒ croatia's accession to the european union in 2013 was a historic moment, which gave a new dimension to the process of accession of the western balkan countries to the eu. technically, the act of accession of croatia introduced a simplified system for the accession of croatia to conventions and protocols concluded by member states, in order to allow the adoption of conventions in the croatian language. these documents include the convention of 26 july 1995 on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, together with the protocols adopted subsequently, with a view to establishing a common basis of protection under criminal law. for those regulations to enter into force for croatia, a council decision is necessary, in accordance with the recommendation of the commission. this document supports this procedural step and i therefore consider that it should be adopted.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the accession of croatia to the conventions on the protection of the european communities' financial interests. the act of accession of the republic of croatia of 2011 introduced a simplified system for the accession of croatia to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states in accordance with the teu. in practice, the council adopts a decision on the date on which those conventions enter into force with regard to croatia and the adjustments to be made to those conventions following the accession of the new member state, acting on a recommendation from the commission, after consulting the european parliament.
the report calls for greater mobility within the union and the development of a european labour market with high levels of employment. i myself consider these objectives to be important, but i would add that all this can only be achieved by strengthening cohesion policy and by bringing the poorest countries of the eu on board. in the present situation, labour migration is mainly from the east and south to the richer member states, and this is not due to the generosity of social benefits but to the general level of wages in these countries. in romania, the average net wage is around eur 400 per month, and the starting salary of a teacher is less than eur 300 per month, while the prices of goods and services are roughly the same in the western and eastern halves of europe. in such circumstances it is impossible to talk about labour market integration or the european labour market. if the process of integration of poorer member states is halted, even greater migration could start here, which could empty these countries' labour markets and create an unwanted distortion.
in writing. ‒ free movement of workers is one of the key elements for the development of an integrated labour market in the union, especially in cross-border regions, which would allow for increased mobility of workers and can contribute to increasing diversity and finding the right skills for vacancies and to removing existing bottlenecks in the labour market. the objective of this regulation is to make the eures network an effective tool for any jobseeker or employer interested in labour mobility within the eu by creating the most comprehensive portfolio of job vacancies and candidate profiles that can be accessed by anyone anywhere in the eu. moreover, it would be desirable for the network to include apprenticeships and traineeships, for which there must, however, be a regular employment relationship. in order to help workers who enjoy the right to work based on free movement to exercise this right effectively, i voted in favour of the initiatives in this report.
in writing. ‒ we know that the eures network is already functioning, but i believe that it needs to be reorganised to improve services for potential beneficiaries through better inter-ministerial coordination, to overcome the legal obstacles that exist for workers who want to work in another country, as many people are currently reluctant to accept job offers in another eu country because of uncertainty or lack of relevant information on social security systems, taxation and other obligations in their country of residence.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this report, which will tackle a number of eures’s shortcomings, such as an incomplete pool of job vacancies and cvs, limitations to automated matching and insufficient information for employers and mobile workers. the new eures network should lead to a considerable improvement regarding the functioning of eures, thereby facilitating the placement of job seekers in europe and contributing to the reduction of unemployment and skill shortages. one major improvement is the fact that the existing eures web portal is transformed into a european platform for exchange of job vacancies and cvs. our key achievements, such as the involvement of social partners at all levels of the network, the definition of cross-border partnerships and the abolition of fees for basic eures services for workers, will make eures much more effective. hopefully, the new database will now become smarter by automatically matching the cvs with job offers. in addition, all vacancies published by public or private employment agencies will be published eu-wide by eures as well.

in writing. ‒ free movement of workers is a fundamental principle of the treaty held as sacred in article 45 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. based on this legislation eu citizens are entitled to look for a job in another eu country, work there without a work permit, reside there for that purpose, stay there even after employment has finished, enjoy equal treatment in access to employment, working conditions and other social and tax advantages. i voted for this report that will create a large online pool of vacancies and jobseeker profiles which can be consulted eu-wide by anyone.
in writing. ‒ the eures network was launched a few years ago to facilitate the free movement of workers within the eu. the main purpose of the platform is to assist workers to overcome barriers to mobility and to increase access to employment opportunities across the eu. a number of shortcomings in the functioning of that network have been identified in recent years, in particular with regard to unequal access to network services across the union and to insufficient exchange of information between member states on labour shortages and surpluses. the legislative proposal under discussion in the european parliament aims to correct the shortcomings identified in the operation of the network, to make it an accessible and efficient tool, and to reorient the services offered by eures from general information and guidance to improved placement and recruitment. the new provisions aim to bring together all job vacancies, job applications and cvs available from public employment services in the member states. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ we voted for this report in view of the importance of the single market and its impact on the eu's current and future economic prosperity. the untapped potential of the single market is estimated at €1 trillion, and is both an opportunity and a wake-up call to ensure that it works for the benefit of all. cross-border development and job creation in rural and poor areas are needed, as are common policies on competitiveness. the network of national competitiveness councils needs to increase its role in common policies in this area. public procurement and the public sector are important vectors, but we need transparency and ethical competition. smes need to be aware of the governance of the single market in the european semester and resources need to be allocated at national and european level, particularly in rural areas. the european parliament regulates, but the commission and the member states have the obligation to find the most intelligent methods of implementation.
in writing. ‒ the single market accounts for 500 million people and an estimated 23 million smes. i agree with the rapporteur that the slow pace of investment in the eu and the difficulties that smes encounter in accessing capital are critical barriers to growth and job creation in the european union. the commission’s investment plan for europe and the european fund for strategic investments are most welcome and ease access to funding for smes. moreover, a wider range of financing options for smes is a priority of the capital markets union.
in writing. ‒ the single market refers to the european union as one territory without any internal borders or other regulatory obstacles to the free movement of goods and services. it stimulates competition and trade, improves efficiency, raises quality and helps cut prices. i voted for this report that will include the single market in the 2016 european semester, the european union’s annual cycle of economic policy guidance and surveillance.
in writing. ‒ home to 500 million consumers and 21 million smes, the single market is not just one of the foundations of the eu, but in its current phase of development, one of the greatest achievements of our european union. this is why i most welcome the adoption of this report identifying both improvements to its governance and avenues through which it could be better adapted to the realities and challenges of the 21st century. seeing that today over 70% of all economic activity in the eu and a similar proportion of its employment are in services, i believe that this is the area which we should most concentrate on by establishing and better implementing and enforcing rules on fair and healthy competition. it is essential that these start with the freedom to provide services across borders, non-discrimination and territorial limitations, such as geo-blocking.
in writing. i voted for the own-initiative report on the governance of the single market in the european semester 2016. according to the rapporteur, the single market is a precious resource on which the eu's current and future economic prosperity depends, with the untapped potential of the single market estimated at €1 000 billion. i agree with her that there are too many trade barriers within the eu and many member states do not implement decisions to which they are signatories. the report also states that coordination of macro and microeconomic policies, accompanied by coordination of fiscal policies, is necessary to ensure the desired structural economic growth in eu member states.
in writing. ‒ since october 2015, the european union and tunisia have started negotiations for a new and much more ambitious free trade agreement, an agreement based on the mandate adopted unanimously by the european union states on 14 december 2011, and the first rounds of negotiations started on 19-22 october 2015. the main arguments for the new contract are the history of cooperation between the european union and tunisia, which dates back to 1969, with tunisia being the first country on the southern shore of the mediterranean to sign an association agreement with the european union in 1995. the conclusion of a new trade agreement between the european union and tunisia should open up prospects for economic growth and, not least, for the rapprochement of the economies of both parties, as this partnership should help tunisia to achieve both political and demographic stability. i voted in favour of this report on the opening of negotiations for a free trade agreement between the european union and tunisia because i believe that this agreement is beneficial for both the european union and tunisia, from an economic, political and demographic point of view.

in writing. ‒ the annual report of the european central bank for 2014 summarises the main aspects of the ecb's activity in the period under review, highlighting the highlights of the ecb's action, which led to the development of certain recommendations. the european central bank acted promptly on the difficult situation of low inflation, declining lending, slow economic growth, and the ecb's use of unconventional monetary policy instruments. however, further sustained efforts are needed to strengthen potential growth and to reduce the high unemployment rates in many euro area member states, as well as to reduce debt. improving conditions for public and private investment to stimulate growth and job creation is also needed. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european central bank needs to continue its contribution to the general economic policies of the union and to the achievement of the objectives of those policies in order to overcome economic obstacles and ensure economic growth in all member states.

in writing. ‒ the european central bank is the central bank of the 19 european union member states that have adopted the euro. its main task is to maintain price stability in the euro area and preserve the purchasing power of the single currency. i have voted for this report on the european central bank’s annual activity report for 2014 that highlights the steps needed for a stronger monetary union, amongst which we can identify the commission’s plan to establish a capital markets union that should diversify sources of financing in the eu economy, boost cross-border investment and increase access to financing for business, especially smes.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the annual report of the european central bank for 2014. the report speaks of the need for further efforts to secure the financing of the real economy in the context of a differentiated return of the euro area economies. the attention the rapporteur has paid to the sme sector is to be appreciated. it notes that there are still discrepancies between the financing rates for smes and those for larger companies, between the interest rates for small loans and those for large loans, and between the credit terms offered to smes in different euro area countries. the report also shows that, despite the ecb's continued efforts to maintain favourable financing conditions, private and public investment in the euro area is still well below pre-crisis levels. the rapporteur also stresses that the ecb's supervisory role and its monetary policy function must be clearly differentiated and the combination of these functions should not give rise to any conflict of interest for the ecb.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution on the opening of negotiations for free trade agreements with australia and new zealand comes as a natural step in strengthening the partnership between these countries and the european union. australia and new zealand are among the eu's longest-standing partners, sharing common values and committed to promoting prosperity and security within a rules-based global system. australia and new zealand also collaborate in a number of international fora, acting against common challenges. furthermore, the eu and new zealand are parties to the agreement on government procurement, and australia is in the process of acceding to it. the eu, australia and new zealand are also engaged in multilateral negotiations to further liberalise trade in organic products. given the significant number of agreements under negotiation between the eu and its main trading partners, the conclusion of free trade agreements between the eu and australia and new zealand will deepen trade and investment relations, creating the conditions for advancing economic relations to a new level, which is why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the leaders of eu and australia, in their meeting on 15 november 2015, agreed to commence work towards the launch of negotiations for a free trade agreement. the eu and new zealand, in their meeting on 29 october 2015, also announced the start of the process for negotiations on a comprehensive free trade agreement. i am strongly in favour of starting a discussion on key global issues such as human rights, security, development and protection of the environment with australia and new zealand. it is important to understand the possible risks of trade diversion resulting from the tpp, and how these affect the potential interest of the eu in concluding high-quality comprehensive ftas with australia and new zealand. launching negotiations for swift, high-quality and comprehensive agreements would further integrate the eu into value chains in the asia-pacific region. i hope that negotiations with these important trade partners will start as soon as possible.

in writing. we voted for the ep resolution on the opening of negotiations for free trade agreements (ftas) with australia and new zealand. in the resolution, the rapporteurs consider that the full potential of the union's bilateral and regional cooperation strategies can only be realised through the conclusion of high-quality ftas with both australia and new zealand. i agree with their view that negotiating a modern, ambitious, balanced and comprehensive fta with australia and new zealand, taking into account the specific features of their economies, is a pragmatic way to deepen bilateral partnerships and strengthen existing, mature bilateral trade and investment relations, while also contributing to mitigating the potential diversionary effects of the recently concluded tpp.
in writing. ‒ there have been reports from various non-governmental organisations, competent authorities and veterinary organisations of an increase in the illegal trade in pet animals, accompanied by numerous abuses within the pet movement system. this abuse of the pet movement system is estimated to be the third most profitable form of illicit trade in the eu, after drugs and arms trafficking. the impact of this practice is serious, with negative implications for both human and pet health. 70% of the new diseases that have occurred in humans in recent decades are of animal origin, and the illegal pet trade is therefore facilitating the spread of diseases that could endanger the health of citizens. in addition, pet animals that are illegally traded are often raised in poor conditions and are at high risk of disease. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that introducing compatible pet registration systems across all member states would ensure compliance with animal welfare requirements and also limit the risks associated with the illegal trade in pet animals.
in writing. ‒ believing in the positive effect that pets have on the lives of millions of owners and families across the european union, i believe that owners should be able to travel with their pets safely and in controlled conditions across the union and, in this context, i welcome the improvements to the pet movement system.
in writing. ‒ i support the introduction of a new passport model, which stipulates that cats, dogs and ferrets can travel with their owners within the eu if they have a passport that contains proof of their identity and their anti-rabies vaccination, all of which must comply with specific conditions. eu countries must provide the public with clear and easily accessible information concerning the requirements applicable to the non-commercial movement of pets and the rules for compliance checks on such movement. i support the call for an eu-wide database for pet registration, and i welcome the fact that the commission agreed to carry out a study on the welfare of dogs and cats forming the subject of commercial practices. if the commission will find evidence that such practices incurred health risks, it should consider additional measures, including the introduction of compatible systems for the registration of pet animals accessible across member states. i am expecting the commission to give an update on the progress made to date.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this motion for a resolution on compatible systems of identification and registration requirements for dogs, cats and wild animals kept as pets that should reduce illegal trading, thus protecting public and animal health and biodiversity.

member of the commission.– mr president, the commission welcomes the report that we will discuss today. i sincerely thank the rapporteur, mr fleckenstein, for the important and future-oriented work he has accomplished. thank you also to the shadow rapporteurs and the committee on transport and tourism for the good quality of the report. the port services regulation is an important piece of the european transport policy to foster investment and push further modernisation of ports. you know about the crucial role of ports for the transport system and our economy. they are europe’s gateways to the world. they provide employment in ports directly and in related sectors. they are hubs for short-sea shipping which we must strengthen as part of our decarbonisation strategy. in short, ports are valuable assets which we must preserve and strengthen. that is what the regulation aims at and that is why it is one of the commission’s priority files for 2016. the regulation will ensure transparency in the use of public funds in ports. we need to ensure a level playing field between european ports, many of which receive considerable financial support from both national and eu budgets. financial transparency is crucial for this. financial transparency will also allow us to simplify the application of state aid rules. the commission is working on the general block exemption regulation; it should exempt certain port investments from state aid rules and focus the commission’s work on critical cases in order to establish a genuine level playing field. a first draft, proposed, was published today for consultation. and today the public consultation has started. the port services regulation will provide an important input into this work, provided it gets your support. the port services regulation will also bring more clarity for the organisation and tendering of port services. it will end today’s unclear situation where ports policy is not decided by the legislator but defined on a case-by-case basis by the european court of justice, only according to the treaty principles. the adoption of the regulation will therefore mean more legal clarity and legal stability for both port workers and investors. the regulation is also important for our decarbonisation strategy, which after cop21 we are even more committed to. making ports more attractive is essential to developing alternatives to congested motorways and avoiding unnecessary land and sea traffic. we need to diversify maritime routes and promote short-sea shipping. the report got broad support in the committee on transport and tourism. all major organisations representing the european port sector stand behind it: the trade unions, port authorities, port terminal operators and port service providers. let me stress that the commission fully supports the social dialogue as well as better training and safety for workers. let me also stress that the regulation does not impose a one-size-fits-all approach. we know that every port in europe is different. the draft regulation respects this. it is compatible with all forms of organisations, including private ports. it does not impose one model. your vote tomorrow, to start the trilogues, is essential for advancing with this important piece of legislation. the council already adopted a general approach in 2014. this was one of the major successes of the italian presidency. it is time for parliament to enter into negotiations with the council and conclude this file. the dutch presidency is very interested in negotiating and concluding the file still before summer. i am inviting you all not to lose this opportunity.

mr president, commissioner, the subject has been and is still being intensely debated. there are diverse and divergent views on some provisions. however, an encouraging compromise has been reached: the regulation will create jobs, develop and increase the competitiveness of the important economic sector of ports; it allows autonomy for setting tariffs, creating better conditions for competition and for better quality services at affordable prices; it introduces financial transparency, ensuring a level playing field for all actors and means of combating illegal state aid. the regulation will apply to all ports included in the tnt. member states shall, however, have the flexibility to exclude ports in the comprehensive network from peripheral regions. small ports have the flexibility to avoid red tape and disproportionate costs in order to enhance efficiency and quality of service. the economic situation and competition in the sector require a decision that has been discussed for more than ten years. negotiation with the council is necessary and can lead to the elimination of the current disputes.

vice-president of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank everyone again for their questions and comments. the commission is committed to maximising the growth potential of the data—driven economy with its digital single market strategy and other initiatives planned for this year. i agree with vicki ford, who underlined the importance of really transparent e-procurement. according to analyses prepared by the european parliament, if we are able to implement e-procurement across europe we could save eur 50 billion per year, which is a huge amount of money – and, i am sorry to say, we do not have this money. we have to implement and introduce e-invoices in all the member states. we have to use digital signatures more proactively. of course, we have to pay attention to privacy issues. we have to protect everybody’s privacy, but we have to allow free data flows across europe. governments have to open their data in all the member states. all of the companies, all the players, have to get access to data – it does not matter whether they are small and medium-sized companies or bigger players. the digital divide is a real issue in the european union. this divide is not only between our member states, but also within member states, even in those member states where it is highly developed. we can see that there is a real digital divide between downtown and rural areas, between men and women, and between young and elderly people, and we have to deal with all those issues. you gave me just a minute, and i have already been speaking for two and a half minutes – i am so sorry, we don’t have time. the commission will propose all those legislative proposals during this year. we have to hurry up, because while yes, of course we have some risks, the real risk is to lose this competition. i would like to thank members for today’s debate. i look forward to working swiftly and efficiently with the co-legislators to design and build the necessary conditions for a data-driven economy that benefits everyone in society – individual people, public bodies and the private sector.

in writing.– data are essential in the current economy. ‘data’ means knowledge, innovation and tools that can help stimulate entrepreneurship, help with administration or improve our education systems. unfortunately, europe is not in the forefront of the data-driven economy, even though it has a huge potential. in order to take advantage of this opportunity we need to be clear on the rules applying at european level, create the instruments to stimulate data-driven entrepreneurship and support the creation of a europe-wide data economy infrastructure. last but not least, we need to create a pan-european exchange of best practice and pool our experience in order to stimulate this sector, which is essential for the future of our economy.
the next item is a short presentation of the report by angelika mlinar, on behalf of the committee on women’s rights and gender equality, on gender mainstreaming in the work of the european parliament [(2015/2230(ini)] (a8—0034/2016).
member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank ms mlinar for this draft report on gender mainstreaming in the work of the european parliament. gender mainstreaming is an important tool to achieve real equality between women and men. for the eu, it is article 8 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union which states that: ‘in all its activities, the union shall aim to eliminate inequalities, and to promote equality between men and women’. gender mainstreaming is therefore not a choice, but an obligation. all major institutions, including the european parliament and the commission, are confronted with the permanent challenge of putting gender mainstreaming into practice and continuously improving its effectiveness. the so-called ‘dual approach’ of specifically targeted gender equality actions, on the one hand, and gender mainstreaming on the other hand, has proven successful not only at european level, but also at national, regional and local levels. the commission also follows this dual approach in the recently published strategic engagement for gender equality 2016—2019. this strategic paper, in line with the principle of gender mainstreaming, emphasises the need to integrate a gender equality perspective into all eu policies, legislation and funding programmes. in practice, this is translated into constant efforts to integrate a gender equality perspective into every aspect of eu intervention. it means assessing the impact of commission action on both women and men and taking responsibility for adjustment if necessary, so that equality between women and men is promoted and equalities are not perpetuated. in order to monitor the implementation of gender mainstreaming in the commission in practice, the strategic engagement announces that the commission will consider issuing a report on gender mainstreaming in 2017. the commission’s inter-service group for equality between women and men, managed by the dg for justice and consumers, plays a key role in implementing gender mainstreaming at the commission. finally, let me congratulate ms ward on her birthday today and wish all of us a good women’s day tomorrow.
the item is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday, 8 march 2016. written statements (rule 162)
in writing. gender and equal opportunities is a concept that came into force on the european agenda in 1996, with the commission's commitment to develop a dual system to address inequalities between women and men. after 20 years, neither the european commission nor the member states have been able to rally behind the principle of equal opportunities and gender equality. it's said that women who want to be equal to men are not ambitious enough, which may be a fitting quote for a feminist cause on international women's day, but it's far from a reality-reflecting quote. the reality is that a significant number of women are still discriminated against in the eu on gender grounds; the reality is that certain areas, such as transport, remain inaccessible to many women; the reality is that we have failed to integrate genuine education on equal opportunities and gender equality into european public policies. the european commission must come up with a new strategy and communication for gender equality in the eu, 20 years after the 1996 commitment. we need concrete solutions, programmes developed and adequately funded to integrate women into decision-making positions in all european institutions.

in writing. ‒ we voted in the european parliament plenary on measures to prevent and control animal disease epidemics such as avian influenza or african swine fever, measures informally agreed with eu ministers in june 2015. the eu legislative proposal on animal-borne and potentially transmissible diseases to humans emphasises prevention and helps professionals in the field keep pace with scientific progress. this law accomplishes three important things. first, it links animal welfare and health and connects them to human health. this direct link, along with the emphasis on responsible antibiotic use, will help us fight the growing resistance to antimicrobials. secondly, it helps authorities and producers to focus more on the prevention and control of transmissible animal diseases. third, it combines some 40 legal documents into one legislative act.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support this law, which will finally streamline the law on animal health, obliging all operators and animal keepers to adhere to the principle of good animal husbandry, as well as taking biosecurity measures to protect their animals. responsible and prudent use of veterinary medicines is also an obligation: member states are called upon to commit themselves to collecting relevant data on the actual use of antimicrobial medicinal products in animals and to send such data to the commission in order to ensure more prudent use of antimicrobial medicinal products in animals, thereby helping to reduce the risk of antimicrobial resistance. the list of diseases covered by the law will be adopted in line with the parliament and council decision, and taking account of expert advice. all operators and animal keepers will be required to apply the principle of good animal husbandry under this law, as well as humane treatment to avoid pain, distress and suffering when disease control measures are taken.
in writing. ‒ animal health is a key part of the european food safety authority mandate. the concept of animal health covers not only animal diseases, but also the critical relationship between animal health, animal welfare and food safety. i have voted against the amendment that rejects the position of the council’s first reading on transmissible animal diseases.
in writing. ‒ on 6 may 2013, the european commission adopted a proposal for a single comprehensive animal health law that was supposed to replace the old and complicated animal health rules. the european parliament and the european council also reached a political agreement on the animal health proposal on 1 june 2015. i have voted against the amendment, which rejects the first reading position of the council.
in writing. the european union has become a space dominated by concern for the welfare of animals, both pet and wild, in recent decades. in line with this principle, the european institutions have in recent years sought to adapt existing legislation to the requirements in this area. a key aspect of this is ensuring animal health, in particular by preventing communicable diseases. the adoption of an 'animal health act' has become a necessity, especially when we think of wild animals that can be completely vulnerable to new diseases. at the same time, antibiotic treatment of sick animals may weaken their immunity. the incidence of animal diseases may also affect the human staff who work with them in one way or another, which amounts to 20 to 30 million people. another aspect of the legislation concerns the treatment of animals, which must avoid suffering, but also their controlled breeding and the protection of elite breeds. as regards pet animals, the registration of specialist breeders in a european database could prevent the spread of certain diseases. as this is an important document in this field, i support its adoption in its present form.
in writing. ‒ the european union's legislative proposal on transmissible animal diseases contains a number of measures to prevent and control outbreaks of animal diseases such as avian influenza or african swine fever. the fact that over 60 percent of human diseases come from animals makes this proposal of major importance. this proposal underlines the need for responsible use of antibiotics to combat the growing antimicrobial resistance in animals. in this regard, veterinarians will be required to draw attention to the interaction between animal health and welfare and antimicrobial resistance. the european commission will therefore monitor the use of antibiotics in the member states and has the ability to take urgent action in the event of epidemics that could seriously affect human health and agricultural production. in such cases, farmers' organisations and veterinary associations will be involved in the establishment of contingency plans. in addition, breeders and traders of pet animals are required to register in a database to avoid the situation where homeless or illegally traded animals transmit animal diseases. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the proposal on transmissible animal diseases.
in writing. the european union is facing a youth obesity phenomenon, with over 22 million young people and children being overweight as a result of excessive consumption of processed foods high in sugars, fats and other additives, and in addition, a sedentary lifestyle. the continuing decline in the consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk products among young people has led the commission to review and bring together the two separate schemes for the distribution of fruit, vegetables and milk in schools. i believe that initiatives to promote healthy eating should not be limited to educational institutions. family and teachers are key factors that play an important role in promoting a balanced diet. the main objective of the new regulation is to convince young people that fruit and milk contribute to their health and healthy growth. on the other hand, to bring young people closer to nature, it is important that they know where these foods come from. in this context, i strongly support the promotion of regional and seasonal agricultural products, firstly because it supports local agricultural producers, but also because the actions contribute to the formation of healthy eating habits.
in writing. ‒ i consider the implementation of the aid scheme for the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk to educational institutions to be particularly important, as the target group of this project, children aged between 6 and 10 years, need to benefit from healthy and fresh food, which is important for their growth and development. for the good functioning of this project, it is extremely important to identify and analyse the needs and costs, from purchasing to supplying schools, so that each school, especially those in disadvantaged areas, receives the necessary quantity without waste. this whole system, from problem analysis to food selection to proper supplying of educational institutions, will lead the target population towards a healthy life by building a balanced diet from an early age. the implementation of this regulation aims at cooperation between member states to reduce childhood obesity and boost the immune system of children, with the help of nutrition experts and farmers. supplying disadvantaged regions with those with high production potential is an important step towards ensuring that children are raised in a healthy environment that is conducive to our future generations and a viable and strong population.
in writing. ‒ eu children should soon benefit from better-funded school milk, fruit and vegetable schemes, along with better lessons on healthy eating. i voted to combine the separate eu milk and fruit schemes and increase the annual budget of the new scheme by €20 million to €250 million per year. the annual funding for milk will be eur 100 million and that for fruit and vegetables eur 150 million. a healthy, balanced diet is the foundation for health. unfortunately, there has been a downward trend in the eu in the consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables, but also milk, in schools. that's why it's very important to strengthen the fruit, vegetables and milk scheme in schools by increasing the budget and focusing more on healthy eating education. by voting for the budget, parliament also ensured the financial stability of the programme, preventing member states from unilaterally cutting the budget or changing the criteria for allocating eu funds between them.
in writing. ‒ i believe this report is absolutely necessary to ensure that the schemes, in future, will prioritise healthy, fresh, unprocessed and local foods as much as possible both in the main scheme and in accompanying educational measures and will also be visible as eu actions. concerning the list of products to be distributed, the text now makes clear, at the request of parliament, that the member states shall prioritise the distribution of fresh products over processed ones with a view to encouraging healthier eating habits among children. i believe the future of the school schemes is assured by this text. management will now be more efficient through a single, visible programme with the milk part operating in parallel with the fruit and vegetable strand. we will therefore be able to promote consumption of healthy, fresh foods by schoolchildren, helping them establish healthy eating habits – especially important when we are facing an epidemic of obesity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the state aid scheme for the supply of fruit, vegetables and milk to educational establishments, as i believe it is essential that the eu and the member states are concerned about children's health. in the context of declining consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables, the report is also important because it promotes healthy eating habits and the consumption of local products. i appreciate the report because it allows member states to include other local, national and regional specialties such as honey, table olives and processed vegetables without added sugar, salt, fat, sweeteners or flavourings. the proposed six-year programme allows member states to provide children with a healthy diet on a permanent basis, alongside education on healthy nutrition. it is important that member states' programmes are monitored and that an evaluation of the results obtained is carried out.
in writing. ‒ the report reiterates that products distributed under this educational school program should not contain added sugar, salt, fat, artificial flavour enhancers or sweeteners, and should contribute to the physical and psychological wellbeing of children and combating child obesity. a trend has been identified in the consumption decline of fruit and vegetables and milk consumption among children, thus their distribution in all programs schools is important in combating child obesity and promotes healthy eating habits, this being the reason i have voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ the measures presented in this report support the distribution of fruits, vegetables and milk in schools. they also represent a critical tool to reconnect children with agriculture and the variety of the eu’s agricultural products, more specifically those produced in their region, with the help of, for example, nutrition experts and farmers. i have voted for this report, which has as its objective the increased consumption of selected agricultural products.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the aid scheme for the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk to educational establishments. this regulation, which applies from 1 august 2017, provides for aid of up to eur 250 million per school year per member state for the supply of fruit and vegetables and milk to schools, for accompanying educational measures and related costs. within the overall limit, the aid shall not exceed eur 150 million per school year for school fruit and vegetables and eur 100 million per school year for school milk. that aid shall be allocated to each member state taking into account criteria such as the number of children aged between six and 10 years or the degree of development of the regions of the member state concerned, so as to ensure that a higher aid is allocated to the less developed regions. member states shall choose the products to be distributed or to be included in accompanying educational measures on the basis of objective criteria such as health and environmental considerations, seasonality, variety and availability of local or regional products. member states may in particular encourage local or regional purchasing, organic products, short supply chains or environmental benefits.
in writing. ‒ i voted to adopt the ep amendments to regulation (eu) no 1308/2013 and regulation (eu) no 1306/2013 on the call for the continuation and strengthening of the consumption of fruits, milk and vegetables among school children through an aid scheme to allow for a more proportionally targeted distribution of these goods based on the number of children aged 6-10 in a member state’s population. moreover, the member states that at present face monetary and logistical challenges in terms of accessing milk, vegetables and fruit will be greatly helped by the proposed aid scheme.
in writing. ‒ the way in which education systems in eu member states ensure the harmonious development of children is an expression of the degree to which we care about the future of our societies. one of the important components of this system is to ensure minimum nutritional intake during the school curriculum. scientific studies have therefore shown that there is a need to encourage the consumption of fruit (including bananas) and vegetables, but also of milk, i.e. healthy, fresh and as little processed food produced locally, including yoghurt and cheese. at the same time, the presence of artificial sweeteners and flavourings, sugars, salt and fats in the school diet should be minimised to avoid the incidence of obesity. they could be replaced by products such as honey, olives and olive oil. the european union supports the integrated approach to this school meal scheme in the member states with the help of the national authorities. to this end, significant financial resources are mobilised, amounting to approximately eur 250 000 for each national school year. the measure supports the development of europe's peripheral regions and can be evaluated after at least six years. the present report is a very important document for the future of our children and can be adopted in its present form.
in writing. ‒ originally envisaged under the common agricultural policy in the 1970s and aimed at supporting farmers and milk producers, the european 'milk in schools' programme, which was joined in 2009 by the 'fruit in schools' programme, now focuses on the objective of healthy eating, in the context of european union citizens facing problems such as obesity and diabetes. in the european union, 14 million children are overweight, increasing by 400,000 a year, while in romania, 13.7% of children aged 2-14 are obese and 8.8% are overweight. moreover, in recent years there has been a decline in the consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables and dairy products, especially among children. it is therefore important that the supply of fruit, vegetables and milk to educational establishments is maintained. to improve the management of the two programmes, the new regulation proposes to merge them and increase the budget by eur 20 million per year, bringing it to eur 250 million. in addition, for a fair distribution of funds, the number of children aged between 6 and 10 years and the level of development of the regions in each member state will be taken into account.
