in writing. ‒ the report on the arrangements applicable to products originating in certain states which are part of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states proposes to regulate imports of products originating in these countries. it is envisaged to provide duty-free access to the eu market for products originating in acp countries which do not fall within the category of least developed countries in the period preceding the conclusion and application of the economic partnership agreements. those rules are based on the simplification and transparency of union law, in order to ensure easy access by citizens to their rights. in the light of the fact that the market access regulation has already been amended nine times since its adoption, a clear and simplified codification of the relevant legislation is necessary. i think it is particularly important to create a concise, clear legal framework that enables citizens to make use of their specific rights, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal refers to the reform of the market access regulation (mar). i voted for a transparency and simplification of eu legislation, after this draft has undergone numerous changes since its adoption in 2007. access to the eu market free of customs duties for products originating in acp countries is a matter of course.
in writing. ‒ this is a codification and recast of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 (the market access regulation) governing imports of products originating in certain acp countries. this temporary instrument provides duty-free and quota-free access to the eu market for products originating in non-least developed countries (ldc) acp countries in the run-up to the conclusion and application of respective wto-compatible economic partnership agreements (epas) before the 1 october 2016. i support the continuation of duty free quota free access to the eu market for those non-least developed countries (ldc) whilst epa negotiations are continuing. continuing market access for these countries at this time is to be supported.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report regarding a codification and recast of the market access regulation that governs imports of products originating in certain states which are part of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states.
in writing. ‒ on 1 january 2008 the provisions of the market access regulation entered into force as a temporary unilateral scheme before the conclusion and application of the revised economic partnership agreements. the commission proposal concerns the codification and recast of the market access regulation, governing imports of products originating in certain acp countries. i have voted for this report that aims to ensure transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of reforming the regulation on the arrangements applicable to products originating in certain states which are part of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states provided for in agreements establishing or leading to the establishment of economic partnership agreements (epas). since 2002, the union has negotiated epas with the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states in the form of seven regions comprising the caribbean, central africa, east and southern africa, east african community, pacific island states, southern african development community and west africa. these agreements must be in line with world trade organisation (wto) obligations, support regional integration and promote the progressive integration of acp economies into the regulated international trading system, thereby encouraging their sustainable development and contributing to the overall effort to eradicate poverty and improve living conditions in acp states. however, given the particular sensitivity of agricultural products, it should be possible to adopt safeguard measures where imports cause or threaten to cause dysfunctions in the markets for such products or in the mechanisms regulating those markets.
in writing. ‒ the european union places a strong emphasis on developing global free trade, with a view to diversifying the supply of products for consumers worldwide. at the same time, the union supports the economic strengthening of states in less developed regions such as africa, the caribbean and the pacific (acp). for these reasons, the eu supports the integration of these countries into the world trade organisation (wto), but is aware that they need a period of preparation of their economies to become compatible with the developed economies in the wto. in these circumstances, the council decided as early as 2007 to exempt from customs duties certain products originating in developing acp countries. the extension of this measure until the adoption of economic partnership agreements between these states and the wto was considered necessary precisely in order to facilitate the development and economic reform of those states. this document takes note of the extension of the period of validity of the measures for the exemption of products from those countries, as well as of a number of amendments to bring the legislation up to date. i believe that these measures are necessary to set an example of good international cooperation and i support the adoption of the document.
in writing. ‒ fisheries is an important economic sector that requires responsible and sustainable policies. there are a number of fisheries partnership agreements signed by the european union, whereby the eu commits to providing financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights in the exclusive economic zone of the state with which it has signed the agreement. one of the most important agreements in this area is the eu-greenland app with the government of denmark and the local government of greenland. the new protocol strengthens the cooperation between the union and greenland by being a mixed agreement, providing eu vessels with access to a wide range of fish stocks in the greenland eez. the current protocol provides for an eu financial contribution of eur 17.85 million per year, which includes support for the fisheries sector at administrative level, but also in terms of development and scientific research. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the new protocol offers significant economic benefits to both parties, being an important pillar in the development of sustainable fisheries policies, including the regulation of responsible exploitation in the greenland area.
in writing. ‒ the new protocol is consistent with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement, thus strengthening cooperation between the european union and greenland. i voted for an extension of the existing agreement for a period of 5 years, during which the annual financial contribution amounts to a total of approximately eur 18 million. provision is also made for a pilot fisheries programme for species not covered by the protocol and for scientific cooperation in the field of sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the renewal of this agreement is in the interest of the european union, as the economic benefits are mutual and in line with the objectives of the cfp.
in writing. ‒ the new protocol is considered to be in line with the objectives of the cfp, to respect the principle of available surplus and the obligation to follow scientific advice. it strengthens cooperation between the eu and greenland and promotes a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fishery resources, including through financial support (sectoral support) for the implementation of programmes, in particular for enhanced monitoring and combating of illegal fishing, as well as the support of the local fisheries sector, including the generation of local employment opportunities. the new protocol ensures improved value for money for the eu by aligning the level of fishing opportunities with the effective level of utilisation; it provides for at least one annual meeting of the joint committee, at which the commission and greenland review the implementation of the fpa/protocol, and, if necessary, adjust the programming of sectoral support/financial contribution. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in recent years the european union has signed a series of fisheries partnership agreements. i have voted in favour of the most recent fisheries partnership agreement that covers a period of five years and provides an annual financial contribution of eur 17 799 987 per year to greenland in exchange for fishing rights.
in writing. ‒ several fisheries partnership agreements have been signed by the eu in recent years. these sustainable fisheries agreements with non-eu countries are negotiated and concluded by the commission on behalf of the eu. i voted for this report that will provide a financial contribution of eur 17.8 m each year from the eu to greenland in exchange for fishing rights.
in writing. ‒ the greenland agreement is the third agreement of importance to the eu in terms of economic value. it is in the interest of both the eu and greenland to renew the protocol, as it provides significant economic benefits to both parties and contributes to ensuring coherence with eu fishing activities in other areas of the region. in july 2015, the european commission adopted the proposals for the renewal of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community, of the one part, and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, of the other part. the new protocol provides for a financial contribution from the eu of eur 17,8 million per year. this amount is: (a) over eur 13 million per year for access to greenland's fishing zone; (b) eur 2,9 million per year corresponding to the additional package mobilised by the eu to support greenland's fisheries policy; and (c) eur 1,7 million as an annual reserve for additional and new fishing opportunities that can be accepted by the eu subject to scientific advice and surplus resources. this protocol is also of strategic importance for the activities of union vessels in the fishing zones of other important bilateral partners in the north-east atlantic, in particular norway and the faroe islands.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the renewal of the fisheries protocol between the eu and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, as it unequivocally supports the conclusion of the protocol. this new protocol is consistent with the common fisheries policy (cfp) and is fair and necessary for both parties. the protocol provides for access to greenland's fish resources by vessels flying the flag of an eu member state, and the eu commits to pay eur 17.85 million per year for fishing opportunities over a period of five years. the previous protocol with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland generated a direct and indirect added value of approximately eur 1,6 for every eur 1 invested by the eu. in this respect, i believe that this protocol should be supported and its repetition in other situations should be encouraged.
in writing. ‒ the european union's relations with third countries and entities have developed strongly in recent years. the relationship with greenland has always been characterised by openness and enhanced cooperation in areas of common interest. although formally dependent on the eu member state denmark, greenland is not part of the territories under the jurisdiction of the european institutions, but enjoys a special relationship with the union. as greenland's main economic activity is fishing, which accounts for almost 90% of its exports, an agreement between the eu and greenland in this area was considered necessary as early as 1985. in recent years, due to the revision of european fisheries policies, the duration of the agreements has been reduced from 10 to 6 and 3 years respectively, the last one being in force from 2013 to 2015. the implementation of a new fisheries protocol for the period 2016-2020 required three rounds of negotiations and concerns the fisheries of several species for which the union has allocated approximately eur 18 million, of which over eur 13 million for access to greenlandic resources, almost eur 3 million for supporting fisheries in the region and the remainder for the reserve. the implementation of this agreement, which supports sustainable development and jobs and combats illegal fishing, deserves to be supported.
in writing. ‒ the draft decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the government of the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china envisages the regulation of certain aspects of air services. international aviation relations between member states and third countries are traditionally regulated by bilateral air service agreements. it is therefore intended to replace certain provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air service agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. the most important clauses are the designation clauses, which replace the traditional clauses with an eu designation clause, allowing all eu carriers to benefit from the right of establishment, and the safety clauses, which ensure that the safety provisions of bilateral agreements apply in situations where regulatory control of an air carrier is exercised by a member state other than that designated by the air carrier. the compatibility clause also prohibits anti-competitive practices. i voted in favour of this draft decision because i believe that the eu-macao agreement on certain aspects of air services contains coherent provisions designed to ensure a secure, mutually favourable legal framework.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the amendment to the agreement which replaces certain provisions of existing bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china, which were in breach of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees equal treatment for both nationals and members of the host state.
in writing. ‒ international relations in the field of air transport between member states and third countries have traditionally been governed by bilateral agreements on air services. the court of justice of the european union estimated in 2002 that traditional designation clauses in bilateral agreements between member states’ air services were contrary to the legislation of the european union. they allow a third country to reject, withdraw or suspend the permissions or authorisations of an air carrier that has been designated by a member state, but whose ownership and effective control is not vested essentially with this member state or its nationals. the court found that this constituted discrimination against carriers of the union in the territory of a member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. this is a violation of article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees nationals of member states who have exercised their freedom of establishment the same treatment in the host member state as that accorded to nationals of that member state. the agreement replaces the traditional designation clauses with an eu designation clause, permitting all eu carriers to benefit from the right of establishment. i therefore gave a favourable opinion on the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ this agreement changes some provisions related to safety, competition and taxation in the 15 bilateral air services agreements between the european union and the macao special administrative region.
in writing. ‒ bilateral air services agreements govern international aviation relations between eu member states and third countries. i have voted for this report that will replace certain provisions in the existing 15 bilateral air services agreements between the macao special administrative region of the people’s republic of china and eu member states.
in writing. ‒ the agreement between the union and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china is the most effective instrument for aligning all existing bilateral air service agreements between member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china with union law. the objectives of these agreements are to provide all european union air carriers with non-discriminatory access to air routes between the european union and third countries and to align bilateral air service agreements between member states and third countries with union law. the proposal also provides for a simplification of the legislation. i voted in favour of this agreement because it will respond to a fundamental objective of the union's external policy in the field of aviation by bringing existing bilateral air services agreements into line with union law.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it supports the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the government of the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china on certain aspects of air services. the conclusion of this agreement was necessary given that the court of justice of the european union has ruled that certain provisions of bilateral agreements concluded by member states are contrary to eu law. in this respect, this agreement rectifies this situation and prohibits anti-competitive practices.
in writing. ‒ air transport is one of the areas where international cooperation is essential for the smooth running of current activities. the european union has been pursuing greater coordination of air services in recent years, both within the territories of the member states and with third countries. in the latter area, bilateral agreements have been concluded with various states, but a number of problems remain regarding discrimination between air carriers of eu countries established in the territory of other states and carriers from those states. this is why special agreements have been concluded between the eu and third parties to avoid this type of discrimination and to regulate fair conditions of safety, competition and taxation. one of those third parties is the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. the eu has negotiated an agreement to replace the 15 bilateral agreements previously adopted, building on its traditionally good relations with the territorial entity. the european parliament is the forum for approving the entry into force of these much needed air services agreements. i therefore support the adoption of this document in its current form.
in writing. i voted for the ep recommendation on the eu-macao agreement on certain aspects of air services. the recommendation follows the commission's negotiation of the agreement which replaces certain provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. this agreement was signed on 23 november 2013 and required the council's approval by the ep for its conclusion.
in writing. ‒ the application of a minimum standard rate in all member states is intended to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. the minimum rates are justified by the fact that the vat applied at the place of origin rather than at the place of destination still applies for cross-border trade and for distance sales below a certain threshold. the value added tax directive therefore provides that until 31 december 2015 the standard rate shall not be less than 15%. the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax as regards the duration of the obligation to comply with the minimum standard rate provides for retrospective maintenance of the principle of a minimum value of 15% for the standard rate of vat, by proposing to extend the current provisions by three years. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a minimum standard rate should be applied to ensure the protection of the internal markets.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur supports the commission's proposal to maintain the minimum value of 15% for the standard vat rate and proposes to extend the current provisions until 31 december 2018. i voted to give member states the possibility to carry out vat reforms, aimed at reducing the standard rate. as in all member states, a standard minimum quota provides a useful safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i support the rapporteur's view that the extension of the time limit for maintaining a minimum value of 15% for the standard vat rate until 31 december 2018 allows for a more comprehensive debate on vat rates in the context of the future vat action plan. it is beneficial for the eu to establish guidelines for future activities and features of the definitive vat arrangements for intra-eu transactions, with a view to adapting the existing rules to a definitive regime characterised by the principle of the place of destination.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the commission’s proposal to retroactively maintain the principle of a minimum standard vat rate of 15%, and i support a more comprehensive discussion on vat rates in connection with the forthcoming action plan on vat. the commission’s 2016 action plan will set out the directions for future work following the achievements attained since the 2011 communication on the future of vat. it will in particular set out the main features of the definitive vat regime for intra-eu trade that the commission wants to propose and the reforms it envisages to adapt the existing rules on vat rates to a definitive regime characterised by the destination principle.
in writing. ‒ the importance of this report is that a minimum standard rate applied in all member states - as is currently the case - provides a useful safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market. in the area of value added tax, the minimum rates are justified by the fact that vat applied at the place of origin rather than at the place of destination still applies for cross-border trade and for distance sales below a certain threshold. given that all member states currently apply a standard rate higher than 15%, the current provisions providing for a minimum standard rate of 15% also provide a margin of manoeuvre for member states by allowing them to carry out vat reforms aimed at reducing the standard rate by broadening the vat base and limiting the use of reduced rates.
in writing. ‒ the standard rate of vat could not be set lower than 15% in any member states starting 1 january 1993 as was stipulated in the directive 92/77/eec. the commission proposal aims at a system of tax harmonization within all eu member states. i have voted in favour of the renewal for 3 years of the vat directive until 31/12/2018.
in writing. ‒ the standard vat rate among eu member states may not be less than 15% as provided in the vat directive that was introduced from 1 january 1993 until 31 december 1996. this directive has been extended five times already and has been into force until 31 december 2015. i have voted for this report that will extend the vat directive for a period of three years, until 31 december 2018. this vat directive represents a transitional system in view of establishing the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that maintaining the minimum value of 15% for the standard vat rate provides a useful safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market of the european union. the report also shows that all member states currently have a standard vat rate of more than 15%, and that maintaining a minimum rate gives member states room to reform. at the same time, the imposition of a minimum vat rate avoids situations of unfair competition between member states, as the european union market becomes increasingly interconnected.
in writing. ‒ vat is a major and growing source of tax revenue in the eu. however, in its current form, the system does not provide guarantees for an efficient collection to the benefit of european citizens, nor does it fully prevent unfair competition among member states. in this context, i believe that a minimum standard rate applied in all member states, as has actually been the case so far, is essential in safeguarding the proper functioning of the internal market.

in writing. ‒ the report on fisheries issues under the international agreement on marine biodiversity in the areas outside national jurisdiction highlights the need for a comprehensive global regime that better addresses fisheries issues. given that seas and oceans cover 71% of the earth's surface and contain approximately 97% of the planet's water, and the marine environment is home to a significant part of the world's biodiversity, increased attention is needed to protect and conserve marine biodiversity. the new agreement thus envisages the creation of certain tools to empower all actors involved, but also the strengthening of capacity and the exchange of information, both between member states and between the eu and third countries. it is also recommended that a legally binding international instrument be established under unclos for the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity of areas beyond national jurisdiction. i welcome the progress made by the un on the issue of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, voting in favour of this report and expressing my continued concern for the conservation of marine habitats and the sustainable development of this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of supporting the position and objectives of the european commission, which is engaged on behalf of the member states in the negotiation of this new international agreement. an important aspect of the report is the inclusion of fishing activities among those regulated by the new international legal instrument. regional fisheries management organisations must also be extended and become more important under the new international agreement. the existence of marine protected areas can only be guaranteed if there is coordination and collaboration in all areas of activity. in this regard, it is very important that this new agreement includes an institutional decision-making structure.

in writing. ‒ blue growth has to be one of our main priorities, as pressure on the sustainability and conservation of marine biodiversity is constantly increasing. in recent decades, human activities at sea have multiplied. the potential for growth and jobs is enormous and should be used within the ecological limits of the marine environment. fisheries and aquaculture play an important role in the marine economy, but we must be determined in tackling the environmental problems and the need for sustainable development. i am therefore in favour of an international approach in order to manage pollution, human activities and increasing dangers to marine biodiversity. responsible fisheries and aquaculture are key to sustainable development and a healthy marine eco-system; fishing must be integrated into this vision of the future of the sea that is blue growth.
in writing. ‒ nowadays, marine activities are developing and multiplying at a fast rate, with the pressure on marine biodiversity constantly increasing. i agree with the rapporteur that the solution for these issues should come from an internationally legally binding instrument, and this can be foreseen in the near future.

in writing. i voted in favour of the nicolai report on fisheries issues under the international agreement on marine biodiversity in outermost areas - un convention on the law of the sea and i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on her work. fishing has intensified recently, but so have related marine activities, and therefore the pressure on sustainability and the conservation of marine biodiversity is continuously increasing. i am pleased that the un general assembly and the ad hoc working group have managed, despite strong opposition, to make progress on the issue of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, with the intention of creating a legally binding international instrument. i hope that the new agreement will include tools to empower all actors involved, because without these tools there can be no expectation of real progress or real efficiency.
in writing. ‒ fishing is a fast-growing economic activity, both at european and global level, which can generate sustainable development for society and, by implication, stable jobs. the development of this activity must, however, take account of the conservation of marine biodiversity and limit pollution and other adverse phenomena that may occur in the maritime space. as most of this area (64%) is governed not by national laws but by the law of the sea, the international community is directly responsible for the observance of the rules adopted in this area. these are, first, the un convention on the law of the sea, adopted in 1982, and, on the basis of that document, the international agreement on marine biodiversity in the areas beyond national jurisdiction, including fisheries issues, adopted in 1995. by 2017, it is expected that binding instruments on fishing activities in international maritime space will be adopted. the european union can only support these measures, which are in line with the principle of 'blue growth' of maritime space. the sustainable development of the world's fisheries is one of the important resources for achieving healthy economic growth, generating jobs and food for the society of the future. i therefore support the adoption of this document.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on zootechnical and genealogical conditions applicable to intra-union trade and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products aims to harmonise trade in this field and to standardise the official controls to be carried out on breeding programmes, taking into account both the cross-border nature and the principle of subsidiarity. current zootechnical legislation promotes free trade in breeding animals and their genetic material, taking into account the sustainability of breeding programmes and the conservation of genetic resources. however, at present, union zootechnical legislation is organised vertically by species, which is why similar provisions have been concentrated and worded in clearer and more coherent language, precisely to avoid their transposition into national legislation creating barriers to trade. the proposal therefore contains a number of new provisions describing the relationship between breeders and breeding societies, provisions on the acceptance of breeding animals and artificial insemination, on performance testing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to create a coherent legal framework that allows citizens to exercise their rights in a transparent regulatory framework.

in writing. ‒ livestock farming is one of the important sectors of agricultural activity in the eu member states. the pursuit of this activity implies compliance with certain zootechnical and genealogical conditions concerning reproduction and germinal material derived from the various species of bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine animals existing in the territory of the states of the union. those conditions concern the use of high-quality genetic material, obtained as a result of long-term hybridisation activities carried out by european farmers and regulated by substantial legislation at european level. this document proposes to unify this legislation, in particular as regards the recognition and publication of lists of professional organisations, breeders' associations and private structures, the registration and classification of animals in databases on herds, genetic specimens and protected species, performance testing and genetic evaluation, and the zootechnical certification of animal specimens and their genetic material. this codification will contribute to the conservation and enhancement of local and threatened species and to clarify the rights of farmers within the union. this is a significant step forward in this area, which is why i support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ a well-functioning breeding sector is essential for eu agriculture, with a potential value-add of €1.89 billion. at present, european zootechnical legislation aimed at promoting free trade in breeding animals and their genetic material is organised by species (cattle, pigs, sheep and goats) and there is a basic directive for each species. the purpose of the proposed regulation is to establish uniform rules on trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products, with a view to promoting sustainable breeding programmes for the improvement of breeds and the conservation of genetic biodiversity of domestic animals. the idea is to avoid obstacles that could arise from the disparities between the existing rules. it also lays down rules on imports of breeding animals and their germinal products from third countries and stresses the need to preserve breeding animals in danger of extinction. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on trade and imports in breeding animals and their germinal products.

in writing. ‒ this report highlights the importance of erasmus+ and other tools to promote mobility in vocational and technical education. these instruments demonstrate that a real and ambitious mobility offer must be part of any overall strategy to recover the economy and reduce youth unemployment rates, which have reached far too high levels in recent times. in some european regions, the real unemployment rate is close to zero, while in other areas it is rising to over 40% among young people, especially those who have not been able to complete secondary education or vocational training. therefore, it is very important for the eu to take the necessary measures to prevent early school leaving, and european mobility programmes are one such measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. erasmus is one of the most successful projects of the european union. we cannot imagine a single economy, a single european market, unless we are talking about a single labour market, mobility of young people within the borders of the european union, exchanges of experience between universities and graduates of higher education who have the same training for the labour market across the european union.
in writing. ‒ erasmus+ is the eu’s programme to support education, training youth and sport in europe. it has a budget of eur 14.7 billion and provides opportunities for over 4 million europeans to study, train, gain experience and volunteer abroad. i have voted for this report that calls, amongst others things, for the expansion and improvement of mobility options for students.
in writing. ‒ a common european area of education based on mobility, including higher education and vocational and technical education (vet), will contribute to the creation and development of a stronger european identity and enhanced citizenship. the transition to the digital economy is redefining jobs and skills, and member states and the commission need to work with the private sector to develop skills strategies and vocational and technical education programmes to retrain workers. the private and public sectors of industry and services, including the manufacturing sector (in particular smes and micro-enterprises) should be consulted and/or involved in the design, development, implementation and support of quality vet mobility programmes. the commission needs to monitor the evolution of demand and supply in the eu labour market, as well as geographical and occupational mobility, in order to adapt to labour market needs. this would reduce the gaps between the supply of training courses and market needs in value-added sectors (e.g. digital and green economy, energy, etc.). i therefore voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on erasmus+ and other tools to promote mobility in vocational and technical education.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that facilitating the mobility of european citizens is the foundation of the eu. we are facing, and i speak for most member states, a very high rate of school dropout, but also an inequitable accessibility in terms of mobility, and here i am referring to the disparity between university and technical education. in this respect, the report adopted today promotes mobility in vocational and technical education through the erasmus+ programme and other instruments, which is beneficial as it increases the inclusion of young people in society, strengthens their ability to work in a multicultural environment and, not least, allows them to acquire knowledge about the eu.
in writing. ‒ for many young people, erasmus may provide their first opportunity to live in another eu member state, and it is a vital basis for educational, cultural and linguistic exchange across the eu. vocational educational training helps to create a mobile and adaptable work force which promotes economic growth and increases employment opportunities for the individual. these programmes are therefore of great social and economic importance and should be protected and enhanced.
in writing. ‒ today, 29 years after its establishment, the erasmus programme is not just the european union’s best known and most successful project, but also the biggest student mobility programme in the world: its existence has allowed more than 3 million students from over 3 000 universities from the eu and beyond to live and study in other countries, fostering not just high quality education and employability, but also understanding, respect and dialogue among cultures. as its success is largely due to the latter aspect, i believe that it is time for the openness that is at its foundation to be taken one step further and its multicultural approach extended to minority languages from within member states. the provision by the member states of erasmus+ documents in minority languages would be the most natural step in this regard.
in writing. ‒ the erasmus programme places great importance on mobility and furthering career prospects through learning and developing intercultural dialogue within academia. the report focuses on the implementation of erasmus+ and the mobility aspect, considering the objectives of the mobility programme and calling on the commission and the members states to adopt concrete measures to improve the social and economic impact. it underlines the diversity of languages requested for the erasmus+ documentation and the importance of developing a highly skilled workforce with inclusive education policies. in my opinion, we need to enhance mobility, in particular for youth apprenticeship and trainees, which will contribute to economic growth and job creation in the eu. in addition, one of the main goals would be to ensure that erasmus+ documentation is available in all eu official languages.
in writing. ‒ the inclusion of several programmes in a single concept, erasmus+, as well as the effects of the economic crisis, felt since 2008, highlight a structural deficit of programmes which are intended for student mobility in terms of the relationship between training and employment. unfortunately, there is a very large difference in the design of courses and study programmes, while the organisation and management of educational centres and the business environment increase above all the costs and operational difficulties in developing mobility between countries and regions in europe. i believe that we must take into account the socio-economic reality in the various member states of the european union and that it is necessary to urgently reactivate this form of vocational training in europe, given the extremely high differences in unemployment rates in different european regions. i strongly support the adoption of the erasmus+ programme because, on the one hand, it speeds up the completion of the recognition and accreditation processes, which is a common reference framework valid in all member states, and the field of vocational training requires major importance in order to overcome the limitations related to both mutual recognition of studies and employment-related aspects.
in writing. i voted for the own-initiative report on erasmus+ and other tools to promote mobility in vocational and technical education. the adoption of erasmus+ in place of the various previous programmes represented an important evolution of the concept of mobility within the european higher education area. the report makes proposals to address a structural shortfall in mobility programmes in terms of the relationship between training and employment.
mr president, i voted for this report because i support the idea of a single european voice. we often face fragmentation and delays due to insufficient or inconsistent implementation of internationally agreed financial rules and guidelines. it is important that the union has ex ante evaluations before it goes to negotiations, to start global negotiations with regard to the financial sector. i also believe that the union should become a member of international economic and financial institutions such as the imf or the oecd, but that does not mean that the member states should lose their seats. and the cooperation between them will be better, and the competition is also very good. last but not least, i support the idea of a european code on transparency, integrity and accountability for those who represent the european union in financial institutions.
in writing. ‒ given the flow of capital and financial professions globally, it is illusory to claim a change in the field without a change in public equity. the eu has achieved a number of strengths, such as a world-class internal market for financial services that will be reinvigorated by the markets union, a single global currency that has adopted support mechanisms and established unprecedented banking supervision and resolution bodies for the crisis period, a committee responsible for systemic prevention, and three authorities that have consolidated their existence in a short period of time. the eu has exceptional know-how in terms of supranational democracy and monitoring of member states' commitments in respect of non-compliance. at the same time, the strategic importance of the financial sector for growth and job creation requires a review of multilateral global cooperation, thus increasing the influence of the eu, but also of the euro area. i voted in favour of this report on the eu's role in international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies because i believe that the eu is an important economic player.

in writing. ‒ in the current international framework, the lack of coherence caused by the fragmentation and diversity of the various organisations/bodies is causing delays regarding rules and orientations agreed at international level. therefore, i support the need to clarify the remit of each organisation and body, as well as the ways in which they operate and are financed. moreover, i agree that improvement is needed on the coordination between the commission and the member states which are members of the financial action task force (fatf) on tax issues. the eu should streamline and codify its representation in multilateral organisations/bodies and the commission should be held more directly accountable to citizens and the role of parliament in this process must be stronger.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this report that should enhance international regulatory cooperation, improve transparency and accountability in order for the eu to defend its strategic interests.
in writing. ‒ due to the financial professions and the global nature of capital flows, it would be unrealistic to attempt and regulate this sector without public initiatives. i have voted for this report that should enable the eu and the euro area to defend its strategic interests.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the european parliament resolution on the role of the eu in international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies because the eu should speak with one voice in these institutions/bodies. we call for greater political coherence and coordination among international institutions through the introduction of comprehensive standards of democratic legitimacy, transparency, accountability and integrity. this should, inter alia, concern: public relations (e.g. public access to documents, open dialogue with various stakeholders, the creation of mandatory transparency registers and rules on the transparency of lobby meetings); and internal rules (e.g. human resources recruited on the basis of competence, sound financial management, prevention of conflicts of interest); the under-representation of least developed countries in most international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies creates an imbalance and, as a consequence, the issues of inequality or of financing for the poorest countries risk not being adequately addressed. there are also certain sectors in particular civil society, smes, consumer representatives and employee representatives whose participation in the consultation process can be enhanced in international discussions on financial, monetary and regulatory bodies. we believe that these bodies and sectors should make efforts to improve the situation.
in writing. ‒ the importance of international monetary institutions and bodies for the economies of all states, including all eu member states, is very great - and understandable - in the context of increasingly interconnected and interdependent economies. in this context, the eu's presence in these international institutions and bodies, through the member states or the european commission, is becoming increasingly important. i support the rapporteur's view, which underlines the importance of coordinating member states' positions and of representing the whole eu with a single voice, a single agenda of objectives and negotiations in these international institutions and bodies. although this is not always possible, the adoption of anti-eu positions by a member state within these institutions and organisations can cause significant damage to the union as a whole. i voted in favour of this report because it highlights the importance of the coherent and coordinated representation of eu economies in such international institutions and calls on the member states and the european commission to work towards this.
in writing. ‒ the european union is currently one of the main structures represented in international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies. however, its representation is fragmented, leading to a certain lack of coherence in the union's positions and causing certain delays in the application of internationally agreed rules. the way in which each international organisation operates also needs to be clarified in light of their increasingly important role in the lives of european citizens, in particular with regard to funding, interests and the legality of decisions. in this respect, the european union's involvement must include a stronger role for the european parliament, the direct representative of the citizens, and a stronger accountability of the commission. the existence of two separate representations, the council and the commission, is also likely to lead to a number of confusions as to the positions of the european institutions and the member states, in particular in the context of the g20 meetings. to address these problems, this report rightly proposes enhanced cooperation within the union to adopt common positions, greater transparency, accountability and democratisation of international organisations with economic impact and greater involvement of the european parliament in this process.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the own-initiative report on the eu's role in international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies. in drawing up this document, the reporting team started from three conclusions: the stability of the financial system, a decisive element for investment and growth, depends on the ability to develop standards and codes of conduct and ensure their compliance at supranational level; the indispensable change of scale must not lead to dilution of responsibilities to the detriment of democracy; the eu and the euro area must be able to defend their strategic interests. the report calls on member states to accept the representation of the banking union in the basel committee on banking supervision, as well as an in-depth analysis of the situation where the council and the commission each have their place at the g20 meetings.
in writing. ‒ coastal fishing is a very important form of fishing in the eu member states, and is of particular importance because it provides a high degree of employment and is an ecologically and socially sustainable fishing activity. coastal and island areas dependent on coastal fisheries require special measures and support to be able to foster both development of the areas and economic growth. the 2013 and 2014 regulations on the economic policy in the field of fisheries focused on economic growth in coastal areas, recognising the importance of offshore island areas that depend on fisheries and need to be supported in order to survive and benefit from the opportunities needed to develop. i voted in favour of the report on the innovation and diversification of small-scale coastal fishing in fisheries-dependent regions because it is very important to encourage and support coastal fisheries-dependent states in order to achieve economic growth for both those states and the eu.
in writing. ‒ when we talk about fishing in coastal and island areas, we are talking about a way of life and even a source of livelihood. they require special measures and support to foster development and economic growth. we voted to amend existing legislation, thus protecting fisheries in coastal and island areas.
in writing. ‒ coastal fishing is an exceptionally important form of fishing in eu countries. it guarantees a high level of employment and is a socially and environmentally sustainable form of fishing. for most coastal and island areas, coastal fishing is a traditional form of fishing that forms a way of life and a significant source of livelihood. areas which depend on coastal fisheries require specific measures and support in order to grow and develop. the report looks at how innovation and diversification can help coastal regions dependent on fishing to survive. not only is coastal fishing a way of life for many communities, but for islands and coastal areas it can also provide a number of people’s livelihoods. coastal regions face decline and depopulation as people move elsewhere to find work. i supported the report as i believe it will protect and create jobs in small-scale, artisanal fisheries. coastal fishing guarantees a high level of employment in coastal areas and generally represents a socially and environmentally sustainable form of fishing.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i support the rapporteur's position on the importance of small-scale coastal fishing both for local economies and for the eu fishing industry as a whole. coastal fishing, whether artisanal or traditional, although defined differently by the member states, is the most important economic activity for some communities, if not the only one. i support the principles expressed in this report, in particular those relating to the application of regionalisation, as also provided for in the common fisheries policy. i also think it is extremely important that the report stresses the need to encourage small-scale fishing, to have a clearer definition of small-scale coastal fishing and to constantly analyse socio-economic realities.
in writing. ‒ fishing activities generate important revenues for the budgets of the eu member states. this is particularly the case for coastal and island fisheries, which are a traditional, clean form of economy and guarantee a high level of long-term employment. unfortunately, the survival of these livelihoods is threatened by economic decline and depopulation of these areas, which are heavily dependent on fishing. to avoid this negative trend, the economies of coastal areas can be diversified and strengthened through the european maritime and fisheries fund, allowing better commercial exploitation of the products of these regions and promoting scientific research on biodiversity in these areas, which can serve as a model for other regions. at the same time, those areas can be better promoted for their tourism and gastronomic potential, creating the conditions for new sources of development in the future. in this respect, this document is a laudable initiative, which deserves the support of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ the pcp was born in the 1980s and consisted of the eu members, the soviet union, japan and the usa. they fish pelagic or in waters far from their own coastal waters. three decades later, the situation has changed radically, with strong competition emerging in all ocean areas. unfortunately, many of the pelagic countries do not fulfil their responsibilities as flag, port and trade states, which gives them an economic competitive advantage over the eu. the eu is the world's largest market for fishery products, has one of the largest fleets under its flags and is among the top three catching powers, and the best strategy to achieve the objective of promoting sustainable fisheries is to use the eu's influence on the international stage to be able to improve standards of transparency and fisheries management, to encourage competition at the top level at the expense of competition at the bottom. i voted in favour of the report on common rules for the implementation of the external dimension of the cfp, including fisheries agreements, because the new cfp includes significant progress and will improve standards for eu pelagic fisheries.
in writing. ‒ the eu is the world's largest market for fishery products, with one of the largest fleets under its flag. i voted for greater transparency in the fishing activities of all the relevant actors and for supporting the eu's objective of promoting sustainable fishing.
in writing. ‒ it is important for europe and its involvement in environmental protection to support cooperation between local and regional authorities and associations of entrepreneurs, fisheries and oceanography research institutes, universities, technology centres and local and regional institutions to participate in the innovation process, as development and innovation can play a fundamental role in job creation in island and coastal communities. in these communities, small-scale fishing contributes to the viability of the communities, to combating the increasing phenomenon of depopulation, ageing in the fisheries sector and unemployment. at the same time, it should be borne in mind that small-scale fishing in certain areas uses old gear and techniques that are more environmentally friendly and have less impact on the status of endangered stocks.
in writing. ‒ the eu is currently the world’s largest market for fisheries products and has one of the largest fleets and usually ranks among the top three world catching powers. i believe we have to improve transparency in fishing activities and support regional approach to fisheries management, including promoting the harmonisation of conditions of access for foreign fleets to third countries’ eezs (exclusive economic zones) and the development of a sustainability framework for joint ventures as part of the implementation of sfpas. moreover, we should improve the supply of fish for food security by supporting the work done by women in the fisheries sector. the external dimension of the common fisheries policy has to be among our priorities for fisheries policy like promoting sustainable fishing in third countries, ensuring that fishery products imported into the eu are produced under acceptable labour and human rights standards, keeping up pressure on states to combat iuu fishing and enhancing controls.
in writing. ‒ the eu is the world’s largest market for fisheries products with one of the largest fleets. its objective is to promote sustainable fisheries on the international stage. i have voted in favour of this report that should improve fisheries management and transparency standards of the common fisheries policy (cep).
in writing. ‒ the common fisheries policy is a set of rules that manages european fishing fleets and conserves fish stocks. designed to manage a common resource, it gives all european fishing fleets equal access to eu waters and fishing grounds, allowing fishermen to compete fairly. i have voted for this report that will bring more transparency in fishing activities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be a balanced report, which sets out both the importance of the external dimension of the common fisheries policy and the main concerns of the committee on fisheries with regard to these agreements with third countries. it is true that the eu is the largest importer of fish products, which means that there is a constant need for fisheries agreements with third countries. however, the eu must ensure that these agreements are mutually beneficial, that they help the development of third countries and, not least, that they are in line with the principles of the cfp. furthermore, given that in some cases information on third countries' fish stocks is incomplete, encouraging better monitoring and combating iuu fishing should always be a priority of those agreements.
in writing. ‒ the european union is now the largest market for fishery products worldwide. the total level of the eu member states' fishing fleet is also among the top three in the world. this level is based on the fishing activity in the internal waters of the member states, but also in international waters or waters belonging to other states. in international waters, fishing is regulated through participation in regional fisheries management organisations (rfmo); in the waters of other countries, fishing is regulated through bilateral conventions with that state. to maintain its global competitiveness in the fisheries sector, the eu generally calls for certain management and transparency standards in the sector, as well as harmonisation of access conditions, development of a sustainable framework, combating illegal fishing, ensuring decent working conditions and human rights, and promoting the involvement of women in the sector. the eu also promotes the importance of fisheries for the food security of the population at international level; the commission therefore focuses on compliance with the fisheries partnership agreements and the development of integrated flag databases. the adoption of this document constitutes a significant improvement to the common fisheries policy (cfp).

has claimed over 180 lives since january 2015 in europe and many more have been seriously injured, many more lives changed forever. you know, because i said it many times before, if we do not put information in the future. europol has a very specific mission by the treaties, but as mr weber reminded us, it is an important one: to support and strengthen action by the member states’ police security union, as president juncker said here today. over the last five months we have put on the table important legislative proposals on terrorism, firearms, criminal records, borders and every good proposal on the table. with regard to information-sharing, here we are finally coming to understand that the less information we share, the less we know and the less we can prevent. our young persons born and raised in the european union. these are our youngsters. the roots of radicalisation are complex and multifaceted. there is no button that we can press to solve it. that is why we must rethink our integration and inclusion efforts, our educational structures, our whole approach to promoting tolerance and common values. let us not repeat ourselves. let us avoid empty words. our challenges are considerable and they are shared. let us prove our unity and resilience with concrete actions.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, let me start by saying i am very glad that we are having this debate tonight. the situation in nagorno-karabakh was probably the centre of my talks both in armenia and azerbaijan when i was visiting those countries last month. when i was looking at the last time this issue was discussed in plenary, i saw that it was in 2011, so i am really glad that this parliament is addressing it for the first time in plenary. it is going to be very helpful and useful, because events in nagorno-karabakh are another reminder of how dangerous a protracted conflict can be. just days before the latest and unprecedented escalation, we had cautioned that the status quo was unsustainable. from a tense situation to large-scale hostilities can be a very short step. for this reason, we are increasing our efforts towards a settlement of the conflict. it has already inflicted too much suffering. it continues to pose a threat to regional security in our neighbourhood, and it is an obstacle towards the development of both countries and of the entire region. the south caucuses is a crucial region for europe. it lies at the crossroads between europe, asia and the middle east. it holds a huge potential for growth, but such a potential is held back by instability and war, and again this came out very clearly in my recent talks in both capitals. a large-scale conflict is not in the interests of anyone and can lead nowhere. this conflict hinders the development and the stability of the two countries and of their neighbours, as well as the rapprochement with the european union. as you know, at the beginning of april, the violence surged to a level that was unprecedented since the ceasefire agreement in 1994. we have all seen reports about the use of heavy weapons and the large numbers of casualties, including among the civilian population. statements from baku and yerevan make it clear that there are serious dangers if the situation is not quickly calmed. immediately, on 2 april, i called on the parties to stop the fighting and observe the ceasefire, to show restraint and avoid any further actions or statements that could result in escalation. i have reiterated my support for the osce minsk group and the three co-chairs as the internationally-agreed format for the settlement of this conflict. the eu special representative for the south caucasus, herbert salber, made immediate contact with the parties and kept these contacts regularly. i myself had separate constructive conversations with the foreign ministers of armenia and of azerbaijan. i will stay in contact with them in the coming days and in the coming weeks, and our special representative is visiting the region this week. let me add that i hope that you can contribute to our efforts with your own parliamentary contacts. as you know, i believe very much in parliamentary diplomacy, both with your fellow parliamentarians but also with civil society organisations. we all know the way ahead. the escalation makes it even clearer that the conflict does not have a military solution. developments on the ground demand that we stay vigilant and continue to insist on the strict observance of the ceasefire and on moving forward in the peace process. in particular, the targeting of civilians must stop. but obviously we cannot settle for the status quo. a political solution is what is needed, and our political goal must be that the sides resume negotiations on a comprehensive settlement of the conflict. the minsk group and its co-chairs are there to further mediate, and the eu has supported a settlement on the basis of the madrid principles proposed by the co-chairs. but ultimately we know well that the solution is in the hands of the parties to this conflict. they need to be ready to make meaningful compromises towards peace. in parallel with observing the ceasefire and engaging in negotiations, it is necessary to create an environment that is conducive to progress. actions and statements which could further complicate the already complex environment have to stop. the european union fully supports measures that can help, for instance, with the repatriation of the bodies of dead soldiers to their families. i am encouraged by the mechanism that has been put in place in recent days by the icrc and the osce. we will also need new efforts that can accompany the political process. these include enhanced security measures, such as the osce-proposed mechanism for investigation into the ceasefire violations. this is a mechanism the european union has endorsed. the eu – complementing the efforts of the minsk group co-chairs – has for several years now supported activities that facilitate peaceful contacts between people across the conflict divide. today this work is more important than ever. the conflict settlement will also continue to be part of the eu’s contacts and dialogue with armenia and azerbaijan, as partner countries, as well as with key international stakeholders. as i said, this was at the centre of our talks when i visited both countries a month ago. after this tragic outburst of violence, talking about negotiations and trust might sound out of place. it is not. actually, it is the only rational thing to do. the alternative to negotiations would be more death and more destruction. everyone now understands that the status quo can only lead to more violence, and this is exactly what happened. let us not underestimate the dangers of this conflict, and let us turn the current situation into an opportunity for peace.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, madam rapporteur, you know how much i care about this global strategy, and we also discussed that recently. i would like to thank you personally for your work in this parliament and outside, in this respect. our world has become so unstable and so dangerous that our foreign policy can simply not afford to guess and check. our mistakes can be too costly, as impulsive reactions can lead us to very dangerous places, and we see this every single day. the security of our citizens calls for a coherent, rational and united foreign policy. you also know how much i care about the broad discussions we are having about this strategy. it has been a clear political decision for me. this has to be a strategy not for the european institutions but for our union, and this means it can only be the result of a collective process. all the commissioners have contributed to it. all the member states, in different formations of ministerial meetings, have discussed their comments and proposals. we have involved think tanks, foreign policy experts and civil society representatives. we have organised a student essay competition and have met recently with former erasmus students – and i have to say this was one of the best meetings we have had in the process. obviously the european parliament and the national parliaments have a key role to play, also because you represent directly our citizens, and our citizens know today that foreign policy matters to their lives. so let me thank the rapporteur for the excellent work, as our thinking on many different issues also goes exactly in the same direction. this is also very encouraging to see because our strategy, our common work, will not stop in june when the document is ready, as you said. in the report you ask for a review of the strategy every five years. i agree. this should be a regular exercise we will have to do – five years, or even less maybe. but i believe that the first sections of the strategy on our interests and principles could have the potential to drive our actions for many years – probably even more than five – but at the same time, the strategy will have to be a living document. we need constantly to adapt the priorities we have set with the reality that surrounds us around the world, in our region, and also in terms of implementation. i will come to the implementation in a moment. from day one we will have to work on this, especially on the implementation of the strategy, for instance with sectorial papers and action plans. this is not going to be a phd thesis or an academic dissertation. this has to be a living document on how we achieve our objectives, and i cannot imagine parliament not being involved in the life of this strategy after june. looking at your report it is clear, and i do not need to explain why we have opted for a global strategy and not simply a security strategy like the previous one. for sure, traditional security will be crucial, and security includes defence. still, we all understand that this is not enough. ‘no security without development’ is what we always say, but also ‘no security without democracy, human rights and the rule of law’. i believe the arab awakening should have told us something about this – that security must be sustainable, and sustainable security cannot be achieved through security and defence instruments alone. it requires development, governance, civil society support, climate action and much more. this is why i put resilience at the core of this strategy: the resilience of institutions, the resilience of societies, the resilience of people and the resilience of countries at the end of today. if you understand this, we should also see that our european union can truly be a global power and, i would say, a superpower. we hold in our hands a unique mix of hard and soft power that no other power in the world can use. as a union of 28, we can mobilise public and private investments, soldiers, observers and an unparalleled diplomatic network. this includes your contacts with other parliaments and with civil society organisations worldwide. the real challenge is making the mix of all these assets truly effective with common political guidance, and this is one of the main aims of the strategy. such a mix already makes us incredibly interesting for our global partners. just hours ago i got back from indonesia and japan, and to them – on the other side of the world – it is absolutely clear that the european union is a global power and the partner they want to partner with. i fully agree with the report when it says that there is no contradiction between our role in our neighbourhood and our global engagement. of course we need to prioritise, and of course our neighbours are the top priority, but let us not forget that our neighbourhood is expanding by the day. think of this simple fact. if we exclude syria, the highest number of refugees in europe comes from afghanistan, but there are also migrants from pakistan and refugees from eritrea. these are faraway places and yet so close to us. we need to be a global player because issues are global. we cannot stabilise our immediate neighbourhood if we do not look at the sahel, the horn of africa and central asia, and our stabilisation efforts must account both for the roles played by other global players in these regions and for global causes of instability, such as climate change. we cannot build a new global order based on rules and cooperation if we do not fully engage with our partners far away in latin america or southeast asia. so indeed, everything is interconnected, and the global strategy is just that: a global response to global challenges and global opportunities. let me mention the three principles guiding our external action, in my view. first: engagement, because turning inwards is simply not an option. it would make us more, and not less, vulnerable, as we see when we underline the link between external and internal threats. second: responsibility – thinking of what happens the day after and what we do the day after an action is taken. having clear ideas of why we are taking any single step, what happens next, who are our allies and how we engage with them. we have seen too many mistakes in the past, just because we did not consider the consequences of an action. third: partnership. the days when the weakness of my neighbour was my strength are long gone. you mentioned that. instability in our neighbourhood can only bring instability here in europe, so we need strong neighbours and strong cooperation with our partners in their neighbourhoods. no country alone, not even our union alone, can carry the whole world on its shoulders. engagement, responsibility and partnership: our engagement needs to be responsible and it needs to be cooperative. the strategy will focus on some broad priorities: the starting points for the work ahead. first, the european union must strengthen itself. we need a stronger union. this includes building up our defence and doing so in a cooperative manner; making our intelligence services work together; working against radicalisation in our societies; monitoring hybrid threats; strengthening our energy security, cyber capacities and strategic communications; and preserving the schengen system with new asylum rules. in a phrase, we need a 21st-century approach to security. second, we need to invest in the resilience of states and societies in and around europe, to the east and to the south. we need to support effective and democratic institutions, protect the space of civil society and promote it, address countries of transit and origin of migration, promote socio-economic development, fight climate change and promote energy transitions. this is a complex priority which will need to be fleshed out, country by country, with a targeted approach. we have all the means to make our partners more internally resilient, but we need to focus on every single one to make it happen. third, we must do all we can to put an end to the current crisis in which the state, far from resilient, is on the verge of collapse – from syria to libya, from somalia to south sudan – and we must prevent the next crisis from addressing problems before they boil up and get out of control. these may not get us in the headlines, but it is the most effective way to save human lives and increased collective security. fourth, we must strengthen regional orders, because the causes of conflicts have an increasingly transnational nature. we are seeing this every single day. more often, the key to solving or preventing a crisis lies not only inside the country but in the region. our cooperation with the us and nato, with the african union, celac and asean, are all key. in some parts of the world, like africa, we need to strengthen existing organisations. in other cases, we need new and creative formats. i think of the talks we have on syria that have somehow established a format that is what i call ‘minilateral’ and that is flexible enough to feed into a process like the complex one in the security council of the united nations, managing to bring results in that multilateral format. we need more of that. a network of bilateral, trilateral, sub-regional and regional organisations can be the best base for a more cooperative and more effective multilateral global order. so the last priority must be better global governance that is truly fit for our age. this was a year of important achievements for the international community, from the iranian deal to the sustainable development goals, to cop21. we need to stick to this path and preserve a system based on rules, but we need to work on how we can be imaginative. in a world of predictable unpredictability, the international system as it is does not suffice. we do not need conservation but change if we want to preserve the principle of effective multilateralism. there is only one way to succeed in all this and to achieve our objectives, and this is a truly united europe. i began by saying that our environment has never been so dangerous. i will add that, perhaps for the first time in our history, the european union faces an existential threat. but these threats do not come from outside our borders. the only existential threat against the european union comes from our internal divisions, the petty nationalisms, the finger-pointing and the lack of forward-looking leadership. we discussed this early this afternoon when we discussed our response to terrorism inside the european union. i still believe we can make it, and we must make it – together with this parliament, which is the best ally in this fight – for the security and benefit of all our citizens.
