last comment that was made: the need maybe to have a mogherini plan or something similar. this would cover for the reconstruction of and support for the middle east but also africa, because we have seen the development of trust funds recently and because we need to mobilise resources on specific strategic targets we have as a european union. this strategy will not, i hope, entail extraordinary plans or measures but rather the pooling of the resources we already have, which are consistent. i hope that we manage to marshal these resources in a natural, coordinated and ordered way to serve our strategic priorities. we all know today what the priorities of tomorrow will be: the reconstruction of the middle east, a major investment in the future of africa. we can continue like this and the strategy will be exactly this. so if we manage to be serious on the definition of the strategy and on the implementation of the strategy, i think we will no longer need emergency measures.
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, let me start by saying that this debate is indeed important. central asia is a region that is increasingly recognised as strategically important. that is why i believe it is quite a shame that we have to have this late night debate with 11 members of parliament in the room while we discuss a highly strategic, important issue. central asia needs to feature high on our foreign policy agenda for a number of reasons. in the previous debate we talked about a more connected world. in a more connected world the most ancient global trade route can only become more relevant. central asia stands at the crossroads between europe, russia and asia. europe and central asia share many interests, from peace in afghanistan to the fight against foreign fighters. for this reason we are engaging directly with all countries in the region. as you know, last year i decided to nominate an eu special representative to central asia – peter burian – going back on a previous decision to remove this position. i personally began discussing the strategy review with central asian ministers of foreign affairs in astana last december. asia’s economic slowdown and the threat against our security are making it very clear, for both us and central asia, that we have a strong interest in reinforcing our cooperation. cooperation with the european union is not an alternative to cooperation with other global powers, namely russia and china. this is not about expanding our sphere of influence; we as europeans do not have that kind of mentality. your report rightly notes that on a number of issues, such as economic development and connectivity, that are key to the region and to us, some kind of cooperation between our european union, china and russia can only benefit both central asia and ourselves. there is space and desire inside the region, as you mentioned, for a more active and result-oriented cooperation between europe and each of the central asian states. we cannot consider central asia to be a non-differentiated bloc. the 2015 review of the strategy reflects some asian partners’ eagerness to distinguish themselves from their neighbours, including in their ambitions to take forward their relationship with europe. for example, the signature of the epca with kazakhstan and the first discussions on an announced format of a partnership with kyrgyzstan signalled these countries’ willingness to go beyond the strategy on an ad hoc basis. we need to seek the right combination of individual and regional approaches, because many of the challenges the countries of central asia face require common solutions. a regional approach is therefore required. water, trafficking and border management, the rising threat of radicalisation, and limited international trade are all issues which call for trans-border coordination. this has already been a specific focus of our regional approach. the areas of education, the rule of law and the environment have been given particular attention. we want to reinforce our common action on these issues and intensify interaction between experts through existing platforms and projects. an ambitious working programme has been set up, for example under the education platform, and we welcome here the commitment and close cooperation of several member states, such as poland and latvia. parliament’s report and the strategy review also underlined economic and commercial relations, and the wish to promote business and investment in the region. this would be possible with the necessary development of a reliable investment climate which calls for, on their side, more work in the fight against corruption, developing interconnections with the international business community and further regional integration. in this respect, like you, we are following with concern certain negative developments in central asia concerning human rights and basic freedoms. let me say, my dialogue with leaders and ministers of the region on all these issues was very frank and very open. it is in their own interest to look for another way. in this regard we want to make better use of existing platforms and dialogues to look for positive solutions. the special representative for central asia is preparing a joint trip to kyrgyzstan, tajikistan and uzbekistan in april with the commission’s directorate-general for international cooperation and development to discuss these issues and put forward positive steps. eu development cooperation can assist countries of the region in dealing with the challenges they are facing. among these we cannot forget the many threats to regional security and stability. regional security will be discussed again in the upcoming meetings of the central asian border security initiative in april in bishkek and of the high-level security dialogue in brussels in may. we are satisfied with the support provided by the rule of law initiative and the new face of border management and drug action programmes. many of these are shared threats for europe and central asia. we share an interest in the stabilisation of afghanistan and have asked regional leaders to actively contribute to the preparation of the conference on afghanistan which we will host in brussels in october. we all deal with the return of foreign terrorist fighters from theatres of conflict in the middle east and elsewhere, and we all know that our youth is exposed to radicalisation. links between europe and central asia date back centuries, but every single day we on both sides understand a bit better how much we need each other. i know you see this very well and i know we can count on your help in defining a new fruitful relationship with central asia.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection under rule 106 of the rules of procedure: renewal of the approval of the active substance glyphosate, given that the commission's proposal was based on the epsa studies which clearly and unequivocally stated that this substance had not been shown to be potentially harmful to human health. furthermore, there are sufficiently clear provisions governing the possibility and even the obligation to withdraw a substance from the market when it is found that it could become harmful to animal health. moreover, the withdrawal of that substance from the market and the control of weeds by mechanical means would cause climatic disturbances as a result of the release of gases from agricultural machinery into the air, which would greatly exacerbate the phenomenon known as the 'greenhouse effect'. however, i believe that research needs to continue in order to identify mechanisms and solutions that will allow effective weed control and at the same time guarantee human health.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is a herbicide that kills all vegetation, regardless of its nature, and is used in agriculture in 76% of cases. i voted to classify this herbicide as a risk factor and carcinogen, as it very often interacts with household use or food. i voted to give the burden of testing to the food and veterinary office to monitor glyphosate residues. the commission and efsa should also urgently present the evidence that led to the classification and authorisation of glyphosate, despite its carcinogenicity and therefore its major risk factor.
in writing. ‒ there are contradicting opinions regarding glyphosate, with a who international agency for research on cancer (iarc) classifying glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans after evaluating a large body of scientific evidence, and the european food safety authority (efsa) dismissing any danger while basing its decision on unpublished studies commissioned by the industry. moreover, there are serious doubts as regards a possible mode of action in relation to the endocrine disrupting properties of glyphosate, and in the absence of proper scientific horizontal criteria an endocrine-mediated mode of action cannot be ruled out. the objection opposes the draft measure on the grounds that the draft implementing act fails to ensure a high level of protection of both human and animal health and the environment, fails to apply the precautionary principle, is therefore not compatible with the aim and the content of the basic instrument, and exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1107/2009. i believe the commission should not renew the approval of glyphosate and should rapidly ensure an independent review of the classification of glyphosate based on all available scientific evidence relating to carcinogenicity of glyphosate as well as possible endocrine disruptive properties.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the objection regarding the renewal of the approval of the active substance glyphosate due to the serious doubts regarding its carcinogenic effect on humans. this issue appeared after evaluating a large body of scientific evidence by the who agency for research on cancer (iarc).
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is a herbicide used by farmers to kill weeds without killing their crops and in 2007 it was the most used herbicide in the united states agricultural sector. i have voted for this report that will enable an independent review of the classification of glyphosate based on all available scientific evidence relating to its carcinogenic nature.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it asks the european commission and the european food safety authority to make public all the information they have on the active substance glyphosate. the possibility that this substance, widely used in agriculture, forestry and gardening, is carcinogenic is a matter of concern. in this regard, i support the clarification and publication of this public interest information, the testing of the presence of this substance in food and the presentation of the results on the implications for human health.
in writing. ‒ the european food safety authority and an agency of the world health organisation have drawn contrasting conclusions about the possible harmful effects of glyphosate. this shows that further investigation is necessary before the substance is authorised for another 15 years. it is not unusual that scientific bodies disagree, but such a profound difference between agencies of this stature cannot be ignored by the commission. it is appropriate to conduct a thorough review of glyphosate and its classification, and also to consider whether eu level authorisation of the active substance and then separate, national authorisation for herbicide and pesticide products is really the best way to ensure the highest standards of health and safety.
in writing. ‒ i supported this objection because the evidence on the effects of glyphosate use is contradictory. we have, on the one hand, studies proving that this substance is carcinogenic and, on the other hand, the efsa decision that removes any negative charge regarding the mode of action of glyphosate. we need scientific evidence, independent studies to classify this substance and to clarify the impact of its use on human health. in view of this uncertain situation and pending a conclusive analysis, the commission should renew the authorisation of glyphosate for a limited period of 7 years instead of 15 years as originally provided for.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is an active substance widely used in herbicides. the approval of the active substance glyphosate in the eu expires on 30 june 2016. the draft measure subject to this objection renews the approval of the active substance glyphosate for the maximum permissible period of 15 years. the who international agency for research on cancer (iarc) classifies glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans after evaluating a large body of scientific evidence. moreover, there are serious doubts as regards possible mode of action in relation to the endocrine disrupting properties of glyphosate. the objection also fails to ensure a high level of protection of both human and animal health and the environment, fails to apply the precautionary principle, and is therefore not compatible with the aim and the content of the basic instrument. based on this, i do not support the renewal of the approval of glyphosate. i believe the commission should rapidly ensure an independent review of the classification of glyphosate based on all available scientific evidence relating to carcinogenicity of glyphosate as well as possible endocrine disruptive properties.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is one of the best-selling herbicide pesticides worldwide. this substance has been on the market since 1974 and currently accounts for 25% of the world pesticide market. in 2014, 825 million tons of glyphosate were used globally, 90% of it in agriculture. it is also used to control the growth of uncultivated herbaceous plants in gardens or in uncultivated areas. in a study by the international agency for research on cancer (iarc), it classified glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans, despite other assessments by supranational institutes and national regulatory agencies concluding that glyphosate is not carcinogenic. moreover, it is not yet known what was the basis of the iarc assessment, as the iarc monograph has not been published. the european parliament's motion for a resolution refers in particular to the precautionary principle and the need to ensure a high level of protection of health and the environment. it also proposes to extend the authorisation for a maximum of seven years, the time needed to carry out the studies. i therefore voted in favour of the objection on the renewal of the approval.
i voted for this report in the end. some of the points that concern the defence capabilities of individual eu member states are very correct, such as the fact that our key partner for the future must be the united states of america, and that nato is the key organisation for european security. i think it is important to note that we are calling on the individual member states to increase their defence spending to 2% of their gdp. i think that is very correct, it is not possible for us here in europe to feel that defence is not our concern and that we can use money in the national budgets for various blasphemous things, not for our own defence capability. on the other hand, i have some doubts about the common defence union. i would not agree with a model that would be in competition with nato, i think it is better to cooperate with nato than to create some parallel defense structure of our own.
mr president, in 2013 the european council gave concrete tasks to the european commission on: 1. a global security procurement regime; 2. the control of defence industrial capacity; and 3. the monitoring of security and defence procurement. but the commission has not fulfilled its tasks in time and this has cost us and is costing us lives today. the european army must become a reality as soon as possible. it is vital to strengthen the partnership between the european union and nato and to address the safety and security gap in the wider european union neighbourhood. if there is a time and a place and a moment for solidarity, it is today, here and now, to stand together and to be able to stand together to defend the lives, the freedom and the security of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ there are a number of challenges today that threaten the stability of the union, which is why a strong political will is needed on the part of both the union and the member states to respond effectively to these challenges and to maintain the values promoted by the union. collective responsibility and solidarity must be reflected in the union's policies, in particular in the common foreign and security policy. threats to member states must be seen as threats to the union as a whole, and solidarity and unity are needed. clear identification and hierarchy of concrete threats is required to formulate appropriate responses and institute coherent measures in line with the resources required. in the light of recent terrorist attacks, there is a need to develop strong security policies to ensure the safety of citizens. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a comprehensive common approach based on solidarity is needed in response to the challenges that threaten internal and external security, and that synergies between external action, human rights and security are needed.
in writing. ‒ in a constant process of globalisation, the eu is becoming increasingly complex, trying to cope with current challenges and risks. in this context, the effects of the crisis that have disrupted the entire global financial and economic system continue to be an important source of vulnerabilities and, by implication, insecurity at national, regional and global levels. the economy is the fuel without which national power, whether political, social or military, cannot function at normal parameters. i support the identification of new ways to achieve better results, such as the principle that member states should spend at least 2% of gdp on defence spending by 2024, to implement the union's foreign and security policy objectives. energy security can also play a fundamental role in the development of the union, complementing the european objectives of re-industrialisation and economic growth. i conclude that we must work together today for the european union of tomorrow. we need a new strategy, one that is ready to respond to crisis situations and with the ability to recover immediately after attacks. we must realise that the eu has the capacity to spread european values, which are meant to restore unity, peace and prosperity.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that the report recognises the united states as key strategic partner of the eu, stresses the need for the eu and its member states to take greater responsibility for their collective security and to be more active in europe’s own neighbourhood, making full use of the lisbon treaty provisions on csdp. i strongly believe we need to promote the strategic autonomy of the eu and its capacity to act in synergy but also autonomously from nato. i advocate an eu that is a real international actor capable of shaping the developments and dealing with a rapidly changing global environment and mounting security challenges. i urge, therefore, the eu member states to work in synergy, develop their defence capabilities and pool and share them more effectively. the eu needs to be more active in its neighbourhood and be capable of preventing and managing crises and conflicts that represent challenges for the security of eu citizens too.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the eu is an important international actor which has the capacity to deal with a changing global environment and numerous challenges to our security. the eu should be more active in its neighbourhood. we have to be capable of preventing and managing crises and conflicts that also represent challenges for the eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ to defend the european union’s people, and its states, societies and values is one of the top priorities of the eu. i have voted for this report that should improve the eu’s strategy by identifying and prioritising threats and challenges, defining a response to the situation and determining the necessary resources for implementation.
in writing. ‒ given the ever increasing volatile regional security environment i support this timely resolution, as it emphasises the urgency of setting out a shared eu global strategy. as the resolution stresses, no member state can alone respond to the many security challenges we face today at home and abroad. thus, a shared eu global strategy with a clear analysis of a wider set of threats to european society and in turn formulated responses to such threats should be a priority to identify. for the eu to become an influential global actor a unified voice is required. speaking from a common foreign and security policy platform is therefore necessary for the eu to globally retain political credibility, allowing it to be an instrument of diplomacy by spreading the values of democracy, good governance, peace, stability, the rule of law and the protection of human rights outside eu borders.
in writing. ‒ this report draws attention to security challenges for the eu and advocates a more strategic role for the european union as an international actor. this document stresses the need for the eu and its member states to take greater responsibility in what concerns their collective security and be more active in europe’s own neighbourhood, making full use and respect of the lisbon treaty provisions. at the same time, it calls on the european union to make use of diplomatic, economic and all other tools that it has at its disposal to promote security, stability and prosperity. we want an eu that is a real international actor able to shape the developments and deal with a rapidly changing global environment and mounting security challenges. so this report urges the eu member states to work in synergy, develop their defence capabilities and to pool and share them more effectively. the eu needs to be more active and be capable of preventing and managing crises and conflicts that represent challenges also for the eu citizen’s security. the truth is that the eu can and must do better. for this reason, i support the report.
in writing. ‒ in the current geopolitical context, the european union faces challenges and threats from state and non-state actors, internal and external. member states and the european union must show firmness and leadership in order to respond collectively and as effectively as possible to guarantee the safety, values and societal model that the eu promotes. i believe that priority should be given to stabilising the eu's immediate neighbourhood, taking into account the threats identified in the 2003 european security strategy on terrorism, weapons of mass destruction, regional conflicts, failed states and organised crime, which unfortunately remain largely topical. the vote in favour of the report on the eu in a changing global environment underlines that human security, the defence of peoples, societies and values must be at the heart of the european union's strategy. enhanced cooperation for defence research must be pursued while respecting human rights and democratisation.

in writing. ‒ the zika virus has become a real threat to citizens, spreading at an alarming rate. there are currently no treatments or vaccines to combat the effects of this virus, so prevention and personal protection measures are very important. at union level, specific measures are required for regions where zika virus has already spread, in order to eradicate all possible transmission methods in those regions. furthermore, support is needed for people already infected. an immediate action plan is also needed to help both member states and third countries to combat this epidemic in the worst affected areas. i welcome the commission's decision to allocate eur 10 million to research into the zika virus and efforts to find effective solutions against this virus. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that a joint effort by the member states and the union is needed to eradicate this virus and ensure a high level of protection of human health.
in writing. ‒ i support the motion for a resolution on the zika virus epidemic, tabled following the debate in last month's plenary, which aims to bring some lines of action in tackling this epidemic at both european and global level through eu support to the most affected regions. as we stated in our written statement last month, our goals are clear: prevent and treat the epidemic. to do that, we need to focus our efforts on finding a vaccine against zika. however, research should also be encouraged through horizon 2020 and beyond. the commission must then commit itself to ensuring that, following the results of the research, patients receive treatment at affordable prices. the european centre for disease prevention and control also has a key role in this process through its continuous monitoring and to which we recommend in this resolution to regularly assess the risks of the epidemic and update the epidemiological reports. as regards prevention, i would stress that both the commission and the member states must act to monitor invasive mosquito species and to eliminate their breeding grounds.

in writing. ‒ considering the fact that experts agreed that a causal relationship between zika infection during pregnancy and microcephaly is strongly suspected, although this has not yet been scientifically proven and therefore all possible causes of microcephaly should be investigated, i support the call on the commission to explain what is the current state of this outbreak of the disease and the incidence of microcephaly in the eu. i strongly believe citizens should be aware of the degree of risk of transmission of the zika virus infection in the eu. moreover, the commission should inform us if they have already considered advising eu health authorities to collaborate with the transport sector to ensure disinfection of cargo, cargo carriers and cabin and passenger compartments of planes arriving from affected areas.

in writing. ‒ an evolving outbreak of zika virus infections is currently spreading in the americas and the pacific region. i have voted for this motion for a resolution that stresses the need for a treatment or vaccine for the zika virus according to the ecdc. the european centre for disease prevention and control was established in 2005 and is the eu agency that strengthens europe’s defences against infectious diseases.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i find the information on the links between zika virus infections and microcephaly cases worrying and alarming. the lack of clear information on the effects of this virus on infants, as well as the lack of certainty on the transmission mechanisms of this virus, requires greater involvement of the eu and the international community in the investigation of these cases. in this respect, the eu's €10 million for zika research, while not a large enough sum in comparison to its implications for human health, is a first step towards finding a vaccine or a way to fight the virus.
in writing. ‒ the link between the zika virus and birth defects has now been confirmed by the us centre for disease control and prevention. zika is already a global public health emergency and there is a greatly increased risk of transmission in the eu in the coming summer months. i welcome the regular meetings of the health security committee, the activation of the eu’s early warning and response system, and the mobilisation of eu funds to support urgent research. recent reports of progress towards a vaccine are encouraging, but it is clear that multiple measures will be needed to deal with this emergency, including preventative actions and proper access to existing health services.
in writing. ‒ on 1 february 2016, the world health organisation declared the zika virus outbreak a public health emergency of international concern and it is considered a serious cross-border threat to health, having been reported in 39 countries or territories worldwide, including two european regions. the appearance of the virus has been associated with clusters of microcephaly cases and other neurological disorders, including cases of guillain-barré syndrome, and who declared that a causal relationship between zika infection during pregnancy and microcephaly is strongly suspected. although no cases of autochthonous zika virus transmission have been reported on the european continent, there is a risk of establishment of local vector-borne transmission in europe during the 2016 summer season and there is no specific treatment or vaccine currently available. i agree that there is an urgent need to raise awareness of the effects of the virus, to adopt measures in order to eradicate all vectors of transmission and to assist regions that have already been affected by the zika virus. furthermore, we need to avoid transmission of the virus on the european continent and to increase our research funding in order to find solutions to eradicate this health-threatening virus. due to all these factors, i support the proposed resolution.

in writing. ‒ recent events in poland, such as the paralysis of the constitutional tribunal and the fact that the tribunal’s verdict of 9 march 2016 remains unpublished and therefore cannot enter into force, undermines democracy, human rights and the rule of law. although the constitutional tribunal was established as one of the central elements ensuring checks and balances in constitutional democracy and the rule of law in poland, the venice commission clearly stated that, in the current situation, the constitutional tribunal cannot fulfil its role as guarantor of the supremacy of the constitution of poland. furthermore, aside from the constitutional issues, there are other issues of serious concern in poland, such as media freedom. the european parliament resolution urges the polish government to respect, publish and fully implement without further delay the constitutional tribunal’s judgment of 9 march 2016 and to implement the judgments of 3 and 9 december 2015, calls on the polish government to fully implement the recommendations of the venice commission and urges future solutions to strengthen democracy, human rights and the rule of law. i support parliament’s resolution.
in writing. the directive on the use of passenger name records (pnr) in the eu for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious transnational crime requires airlines to provide law enforcement authorities with passenger data for flights to and from third countries. it's a big legislative step forward that has been waiting for more than 5 years to be adopted because of the lack of consensus on how to process personal data. i think the pnr is a good legislative tool, but it is not enough. security measures on the ground, prior to the transfer of pnr data to the competent authorities, is paramount. the exchange of such data between member states, as well as between member states and europol, should take place through an eu secure system managed by europol. unfortunately, europol's responsibility is limited and europol's involvement is voluntary, not mandatory in this directive. a single point of contact would also be needed to be responsible for the storage, management and access to pnr data and for the recording and transmission of requests for information exchange. the existence of this counter, as proposed by this directive, is again optional.
we are dealing with well-funded, well-organized international terrorist groups determined to do harm to the extreme. let's not wait until we're hit again. europe needs more than ever to be united and to use any means against jihadist terror. that does not mean violating human rights, but on the contrary, preserving them against those who would destroy them. the directive on the transmission of passenger data by airlines requires airlines to transmit the name, ticket number or payment method of passengers entering or leaving the european union. and that includes european citizens. that's because it's urgently necessary that we identify the european citizens who are going to fight alongside the jihadists. no one is saying that this law is a silver bullet that will succeed on its own in ending terrorism in europe, but together with other measures, we must succeed. answer to a question asked under the 'blue card' procedure. of course, member states are not equal in the way they protect the eu's borders, nor in the level of crime, including, as you said, the possible sale of citizens. and these are all goals that we have to defeat and fight for, to make disappear from our reality. because all of them, together with the others, planned and prepared by the terrorists, lead us to what happened, to the loss of human life.
madam president, i would like to congratulate everyone who has worked on this report, but at the same time i cannot help but regret the unacceptable delay in its discussion. recent events in brussels and paris, but not only, have shown that the peace and security of the european citizen is more fragile than ever before in the face of terrorism and cross-border crime, which have become increasingly aggressive and sophisticated. the attacks have brought us face to face with a reality we've refused to see for too long. the enemy is inside the city, and unfortunately, we lack the tools to prevent tragedies like london, madrid, paris or brussels. the use of passenger name record data will allow not only reactive but also preventive intervention, which will increase the capacity of nation states to disrupt terrorist networks and prevent serious or organised crime. however, i would draw the attention of all those responsible to the fact that the adoption of this directive is only a small step in the fight against terrorism and in strengthening the process of ensuring the security of citizens. beyond the efforts made at european union level, the national states that have to implement this legislation are responsible for its effectiveness.
madam president, even if we concede that the european passenger name record would not have prevented the deadly brussels attack last month, there are strong arguments that showed that it could be one of the most effective instruments in our european security toolbox for averting the next attack in the future. the experience of the countries that use pnr data in the fight against drug and human trafficking and terrorism long ago demonstrated the advantages of proactive and real-time use of this instrument. this makes it all the more difficult to understand why this house has taken so long to vote on this directive. although praising the way in which usefulness, proportionality and data protection concerns are reflected in the final text, i can only regret that the directive we vote on tomorrow does not include intra-eu flights, given the increased level of efficiency and security such a comprehensive approach would have had.
in writing. in the current volatile european security environment, the report on the use of passenger name record (pnr) data is absolutely necessary, as its central objective is to establish a mechanism to improve the security of eu citizens and member states. the report, which is a significant step forward in the fight against terrorism in europe, establishes a legal framework for the protection and exchange of passenger name record data between member states and the services responsible. such data may only be used for the prevention and detection of terrorist offences and certain types of serious transnational crime and for the investigation and prosecution of such offences. this list of crimes includes: terrorism, human trafficking, sexual exploitation of children, trafficking in drugs, weapons, ammunition and explosives, money laundering and cybercrime. to this end, the report provides for the transfer by air carriers and non-air carrier economic operators (such as travel agencies and organisations) of data from passenger files on international flights to or from member states, and the exchange of such data between those member states and member states and europol.

madam president, the protection of know-how and confidential commercial information against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure is a priority for us in the european parliament. uniform legislation at european level allows us to protect our competitive advantage and maintain our innovation performance. in this respect, particular attention has been paid to small and medium-sized enterprises, which face the greatest difficulty in protecting their intellectual property. small entrepreneurs and innovators, for example in romania, especially in the digital sector, have often been subject to theft of confidential information, which has affected their potential and hard work. the same happened to companies in the 1990s, which lost their competitiveness due to a lack of protection against theft and illegal disclosure of confidential information. that is why i believe that the report is a balanced formula for protecting them at european level, without, however, hindering the dissemination of knowledge or the mobility of the workforce.
madam president, the report on the estimate of the revenue and expenditure budget of the european parliament for the financial year 2017 reflects a balanced approach to the funds needed for the functioning of the european legislator. important measures are proposed to increase the efficiency of parliament, but also to increase transparency. the publication of the detailed budget on parliament's website is thus a sign of our desire to enable all citizens to better understand our activities and priorities. a strong democracy requires a strong parliament, with increased activity, that communicates with citizens wherever they are. the european parliament must be known not only in brussels or strasbourg but also in the remotest localities. i must therefore reject any wish by some to maintain or impose new differences between the member states and their meps. i therefore reject the limitations imposed on eastern european staff, which are imposed on the simple grounds that if the area is less developed, employees from those countries must be paid less.

in writing. ‒ the data protection package provides individuals with information on how their personal data is processed, it requires consent before personal data is used, it makes it easier for people to transfer their personal data between service providers and it provides individuals with the right to know when their personal data has been hacked. furthermore, it is beneficial to businesses, as it sets a single set of rules across europe, with one supervisory authority. this directive is in the interest of the consumer, who is granted a higher amount of control over his/her personal data. greater consumer transparency and choice leads to more trustful, consumer-friendly and secure products and services. having considered the benefits of the new rules, i support the data protection package.
in writing. ‒ there is a growing need for law enforcement authorities in member states to process and exchange at rapidly increasing rates for the purposes of preventing and combating transnational crime and terrorism. in this context, clear and consistent rules on data protection at eu level will help fostering co-operation between such authorities. in addition, there are practical challenges to enforcing data protection legislation and a need for cooperation between member states and their authorities, which need to be organised at eu level to ensure unity of application of european union law. in certain situations, the eu is best placed to ensure effectively and consistently the same level of protection for individuals when their personal data are transferred to third countries. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the police directive will improve cooperation and efficiency between police forces of all member states and will make for smoother exchange of information between member states’ police and judicial authorities, which is crucial in the current security context. the directive is about ensuring the correct and lawful treatment of personal data in the law enforcement context, while respecting the fundamental right of privacy for citizens. as we do not have a common european union framework on data protection or data processing for the police, i strongly support this directive.
in writing. ‒ security and protection of life is a decision-making factor in the suppression of terrorist offences and serious transnational crime. the processing of personal data shall be necessary and applicable at operational level. i voted for the collection of such data by air carriers and the transfer of this data to a single designated unit. the introduction of an eu-wide pnr system is necessitated by the current situation of acts of terrorism and violence and can lead to the ensuring of international security.
in writing. ‒ i expressed my support for the pnr (passenger name record) directive and the data protection package. it is clear that we do not have enough information on terror suspects and the little we do have is not being used or shared effectively by national law enforcement agencies. the data protection package and pnr will establish a clear legal framework for how personal data can be used and shared. this will make it significantly easier for national law enforcement agencies to share information quickly and effectively. these measures are fundamental for the fight against terrorism. the pnr directive can be a useful tool in the fight against terror if the data collected is used and shared effectively by law enforcement agencies. i expect national governments to make use of existing eu measures to fight terrorism.
in writing. ‒ i believe that passenger name record data is crucial in order for law enforcement agencies to deal with the current terrorist challenges in europe. securing air transport is important in combating so-called ‘foreign fighters’ and disrupting terrorist networks.
in writing. ‒ i support the commission’s proposal on the use of passenger name record data (eu pnr). this complementing tool will enable law enforcement authorities to solve possible security gaps in a well-organised and competent manner. moreover, it provides a harmonised legal base to fight against cross-border organised crime and terrorist offences. on the basis of solidarity and data protection clarification, the eu pnr was aligned with the data protection package in the agenda and received a majority vote in parliament.
in writing. ‒ passenger name records (pnr) consist of the information provided by passengers to air carriers during reservation and check-in procedures. travel agencies and tour operators using charter flights will also collect and process pnr data from their passengers. i voted for this report that would oblige airline carriers to hand over their passengers’ data to eu countries in order to help the authorities to fight terrorism and serious crime.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting in favour of this report because i was not satisfied with the final form of the text. while i agree with the principle of the use of passenger name record data by authorities whose task is to prevent, detect and prosecute persons suspected of terrorism and serious crime, the fact that the amendment requiring member states to exchange such data was rejected leaves this directive without its most important component. if the authorities of the member states do not have this obligation, recent cases will be repeated where terrorists were targeted by other member states but the information was not made available to the other states precisely because there was no legal obligation to do so. in these circumstances, we risk having a directive on the processing and use of certain personal data, with a purpose that is not very clear, and with a very obvious risk of continuing to have terrorist propagation networks among us.
in writing. ‒ this directive states that airlines must submit passenger name record (pnr) data in the form of passenger names, ticket numbers or payment methods for passengers leaving and entering the european union, including european citizens. pnr data can help law enforcement authorities prevent, detect, investigate and prosecute serious transnational crime, by comparing them with various databases of persons and objects sought, to find the necessary evidence of criminal networks. this directive will help combat human trafficking and child trafficking, drug trafficking, paedophiles and murderers. furthermore, it will represent an important tool in combating and preventing terrorism, as it will put in place a coherent and harmonised framework for pnr exchange between member states. in light of the recent brussels and paris attacks, i believe that such information is crucial in order to protect the security of european citizens. in conclusion, i supported this directive.
in writing. ‒ in today's knowledge-based economy, the ability of businesses to innovate and compete can be seriously affected when confidential information is either stolen or misused. the protection of trade secrets is therefore of particular importance for smaller eu companies, whose bases are less solid than those of a large company. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (oj l 347, 20.12.2011, p. this fragmentation only hinders economic prosperity and the development of the eu's single market. last but not least, the improvements that the european parliament has managed to make to the original text provide a solid and at the same time balanced framework. support for european protection, know-how, but not at the expense of transparency, the dissemination of information and the exercise of fundamental freedoms are important elements that are reflected in the final text, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure of trade secrets is a risk factor as it leads to the commission of crimes such as theft, bribery, fraud. the manufacture or placing on the market of goods infringing proprietary rights is also an unlawful use of trade secrets. i voted to protect this data, to evaluate it on the basis of its accuracy and applicability. the acquisition or use of a trade secret by a third party may have a negative impact on the legitimate holder and such a measure is in support of the avoidance of moral and financial harm.
in writing. ‒ i strongly believe the trade secrets directive will be fundamental in order to offer protection to european businesses faced with economic espionage, both at eu and international level. currently, there are no europe-wide provisions and the legislation in member states varies from none to high protection of trade secrets. i welcome the fact that the directive proposes an unprecedented text on the protection of whistle-blowers, which could become a positive precedent. moreover, it excludes media freedom and freedom of expression in a very clear way from the application of the directive. finally, i welcome the fact that it secures strong guarantees on workers’ mobility, and workers’ right to information and representation, as well as safeguards for disclosure to public authorities.
in writing. ‒ the protection of trade secrets against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure has been a concern of mine both when i worked in the private sector and when i was minister for smes in my country. i have made several amendments to this report and voted for it because, by adopting it, it protects labour and intellectual property, defines and clarifies what constitutes a trade secret and protects the exchange of knowledge between businesses, especially smes, research institutions, both in the internal market and outside it. the report clarifies how to award damages in case of disclosure of trade secrets by anyone who is not legally empowered and at the same time does not impede the mobility of workers. i wanted to stress the need to define in each company what trade secrets are so that workers are aware of them and to provide in individual employment contracts a confidentiality clause for all workers who have access to trade secrets through the exercise of their functions or duties.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i believe that it is paramount to protect european businesses that must deal with economic espionage. also, it is important to note that the directive is compatible with the agreement on trade-related aspects of intellectual property rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the directive on the protection of undisclosed trade secrets because we need to ease as much as we can the burdens faced by our key industrial sectors. we have very innovative and competitive companies that should be channelling their efforts into designing and developing new products rather than wasting resources in fighting against unfair commercial practices coming from third countries.
in writing. ‒ protection against unlawful acquisition, disclosure and use of trade secrets is key to allowing a fair commercial environment for businesses. i voted for this report that should clarify the definition of what should be considered as trade secrets.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i believe that the protection of trade secrets against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure is beneficial to the proper functioning of the internal market and to ensuring economic growth. in this respect, today's report sets out the directives that member states must comply with in order to improve the protection of trade secrets. i welcome the rapporteur's proposal that future measures to be taken by the member states should ensure a fair balance between the protection of trade secrets and the freedom to conduct a business, between freedom of expression and freedom of information, with a focus on fundamental citizens' rights (public security, consumer protection, public health or environmental protection). i also welcome this directive as the legislative text aims to avoid affecting the freedom of movement of workers and the freedom of establishment, two fundamental european rights.
in writing. ‒ the trade secret debate highlights the need for, but also the fragility of, a balance between measures to maintain european competitiveness and the protection of fundamental rights. we cannot talk about economic performance without freedom of the press and without protecting those who report wrongdoing. that said, i am pleased to see that the political groups have succeeded in summarising these needs in a text that lays the foundations for a clear and fair european system. article 1 on scope and article 5 on exceptions are a step forward for business actors and a win for european citizens. although we do not yet have regulations at european level and the legislation in the member states varies greatly, the current text of the directive sets a positive precedent in trade secret law.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union must continue, in the current political context, to support its external partners with whom it shares the same priorities: ensuring peace, democracy, security and prosperity. in this respect, today's report presents the state of relations, the progress and setbacks of turkey's efforts to join the european union. it is right that turkey's economic development, good cooperation and commitment to the fight against terrorism, but also to the hosting of migrants, with turkey being the country with the largest number of refugees, are highlighted.

in writing. ‒ it is very important to understand the importance of eu relations with turkey and to implement more measures which will lead to concrete progress. this report urges turkey to act against intimidation of journalists and condemn the violent takeover of several newspapers. the european union strongly supports the freedom of speech, expression and opinion, both online and offline. to match the eu’s commitment to the rule of law and fundamental freedoms, which are core european values, reforms of the judiciary, freedom and security are urgently needed in turkey. regarding eu-turkey cooperation on migration, i think this should be uncoupled from the eu accession negotiating process. the active and credible negotiations provide a suitable framework for exploiting the full potential of international relations. turkey remains a key partner for the eu, but needs strong progress on rule of law and fundamental values. for this reason i support this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the 2015 report on albania, as i appreciate that important progress has been made in albania's path towards accession to the european union. since june 2014, it has been granted eu candidate status in order to encourage the progress made by this balkan state in the fight against corruption and organised crime. unfortunately, without democratic structures, without the rule of law, without the independence of the media and the judiciary, but also without a consistent fight against corruption, eu accession cannot take place. thus, a greater intensification of reform efforts in these key areas is needed in order to open accession negotiations and strengthen its democratic transition.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the steady progress in meeting the key priorities for opening accession negotiations and i support the call on all political parties to work constructively together for the implementation of the reforms. further efforts are needed, in particular in the field of judicial reform. the success of the reform process depends on the existence of a democratic political environment. to secure the sustainability of the integration process all political parties need to cooperate and work constructively together. i support the call on the commission to monitor closely the progress and to report to parliament and the council as soon as albania has sufficiently advanced with the judicial reform, with a view to opening accession negotiations. i believe that the opening of accession negotiations, as soon as possible, will provide a tangible incentive for the positive transformation of the country.
in writing. ‒ albania has made significant progress with regard to its european integration process. however, the country still has important reforms to make in the judicial field. i look forward to albania’s on-going progress with a view to opening eu accession negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report on albania that monitors the steady progress made by albania with respect to the key priority reforms required for opening accession negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i endorse this resolution as it remains crucial to stability and prosperity in europe that the eu continues to support the western balkans and albania’s democratic transition towards eu membership by holding candidate and potential candidate countries to account for their reform progress or lack thereof. this resolution sets out those specific areas in which albania still has a lot of work to do in order to meet the requirements of the eu enlargement policy. the lack of independence of the judiciary from political branches, high unemployment rates, a flawed child protection system, excessive corruption particularly in education, healthcare and the judiciary, and socio-economic discrimination against roma and egyptian minorities, are particularly concerning in this regard. however, the resolution also stresses positive developments as evident in the strategy and law on decentralisation of governance to local governments, the spread and consolidation of religious tolerance and the willingness of the parliament to cooperate with civil society organisations.
in writing. ‒ considering albania’s achievements in its european integration process, we should positively encourage its steady progress in 2015 in meeting the key priorities for opening accession negotiations. i think the european parliament should call on all political parties to work constructively together for the implementation of the reforms. this resolution urges the albanian government to keep up the reform efforts and supports the country’s european perspective. the rapporteur believes that the opening of accession negotiations will provide an incentive for the positive transformation of the country. further efforts are needed, in particular, in the field of judicial reform. also, the commission needs to monitor progress closely and to report to parliament and the council as soon as albania has sufficiently advanced with the necessary reforms, with a view to opening accession negotiations. i fully support this approach.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the 2015 report on bosnia and herzegovina, taking into account both the progress made by this country and the steps it needs to take to become an eu member state. the european union has initiated a renewed approach to bosnia and herzegovina, in order to make progress towards eu accession, but also to address socioeconomic and rule of law issues. to this end, the european commission will allocate €1.5 billion over the next three years to support reforms in bosnia and herzegovina and infrastructure development. unfortunately, however, this country faces challenges in terms of human rights and the protection of minorities. the legal and institutional framework for human rights monitoring requires substantial improvements and appropriate legislation to be effectively implemented.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the presentation of an eu membership application by bosnia and herzegovina. after a long period of stalemate, there is some positive progress and i therefore encourage the country and its political leadership to intensify the reform efforts with a view to making the state more efficiently functional on its way towards the eu. the eu has to be unequivocally committed to the european perspective of bosnia and herzegovina, stressing the need for the country to implement the stabilisation and association agreement to make the eu membership application a success. the eu membership application of bosnia and herzegovina presents a unique opportunity for the country to unify around a common goal. the political leaders of the country need to work together constructively to respond to and fulfil the european aspirations of all bosnia and herzegovina citizens.

in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report on bosnia and herzegovina that reiterates the need for the authorities to show determination in pursuing institutional and socio-economic reforms with their effective implementation, thus taking steady steps towards an eu integration.
in writing. ‒ the membership application submitted by bosnia and herzegovina in february this year shows that the country is taking important steps towards gaining eu membership. however, for bosnia and herzegovina to integrate into the european community as a democratic and functional state, further constitutional, political and legal reform is much needed. the resolution stresses, amongst other things, that corruption, growing radicalisation amongst youth and the decreasing space of independent media are of particular concern. it further highlights that there are still structural problems causing societal division and preventing integration, the ‘two schools under one roof’ being an example hereof. therefore, it is as important as ever that the eu continues to encourage reform in bosnia and herzegovina, which is essential for fostering societal and political stability in the western balkans region. it is for these reasons that i support this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this resolution notes some positive progress and encourages bosnia and herzegovina and its political leadership to intensify the reform efforts with a view to making the state more efficiently functional on its way towards the eu. the european parliament welcomes the presentation of an eu membership application by bosnia and herzegovina, which presents a unique opportunity for the country to unify around a common goal. this is the beginning of an important process that will require commitment and enhanced reform efforts. the political leaders of the country need to work together constructively to respond to and fulfil the eu aspirations of all bosnia and herzegovina citizens. the eu strategy, and especially this resolution, presents a unique opportunity for the politicians and all citizens of the country to leave aside the divisions along national lines and work together for a common future within the eu. i support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the recent economic stagnation and decline in the competitiveness of national economies has meant a sharp decline in consumption and a visible increase in spending, which has implicitly led to an increase in the level of poverty. although the global economy is in the process of recovering from the financial crisis, the imf's economic growth forecasts for 2016 remain cautious, with an annual rate of only 3,4%. the global economy has been experiencing very low growth for a long time and international trade is facing numerous obstacles due to delays in finalising international trade agreements. the fight against poverty at eu level needs to have the strong support of all member states so that by implementing coordinated measures a minimum income above the poverty line can be established to counteract the negative effects in the long term. i believe that we must give high priority to the circumstantial problems that lead to the increase in poverty and, by implication, social exclusion. i voted in favour of this resolution because i am convinced that by taking firm and immediate action we can make a concrete contribution to combating poverty.
in writing. ‒ today, poverty is the unfortunate reality in which millions of children in european societies live, thus damaging their future chances. the economic and financial crisis that started in 2008 has affected children and families across europe, with impacts on employment and social assistance systems. increasing expenditure on housing, food, utilities, transport, healthcare or education-related expenditure further complicates the situation of families, which, due to the decline in living standards, find it increasingly difficult to cope. achieving the eu poverty reduction target will require a cumulation of all efforts and instruments at both eu and national level. in line with the europe 2020 strategy, member states and the union have committed to reduce the level of poverty and social exclusion by at least 20 million people over the next decade. in this respect, i believe that identifying poverty indicators can help to develop complementary national targets on social exclusion for all 28 member states. a high quality of life for the population should be the aim of social development efforts and should be the measure of social progress.
in writing. ‒ since the start of the crisis, inequality in the eu has worsened, with one in six european citizens at risk of poverty. we voted to modernise legislation and develop new measures so that the poverty reduction target set in the eu 2020 strategy is met.
in writing. ‒ combating poverty is one of the five measurable objectives proposed for eu 2020, encouraging the adoption of national policies to protect women, in particular, from the risk of poverty. in this context, i consider it important to reform macroeconomic, social and labour market policies in line with gender equality policies, as the objectives of fighting poverty cannot be achieved without fighting women's poverty.
in writing. ‒ poverty levels in the union are unacceptably high. clearly, the increase in poverty is directly linked to the financial crisis and the subsequent austerity policies. i believe the commission and the member states must make more efforts to reach the anti-poverty targets, and that a minimum income scheme above the 60% national median income in all member states, a european energy observatory and a winter heating disconnection moratorium are essential tools in this respect. moreover, i believe financially vulnerable households need better protection against energy poverty and more support to improve their energy efficiency. i therefore support the call for a winter heating disconnection moratorium, to prevent energy cuts during winter months in case of financially vulnerable households, the call for an eu summit dedicated to the reduction of poverty and the support for a stronger role for consumers and for stronger consumer protection.
in writing. ‒ it is absolutely unacceptable for poverty to increase in the union. the commission and the member states must make greater efforts in order to meet anti-poverty targets. minimum income schemes and a winter heating disconnection moratorium are first steps. disadvantaged households need better protection against energy poverty.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that aims to build bridges between energy policy and social policy in a european debate by stressing that the eu is getting further from the eu 2020 anti-poverty target. amongst the main pillars to fight against poverty is the effective reduction of household costs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the problem of poverty in the context of increasing household current expenditure is extremely topical and more common, with more than 120 million european citizens, according to official statistics, at the threshold of poverty and social exclusion. the report adopted today thus proposes a series of measures that member states can use to achieve the europe 2020 target of reducing the number of people living in poverty by at least 20%. it is important that the european executive works with the member states to adopt and promote an integrated strategy to combat poverty. it is largely about passing economic, social, employment and education laws for the purpose of economic development and, by implication, poverty reduction.
in writing. ‒ the financial crisis that has hit the european union in recent years and the austerity policy pursued by a number of member states have led to an increase in the share of the population affected by poverty at union level, from 117 million people in 2008 to 122 million in 2013. this is reflected in the high share of expenditure on food, housing and utilities. regarding household current expenditure, around 10% of the eu population cannot pay their utility bills, 12% do not have adequate heating and 16% live in unsanitary spaces. against this background, the european institutions have developed thermal rehabilitation projects for housing, which are an important step forward. however, more action is needed in this regard, such as the adoption of a european moratorium on the unpaid winter debts, the establishment of a european minimum income guarantee of 60% of the average eu salary, the organisation of a european summit on combating poverty, and more effective protection of consumer interests. i consider this to be a very important document and therefore support its adoption as a first step towards a more elaborate european strategy against poverty.
in writing. ‒ between 2008 and 2013, the number of people at risk of poverty in the eu rose from 117 million to 122.6 million. this is contrary to the eu's strategic objective set out in the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to reduce by 20 million the number of people affected or threatened by poverty and social exclusion by 2020. in this perspective, this report establishes a link between energy poverty and general poverty and highlights that this is the result of a number of underlying conditions, including high energy prices, health and disability issues, the type of heating system used in homes and the quality and energy performance of the housing stock. the report proposes as a solution the provision of microcredit or low-interest loans, for example through the european investment bank, to low-income households to support their investments in renewable energy and energy efficiency. another proposed aspect is to increase investment in energy efficiency in social housing through european funds and to guarantee access to adequate housing for all, especially the most disadvantaged. i therefore voted in favour of the report on combating poverty in the context of increasing household current expenditure.
in writing. ‒ private investment in the public sector contributes to the efficiency of public investment. public-private partnerships in development have successfully contributed to reducing poverty among the most marginalised. support for development partnerships through coordination of member states with international organisations and the private sector is a major boost for developing country economies. micro-enterprises can play a key role in development strategies because of their ability to adapt more easily to market needs. i voted in favour of this report because i am convinced that promoting private initiative in developing countries creates an attractive environment for investment.
in writing. ‒ there is a need to identify new sustainable and effective instruments to invest in the growth and development of people and businesses, with industrialisation as a driver of well-being and development. i support the expansion of the private sector to ensure individual freedom and economic efficiency. social security or social insecurity are considered to be fundamental social problems. from an economic point of view, the security of individuals is influenced by their financial independence, in other words, the lack of income, the state of poverty automatically attract and the feeling of insecurity. it's widely acknowledged that having a decent job is the best way out of poverty. the private sector provides about 90% of jobs in developing countries and is therefore a key partner in the fight against poverty. full and productive employment and decent work, including the implementation of labour standards, are essential to tackling inequality and social exclusion. the new agenda should aim at eradicating poverty in all its forms and at achieving sustainable development in a balanced and integrated manner.
in writing. ‒ globally, there is no significant project that has not been done in a public-private partnership. i voted to support smes in developing countries that face greater constraints than those within the european union. the creation of an enabling environment and their retention in the formal economy is a priority.
in writing. ‒ as the private sector is the engine of economic growth in all market economies, i believe it is necessary to look at how it can be more involved in sectors such as agriculture, education, green technologies, research and innovation, health services and property rights, which remain largely untapped.
in writing. ‒ in the context of aid resources declining and new global challenges, such as climate change, the private sector will play a key role since these donors can bring innovation, expertise and effectiveness in development policy. however, the role of the private sector in development should be well-defined to ensure that there is full accountability and that development goals are not distorted. i would like to express my satisfaction for the outcome of the negotiations; this is a very-balanced report in which the crucial role of the private sector in development is recognised and positively assessed without ignoring the need to frame their work and to ensure that poverty reduction is their main goal when involved in development. i am especially in favour of supporting efforts to better frame the methodology and services that can be covered by public-private partnerships (ppps), ensuring access to ppps to firms not only from donor countries, and avoiding the risk of supporting eu companies through eu development funding.
in writing. ‒ the private sector is the backbone of the economy and public policies must be designed to develop the private sector, especially smes. according to the united nations development programme's human poverty index, 1.2 billion people earn less than $1.25 a day, and this should concern us all. the only way out of poverty is through economic development and, in particular, through the development of the private sector. i voted for this report because i support the development of the private sector, especially smes. i welcome the provision reiterating that the eu has a responsibility to support a fair global tax regime, the introduction of mandatory public reporting requirements for each country in respect of transnational corporations, which currently create unfair competition for smes in many cases. the report contains many proposals that can bring economic growth and sme development, more jobs and more income to every citizen.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will engage european and international enterprise sectors in order to achieve sustainable development in areas such as agriculture, land tenure and property rights, sustainable energy and green sectors, education, healthcare and sanitation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is concerned with creating conditions for the development of the private sector at member state level. i am pleased that the european parliament is trying to stimulate a sector that plays a major role in economic growth, with private firms contributing around 80% of gdp to member countries and being a source of job creation. the report voted on today proposes a series of measures that the european union and the member states should promote in order to develop the private sector. it is essential for national governments to adopt development strategies focusing on cooperatives, smes and small producers, which is one of the provisions of this document. i also welcome the report's proposal to promote the concept of women entrepreneurship in member states' strategies by proposing training programmes and with the aim of improving a long-term objective of the european union: gender equality.
in writing. ‒ the european union's financial assistance for the development of poor countries around the world is a significant instrument that has allowed remarkable progress to be made in many areas of interest, such as health, education and agriculture. however, the assistance provided by the european institutions and the member states cannot cover all the investment needs of developing countries. this is why it is necessary to involve private partners in existing projects, as this may generate an additional influx of financial or other resources. public-private partnerships can be a solution to the achievement of the millennium development goals, but only to the extent that they respect existing transparency and accountability regulations in the field, avoiding the promotion of private interests that may be contrary to the achievement of public development goals. in this respect, i appreciate the contribution of the private sector to the development of the world's poor countries, through its expertise, innovation and efficiency. however, i believe that all this must be put to the service of achieving the development objectives internationally agreed by the european union, while respecting existing standards and avoiding hidden subsidies. the present report is only a first step in the right direction.
