president-in-office of the council.– madam president, i am happy to be here and to participate today in this important debate on the implementation of the eu budget for the financial year 2014 in the context of the annual discharge procedures, as foreseen in article 319 of the treaty. on 23 february my colleague jeroen dijsselbloem, the dutch finance minister, had the honour of presenting the council’s recommendation to grant discharge to the commission – to the committee on budgetary control – and tomorrow this plenary will cast its vote. clearly the citizens of europe expect us to be particularly attentive to the quality of eu spending, and rightly so. however, sound financial management is not only important from a public opinion perspective; it is our legal obligation to execute the eu budget in compliance with the agreed rules. keeping eu expenditure under strict control is crucial for all of us. the council recommended that discharge be granted to the commission and outlined the reasons leading to this recommendation. nevertheless, the council also reaffirmed that there is still a lot to improve in the execution of the eu budget. first of all, the council regrets the insufficient reduction of the error rate of 4.4% and thus the fact that most spending is still affected by a material level of error, and that important policy areas such as agriculture, cohesion and research remain prone to error. the council was particularly concerned about the fact that, according to the court’s findings, the commission, national authorities and independent auditors had enough information to prevent, detect and correct these errors. clearly, all financial actors involved in the management of eu funds need to assume their responsibilities in full, including member states. the council urged the commission and member states to strengthen their mutual cooperation and stressed the importance of avoiding errors in the first place. therefore it highlighted the need to increase the quality of controls in order to prevent or detect and correct errors before declaring costs to the commission. so yes, i agree with the rapporteur, claudia schmidt, that what we need is not more controls but better implementation of the existing control mechanisms. in other words, this should – and could – be done in a cost-efficient way without adding extra layers of control. moreover, the council recommendation also recalled that recoveries and financial corrections are essential elements in the protection of the union’s financial interests. payments should be interrupted and suspended whenever significant deficiencies are identified and until corrective action has been fully implemented. unduly-paid amounts must be recovered without delay, and full transparency regarding the implementation of corrective action must be ensured. the council further calls upon the commission to provide the budgetary authority in the year 2016 with a comprehensive report based on systematic data already available on the areas where the level of error identified is persistently high, as well as on the root causes. additionally, the council also agrees with parliament that the simplification of rules remains paramount in achieving an unqualified audit opinion. simplification and improved guidance not only reduces the administrative burden on the beneficiaries and respective authorities but also allows for more efficient and less costly controls. the council welcomes the commission’s work in the management of payment appropriations and calls for a constant monitoring of outstanding commitments. it also recalls its request to the commission to provide transparent and timely information on the long-term cash flow forecast in order to better match payments and available funds with needs. despite the fact that the revenue part of the budget was not affected by material error, the council underlines the importance of mitigating the impact of revisions of national gni data as well as measures to reduce the length of outstanding reservations. finally, the council welcomes the court’s approach in evaluating the results of eu spending and measuring aspects related to performance. the council encourages the commission, following the court’s recommendation, to identify the most suitable and effective performance systems for the eu budget in cooperation with the court and member states. so i agree with the emphasis that rapporteur dlabajová puts on a performance—based budget. within this context, the council – while of course being cautious not to prejudge conclusions – welcomes the commission’s initiative budget, for the results of which i believe the first expert meeting took place last week. it is evident that we are still far from the overall aim of an unqualified audit opinion from the court. the council therefore reiterates its wish to see year—on-year improvements in the financial management systems and in the estimated level of errors across all policy areas. the council is constructively engaged in discussions on how to improve the performance framework of the eu budget and to ensure that this budget delivers better results in view of the multiannual financial framework mid—term review and of the next mff. the council invites the court to provide its input for this review in a timely manner. in conclusion, the presidency has started to work on the next mff through the conference in january and the following discussion at the general affairs council on 12 april. the aim is to explore, at an early stage, possibilities for improvement and reform. from this several principles have been identified that could provide a way forward, and the joint results of these discussions will be presented in a presidency report to the council, parliament and the commission.
vice-president of the commission.– madam president, dear rapporteurs, madam minister, president caldeira, honourable members of the european parliament, of the court of auditors, i would like to start by thanking all of you, and in particular the rapporteurs we have listened to, and the court of auditors, the council, for the seriousness with which you approach the debates on the 2014 discharge procedure. we are at a time when europe requires from us to concentrate on making absolutely best use of our people’s sacrifice. they are those who fund our budget. this year’s discharge is remarkable, with the alignment of all institutions – parliament the council, the court of auditors, the commission – on the importance we assign to focusing on the performance of the budget, what and how well it delivers for the eu economy and for our citizens, as well as the compliance with the rules: i recognise we have work to do in both areas. we have stabilised the error rate – we have to continue to drive it down – and, very importantly, we have to work on extracting the highest possible value from our budget. as the minister just mentioned, five or six days ago, on 22 april, we had the first meeting of the interinstitutional working group on performance. we start by defining what is performance so we see eye to eye, how we should measure it, as well as how we can move most systematically towards performance-based budgeting. i want to recognise the rapporteur madam dlabajová for her determination to make us expand our discussions from what used to be primarily focus on the error rate to a very strong footing in policy objectives and results achieved, and in that spirit i would draw four conclusions for us (not pretending that this exhausts all we have learned from the debate) in the following. first: alignment of budgetary priorities; second: better reporting on performance and budget focus on results; third: dealing with persistently high error rates, a topic that the minister brought up; and last but not least: how we strike the right balance between risk management and risk avoidance. so let me start with the first point. as we approach the midterm review revision, it is time to honestly identify to what degree we are capable of matching political priorities with the dedication of our budget. it is a question that will take us, hopefully, to important conclusions for the rest of this financial perspective, and also it would help us to see whether we are fully and entirely using the flexibility of the budget that has been granted in this multi-year financial perspective. another part of the debate would be how these political objectives are translated into operational objectives on the ground and how to ensure adequate reporting back on the results achieved. we know that in the current financial perspective we have made a very big step forward in respect of priorities and measures to what extent we achieved what we have said we would achieve, but we are not perfect; there are lessons to be learnt and fed into the preparation for the next generation of programmes, and i want to stress again the importance of interinstitutional dialogue. working together we can achieve significant improvements. second, the debate showed a need for better reporting on performance. we have a lot of information available, but we have to organise it so it guides our allocation of resources that we streamlined reporting better, we improved the quality of our indicators. in this respect, i want to announce that we will take an important step this year when the synthesis report in the article 318 report are combined in one, and this would provide a more complete picture on the implementation of the eu budget. in addition, we are very much aware of the necessity to insensitise earlier detection of risks of errors and errors. avoiding them in the first place is the best way to deal with them. we also will continue our work on the multi-annual nature of errors. we know that we measure them on an annual basis, but our programmes are multi-annual. we want to provide incentives for corrections so they are actually driving down the cost on errors on our citizens. third, we have been asked to look into the persistently high level of errors. we are going to present, later in this year, a report with analysis in this area. i want to stress that it would be drawn mostly on the prior experience from the previous multi-year financial framework 2007-2013. there are limitations how much we can translate lessons from there, but we would do our best to assess, on the basis of the latest information, what are the systemic risks and how we can best reduce them. last but not least, we want people to be mindful of risk management opportunities. the minister talked about simplification – very important. we have a huge opportunity with the changes in the financial regulation to achieve simplification, but we can never bring errors to zero, and we do not want us to shy away from what may be riskier but very high-value activity. take for example development. if we want to prevent conflicts, to reduce the catastrophic impact of lack of development, we ought to invest in fragile situations. they are riskier, and therefore we have to help our teams to manage these risks. but we do not want them to not to do the right thing because they want to be protected by inaction. similarly in migration: speed of action there is critical, and we are going to be working under demanding circumstances, where challenges change every day. let me finish with a quote from ms dlabajová. she says: ‘the future becomes the past’. i would add that we should learn from the past to secure a better future, and discharge is fantastic in this regard.
president of the court of auditors.– madam president, the european court of auditors welcomes this opportunity to participate again in the closing debate of the discharge procedure for the financial year 2014. i would first like to congratulate all the rapporteurs who have intervened and, in particular, mrs dlabajová for the huge amount of work she has done, and of course the whole committee on budgetary control. their reports are indeed valuable for this exercise, and the report on the european union budget, in particular, draws important lessons that we cannot afford to ignore. many of those are based on the work we have performed in our reports, so for those working at the court – for our members, for our staff – it is very gratifying to see how seriously our recommendations are being addressed in the different discharge reports. in particular, as regards the european union budget discharge, we think indeed that the challenge now is to ensure that the lessons we have learned from the past, in particular in the 2014 financial year, will lead to short and long-term improvements in the way the european union funds are used. it is very encouraging to have already listened today to the commitment that all the institutions are showing on the need to act. for that to happen, we need those lessons to be reflected in the mid term review of the current multiannual financial framework; we need them also to be reflected in the revision of the financial regulation, and we need to work together – all the institutions in their different roles and capacities – to develop a budget more focused on results. as i said in november last year, we believe it is time to start developing a wholly new approach for european union spending and investment. that implies the european union budget being better targeted to the european union’s strategic objectives; it needs to be more flexible in a crisis – refugees and migration were mentioned – and it also needs to be used more efficiently, and then there is also huge room for improvement. our 2000 annual report highlighted the scope for tackling financial backlogs, reducing payment errors, and improving reports on results. the commission has welcomed the message, has accepted our recommendations and, as we listen now, is acting upon them. that is very encouraging. in turn, the court will follow up all these developments in our 2015 annual report, which we are currently preparing. this year we hope to be able to publish it in october, earlier than in previous years. i want to thank the commission, and in particular vice-president georgieva, for their support in achieving this target, and we also very much count on parliament’s acceptance of this. we are also actively engaged in strengthening dialogue with this parliament and its committees to ensure that we produce reports that provide you in this house with the maximum assistance for you to exercise effective public oversight over the implementation of the european budget and european union legislation. i will conclude by saying that the european union must make the most of the opportunity it has now to fundamentally review how public funds are raised, spent and managed to achieve the european union objectives.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs. as the author of the afet opinions on the discharge of the european commission and the european external action service, i would like to express my support for the recommendations made to these two institutions in the various reports we are debating today on the way the budget for the union's external activities is managed. i think that when we discuss how the money that has been and is being spent on foreign policy in third countries, it is essential to remember that the impact we will have depends on a lot of factors: local, regional, factors that we cannot control. i therefore consider that the management of the budget allocated to the union's external activities must be sufficiently flexible to be able to respond quickly and effectively to developments in third countries. i also believe that the management of these funds should be made fully transparent. it also seems important to me that both the commission and the european external action service should make efforts to drastically reduce delays in payments, errors and to improve the number of projects financed by the union in third countries.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development.– madam president, as rapporteur for the committee on development opinion on discharge implementation of the eu general budget for 2014 and on the 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th european development funds (edf), i would like to raise some concerns about certain points that were included in the political resolution accompanying the discharge. first, in both the committee on development and the committee on budgetary control (cont), we expressed concerns at the inclusion by the rapporteur of some critical and unjustified phrasing and figures drawn from an unofficial working document by a colleague on the cont committee and which had never been approved by the cont committee. i strongly oppose the inclusion of any references to this document in the edf discharge. moreover, the rapporteur calls for one quarter of the 11th edf to be used in combating the migration crisis. however, the scope of the edf is to tackle the root causes of migration by supporting sustainable development, and focusing it on addressing existing migration flows would send out a false signal and may lead to a misappropriation of funds. i therefore ask you to vote in favour of amendments 5, 6 and 7 in order to ensure that the resolution we will adopt tomorrow not only paints an accurate picture of the reality of projects in our missions in this region but also that it does not call into question the fundamental principles of this important fund.
in writing. without underestimating the results achieved in the economic and social development of some countries and regions through the use of the european development fund, i draw attention to the fact that some of these countries, recipients of european funding, have not adhered to the agreements on tax transparency, combating money laundering and tax evasion. i therefore believe that such countries should be excluded from european funding until they join the tax transparency agreements. otherwise, instead of european money reaching the people who need it, it will end up in tax havens, in the accounts of kleptocrats and other corrupt people.
president-in-office of the council.– madam president, i am very pleased to be here tonight. let me be clear: attacks on hospitals and schools in conflict areas are simply intolerable. the council – as you do – explicitly condemns such atrocious acts. as you know, promoting compliance with international humanitarian law is a clear commitment by the european union, including the council. in this respect the eu guidelines on promoting compliance with international humanitarian law were adopted by the council in 2005 and reviewed in 2009. the union’s support for compliance with international humanitarian law is also reflected in the action plan on human rights and democracy for 2015—2019. at the 32nd international conference of the red cross and the red crescent movement, the union quite rightly reiterated its commitment to advocate strongly and consistently respect for international humanitarian law. in the context of the world humanitarian summit’s global consultation, common messages were also agreed. the council noted in december in the council conclusions that the world humanitarian summit should produce practical outcomes and specific commitments made by all relevant actors, in particular as regards safeguarding humanitarian access and respect for international humanitarian law. we definitely look forward to discussing summit preparations at your next plenary in may. when it comes to specific situations, the council, for example, in october last year addressed the situation in syria and called upon all parties – and will continue to call upon all parties – to stop all forms of indiscriminate shelling and bombardment against civilian areas and structures, such as hospitals and schools. concerning syria and iraq, in view of the third kuwait pledging conference, the eu and its member states have expressed their concern regarding grave violations of international humanitarian law, including attacks against schools, medical facilities, markets and other civilian areas. regarding yemen, the council, in november 2015, stated that ensuring accountability for humanitarian law violations is an important part of the process to achieve a lasting settlement of the current conflict. it also reiterated its call for the independent investigation of all alleged violations. the monitoring, control and promotion of international humanitarian law is also an essential part of the conclusions on the eu regional strategy for syria and iraq as well as the isil/da’esh threat, adopted by the council in march 2015. also on this occasion, the council called for the protection of medical facilities to be ensured at all times and, on many other occasions, the council has discussed the situation in libya, south sudan, sudan, iraq, nigeria and ukraine and addressed the specific situation of – yet again – educational and medical facilities. as regards the promotion by the union of the prevention and repression of such international humanitarian law violations, the council adopted its cfsp decision in 2011, under which the union and its member states must raise the issue of the widest possible participation in the international criminal court in negotiations or political dialogues with third states, groups of states or regional organisations as an essential means of promoting respect for international humanitarian law. finally, violations of international humanitarian law are targeted by many of the restrictive measures imposed by the union against third states in the context of its external action, for example, syria, yemen, libya, burundi and other third countries. without a doubt, the council shares your deep concern regarding violations of international humanitarian law, including those relating to medical and educational facilities. the council continuously monitors situations, undertakes action, and will continue to act accordingly. in closing, why is this important? let me stress that once more that we should never forget what international law is all about. it is about human beings – men, women, children, families – and we cannot, and should not, lose sight of humanity in our foreign policy. indeed, we have to stay true to our founding values.
on behalf of the epp group. madam president, the resolution we have negotiated and which we will be voting on tomorrow condemns very strongly the frequent attacks on schools, hospitals, other civilian structures in conflict situations. these are clearly unacceptable attacks on international humanitarian law and on respect for human rights, the principle underlying humanitarian law being precisely that of protection for those who are not part of a conflict but are caught up in it. the text agreed by the various political groups is a very balanced text. unfortunately, the far left is doing again what it has been used to do on other occasions: it is introducing amendments that have nothing to do with the subject: about western sahara, about abortion, about israel. it's unacceptable to miss the main topic by introducing the same left-wing obsessions. i hope that other left-wing groups will not support this destruction of the main subject we have.

question no 3 by mr pimenta (h-0026/97) subject: the commission's proposal for a regulation on the conclusion of the agreement with turkey my question to you is this: what would your alternative be if we, the european union, had not been able to solve the refugee problem in order to ensure, on the one hand, the safety of those people and, on the other hand, the safety of europeans? if we don't make the deal with turkey, what's your alternative?
madam president, as we know, the resettlement scheme adopted in autumn 2015 is not working, unfortunately. on the other hand, the agreement with turkey adopted a month ago is working and its objectives are beginning to be achieved: first, as vice-president timmermans said, the drastic reduction in the number of migrants, and secondly, the protection of greece, which was very exposed. however, there are three side effects to be taken into account: firstly, the change in routes - libya is beginning to become the new starting point - secondly, the emergence of tensions in europe over visa liberalisation and the negotiation of chapters, and thirdly, and not negligible, the rise in tensions in turkey, in particular between president erdoğan and prime minister ahmet davutoğlu, including on a very sensitive issue for turks, that of secularism. these three points, i think, deserve our attention.
first vice-president of the commission.– mr president, with all the criticism of the agreement reached with turkey, one almost forgets that since the implementation of this agreement people are no longer drowning in the aegean sea. one almost forgets that this uncontrolled irregular arrival of refugees in europe is no longer happening on the scale we saw before, so there are many things that need to be improved, and there is a long way to go, but let us at least acknowledge that human suffering has been limited through joint action with turkey. yes, we need to do more as i said in my introductory remarks, but one aspect i would like to come back to which was not mentioned by all of you is the need for member states to do their part. it is now that member states should take in people in a legal way, those who have the right to asylum and should be coming to europe. there is still a war in syria, people are still fleeing and people deserve international protection. it is our moral duty and legal duty to provide that protection, and now that we have ways of bringing people to europe in a safe and legal way, member states should deliver on what was agreed. on turkey, should we engage, should we not engage? president-in-office of the council.– mr president, the council is fully aware that the agreement is not the end. it is not the solution. it is an outline of possible solutions and it is the beginning we have to work at full speed and i also hope for the parliament’s support in that process to work on the european border guard. but if you want to control your borders well, you need to engage with the country on the other side of the border. you cannot just say that you have built a fence and are not talking to the country on the other side, especially when we are talking about borders at sea. you cannot just stay on the shore and say you that ‘you cannot get in, period’. you cannot survive being at sea so you have to engage with the country on the other side and you have to engage with countries on the other side of the external borders. so agreement with turkey would have been necessary in any case. even if we have the strongest european border guard in place ever, you still have to engage with the country that has to take in the people that are not allowed to cross your border and have to have good agreements about re-admission and how you deal with the situation and, in the end, offer security, safety and good conditions for real refugees. regarding the discussion about whether it is a statement or an agreement, i have a lot of agreements with a lot of people that are not legally taken to court so, from the council position, we can have a discussion. but in our position it is not an agreement within the legal meaning of article 218 of the treaty. of course, a lot of the things in that agreement between the union and the member states and turkey have to be dealt with and elaborated on and those individual aspects will of course, when it is legally bound to be dealt with by the proper institutions. to conclude, looking forward, i fully agree that we need to do much more than just implement what we have discussed today. we need to work at full speed on a in writing. the eu-turkey agreement of 18 march shows us that there is concrete cooperation between turkey and the member states, especially with greece, which is the country in the eu most affected by the influx of refugees. we are pleased to see that there are legislative amendments in these countries, that there is frontex support for eu border security and control, and that refugees are no longer putting their lives at risk, as a legal pathway is being created for syrian refugees from turkey. the eu has a moral duty to provide assistance to refugees, but this must be done in a realistic and not utopian manner. the adoption of all refugees by member states does not constitute a concrete measure for the syrian people. the eu must support the reintegration into an education system of syrian refugee children in turkish camps, as they will be the generation that will participate in the reconstruction of syria in the years after the end of the war. i therefore welcome the commission's intention to support the creation of educational programmes in turkey for refugee children. and last but not least, i call on the commission to facilitate, through european programmes, the provision of better health services and medicines to syrian refugees.

in writing. as also mentioned in the recitals to this resolution, although the eu acquis constitutes an internal market for rail transport services, the share of rail transport in the eu market is modest and stagnates at 6%. at the same time, 54% of users are dissatisfied. since 2013, the european commission has presented the fourth railway package, precisely to improve quality and efficiency in this area. commissioner, how can we talk about an internal rail market when we have huge disparities in the quality of rail infrastructure and when the allocation of the strategic investment fund does not take account of needs on the ground, with investment funds concentrating on the first five or six more developed economies? railway interoperability is of the utmost importance for the development of the transport economy, especially for smes, and therefore i believe that the quality of rail infrastructure in eastern countries should be taken into account when taking measures to create a single railway area.
in writing. the european parliament's agreement on the council's proposal on the technical pillar for the fourth railway package is a win for all of europe, not just for transport. the three directives in the package remove international barriers to infrastructure and interoperability, increasing not only the quality and safety of rail services but also the chances of new players entering the market. it is inconceivable to talk about a single european market, but no operator's trains can go from one end of europe to the other without stopping at every border. it is also incomprehensible how each european authority has to decipher some 11000 laws, rules and other provisions before taking a decision. i would stress that this package is the encouraging signal given to small producers and operators. less bureaucracy means lower costs and shorter trips. a win for producers and operators on the one hand, and for european citizens on the other. last but not least, the development of rail freight and passenger services will help to balance transport forces, providing a viable alternative to road and air transport in europe.

in writing. ‒ with this motion for a resolution, the european parliament brings the brussels iia regulation to the table and expresses its wish to update the transnational and crossborder mechanisms of child protection systems. while child protection remains a competence of the member states, article 81 tfeu clearly emphasises the role of the union in adopting measures on family law when they have cross-border implications. we live in a world governed by mobility, which we have managed to legislate very well, but unfortunately we have not considered its implications in the area of family law. together with my romanian colleagues, i also brought to the attention of the plenary the situation of a romanian-norwegian family in norway in which the child protection service of this eu partner state took custody of its children, one of whom was still breastfeeding. personally, i consider this to be a serious act of infringement of a fundamental right of a european citizen in a state with which the eu has close economic and trade relations. the best interests of the child are a priority for the eu, but they must be addressed effectively and a review of the brussels iia regulation is therefore necessary.
in writing. ‒ as the migratory phenomenon and freedom of movement have led to an increase in the number of children with parents of different nationalities, i believe that there is a need to deepen cooperation at european level to ensure that the interests of the minor are respected and protected. this involves developing synergies between the child protection systems of the 28 member states, in particular in the areas of protection and judicial cooperation, to which is added the role of social services in ensuring protection, legal procedures for the care of minors, placement and adoption, and the management of cross-border abduction situations. in light of recent events and the refugee crisis, i consider that child protection is essential. in voting in favour of this report, i would like to emphasise the need to create a helpline at european level which could be used in cases of abduction or abuse, but also for advice on care or adoption procedures.
in writing. ‒ all child protection systems should have transnational and cross-border mechanisms in place which take into account the specificities of cross-borders conflicts. i believe the commission and the member states should co-finance and promote the establishment of a platform providing assistance to non-national eu citizens in family proceedings, and of a single european helpline for cases of child abduction or abuse, as well as counselling concerning care and adoption proceedings. therefore, i strongly support the oral question to the council and commission, as the committee on petitions has received a large number of petitions regarding cross-border issues of child welfare, such as the non-recognition of national judgments concerning parental custody, forced adoption and difficult judicial proceedings. it is fundamentally important to communicate the shortcomings experienced by eu citizens and to ensure they may be addressed in the new regulation.
in writing. ‒ the high number of petitions in child-related cases indicates a poor application of the brussels iia regulation. there are major issues related to: child protection in the member states, judicial cooperation, legal proceedings in the field of childcare and cross-border abductions of children by one of the parents. it is necessary to revise that regulation and to define more clearly the concept of 'usual residence'. i recommend that member states ensure that embassies or consular posts are informed from the outset of childcare procedures involving their own nationals and have access to the relevant documents. i also believe that member states should inform parents about the legal rules by making available to them a list of specialised bilingual lawyers and interpretation services. i recommend separate hearings of parents and children before a judge or social worker to avoid influencing them. there is no mechanism at european level for the automatic recognition of national adoption decisions in other member states. i ask the council to present concretely the results achieved in setting up alert systems in the event of child abduction with cross-border implications.
in writing. ‒ the brussels iia regulation (ec) no 2201/2003 is a regulation within the european union regarding conflict of law in family law between member states in relation to divorce, child custody and international child abduction. the large number of petitions received regarding child-related cases has raised questions about the implementation of the brussels ii regulation. i voted in favour of this report that will improve child protection and judicial cooperation within the european union.

in writing. ‒ this resolution is a response to the large and growing number of petitions of a cross-border nature received over the years from citizens from various eu member states who are affected by the practices of child welfare authorities, and concerning the protection of children’s rights, child custody, child abduction and child care. all child protection systems should have transnational and cross-border mechanisms in place which take into account the specificities of cross-border conflicts. member states need to put in place monitoring and evaluation systems (with relevant socio-economic and nationality-disaggregated statistics) within a national coordinating framework on cross-border cases involving children. the best interest of the child must be paramount in all eu policy and in all eu legislation, including the revision of the brussels iia regulation, relating to childcare issues.

in writing. ‒ the european commission is responsible for the implementation of the budget of the european union. it involves member states to which the commission delegates implementation tasks relating to a significant part of the budget. each year, the discharge procedure ensures democratic ex-post control at political level, showing how the annual eu budget has been used. the procedure shall aim at verifying the correct implementation in accordance with the relevant rules, including the application of the principles of sound financial management. the discharge procedure has proved to be a powerful tool, which has had an impact on the evolution of the budgetary system of the european union, while contributing to increasing the political leverage of parliament. i voted in favour of this report on the general eu discharge 2014, the european commission and the executive agencies calling for a more vigilant stance on discharge, asking the commission to check more frequently the areas where money has been allocated and which are at high risk of error, to focus on ex-ante controls, to work more effectively with member states to correct errors before declaring expenditure and to introduce more transparency and flexibility on unused appropriations.
in writing. ‒ ultimately responsible for the execution of the european union’s budget is the european commission. the decision on whether to grant discharge for the execution of the eu budget is made by the european parliament. the discharge procedure ensures ex-post democratic oversight at political level of how the eu’s annual budget has been used. its aim is to verify that the implementation was in accordance with relevant rules and principles of sound financial management. the report underlines that the eu funding must be efficient in advancing eu goals, projects should be aligned with eu policies and better synergy should be achieved between all available resources in the fields, such as neighbourhood policy, external aid, and tackling the youth unemployment. i have voted for this report on european commission and executive agencies discharge that calls for a more vigilant position on the discharge, asking the commission to control more frequently areas and recipients with high risk of errors, focus on ex-ante controls, collaborate with the member states to correct errors before declaring expenditure and introduce more transparency and flexibility in spending so that unused appropriations could be used for new priorities.

in writing. ‒ ultimate responsibility for the execution of the european union’s budget lies with the commission. the decision on whether to grant discharge for the execution of the eu budget is made by parliament. the discharge procedure ensures ex-post democratic oversight at political level of how the eu’s annual budget has been used. its aim is to verify that the implementation was in accordance with relevant rules and with the principles of sound financial management. the report emphasises that eu funding must be efficient in advancing eu goals, projects should be aligned with eu policies and better synergy should be achieved between all available resources in the fields concerned, such as neighbourhood policy, external aid, and tackling youth unemployment. i voted for this report on the court of auditors’ special reports in the context of the 2014 commission discharge, which calls for a more vigilant position on the discharge, asking the commission to check on areas and recipients with a high risk of errors more frequently, to focus on ex-ante controls, to collaborate with the member states to correct errors before declaring expenditure, and to introduce more transparency and flexibility in spending, so that unused appropriations could be used for new priorities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the eighth, ninth, tenth and eleventh european development funds (edfs) for the financial year 2014. i consider this fund to be an instrument in the framework of development cooperation. i would like to point out that this fund is dedicated to the development of socioeconomic structures in third countries in order to prevent the flow of migration and should not be used for the management of the refugee crisis. in order to use this fund for the purposes for which it was created, it is necessary for the european commission to develop synergies between the union budget, the edf and bilateral cooperation in order to prevent the migrant crisis.
in writing. ‒ i support granting discharge for the 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th european development funds for the financial year 2014. however, as rapporteur for the development committee opinion on discharge implementation of the eu general budget for 2014, and on the 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th european development funds, i would like to raise some concerns on certain points that were included in the political resolution accompanying the discharge. in both the development and budgetary control committees we expressed concerns on the inclusion by the rapporteur of some critical and unjustified phrasing and figures taken from an unofficial working document drawn up by the chair of the committee on budgetary control (cont), which had never been approved by the cont committee. i strongly oppose the inclusion of any references to this document in the edf discharge. moreover, the rapporteur calls for one quarter of the 11th edf to be used for combating the migration crisis. however, the scope of the edf is to tackle the root causes of migration by supporting sustainable development: focusing it on addressing existing migration flows would send out a false signal and might lead to a misappropriation of funds.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is responsible for the implementation of the budget of the european union. it involves member states to which the commission delegates implementation tasks related to a significant part of the budget. each year, the discharge procedure ensures democratic ex-post control at political level, showing how the annual eu budget has been used. the procedure shall aim at verifying the correct implementation in accordance with the relevant rules, including the application of the principles of sound financial management. the discharge procedure has proved to be a powerful tool, which has had an impact on the evolution of the budgetary system of the european union, while contributing to increasing the political leverage of parliament. the european development fund is the main instrument of eu support for development cooperation in africa, the caribbean and the pacific and for territories aiming at poverty reduction and eradication. i voted against this political resolution following the position of the s&d group.
in writing. ‒ ultimate responsibility for the execution of the european union’s budget lies with the commission. the decision on whether to grant discharge for the execution of the eu budget is made by parliament. the discharge procedure ensures ex-post democratic oversight at political level of how the eu’s annual budget has been used. it aim is to verify that the implementation was in accordance with relevant rules and principles of sound financial management. the report underlines that the eu funding must be efficient in advancing eu goals, project should be aligned with the eu policies and better synergy should be achieved between all available resources in the various fields, such as neighbourhood policy, external aid and tackling the youth unemployment. i voted against this report due to some unjustified negative phrasing and criticism by the rapporteur.
in writing. ‒ on the general expenditure allowance (gea), besides the reiteration from the previous year, there are amendments adopted which call for more transparency and for revision of the list of expenses which may be defrayed from the gea. it was reiterated that this should not create any new administrative burden. an important compromise which brings more clarity on the future of the voluntary pension fund got adopted, calling on the bureau, immediately after reception of the external assessment, to make a proposal for a comprehensive action plan to address parliament’s responsibilities. we need to address even more strongly the importance of security measures. an amendment calling for a single seat was adopted. i voted in favour of granting the discharge.

in writing. ‒ i voted to grant the discharge for the 2014 financial year to the court of auditors. the annual accounts of the court of auditors shall be audited by an independent external auditor in order to apply the same principles of transparency and accountability as those applied by the court to the entities it audits. in 2014, the overall implementation rate of the court of auditors' budget was 98,8% compared to 92% in 2013. we welcome the improvement in the execution rate in the context of a low budget and stress that the court's budget is purely administrative, with a large amount being used for the expenses of the persons working in the institution. the court of auditors plays a crucial role in ensuring that european funds are spent more efficiently and intelligently. this institution is in a prominent position to provide the legislative and budgetary authority with valuable advice on the results and effects of union policies, with a view to improving the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of union-funded activities.

in writing. ‒ i voted to grant the european ombudsman discharge for the financial year 2014. any citizen of the union and any natural or legal person residing or having its registered office in a member state of the union may refer to the ombudsman cases of maladministration in the activities of community institutions or bodies in the exercise of their judicial powers. in this connection, we stress that the european ombudsman must in particular guarantee equal treatment and equal opportunities for all union citizens and that respect for linguistic quality and diversity, as well as the ombudsman's communication policy, must remain pillars of the institution. in accordance with the 2019 strategy, the ombudsman has undertaken own-initiative inquiries, and this is an effective tool. we invite the ombudsman to inform the discharge authority periodically of the outcome of these inquiries and to clearly define the tasks of the coordinator. we also recall that the european ombudsman's priority must be to deal with complaints received from citizens within a reasonable time and that in no case should own-initiative inquiries be carried out to the detriment of this priority.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution envisages granting discharge to the european data protection supervisor (edps) in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014. the favourable opinion of the parliament follows the analysis of the court of auditors' annual report on the implementation of the authority's budget. the report shows that the payments made by the authority for administrative and other expenditure during the year ended 31 december 2014 are free from material error and that the expenditure surveillance and control systems examined were effective. although the discharge vote is favourable, parliament calls on the authority, through this resolution, to improve its financial autonomy, review its conflict of interest policy and publish detailed information on procurement procedures and contractor selection criteria on the website.

in writing. ‒ the main purpose of the eu agencies was to carry out independent technical and scientific assessments, so the work of the agencies should have a direct impact on the daily lives of union citizens. in this regard, we stress the importance of the autonomy of agencies, in particular regulatory agencies and those performing independent intelligence gathering functions. many agencies do not explicitly and responsibly include information on the effectiveness and efficiency of their activities in their annual reports. we ask the court of auditors to carry out an evaluation of the performance and results of the agencies and to present its findings in a timely manner, before the revision of the 2016 multiannual financial framework. we invite the agencies to further step up their efforts and improve their communication policies and to ensure greater visibility of their activities through the various tools on social networks to make their activities and achievements known and to ensure that citizens are properly informed about their work. in view of the favourable analysis made by the court of auditors, i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european union agencies for the financial year 2014: performance, financial management and control.

in writing. ‒ the 32 decentralised agencies of the european union have vital importance in terms of delivering the goals and results of eu policies. there is now good progress being made in terms of the agencies sharing best practice and, where feasible, support services. their network is strong and they are working with the commission to implement the roadmap on decentralised agencies. i support the agencies in their many areas of work e.g. to keep our food safe, our environment clean or our planes and flights safer and more secure. this is of clear benefit to eu citizens and their performance is improving year on year.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is responsible for the implementation of the budget of the european union. it involves member states to which the commission delegates implementation tasks related to a significant part of the budget. each year, the discharge procedure ensures democratic ex-post control at political level, showing how the annual eu budget has been used. i voted in favour of this 2014 general discharge report on the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer) calling for a more vigilant discharge stance, asking the commission to check more frequently the areas where money has been allocated and which are at high risk of error, to focus on ex-ante controls, to work more effectively with member states to correct errors before expenditure is declared and to introduce more transparency and flexibility on unused appropriations.
in writing. ‒ ultimately responsible for the execution of the european union’s budget is the european commission. the decision on whether to grant discharge for the execution of the eu budget is made by the european parliament. the discharge procedure ensures ex-post democratic oversight at political level of how the eu’s annual budget has been used. its aim is to verify that the implementation was in accordance with relevant rules and principles of sound financial management. the report underlines that eu funding must be efficient in advancing eu goals, projects should be aligned with eu policies and better synergy should be achieved between all available resources in the field, such as neighbourhood policy, external aid, and tackling youth unemployment. i have voted for this report on the agency for cooperation of energy regulators (acer) discharge, that calls for a more vigilant position on the discharge, asking the commission to control more frequently areas and recipients with a high risk of errors, focus on ex-ante controls, collaborate with the member states to correct errors before declaring expenditure and introduce more transparency and flexibility in spending so that unused appropriations could be used for new priorities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the related 2014 discharge for the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer). the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of acer, stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. the agency's budget comes entirely from the union budget and, according to its financial statements, the final budget for the financial year 2014 was eur 10 880 000, representing a decrease of 8,8% compared to 2013. as coordinator of the s&d itre, i would like to underline acer's contribution to ensuring the smooth functioning of the single european gas and electricity market. the agency shall support national regulatory authorities in their regulatory function at european level and, where appropriate, coordinate their work.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report issued by the committee on budgetary control on the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the office of the body of european regulators for electronic communications for the financial year 2014, and welcomed the introduction of the detailed monthly procedure for monitoring, which led to an improvement in the budget implementation rate.

in writing. ‒ i voted to grant discharge to the translation centre for the bodies of the european union. this european public law agency, with legal personality, was set up in 1994 to provide a judicious response to the translation needs of a large number of european agencies and offices. the centre complies with 80% of the internal control standards (ics) and has made considerable efforts to implement the remaining measures of the ics action plan. the budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 79,34%, representing a reduction of 4,13% compared to 2013. the commission notes that the rate of execution of payment appropriations was 71,97%, which represents an increase of 5,71% compared to the financial year 2013. the translation centre introduced a new budget planning and monitoring tool, which was used in the preparation of the 2015 budget, a new translation flow management system, e-cdt, and a new computer-assisted translation tool that will improve performance and financial management.

in writing. ‒ i voted for the discharge for 2014 of the european centre for the development of vocational training. according to its financial statements, the final budget of the european centre for the development of vocational training in 2014 was eur 17 275 766, representing a decrease of 3,62 % compared to 2013. we note the centre's work to raise the profile of vocational education and training in the eu and its role through its website, social media platforms and the organisation of various events in the host member states. contributions to and support for policies to combat youth unemployment play an important role. the european centre for the development of vocational training contributes to the development and implementation of eu vocational training policies. it monitors labour market trends and helps the european commission, member states, employers' organisations and trade unions to provide vocational training services that meet the needs of the market.

in writing. ‒ according to its financial statements, cepol's final budget for the financial year 2014 was eur 8 575 859, representing an increase of 1,48% compared to 2013. the budget of the college shall be entirely derived from the budget of the union. cepol is a european union agency whose mission is to provide training and learning opportunities for law enforcement agencies on issues fundamental to the security of the union and its citizens. the activities are designed to facilitate the exchange of knowledge and good practice and to contribute to the development of a common european law enforcement culture. the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european police college for the year 2014, stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the college's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. the college has improved its budget monitoring system by implementing monthly budget reports and by holding regular meetings with all financial actors to analyse and minimise potential carry-overs. we call on cepol to improve its procedures and practices aimed at protecting the financial interests of the union and to contribute actively to a results-oriented discharge process.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution envisages granting discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014 to the european police college (cepol). the resolution welcomes the college's efforts to improve the budget monitoring system by implementing monthly budget reports and by organising regular meetings with all financial actors to analyse and minimise potential deferrals. the resolution calls on the college to strictly apply the measures on discretion and exclusion in public procurement, to carry out appropriate checks of substance in all cases and to apply the exclusion criteria to eliminate any conflicts of interest, as this is essential for the protection of the financial interests of the union. it also calls for improvements to recruitment procedures and for full transparency in recruitment procedures. although the college adopted a number of guidelines on how to rank candidates, these were not made public. it is regrettable that there is no information in relation to the guidelines in question in the 2014 annual activity report, therefore the college is requested to publish this information and inform the discharge authority of the impact of the guidelines on the recruitment procedure.

in writing. ‒ i voted to grant discharge to the european aviation safety agency. this agency plays a key role in ensuring a high level of aviation safety throughout europe. the agency has also been involved in the implementation of the new flight time limitation regulation (ftlr) and the new flight time limitation regulation (ftlr) as well as in the implementation of the new flight time limitation regulation (ftlr). in the context of a rapidly developing civil aviation sector, the agency should have the financial, material and human resources necessary to successfully fulfil its regulatory and executive tasks in the areas of safety and environmental protection, without compromising its independence and impartiality. the final budget of the agency for 2014 was eur 181 179 098, representing an increase of 8,47% over the 2013 budget. the budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 97,1%, representing a reduction of 0,9% compared to 2013. ;21,1% of the agency's budget comes from the union budget, the rest from aviation companies. these financial links with aviation companies could affect the agency's independence, and we therefore call on the agency to provide safeguards to ensure its independence and avoid conflicts of interest.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's proposal for a decision on the closure of the accounts of the european asylum support office for the financial year 2014. we welcome the fact that, following the 2013 discharge, the european asylum support office introduced measures to address recurring problems related to miscalculation of budgetary needs and late payments, as well as transparency and conflicts of interest. the agency plays an important role in the practical implementation of the common european asylum system and was established to enhance practical cooperation on asylum issues and to support member states in fulfilling their obligations at european and international level. the agency's tasks will probably increase further in view of the difficulties encountered in managing the current refugee crisis and its budget and staff will have to increase accordingly. we call on the agency to step up its efforts and improve its budget management and to present an action plan in order to ensure optimal performance in the coming years.

in writing. ‒ the european banking authority (eba) is an independent eu authority whose objective is to ensure an effective and consistent level of prudential regulation and supervision throughout the eu banking sector. its general objectives are to maintain financial stability in the eu and to ensure the integrity, efficiency and soundness of the banking sector. we call on the commission to initiate, in the framework of the white paper for the second quarter of 2016, another financing mechanism based on a separate budget line in the union budget and the full replacement of contributions from national authorities with fees paid by market participants. in all aspects of the authority's resources, it should be ensured that the mandate can be fulfilled consistently and that budgetary constraints do not in practice limit the independence, reliability and effectiveness of the supervisory activity. it is also of particular importance that the provisions developed by the authority are designed in such a way that they can be applied to the same extent by smaller entities. finally, i voted in favour of parliament's report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european banking authority for the financial year 2014.
in writing. ‒ by this resolution, parliament granted discharge to the european banking authority in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014. the favourable opinion follows the analysis of the court of auditors' report and the court's statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions for the financial year 2014. the court's report shows that the budget planning and monitoring efforts of the authority during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget execution rate of 99,81%, which represents an increase of 2,28% compared to 2013. parliament called on the authority to respect at all times the mandate given by the european legislator and not to set standards in areas where the legislative processes have not yet been completed. as regards the authority's blending mechanism, it is found to be inadequate, inflexible and a potential threat to the independence of the authority. therefore, this resolution calls on the commission to initiate another financing mechanism, based on a separate budget line in the eu budget and on the full replacement of contributions from national authorities with fees paid by market participants.

in writing. ‒ as vice-president of the committee on budgetary control, in the light of the court of auditors' report, i support the closure of the accounts of the european environment agency for the financial year 2014. we call on the agency to strictly apply the measures on discretion and exclusion in public procurement, carrying out appropriate substantive checks in all cases, and to apply the exclusion criteria to remove companies in case of any conflict of interest, as this is essential to protect the financial interests of the union. as s&d itre coordinator, i draw attention to the fact that the agency has contracted data backup services, including e-mail services, from a cloud service provider through an interinstitutional contract provided by the commission. unfortunately, the place of storage of the agency's data is not properly defined in the contractual terms, which means that there is a risk that the privileges and immunities of the european communities applicable to the agency are not guaranteed and that the service provider does not fully comply with the privacy safeguards provided for in article 7 of the charter of fundamental rights of the eu. the agency shall undertake to carry out regular reviews of the implementation of contracts with a view to reassessing risks and taking appropriate and remedial action, if deemed necessary.

in writing. ‒ as vice-president of the committee on budgetary control, in view of the court of auditors' report on the reliability of the annual accounts of the european fisheries control agency, i support the closure of the agency's accounts for the financial year 2014. given the agency's important contribution to the implementation of the objectives of the common fisheries policy, i would like to underline the importance of cooperation between the agency and the member states in organising the monitoring of the landing obligation, by improving the control and surveillance of fishing activities, by facilitating cooperation, by promoting interoperability and by developing joint capacities. the agency should create a section of its website presenting the agency in all official languages of the union and we encourage the agency to do so, within the limits of its available resources, in order to improve its visibility and reputation. the mandate of the agency should be strengthened to initiate joint operational actions with other european agencies specialised in the maritime field, to prevent maritime disasters and to coordinate coast guard activities at european level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report for the financial year 2014 of the european fisheries control agency. the report shall include and highlight the main observations and assessments made by the fisheries committee to the agency in respect of the 2014 budget year, inviting and encouraging further improvement of the budgetary performance.
in writing. ‒ i backed this report as agreed in committee, granting discharge to efsa.

in writing. ‒ following the examination of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts of the european maritime safety agency for the financial year 2014, and having regard to the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors, the european parliament has decided to grant discharge to the agency in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014. during the financial year 2014, budget monitoring efforts resulted in a budget implementation rate of 94,78%. the provisions of the resolution underline the importance of the agency in maintaining maritime safety, preventing pollution from ships in europe and assisting member states and the commission under international and union law. the budgetary and staff cuts implemented during 2014 are regrettable, all the more so as this year the scope of competence was extended to a new set of main tasks and new ancillary tasks were introduced. parliament also requests the agency to complete the necessary corrective actions following the court of auditors' observations of 2012 and to publish on the agency's website, in addition to cvs, the declarations of interests of the members of the management board, the executive director and the members of the senior management.

in writing. ‒ i voted for the discharge for the 2014 budget for the european railway agency. i would emphasise the role played by the agency in ensuring the safety and interoperability of the european rail system, the subsequent role of the agency after the development, testing and introduction of the european rail traffic management system (ertms) and in the evaluation of the different ertms projects. the fourth railway package provides for a review of the role (e.g. a single ticketing point for vehicle authorisation and safety certification) and competences of the agency. as the responsibilities increase, the agency will need to be provided with the financial, material and human resources necessary to carry out its new additional tasks effectively and efficiently. unfortunately, the budget cuts applicable to the agency in the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework are in contradiction with the recently adopted legislation extending the mandate of the agency. the agency should work with member states to increase the number and quality of rail projects, in particular ertms projects, proposed under the connecting europe facility (cef) transport programme.
in writing. ‒ the work of the european securities and markets authority, despite its purely technical nature, is of particular importance in strengthening the safety and soundness of the financial sector and ensuring compatibility with union law, respect for the principle of proportionality and respect for the fundamental principles of the internal market for financial services. i therefore voted in favour of granting the executive director of the european securities and markets authority discharge in respect of the implementation of the authority's budget for the financial year 2014, stressing the need to ensure a mandate that can be fulfilled consistently without budget cuts having an impact on the independence, reliability and effectiveness of the supervisory work.

in writing. ‒ i voted to grant discharge to the european securities and markets authority in respect of the financial year 2014. the european parliament has been a strong supporter of the efforts to establish a new and comprehensive european system of financial supervision (esfs) in the wake of the financial crisis and of the establishment of the authority in 2011 as part of this system. the authority's role is to promote a common supervisory regime across the internal market, which is crucial for ensuring financial stability and a more integrated, transparent, efficient and secure financial market, as well as a high level of consumer protection in the union. the authority's work is purely technical, with key policy decisions being the prerogative of the union legislator. the budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 98,89%, representing an increase of 5,71%, compared to 2013, indicating that commitments were made to a greater extent in a timely manner.

in writing. ‒ ultimately responsible for the execution of the european union's budget is the european commission. the decision on whether to grant discharge for the execution of the eu budget is made by the european parliament. the discharge procedure ensures ex-post democratic oversight at political level of how the eu's annual budget has been used. it aim is to verify that the implementation was in accordance with relevant rules and principles of sound financial management. the report underlines that the eu funding must be efficient in advancing eu goals, project should be aligned with the eu policies and better synergy should be achieved between all available resources in the fields, such as neighborhood policy, external aid, and tackling the youth unemployment. i have voted for this report on european training foundation (etf) discharge that calls for a more vigilant position on the discharge, asking the commission to control more frequently areas and recipients with high risk of errors, focus on ex-ante controls, collaborate with the member states to correct errors before declaring expenditure and introduce more transparency and flexibility in spending so that unused appropriations could be used for new priorities.
in writing. ‒ the european training foundation operates in a dynamic environment which requires a high level of flexibility, constant updating and adjustment of its activities to support partner countries. the year 2014 was marked by continued political instability in the southern and eastern mediterranean and in eastern europe due to the crisis in ukraine, and therefore the full use of the foundation's work in the field of migration and training needs to be made. since the adoption of its reformed mandate in 2008, the foundation has been working to reduce staff in central administrative functions while maximising the number of experts used, which has resulted in a 19% increase in staff in the operations department, namely from 64 in 2008 to 76 in 2014. we invite the foundation to improve its procedures and practices aimed at protecting the financial interests of the union and to contribute actively to a results-oriented discharge process.
in writing. ‒ following the examination of the final annual accounts of the european training foundation and taking into account the court of auditors' report and the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions, the european parliament has decided to grant discharge to the foundation in respect of the implementation of its budget for the financial year 2014. the budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a high budget implementation rate of 99,90%, demonstrating that commitments were made on time and that the execution rate of payment appropriations was high. the resolution welcomes the foundation's efforts to publish on its website the cvs and declarations of interests of its board of directors, director and senior management. the resolution also recommends that the foundation include in its annual report a special chapter on transparency, accountability and integrity.
in writing. ‒ following the opinion of the committee on budgetary control and the opinion of the court of auditors on the reliability of the agency's accounts, i voted in favour of the discharge for the financial year 2014 of the european agency for the operational management of large-scale it systems in the area of freedom, security and justice.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is responsible for the implementation of the budget of the european union. it involves member states to which the commission delegates implementation tasks related to a significant part of the budget. each year, the discharge procedure ensures democratic ex-post control at political level, showing how the annual eu budget has been used. i voted in favour of this general discharge report 2014 on the european agency for the operational management of large-scale it systems in the area of freedom, security and justice, which calls for a more vigilant position of the commission on discharge, calling on it to check more frequently the areas where money has been allocated and which present a high risk of error, to focus on ex ante controls, to work more effectively with member states to correct errors before declaring expenditure and to introduce more transparency and flexibility on unused appropriations.

in writing. ‒ the european agency for the operational management of large-scale it systems in the area of freedom, security and justice, established in october 2011, took over its main responsibilities as from 1 december 2012. the agency's core task is to ensure the operational management of the vis and eurodac and to complete the preparations for the takeover of sis ii (schengen information system) operations. the agency will need to ensure that it is fully prepared to take on the difficult task of managing this critical system from now on. in the medium term, it is also developing new large-scale it systems in this strategic area. the court of auditors, in its report on the agency's annual accounts, stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution envisages granting discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014 to the european agency for the operational management of large-scale it systems in the area of freedom, security and justice (eu-lisa). the parliament's favourable opinion follows the analysis of the court of auditors' annual report on the implementation of the agency's budget. through this resolution, parliament calls on the agency to further improve its budget planning and management as well as its human resources management. although the parliament asked the agency a year ago to establish policies for the prevention and management of conflicts of interest, it did not act on the recommendation. therefore, this resolution requests the agency to remedy this issue and to publish the cvs and declarations of interests of the staff. it also recommended that the agency publish a comprehensive organisation chart containing the names and functions of all its staff and stressed the need for clear, binding internal rules on the prevention and management of conflicts of interest, on whistleblowing procedures and on so-called 'revolving door' situations.

in writing. ‒ following the examination of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts of the european agency for health and safety at work for the financial year 2014, and having regard to the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors, the european parliament has decided to grant discharge to the agency in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014. in this resolution, parliament welcomes the agency's implementation in 2014 of its new multiannual strategic programme for 2014-2020 and appreciates the positive signals reflecting the progress made by the agency in the first year of implementation of the strategy. parliament also welcomed the development of an interactive online risk assessment tool and the agency's efforts, through the healthy workplaces campaign, to strengthen risk prevention and promote sustainable and healthy workplaces. the resolution calls on the agency to make progress overall in preventing and combating corruption by improving public access to documents, tightening conflict of interest rules, introducing or using more stringent transparency registers and providing sufficient resources for law enforcement measures.

in writing. ‒ following the examination of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts of the european police office (europol) for the financial year 2014, and having regard to the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors, the european parliament has decided to grant discharge to the office in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014. the court's report shows that budget monitoring efforts during the financial year 2014 improved considerably and resulted in a high budget implementation rate of 99,70%. the resolution calls on europol to maintain as low a level as possible of committed appropriations carried over to the following year in order to better comply with its obligations of transparency and accountability. the office is also required to publish the exclusion criteria relating to eligibility to participate in the procurement procedure, the selection criteria relating to the ability to fulfil the provisions of a contract and all contracts awarded in 2014.
