in writing. ‒ the artemis joint undertaking was set up in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to define and implement a research agenda for the development of key technologies for integrated information systems in different application sectors, with the aim of enhancing the union's competitiveness and sustainability and facilitating the emergence of new markets and societal applications. the maximum contribution from the union to the joint undertaking for the period of 10 years shall be eur 420 000 000, to be paid from the budget of the seventh framework programme for research. the total financial contributions from the artemis member states should be at least 1,8 times the union financial contribution and the in-kind contribution of the research and development organisations participating in projects during the lifetime of the joint undertaking should be equal to or higher than the contribution of the public authorities. artemis and eniac have merged to create the 'electronic components and systems for european leadership' joint technology initiative (ecsel joint technology initiative), which started in june 2014 and will continue for 10 years. the commission shall be assisted by the european parliament and the council.

in writing. ‒ as s&d itre coordinator, i would like to underline the importance of the ecsel joint undertaking established for the implementation of the joint technology initiative 'electronic components and systems for european leadership' for a period ending on 31 december 2024. the joint undertaking was established as the successor and replacement of the eniac joint undertaking and the artemis joint undertaking. public-private partnership in the field of electronic components and systems should combine the essential financial and technical means to keep pace with the complexity and the frenetic pace of innovation in this field. the members of the joint undertaking shall be the union, the member states and the countries associated to horizon 2020 on a voluntary basis, private associations representing their constituent companies and other organisations active in the field of electronic components and systems in the union. the joint undertaking should be open to new members. we support the joint undertaking's initiative to work with smaller contributors and to extend the coverage of grant evaluation to 90% of the grants awarded. the joint undertaking shall be responsible for the implementation of the budget and the implementation of the budget for the financial year.

in writing. ‒ the eniac joint undertaking was set up in december 2007 for a period of 10 years with the aim of developing and implementing a 'research agenda' to develop key competences in nanoelectronics for different application sectors. the joint undertaking was granted financial autonomy in july 2010. the maximum contribution from the union to the joint undertaking for the period of 10 years shall be eur 450 000 000, to be paid from the budget of the seventh framework programme for research. the joint undertaking and the artemis joint undertaking (artemis) have merged to create the 'electronic components and systems for european leadership' joint technology initiative (ecsel), which started in june 2014 and will continue for 10 years. i voted in favour of granting discharge to the eniac joint undertaking.
in writing. ‒ i backed this report as agreed in committee, granting discharge to the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is responsible for the implementation of the budget of the european union. it involves member states to which the commission delegates implementation tasks related to a significant part of the budget. each year, the discharge procedure ensures democratic ex-post control at political level, showing how the annual eu budget has been used. i voted in favour of this 2014 general discharge report on the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking, calling for a more vigilant discharge position from the commission, calling on it to monitor more frequently the areas where money has been allocated and where there is a high risk of error, to focus on ex ante controls, to work more effectively with member states to correct errors before declaring expenditure and to introduce more transparency and flexibility on unused appropriations.

in writing. ‒ the european investment bank plays a key role in stimulating economic growth, but also in the balanced development of the internal market, actively contributing to strengthening social and economic cohesion by reducing territorial disparities. the 2014 annual reports of the european investment bank capture the institution's efforts in terms of employment and support for smes, with the eib setting up 285 000 small and medium-sized enterprises, thus creating 3,6 million jobs. the eib has also played a central role in supporting education, making significant investments for young people. i also welcome the continuing concerns about environmental protection and new instruments to support climate action. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the actions of the european investment bank have led to significant progress in terms of economic development, social development, environmental protection, its efforts having a positive impact on the quality of life of the citizens of the union.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support this report that, if adopted, will encourage the eib towards a more balanced lending strategy for all the member states. in particular, i would like to highlight the need to ensure consistency and complementarity with the investments from the european structural and investment funds and other public funds; the need to implement and further develop the efsi in close cooperation with the co-legislators, including through a timely and mandatory conclusion of the pending agreement between parliament and the eib; and the need to develop and deploy the necessary comprehensive approach in response to the severe challenges generated by the flow of migrants to europe, including enhanced operations in countries of origin of such flows as well as in countries which border directly on countries of origin. investments to accelerate recovery and enhance productivity have to be a priority. through these actions, we will promote youth employment, innovation and smes, enhance environmental sustainability and climate action, and finally, promote economic and social cohesion and convergence in all member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this 2014 european investment bank report, which ensures consistency and complementarity with investments from the european structural and investment funds and other public funds.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that calls on the eib to ensure consistency and complementarity with the investments from the european structural and investment funds and other public funds; promote youth employment, innovation and smes; update the external dimension of eib interventions; enhance environmental sustainability and climate action; promote economic and social cohesion and convergence.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, the european investment bank (eib), the eu’s public bank and largest multilateral lending institution, contributed financing of eur 80.3 billion (including the eif – the european investment fund). the report takes account of the work of the eib on an annual basis. a more consistent way of complementarity with the investments from the european structural and investment funds and other public funds must be ensured, thus contributing to the balanced development of the internal market and to social, economic and territorial cohesion. moreover, the eib shall prioritise investments to accelerate recovery and enhance productivity, especially by promoting youth employment, innovation and smes or enhancing environmental sustainability and climate action. i therefore welcome the motion for a resolution on the european investment bank (eib) – annual report 2014 which provides clear messages to be considered.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, internal armed conflicts have become the main cause of man-made humanitarian crises, with people increasingly exposed to violence and suffering. it is worrying that the number of terrorist attacks on humanitarian workers, especially on hospitals or even schools, has increased significantly, despite the fact that they are prohibited under international law, constituting either serious violations of the geneva convention or even war crimes under the rome statute. furthermore, international humanitarian law prohibits any attack on patients and medical personnel. the world humanitarian summit will be an opportunity to raise the alarm about serious violations of ihl and we want the union, with the support of the member states, to continue its commitment to protect civil society and ensure respect for human rights among citizens. i support this motion for a resolution because the ep, the commission and the council are the basic pillars of the fight against terrorism and must respond directly to terrorist challenges that violate the fundamental objectives of international humanitarian law.
in writing. ‒ the international community has in recent years faced a very high increase in the number of attacks on schools and hospitals in armed conflicts. there has been an increase in the cases of denial of humanitarian aid and access for humanitarian workers, execution of civilians and humanitarian personnel, which has led a number of organisations to temporarily suspend various forms of support to the affected population. i voted for the effective implementation by the eu and its member states of the eu guidelines on promoting respect for international humanitarian law and facilitating humanitarian response in affected areas. the un and the eu must promote campaigns to ensure that all actors meet their obligations to facilitate humanitarian assistance and protect civilians.
in writing. ‒ attacks on humanitarian workers are now ‘common currency’ and have reached alarming levels. i therefore support the question submitted to the hr/vp and the council to respond on how the relevant council bodies have implemented the eu guidelines on promoting compliance with international humanitarian law with regard to the conflicts in syria, yemen, afghanistan and other recent or current armed conflicts. the un security council has a clear role to play in ensuring respect for international law relevant to the protection of all humanitarian workers. therefore, it is fundamental that the eu and eu member states request the un security council to remind parties involved to comply with legal obligations and when they do not, to impose targeted measures on persistent violators. moreover, unsc must use all available tools to bring those responsible for such acts to justice.
in writing. ‒ the number of attacks on hospitals and schools is increasing, and the attacks on the hospital in kunduz (afghanistan) in october 2015 or razah (yemen) in january 2016 are only the latest. international humanitarian law, which is supposed to protect those not involved in the conflict, is being flagrantly violated. i call on the parties to the conflict to stop blocking humanitarian access and to stop causing direct or physical damage to schools and hospitals. any attack on hospitals or schools is prohibited under international law. i recall the position adopted in the eu guidelines on examining, where appropriate, the possibility of using the services of the international humanitarian fact-finding commission, which promotes compliance with international humanitarian law. i note that these services have never been used and therefore i urge member states to start an investigation into attacks on hospitals and schools and to activate this commission. what good is it to increase humanitarian aid when we don't even use what we have, like fact-finding services to eliminate impunity?
in writing. ‒ i have abstained in voting this motion for a resolution regarding the hospitals and schools as violations of international humanitarian law.
in writing. ‒ attacks on hospitals and schools, and civilians in general, are increasingly taking place in conflict zones. although hospitals and infrastructure housing civilians are designated under international humanitarian law as being inviolable, compliance with this law continues to be ignored by conflict parties (state and non-state actors alike). i voted in favour of this joint resolution because it stresses the importance of strengthening accountability mechanisms such as the international criminal court in order to prevent impunity while it also identifies an urgent need to advance compliance with international humanitarian law, insisting in this regard on the essentiality of already established relevant eu guidelines and the possibility of instituting an international humanitarian fact-finding commission.
in writing. ‒ i support this joint motion for resolution as attacks on hospitals and schools are increasing in armed conflicts around the world, in countries such as syria, afghanistan, yemen, nigeria, kenya and others, and such attacks are in breach of international humanitarian law. this resolution could potentially lead to a reminder from the un security council that parties to an armed conflict need to comply with legal obligations and if they fail to do so, they will be faced with strict measures. the resolution also calls for the unsc to use all available measures to bring violators to justice.
in writing. ‒ taking into account regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 of the european parliament and of the council on public access to european parliament, council and commission documents, and the fact that transparency is at the heart of citizens' trust in the vast majority of institutions within the union, it leads to awareness of the rights that are part of the legal system of the union and to knowledge of the decision-making process, including the correct application in practice of all administrative and legislative procedures. the right of access to documents is also a fundamental right recognised in the charter of fundamental rights of the treaties and put into practice by regulation 1049/2001 and intended to guarantee it as easily as possible and at the same time to promote good administrative practices with regard to access to documents, thus ensuring democratic control of all the activities of the institutions and its compliance with the principles enshrined in the treaties. i voted in favour of the report on public access to documents in 2014-2015 because i believe that transparency is needed with regard to documents within the eu institutions and i also believe that transparency strengthens and contributes to the implementation of the principle of good administration.
in writing. ‒ i strongly believe that the council and the commission need to seriously engage with parliament to unblock the revision of european union law on access to documents. i am in favour of increased public access to documents and the proper implementation of eu law, while remaining pragmatic about the limits of transparency. the issue of transparency surrounding trilogues is particularly sensitive in the light of the investigation being carried out by the european ombudswoman into the functioning of trilogues. transparency can be increased through better reporting back to committee on the outcome and providing that certain documents relating to trilogues, such as agendas, minutes or summaries of outcomes, where they exist, should be publicly accessible. i welcome the fact that co-legislators have been given adequate ‘space to think’ and that the four-column table is deliberately not included in any list of documents which should be accessible to the public.
in writing. ‒ under article 17 of regulation (ec) no 1049/2001, the union institutions are required to prepare an annual report on the granting of access to documents, in accordance with the aforementioned regulation. i voted in favour of this report on improving public access to documents and the correct implementation of union law and their transparency.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that acknowledges that transparency needs improving, inter alia, via better reporting back to the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs on the outcome and providing that certain documents relating to trilogues, such as agendas, minutes or summaries of outcomes should be publicly accessible.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i believe that the transparency of public institutions is the key to a democratic society, where citizens have confidence in state institutions, precisely because they can always have access to the information and documents of these institutions, which they finance through taxes and fees. as regards the classification of certain documents, this procedure must be exceptional, covering a limited number of documents, on the basis of very clearly defined procedures and legislation. unfortunately, as this report also points out, the eu institutions are not sufficiently transparent. this is why i support the rapporteur's call on all institutions to make further efforts to make the decision-making process more transparent by publishing documents and ensuring that they are easily and quickly accessible.
in writing. ‒ institutions, agencies and other bodies of the european union still fail to take fully into account and to comply with the rules and the changes provided for in the lisbon treaty and the charter of fundamental rights when applying regulation (ec) no 1049/2001, especially as concerns participatory democracy. the actual public access to documents and the management of registers of documents need to be based on standards which adequately comply with articles 41 and 42 of the charter. it is a priority that eu institutions ensure transparency as regards access to documents in order for citizens to understand how and why decisions have been taken. i am therefore in favour of increased public access to documents and the proper implementation of european union law.
in writing. ‒ domestic workers and home care workers are an important element of european society, their services covering a wide range of areas, including care of homes or of dependent persons. professionalisation in these areas means giving workers in a particular sector labour and social protection rights that are equivalent to those held by employees working under legally regulated employment contracts, such as decent wages, a regulated work schedule, leave, health and safety at work. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there needs to be a uniform recognition at eu level of domestic and care work as real and valuable work. regulation of this occupational sector can also lead to a reduction in undeclared work and promote social inclusion. thus, by improving the quality of life of people who carry out these activities and by providing social protection, the risk of poverty, marginalisation and stigmatisation can be reduced. i voted in favour of the report drawn up by the committee on women's rights and gender equality on homeworkers and carers in the eu.
in writing. ‒ today 2.5 million people work in the care and domestic work sector in the eu, 88% of them women. they work in public or private institutions, and private homes, without proper recognition or labour rights, and their work is very unevenly regulated across europe. i supported this report, which calls for recognition of the profession and value of domestic and care work, to reduce undeclared work in the sector and to provide for common rules by introducing a framework for professionalisation and guidelines. moreover, it asks the commission to propose a carers’ leave directive for non-professional carers (mostly family members providing care for the elderly, sick or other dependants). member states should ratify ilo convention n189 concerning decent work for domestic workers, promote regularisation schemes for irregular migrant workers, implement the anti-trafficking directive, and develop inspections in accordance with their national laws and the ilo convention. through the implementation of labour laws, we will be able to protect women domestic workers and free them from violence.
in writing. ‒ currently, in the eu, some 2.5 million workers work in the care and in-house sector in private institutions without proper recognition of the right to work, and the work they do is not regulated according to eu standards. i voted in favour of this report on the recognition of the profession and the value of domestic and care work to reduce undeclared work in this sector and to introduce a framework for professionalisation and guidance and the labour and health rights at work of domestic workers and carers in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that will tackle several problems in the domestic work and care sector across member states such as illegality, non-coverage by labour law, harassment, migrants’ specific issues, trafficking, social exclusion, poverty, lack of perspectives, psychological burdens, lack of access to information, protection structures and trade unions.
in writing. ‒ i endorse this resolution as the lack of common rules and regulation regarding domestic work and care across the member states of the eu remains an obstacle towards the protection of the rights and social inclusion of, most often and in particular, women of minority migrant backgrounds working in these occupations. furthermore, when not regulated under labour law, domestic work and care undermine social welfare systems by creating shadow economies. there is therefore a clear need to identify best practices when it comes to regulation of domestic work and care across the eu, encouraging member states to take measures to implement laws that guarantee the fundamental rights and protection of domestic workers and carers, thus creating work conditions that empower them and facilitate a better quality of life.
in writing. ‒ according to ilo figures (2010), the domestic care sector employs 52 million people around the world, the majority of which are women. in the european union alone, 2.5 million people work in the domestic care sector and 88% of them are women. most of the domestic work is poorly regulated, without recognition, labour rights or employment benefits, such as maternity leave and set working hours. this report calls for the recognition of the importance of domestic and care work and demands the implementation of common rules and guidelines throughout the european union. moreover, the report asks for the reduction of undeclared work and the promotion of regularisation schemes for irregular migrant workers. i support this resolution because i strongly believe that domestic and care workers have the same social and employment rights as any other workers.
in writing. ‒ the information society, driven by information and communication technologies (ict), offers immense opportunities both for promoting direct democracy and for generating and distributing knowledge or developing and modernising the labour market. despite the many benefits introduced by digitalisation, there are difficulties such as: the integration and retention of women in the ict sector, the effects of gender stereotypes or the misuse of technology to threaten and intimidate women's activities. the gender pay gap is also evident in the pay gap, where wage gaps persist, with 54% of women in the ict sector in a lower-paid job than a man with the same skills. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that european policies, the digital agenda and the digital single market strategy must consider developing mechanisms both to tackle gender gaps and to increase investment in social inclusion policies, to promote access to ict education for women and to respect the principle of equal pay, which is one of the fundamental pillars of social equity in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ the digital age provides for the empowerment of women in the labour market, and in political and societal participation and has the potential to contribute to more gender equality. however it also bears risks, especially for women, in terms of precarious work, violence against women such as sexual exploitation, cyber-bullying, trafficking in human beings and hate speeches via internet, etc., and therefore needs appropriate monitoring and legal framework. the report emphasises the potential that the information society, ict and the internet have to promote women’s empowerment. its influence can help to improve the participation of women in political and other decision-making processes as well as the promotion of gender equality in the labour market. in order to do so, further education and training in ict, and investment and funding for female entrepreneurs in ict-related businesses are needed. the report also stresses the need to fight violence against women in the context of a digitalised world and notes that cyber-bullying, cyber-stalking, trafficking in human beings and hate speeches represent a serious threat to women and ultimately, their empowerment. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights the potential that the information society, ict and the internet have in promoting women's empowerment. its influence can help to improve women's participation in political and other decision-making processes and promote gender equality in the labour market. this requires investment and funding for women entrepreneurs in ict enterprises. i voted in favour of this report for gender equality, the involvement of women in the labour market, combating violence against women in a digitalised world, online harassment, human trafficking and sexual exploitation of women.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that reiterates the potential that the information society, ict and the internet have to promote women’s empowerment. its influence can help to improve the participation of women in political and other decision-making processes as well as the promotion of gender equality in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ digitalisation represents an important platform for the economic, political and social empowerment of women and girls. the ict sector is growing and will continue to generate a significant pool of jobs in europe. as the resolution stresses, it is therefore imperative that stereotypes are deconstructed and girls and women are encouraged, for example through it focused education, to take up employment in the ict sector where they are currently significantly underrepresented in comparison to men. digitalisation is also promising in that it is a powerful medium through which to advance awareness of gender issues and inequality because of easy access to information. however, as the resolution rightly points out digitalisation can also be used in ways that are harmful to the equality and safety of women and girls. it is important that we work to prevent online violence and abuse against women and girls through different approaches and at various levels, strengthening online education and training but also prosecution of online offenders. it is for the above-stated reasons that i fully support this resolution.
in writing. ‒ in europe, women represent only 19% of bosses in the ict and communications sectors and 9% of developers, which is unacceptable, since the ict and communications sectors can promote women’s empowerment in all sectors of the economy. digitalisation has a great impact on the labour market and it is an effective tool for the promotion of gender equality to the younger generations. thus, i believe that women need further education and training in ict, in order to take advantage of the full range of benefits that this sector of the economy provides. furthermore, i stress the need to fight violence and gender stereotypes against women in the digital area and i gave my full support to this resolution.
mr president, i would first like to thank the rapporteur, mrs ruža tomašić, for her good cooperation in this report. the absorption of european funds has been a constant concern for all member states. in this respect, the european commission and the european parliament have sought to identify mechanisms and procedures to simplify this process, which member states complain is extremely cumbersome and difficult. i therefore welcome the identification of new territorial development instruments in cohesion policy 2014-2020 and the strengthening of the two mechanisms, namely integrated territorial investment and community-led local development. they will make a significant contribution to achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion, but above all, and i stress above all, to creating new jobs. it is also very important to create a framework within which it is possible to combine the flows of funds with local initiatives, so that we are dealing with a strengthening of the capacity of communities to organise and implement projects, which take into account the needs of citizens and always from the bottom up. the implementation process requires the appropriate identification of resources and strategic advantages, both by local and regional authorities, and effective cooperation between rural and urban areas, with a view to strengthening regional competitiveness. participatory performance-based budgeting should aim at the efficiency of european funds so that there is as much added value as possible. the european parliament and the commission must, however, identify further the mechanisms by which member states are obliged to simplify their process of absorbing european funds and at the same time expressly prohibit them from creating additional conditionalities over and above european provisions.
mr president, mountain ranges in europe extend over the territory of several member states, including third countries. in these areas, mountain agriculture, forestry and tourism are important sectors for the identity and culture of mountain regions, making an important contribution to employment and the continued diversification of these regions' economies. it is beneficial for europe to develop multiple agricultural production, in relation to the development of tourism and environmental protection activities and an appropriate structuring of the food chain in mountain areas. i support the rapporteur's proposal to initiate a debate on the introduction of special labels for mountain food at european union level. mountain areas have significant potential for the production of high quality food, which will allow for better promotion and marketing of agricultural products and their inclusion among the general tourist products of a geographical area.
mr president, cohesion policy is not a new topic, it is an obligation in the treaty. however, within the framework of the general cohesion policy, the policy for the mountain region is a special one and i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and all the colleagues who worked on this report. in my country and in many other countries in the european union, we have mountain areas. mountain regions face specific terrain challenges, often with access to resources becoming more difficult, with additional transport costs, climate change, no human resources, no vocational training, no infrastructure. that is why i believe that special places need special policies, and i particularly appreciate and support the proposal to harmonize agricultural policies with those of tourism, with those of the development of traditional handicrafts and handicrafts. and i particularly support the rapporteur's proposal that both the member states and the commission should carry out periodic evaluations in order to conduct an appropriate funding policy. in the mountain areas, we must support small and medium-sized enterprises, manufacturing and tourism. attracting young people to this area is extremely important.
mr president, europe's mountain areas must be protected and supported in their development. they must therefore benefit from dedicated programmes and local initiatives to help the people in these areas must be integrated into a coherent and consistent strategy at european level. personally, i lived in the mountainous regions of romania, specifically in transylvania. and so i can give you the example of the apuseni mountains, a region of great beauty, with unrealized potential, with over half a million inhabitants. the priorities of this area are valid for all mountain areas: infrastructure development, access to education and health, job creation or attracting investment. the communities in european mountain areas are a tradition for our countries and deserve to be treated with respect and supported so that the lives of their citizens are no different from those of other european citizens. in this respect, cohesion policy plays an important role and this mechanism allows the gaps to be reduced. we need to strengthen cohesion policy to make it more accessible and to have a greater impact in all these areas.
in writing. in romania, the mountain region covers over 30% of the country's surface. this region is characterised by a slow but steady process of depopulation. the lack of adequate infrastructure, climatic conditions and limited employment opportunities make young people reluctant to stay in mountain areas. raising animals, logging, harvesting fruits from the forest are no longer the jobs that encourage young people to stay in these areas. the european union can therefore use the structural funds, and in particular the cohesion fund, to finance programmes supporting the development of mountain tourism, while at the same time providing infrastructure for access to mountain areas. only by combining traditional mountain crafts with the development of mountain infrastructure and tourism can a decent living be ensured for those who want to settle and live in mountain areas.
mr president, europe is talking about energy union and energy security. you talk a lot, you don't put it into practice at the same level. the best example is the connecting europe facility: energy funding has been cut by over 50%. energy security without resource security does not exist. security of supply without diversification cannot be achieved. nord stream does not fall under any security rule, either as a source, which has proven unpredictable, politicised and generating conditionalities, or as a market rule, resulting in a dangerous reliance on a single source. it's obvious that gazprom is trying to increase europe's dependence on russian gas, south stream, turkish stream, nord stream. europe's passivity in relation to attempts to diversify in the southern corridor is incomprehensible. is there a need for active, financial, political involvement for the supply of gas to the european union from the south-east from existing or new sources: azerbaijan, iran, the black sea, the mediterranean, and the gulf of aden. involvement on the ground, not just in the debates.

in writing. ‒ the proposal on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the union aims to codify council regulation (ec) no 597/2009 of 11 june 2009. this proposal does not change the content of the acts, but only changes their form so that they are more accessible to citizens. it is important that the citizen is provided with a favourable framework for exercising the rights conferred on him by those acts. this requires greater clarity and transparency of the legal provisions so that these acts become accessible and serve the interests of citizens. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that codification of legislation is necessary to improve citizens' understanding of the provisions and to ensure the conditions for citizens' involvement.
in writing. ‒ the proposal fully preserves the content of the acts being codified. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that contains a codification of the existing texts without any change in their substance regarding protection against subsidised imports from countries that are not members of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that protection against subsidised imports from non-eu countries is absolutely necessary for the sustainable development of the european community and for ensuring fair competition on the market. in this respect, the report voted today reiterates the rules adopted in 2009, the latter being grouped together, a change of form necessary for the codification operation. last but not least, i am in favour of the provisions of this report as i believe its most important role is to protect and encourage domestic production and thus the economic development of the member states.
in writing. ‒ the unprecedented development of international trade in recent decades has generated an abundance of goods on world markets. this is in favour of consumers, who thus have a wide range of products to purchase. however, the commercial activity must be carried out within a certain regulatory framework, which offers all the agents involved equal conditions to promote their products on certain foreign markets. the european union is an integrated market which operates on the principles of a free market, but which has made it a priority to protect commercial agents in the member states against unfair competition from agents in third countries. thus, when a number of third-country traders benefit from subsidies from that state, they acquire an unnatural advantage over european traders. in these circumstances, the european institutions can and must impose a series of compensatory measures, through common customs duties, to balance the situation. the text makes minor changes to existing european rules in this area, which provide the necessary protection for the member states. i therefore support its adoption in this form.

in writing. ‒ making imports allows european consumers to benefit from products they would not have had access to if they had relied solely on domestic production. in this respect, the presence on the european market of products from third countries all over the world is a significant advantage. however, in situations where certain products of this type are made at very low (dumped) prices, which jeopardise the development of similar european sectors (and which cannot compete with these low prices), endangering the jobs of workers in the member states, measures are required to balance the situation by introducing proportionate customs duties. this document updates existing european regulations, which are sufficient to maintain a balanced situation at union level without substantial changes. i therefore support the adoption of this report in its current form.
in writing. ‒ the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and liberia lays the foundations for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the rational exploitation of fisheries resources in the liberian fishing zone. there are a number of fisheries partnership agreements signed by the union and third countries through which the eu provides technical and financial assistance in exchange for fishing rights for a range of fish stocks from a particular economic area of the partner country. the main purpose of this agreement is to provide fishing opportunities for union vessels in the liberian fishing zone, taking into account the standards of environmental protection, conservation and sound management of fish stocks. the union will also provide financial support for the development of sectoral policy in the fisheries sector. i spoke in favour of this partnership agreement because it promotes a partnership framework that strengthens the links between the union and liberia, favouring the development of sustainable fisheries policies.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the european union has signed a number of financial and technical assistance agreements for fishing rights for a wide range of fish stocks. i voted for cooperation between the european union and liberia. eu vessels can fish 6 500 tonnes of tuna per year against a total contribution of €3.25 million over five years.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this new agreement and protocol. failure to act by the eu would allow the emergence of private agreements which would not guarantee sustainable fisheries. the liberian authorities undertake not to give more favourable conditions than those accorded under this agreement to other foreign fleets operating in the liberian fishing zone. these conditions relate to the conservation, development and management of resources, financial arrangements, fees and rights relating to the issuing of fishing authorisations. in this regard, we particularly welcome the fact that liberia renders public any agreement authorising foreign fleets to fish in the waters under its jurisdiction. the protocol takes into account the priorities of the reformed cfp and its external dimension. i particularly welcome the inclusion of a human rights clause as well as ilo provisions on fundamental principles and rights at work. sectoral support will contribute to the development of the country’s fisheries infrastructure, to the capacity-building of the liberian fisheries authorities, and encourage local employment. although measures for the protection of the marine environment as well as observer coverage (15%) could be more ambitious, i fully support this very important sfpa.
in writing. ‒ this is the first sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and liberia. it will reinforce cooperation in the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. moreover, it will help the country to improve its fisheries monitoring and control, and the development of its fishing sector as well.
in writing. ‒ fisheries partnership agreements represent an understanding where the eu offers financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights. i have voted for this report that will grant the european union’s distant water fishing fleets access to the gulf of guinea’s tropical tuna. this agreement will strengthen cooperation between the eu and liberia as well as with other west african countries where important tuna fishing zones are located.
in writing. ‒ this eu-liberia partnership agreement encourages closer economic cooperation between the two parties in the field of the fishing industry and related activities. the agreement establishes the principles, rules and procedures governing the conditions under which union vessels may engage in fishing activities in the liberian fishing zone and the economic, financial, technical and scientific cooperation in the fisheries sector. the actions undertaken shall take into account the promotion of sustainable fishing in liberian fishing areas and the development of the liberian fisheries sector.
in writing. ‒ ocean fishing is one of the european union's main sources of food. it may be deployed both in the territorial waters of the member states and in the territorial waters of third countries. to this end, the union shall conclude fisheries partnership agreements with those states, which take into account the provisions of the common fisheries policy. at the end of last year, a similar agreement was signed with liberia, the first such document signed with the west african country. the agreement provides for the eu to allocate a total of eur 3.25 million over the next five years to grant the permission to catch 6 500 tonnes per year, subject to compliance with european standards of transparency, employment and full compliance with the standards of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and the food and agriculture organisation (fao). the agreement will be beneficial to both parties, allowing the liberian side to develop port infrastructure, combat illegal fishing, sustainably develop the fishing sector and economy affected by the civil war and the ebola epidemic and enhance scientific cooperation between the two sides. in conclusion, i support the adoption of this document.
in writing. ‒ since 1989, there have been a number of fisheries agreements with mauritania, which have allowed european vessels to fish in its waters. this new agreement comes with a number of improvements, which close the gaps in the previous protocol. this has helped a number of fleet fishing areas, including those for seafood, to increase fishing opportunities. the new protocol also sought to clarify the methodology for applying the rule requiring european vessels to donate 2% of their pelagic catches to disadvantaged persons. in addition, the focus is on increasing transparency, with mauritania committing to publish all public and private contracts with third countries. i voted in favour of this partnership agreement because i believe that mauritania's new commitments lay the foundations for strengthening a partnership based on transparency, mutual trust and non-discrimination between the european fleet and other foreign fleets.
in writing. ‒ european vessels have been fishing in mauritian waters since 1989. the agreement with that country is an example for the agreements concluded by the european union with other third countries. i voted to increase the length of the protocol to four years. this will lead to greater stability for the fleet fishing in mauritania.
in writing. ‒ mauritania is one of the poorest, least developed countries in the world, ranking 161 out of 187 on the human development index 2014. 42% of the population is living below the poverty line (usaid). the economy remains weak. the economy is therefore centred on mining activity and fisheries. support for the development of the sectorial fisheries policy of the islamic republic of mauritania amounts to eur 4 125 000 per year. this support meets the aims of national fishing policy and in particular the needs of mauritania as regards supporting scientific and technical cooperation, training, fisheries monitoring, protecting the environment and development infrastructure. the increase in support for the local mauritanian fishing sector demonstrates the european union’s resolve to bolster the development of the fleets in countries with which it has signed agreements, and its desire to export the model of environmental, economic and social sustainability that it advocates in its fisheries policy. some 30% of the population (42.9% of youths) remain unemployed. the protocol’s requirement to hire mauritanian fishermen (60% of the crew for shrimp vessels and pelagic trawlers) is therefore welcomed. i welcome this agreement and protocol.
in writing. ‒ the agreement is in line with the reformed cfp. we welcome the new commitments given by mauritania in relation to transparency and priority access for the european fleet. i believe that the agreement with mauritania should serve as an example for future agreements signed by the european union with other third countries.
in writing. ‒ fisheries partnership agreements represent an understanding where the eu offers financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights. i have voted for this report that will grant the european union’s fishing fleets access to mauritanian waters for a period of four years through the newly installed protocol on 10 july 2015.
in writing. ‒ the new eu-mauritania fisheries agreement addresses some of the shortcomings of the previous protocol. in order to increase transparency, mauritania undertakes to publish all public or private contracts with third countries and also to grant preferential access to its surplus to the eu fleet. the annual financial contribution to be paid by the eu to this country to allow european vessels access to its exclusive fishing zone is eur 55 million per year, compared to eur 67 million under the previous protocol. in addition, financial assistance of eur 16,5 million is provided for the duration of the agreement (eur 4,125 million per year, as opposed to eur 3 million under the previous protocol) to promote sustainable development of the fisheries sector and environmental protection in marine protected areas and coastal areas. thus, sectoral support was increased to improve european assistance for the implementation of the new sectoral strategy on the sustainable development of fisheries in this country. i voted in favour of the agreement with mauritania, which should be an example for the agreements concluded by the european union with other third countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation because it approves the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the islamic republic of mauritania, which is a normal course of action. we are looking at a mutually beneficial agreement, which is an integral part of the new fisheries agreements between the eu and various third countries. under this agreement, the eu will pay around €55 million a year for four years for the opportunity to fish 287 500 tonnes of fish that will reach the european market. it is also important to note that the funds paid by the eu will help the mauritanian fishing industry and support the authorities' fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, and the obligation for eu vessels to employ 60% of mauritanian personnel will help local communities and support the increase in the specialisation of the workforce.
in writing. ‒ the signing of fisheries partnership agreements between the eu and third countries has become a priority of the common fisheries policy in recent years. these agreements are intended, in addition to increasing the union's marine food resources, to contribute to the sustainable development of this sector worldwide and to economic assistance to developing countries. mauritania is one of the poorest countries in the world, with an alarming unemployment rate (30%), especially among young people (43%), where fishing accounts for a large proportion of the economy (5-10%). the eu has had fisheries agreements with this country since 1989. in july 2015, a new four-year agreement was concluded, allowing eu vessels access to fish for cephalopods, crustaceans, tuna and pelagic species in exchange for the eu contribution of eur 55 million, to which is added eur 16,5 million for the sustainable development of the mauritanian fisheries sector and the protection of the environment. the agreement is conditional on compliance with european standards of transparency and the involvement of a majority indigenous workforce (60%), which will lead to the development of the local economy. i therefore support the adoption of this document.

madam president, the 2008 treaty of lisbon establishes territorial cohesion as one of the main objectives of the union. territorial cohesion must be supported by cohesion policy and structural funds, in particular funds, to avoid territorial and demographic disparities, with a view to integration and development in the member states of the european union. the 2014-2020 programming period introduces the tools to strengthen cooperation between public and private actors, as well as policies for more sustainable urban development. in europe, growth can be generated by networks between major agglomerations and, in the absence of european public intervention, countries tend to prioritise investment in connections to the heart of europe over the suburbs. this is why policies aiming at greater territorial cohesion, especially in romania, where 47% of the population lives in rural areas, are a form of financing so that people remain connected to the territory, encouraging income generation, development and competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ the new territorial development instruments in cohesion policy, namely integrated territorial investment and community-led local development, were developed in response to the multiple challenges facing member states, with an integrated and territorial approach being desired. the dlrc is a particularly important tool for local communities, as it follows a bottom-up approach, placing accountability to the community through local action groups. iti is also a valuable tool as it tracks the region's situation on the ground, making a direct contribution to improving the untapped potential of the area. these tools can strengthen community capacity and stimulate innovation by encouraging entrepreneurship. i believe that both the dlrc and iti need to play an even more important role in cohesion policy, with the need for active involvement of both local authorities and civil society in the territorial development strategy. i spoke in favour of the new instruments because i believe that they can be used to achieve community development in the interests of citizens, with their active participation.
in writing. ‒ eu cohesion policy has a key role to play in promoting the development of the union's regions, offering tangible solutions that could not be solved by investing at national, regional or local level alone. given the challenges at regional level, cohesion policy 2014-2020 plays a crucial role in the shift towards investing in smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, providing solutions by supporting activities that tackle climate change, promote more efficient energy use and create new jobs for young people. at the same time, the new iti and dlrc territorial development instruments will provide the prerequisites for sustainable and balanced growth in disadvantaged areas. i support this report because, while communities will be encouraged to work together to identify their own development needs and resources neutralized using the dlrc strategy, iti gives member states both flexibility in the development of operational programmes and efficiency in the implementation of integrated actions through simplified funding. these two new instruments can play an important role in adapting to demographic change and reversing development imbalances between regions.
in writing. ‒ territorial cohesion has been recognised as a fundamental objective of the eu and enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. in this context, the new generation of cohesion policies for 2014-2020 places greater emphasis on integrated and reality-based approaches to boost economic, social and territorial cohesion. local actors often lack the capacity to develop and implement development strategies that are relevant to their territory. they need support, both at national and union level. this is particularly important for smaller towns and disadvantaged areas. i voted for the use of multi-fund funding opportunities to achieve a truly integrated approach to cohesion policy measures.
in writing. ‒ youth unemployment is one of the most pressing problems facing a large number of member states. in this context, i believe that local and territorial development strategies must include among their top priorities the fight against youth unemployment, taking into account local and regional specificities, and the promotion of public-private partnerships with the development of vocational training programmes appropriate to adapt to developments on the labour market.
in writing. ‒ two tools – community-led local development (clld) and integrated territorial investments (iti) – are the new instruments in the current cohesion policy for this purpose. it is expected that around 5% of the cohesion policy budget will be used for these tools. it is still too early to evaluate the effectiveness of these tools, however, some challenges can already be identified, such as fear for increase of local influence in certain member states, limited budget and the integration of multiple funds. the main problems identified in the report concern the lack of trust between the different levels of government. furthermore, the often weak capacity of local governments to develop and implement strategies for their territory needs to be mentioned. these tools should help the latter. the current cohesion policy allows for a multi-fund approach which seeks an integrated use of different cohesion policy funds, although this may add to the complexity of the usage. furthermore, difficult administrative procedures and additional, (unnecessary) legal requirements imposed by member states (‘gold plating’) may add further complexity to it. this is an issue which needs to be looked at, possibly by the high level group of independent experts on monitoring simplification for beneficiaries of the esi funds, recently established by the european commission.
in writing. ‒ i support this report because territorial cohesion, enshrined in the lisbon treaty, is a fundamental objective of the eu. the new generation of cohesion policies for the 2014-2020 programming period places greater emphasis on the use of integrated and reality-based approaches to foster economic, social and territorial cohesion. two new instruments have been introduced under the european structural and investment funds in the 2014-2020 programming period to meet the territorial cohesion objective: local development with community responsibility (ldcr) and integrated territorial investment (iti). the contributions of local authorities are essential to the achievement of cohesion policy objectives but unfortunately in many member states there is a lack of trust between the different levels of governance when it comes to the implementation of the dlrc and iti and this can be a serious problem that can seriously affect the implementation of the territorial approach.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it considers youth unemployment to be the most pressing issue for the member states, together with smes’ lack of financing, and stresses that local and territorial development strategies have to address these issues as one of their priorities. the report points out to the commission that more attention needs to be paid, in the review of that strategy and of the mff, to regional and local contexts, and to the specific circumstances of the areas concerned. moreover, improved coordination between the commission, the member states and the regions with regard to guidance for these tools is a must.
in writing. ‒ one of the fundamental objectives of the european union is territorial cohesion. i have voted for this report that will bring a new tool to be used at sub-regional level based on the leader experience of community-led local development. the new tools can also be used for delivering the sustainable urban development objective.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the new territorial development instruments in cohesion policy 2014-2020: integrated territorial investment and community-led local development. integrated territorial investment (iti) and community-led local development (cld) are innovative cohesion policy instruments that some member states will implement in this form for the first time and can make a significant contribution to achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion, quality local jobs, sustainable development and the europe 2020 objectives. we call for the development of strategies in the early stages of the implementation process together with regional and local actors, in particular in terms of specific and specialised training, technical and financial support, as a result of a real partnership between regions, member states and the eu. while measures adopted under these instruments should take into account the priorities of local actors, they should be aligned with the overall objectives of operational programmes, as well as with other national, regional and local development strategies and smart specialisation strategies, allowing for flexibility.
in writing. ‒ decentralisation of decision-making to regional and local actors is central to strengthening the objectives of the cohesion policy. i support this resolution and the creation of the integrated territorial investment (iti) and community-led local development (clld) tools as they will allow local stakeholders, well informed about the specific regional or local needs of their communities, to participate for example in making decisions on how best to use funds to create high-quality jobs to spur growth and ensure a more even economic and social development across eu regions in line with the objectives of the cohesion policy for 2014-2020.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy for 2014-2020 places a strong emphasis on the economic and social dimension. it will use two new instruments to this end: community-led local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). in this context, the weak capacity of local administrations to develop and implement strategies for their territory is worth mentioning. these instruments are intended to improve the situation, in particular by facilitating the integrated use of several funds under cohesion policy. for that reason, the proposal receives my support.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the new territorial development instruments in cohesion policy for 2014-2020. the rapporteur welcomes the approach, which considers that the bottom-up approach and the participation of local actors are essential for achieving the objectives of cohesion policy. it notes that in a number of member states there is a lack of trust between the different levels of governance when it comes to the implementation of the community-led local development instrument and the instrument for integrated territorial investment. this is an important issue that needs to be addressed as it can seriously affect the implementation of the territorial approach.
in writing. ‒ the present proposal on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment statistics aims to amend regulation (ec) no 184/2005 in order to align it to the new institutional context. it is therefore desirable to identify the powers conferred on the commission and to implement the procedures for adopting measures on the basis of those powers. the powers referred to are those for adopting delegated acts in situations where, for reasons related to economic and technical changes, updating of data requirements is necessary. it is also proposed to confer powers on the commission to adopt common quality standards and to harmonise the content and periodicity of quality reports. as regards the european statistical system, the commission has concrete proposals to improve the partnership within this system, to make the related activities more efficient. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the commission should be given powers to update data requirements and to ensure that they are adapted to the new institutional context.
in writing. ‒ the regulation on community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment is part of the eu's overall framework for monitoring the evolution of the economic situation in each member state and in the union as a whole. the development of reliable statistics in these areas is particularly necessary to monitor certain key elements, such as financial flows within the eu but also outside its borders. these statistics are thus useful to ensure that the economic policies of the member states are consistent with the eu's general guidelines. i voted for greater transparency of this data and for turning this statistics into a tool for economic policy decision-making.
in writing. ‒ i support the call on the commission to improve the quality of the data (article 4) and for a delegated act on enhanced foreign direct investment statistics, with improved granularity and transparency: this will allow for more detailed analysis of flows that are essential to a better understanding of the functioning of globalised economies. the revised text will allow us to better understand whether a foreign direct investment is leading to real job creation and greenfield investments or is just a complex legal construction for channelling funds in an opaque way (recitals 6, 16, 17, article 1) and to start compiling fdi data based on an ‘ultimate ownership concept’ (article 5(2)-(3)). this is also topical in view of the ongoing tax evasion scandals. eurostat has also agreed to step up efforts to enhance its website for a more user-friendly presentation of the data (recital 1). bad quality statistics played an important role in 2008 financial crisis. therefore, it is crucial to further harmonise statistics collection in the eu and improve the quality of the data collected.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. bad quality statistics played an important role in the financial crisis. we should have a harmonised statistics collection in the eu and an improvement of the quality of the data collected.
in writing. ‒ the eu’s framework that monitors the economic development in each member state also consists of european commission regulation no 184/2005 concerning statistics for balance of payments (bop), international trade in services (its) and foreign direct investment (fdi). i have voted for this report that amongst others, will increase transparency.
in writing. ‒ high-quality statistical information is a fundamental public good for academic research and informed public policy-making. community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment are essential for the development of sound economic forecasts and informed economic policy-making. member states should provide the data necessary to produce community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment in a timely manner, in an appropriate form and of the required quality. this proposal aims at harmonising community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. this is important to better anticipate future crises.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it brings the necessary changes to regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign services, which are tools for monitoring the economic situation in each member state and in the union as a whole. those amendments were necessary to ensure the alignment of that regulation with the provisions of the tfeu, while allowing for the revision of the data collection methods necessary for good transparency. it is very important that these statistics are adapted to the reality and needs of the member states and the eu in order to provide a correct view of the economic situation for economic policy decisions.
in writing. ‒ the outbreak of the global financial crisis in 2008 has put the european union in the position of having to identify new approaches to ensure that such phenomena are avoided in the future. such instruments include the adoption of a new way of producing economic statistics in an integrated manner at european level. these statistics must be produced in a high-quality manner, in particular with regard to foreign direct investment (fdi), balance of payments and international trade in services flows. in particular, consideration should be given to how isd translates into sustainable job creation and real economic growth. improving these statistics will also indirectly contribute to tackling tax evasion affecting member states today. this will enable eurostat to provide statistics that are as close as possible to the reality on the ground, thus enabling appropriate policies to be adopted in the areas concerned. i believe that this initiative will help to improve the lives of european citizens, which is why i support this document.
in writing. the regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment statistics is part of the overall eu framework which allows the monitoring of the evolution of the economic situation in each member state and in the union as a whole. i voted for the ep report on this regulation because the production of reliable statistics in these areas is particularly necessary to monitor certain key elements, such as the evolution of current accounts and financial flows within and outside the eu.

in writing. ‒ cohesion policy in mountain regions is a subject that has been of constant concern to me, given the importance of these areas both for romania and for all member states. these regions cover over 30% of the eu territory and contribute to the economic development of the countries, mainly through their specific characteristics, namely the diversity of renewable energy sources. these mountain areas have a positive impact in terms of combating climate change and conserving and protecting the ecosystems of these territories. however, it cannot be overlooked that these mountain areas have been neglected, in particular because of the infrastructure and the additional costs of their isolation. as a result, in the absence of investment, many mountain regions face depopulation and population ageing due to extreme conditions and their peripheral nature, which affects the natural cycle of generations and leads to a reduction in social standards and quality of life. this leads to increased unemployment, social exclusion and population migration. i therefore voted in favour of this report because i am confident that this policy of mountain cohesion will achieve better socioeconomic and territorial cohesion, ensuring the sustainable economic development of the mountains.

first vice-president of the commission. – madam president, the eu was instrumental in shaping the global 2030 agenda for sustainable development, and i see several of the key players before me here today. but new york was only the start; and europe has a duty – to itself, and to the international community – to lead in the implementation of the sustainable development goals (sdgs). the commission is committed to delivering its part in an integrated way, and we have made our response to the sdgs one of the priorities of the 2016 work programme. we will present to you an initiative in the course of this year on ‘next steps for a sustainable european future’ to map out the eu contribution. delivering on the sdgs is deeply entwined with our objectives under the 10 priorities of the juncker commission. vice-president katainen and i are coordinating this, while working closely with high representative/vice-president mogherini for the external side. this work builds on a solid basis. through the europe 2020 strategy, and through a wide range of eu policies, from climate change to skills and innovation, the eu is already delivering on many sdgs. one of the challenges in our institutions, in our member states, will be to prevent dividing up implementation between an international, a national and a european strand. what we do at home needs to be consistent with what we do in europe and internationally. if we are serious about the sdgs, we need to understand the philosophy behind them; namely that it is an integrated and universal agenda, and no longer the ‘developed world’ telling the rest of the world what they need to do. it is also us telling ourselves what we need to do. externally, the sdgs are already playing a big role in shaping our development cooperation but also more broadly. the commission will present later this year a proposal to revise the european consensus on development in the light of the sdgs and changing global trends. we need to address all three dimensions of sustainable development – economic, social and environmental. eradicating poverty, eliminating inequalities and combating climate change are not competing objectives; they go hand in hand. this means change in europe too. and 2030 is the day after tomorrow, if not already tomorrow. i strongly believe that if we take a hard look at our prospects as european society in a business-as-usual scenario, if we do not step up our efforts over the next generation, what we can hope to achieve in terms of structural economic growth is not encouraging – an annual average of perhaps 1 to 1.5% if we are lucky. with our demographic realities, that is simply not sufficient to sustain our social model, our european way of life. it is a very uncomfortable truth, but it is nonetheless true. if we want to be in a position to provide for our parents, our children, for everyone in need, if we really want a sustainable, social model for our societies, we need to move much more quickly to a sustainable economy, to a low-carbon, resource-efficient, circular economy. we need to make sure we enable people to fully participate in society. this is not about something that is ‘nice to have’; it something that is urgent and something we need to have. this is about competitiveness in the widest sense of the word. this is about the future of the european way of life. it will not happen all by itself. i am deeply convinced that new forms of governance and smart regulation are increasingly going to play an important part in that respect. to make this transition from where we are now to where we need to be tomorrow and the day after tomorrow, you need governance; you need broad alliances with businesses, ngos and society at large. this is what we need to create in europe, and i count on working with you hand in hand. the european parliament will lead on this. if we fall in the trap of only defending the past, all we will find ourselves able to do, is to slow down decline. this is about shaping the future. a prosperous future for all europeans. so the commission sees the global 2030 agenda as a tremendous opportunity – for europe, for the international community at large. an opportunity also for us all to overcome our own silos, whether they are in the services or between countries and between institutions. our intention is to make the implementation of the sdgs, like the circular economy, a team effort. we encourage you to do the same, and i look forward to work closely with this house on this agenda over the months and years to come, and with the council of course.
