in writing. ‒ the automatic exchange of financial account information is an important method of combating cross-border tax fraud and evasion, based on cooperation and strengthening of relations between tax administrations worldwide, while ensuring tax transparency. the protocol amending the eu-monaco agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information is intended to align the measures provided for by the agreement with the similar measures provided for in council directive 2003/48/ec, building on the latest developments at international level with regard to the automatic exchange of information, namely the global standard for the automatic exchange of financial account information in tax matters developed by the organisation for economic cooperation and development. the amendment protocol thus transposes the global standards between the member states and monaco with a view to strengthening the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. i consider that transparency in the exchange of information in the tax field is a prerequisite for combating forms of tax evasion, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ negotiations between the european union and monaco to improve tax cooperation and international tax compliance have been concluded with the signing of a new agreement ensuring that monaco applies enhanced measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu legal framework updated in december 2014. the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco implements the global standard for the automatic exchange of financial account information in tax matters developed by the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd), in accordance with and consistent with union law. i support the ep report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco providing for measures similar to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec, as i consider that this arrangement represents an important step towards strengthening the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. the eu needs to adopt a clear and coherent policy towards third countries in order to promote its standards internationally and ensure a level playing field.
in writing. ‒ in february 2016, representatives of the european commission and the principality of monaco initialled the agreement establishing arrangements for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts with a view to enhancing tax cooperation and compliance at international level. thus, as of 1 january 2017, it will be possible to combat tax fraud and tax evasion by developing a common tool that will allow tax authorities to identify, assess and investigate potential risks, and in the case of criminal offences, to authorise the administration and enforcement of tax legislation in cross-border situations. wishing to reaffirm the need for transparency on the issue of fees, both at the level of the european union and in relations with third states, i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco establishing measures similar to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec.
in writing. ‒ the european union and monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, aimed at improving international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement represents an important step in on-going efforts to clamp down on tax fraud and tax evasion and upgrades the 2004 agreement that ensured that monaco applied measures equivalent to those in an eu directive on the taxation of savings income. i believe that this agreement is in line with the need for more transparency on tax issues in the eu and in its relations with third countries. the eu member states and monaco will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts held on their territories by each other’s residents, starting in 2018 for information collected since 1 january 2017. i support its aim to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide capital representing income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. furthermore, in line with that oecd standard, i welcome the further provisions in the agreement which aim at securing that exchanged information concerns not only income such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets.
in writing. ‒ the european union and monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, aimed at improving international tax cooperation and compliance. i have voted for this report that will start in 2018 an automatic exchange of financial account information held on each other’s territories.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that in the current economic context we need to become increasingly active in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. in this respect, the report voted on today encourages the exchange of information on financial accounts between the european union and the principality of monaco, which will bring more transparency to monegasque banking and facilitate the fight against fraud on european territory. at the same time, the message we are sending to the world is that the eu is no longer tolerant of tax havens and i hope it will continue to do so in the future, by imposing more and more restrictions on companies and citizens who use these spaces to avoid paying taxes and duties.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the european union's fight against tax evasion in the member states, the european institutions have taken steps to adopt automatic exchange of information agreements with a number of third countries in order to improve tax cooperation and compliance with tax rules at international level. these agreements are designed to combat tax fraud and evasion on taxation of savings income, including through so-called 'tax havens'. the principality of monaco is one of the small european states considered a tax haven, where some european citizens hide their income. in this context, as early as 2004, the eu concluded an agreement with monaco for the application of equivalent taxation measures. the new agreement, signed by the european commission in february 2016 and to enter into force in 2018, will facilitate the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts held by residents of the two parties in each other's territory. this agreement will improve administrative cooperation procedures between the two parties in line with the 2014 oecd global standard. i consider this to be a salutary measure and i support the adoption of this report in its present form.
in writing. ‒ the importance of automatic exchange of information has been internationally recognised as a means of combating cross-border tax fraud and evasion. in this context, the organisation for economic cooperation and development has established a single global standard for the automatic exchange of financial account information, effective as of july 2014. the protocol proposes that the global standard established by the oecd shall apply between the eu member states and monaco. the new arrangement will allow member states and monaco to automatically exchange information on financial accounts existing in their territories as of 2018. this is information that has been collected since 1 january 2017. the aim is to avoid situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide his capital by representing income or assets for which no tax has been paid. the agreement also aims to ensure that monaco applies enhanced measures that are equivalent to the legal framework of the european union and that it complies with the procedures for the automatic exchange of financial account information. i therefore voted in favour of the protocol to the agreement between the european union and monaco.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the protocol amending the eu-monaco agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the eu and the principality of monaco have concluded an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information with a view to improving tax cooperation and compliance at international level. as a result of the new agreement, the tax authorities of the member states and monaco will be able to correctly and unequivocally identify the taxpayers concerned; administer and enforce their tax legislation in cross-border situations; assess the likelihood of tax evasion; and avoid unnecessary additional investigations.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund plays a key role in supporting workers affected by structural changes in world trade practices. in the present case, the european adjustment fund was requested by belgium to facilitate the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in three undertakings. the factors triggering these redundancies are both the decrease in public and private investment in infrastructure within the eu and the significant increase in steel prices in europe, which had a negative impact on trade, generating a loss of competitiveness for european construction machinery factories. by mobilising this fund, workers will benefit from various active labour market measures such as: vocational guidance services, job search facilitation, integrated training, job search and training allowances. i voted in favour of this request because i believe it is necessary to support workers who have been made redundant for external reasons through various forms of facilitating their reintegration into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ the economic and financial crisis, the recession and the austerity measures imposed in certain member states to restore the economy have often had a strong impact on the well-being of citizens. along with falling wages, mass layoffs and a sharp rise in unemployment, especially among young people, have caused a reduction in household income and, by implication, in the purchasing power of citizens. since 2012, following major disruptions caused by rising raw material prices and the relocation of various industries to asian countries, the province of hainaut (belgium) has experienced a rapid increase in the unemployment rate. believing that a global perspective requires first and foremost local action, i voted in favour of this report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, under which 488 displaced workers and 300 young people under 25 in hainaut who are not in employment will receive support for finding a job, training, retraining and vocational training, contribution for setting up businesses and social or mobility allowances.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report giving the green light for the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egaf) in belgium, mainly hainaut. the application relates to 488 redundancies of the enterprise hainaut machinery in belgium operating in the economic sector, classified under nace rev. 2 division 28 (manufacture of machinery and equipment) during the reference period 25 december 2014 to 25 september 2015. the egaf funding of eur 1,824,041 shall contribute to the costs of a coordinated package of eligible personalised services, providing assistance for 488 targeted beneficiaries following redundancies in three enterprises operating in the hainaut region in the construction machinery sector, as well, as for 300 targeted young persons not in employment, education or training (neets) under the age of 25, with the aim of providing assistance for integrating the affected persons into the labour market. the redundancies were caused by major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide real support to workers made redundant as a result of the global financial crisis. this fund may not exceed the ceiling of eur 150 million per year. the application by hainaut machinery for access to the amount of eur 1 824 041 for belgium from the egf, concerning the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in three enterprises, has been adopted by the european commission. i voted in favour of this report which provides concrete and effective measures for support, guidance and integration into the labour market, vocational training and courses in this respect, allowances for job search and labour mobility.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to provide belgium with €1.8 million from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to help 488 workers made redundant by several manufacturers of construction machinery in the province of hainaut (wallonia, belgium). the aim of the funding is to help these former workers to find new jobs. 300 young people not in employment, education or training (neets) will also be included in the actions planned. the proposal now goes to the european parliament and the eu’s council of ministers for approval. as rapporteur i have voted for this report that would help the workers and the neets find new jobs by providing them with active career guidance, job-search support, vocational training and retraining, promotion of entrepreneurship and contributions to collective projects. job-search and training allowances will also be made available.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the negrescu report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. i am pleased that, as a result of this decision, 488 redundant workers and 300 young people under 25 in hainaut who are not in employment will receive support for finding a job, training, retraining and vocational training, contribution for setting up businesses and social or mobility allowances.
in writing. ‒ the eu has set up legislative and budgetary instruments to provide additional support to workers who are suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns or of the global financial and economic crisis and to assist their reintegration into the labour market. i welcome the green light for the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egaf) in belgium, which will cover the 488 redundancies of the enterprise hainaut machinery operating in the economic sector during the reference period 25 december 2014 to 25 september 2015. the egaf funding of eur 1 824 041 shall contribute to the costs of a coordinated package of eligible personalised services, providing assistance for 488 targeted beneficiaries following redundancies in three enterprises operating in the hainaut region in the construction machinery sector, as well, as for 300 targeted young persons not in employment, education or training (neets) under the age of 25, with the aim of providing assistance for integrating the affected persons into the labour market. the redundancies were caused by major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. this is the sixth mobilisation of the egaf in 2016.
in writing. ‒ responsible exploitation of aquatic resources is required, taking into account sustainable economic, environmental and social conditions. this proposal is intended to transpose into union law the measures provided for in the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, so that the latest measures are applied uniformly and immediately throughout the union. a number of new provisions are needed to restore bluefin tuna stocks, including the progressive reduction of total catches, certain fishing restrictions according to zones and periods, a new minimum size for bluefin tuna, and measures relating to spawning and fishing capacity. the purpose of this initiative is therefore to restore bluefin tuna stocks by laying down a series of provisions on reducing total allowable catches and fishing capacity and strengthening control measures. i believe that the exploitation of aquatic resources, and not only, should always be based on principles such as sustainable development and take into account the protection of natural resources, which is why i voted in favour of this initiative.
in writing. ‒ the european union, as a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) - the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) - has responsibility for the management of bluefin tuna and other similar stocks in the eastern atlantic ocean and the mediterranean sea. the proposal drawn up by the european commission contains a number of technical measures relating to industrial and non-industrial fishing efforts, highlighting the low impact on marine ecosystems of artisanal fishing techniques and their importance for the recovery of tuna stocks and the economic support of smes. i voted in favour of this report, on the one hand, to draw attention to the importance of using transparent, objective, social and environmental criteria in dealing with the subject of fishing in european waters and, on the other hand, to affirm the importance of maintaining the codecision procedure in the transposition of the rfmo recommendations.
in writing. ‒ when dealing with this fishing sustainability, we must safeguard long-term productivity, promote local employment opportunities, encourage the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and a responsible exploitation of fisheries resources. unfortunately, the current bluefin tuna fishing quota system penalises small-scale fishermen, and needs to be reviewed. owners of large vessels are too dominant and might harm fishing sustainability. i therefore support transposal into union law of the measures of the multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) at its annual meetings between 2012 and 2014. i believe that the technical measures included in the multiannual recovery plan will lead to positive developments for environment, nature and local employment.
in writing. ‒ the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) has been the decision-making authority since 2006 for the conservation and management of fisheries, the most important regulated species being bluefin tuna. i voted in favour of this report for the effective implementation of the bluefin tuna recovery plan with a significant impact on the marine ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims at transposing into union law measures of the multiannual bluefin tuna (bft) recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) at its annual meetings between 2012 and 2014. i have voted for this report that contains technical measures such as those on transfer and caging operations of live bft, including also measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate the quantities of bft and releases, catch reporting requirements, and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i believe it is extremely important that these multiannual plans for the various fish stocks be adopted as soon as possible. the negotiation and adoption of this multiannual plan for bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic ocean and the mediterranean sea is part of the process of establishing these multiannual plans for fish stocks in eu seas as part of the cfp. multiannual plans are the basic instrument of the cfp, without which we will not be able to meet the objectives of sustainable fisheries and the protection of fish stocks set by the cfp. in this respect, the unblocking of this situation, which has been achieved today by the adoption of this multiannual plan, gives us hope that we will be able to achieve the objectives set.
in writing. ‒ stocks of bluefin tuna are particularly vulnerable to over-exploitation and therefore need careful management. i have been a rapporteur on this issue in the past and i am aware of the tensions and difficulties which can arise when setting quotas. however, if strict rules are not applied to ensure that catches are below maximum sustainable yields then the future of the fishing industry itself is put at risk. management of fisheries and enforcement of these regulations at sea remain big challenges with important social, economic and environmental consequences.
in writing. ‒ fishing is one of the european union's important economic activities, generating jobs, income and significant food resources for the member states. one component of this activity is the tuna fishery in the atlantic region, which provides significant quantities to the member states concerned. at the same time, however, the eu is a signatory to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), a regional fisheries management organisation which regulates maximum catch levels to avoid harming the biodiversity of the marine fauna in the area. scientific studies carried out in recent years have concluded that bluefin tuna stocks have been dramatically regenerated, allowing the eu quota to be increased. in those circumstances, the commission proposed a uniform and effective approach to iccat regulations across the union, including technical measures for transfer and declaration of bluefin tuna catches, the use of stereoscopic cameras, the obligation to land in case of overfishing. this is a constructive proposal, but the role of the european parliament could be more important in this area which directly concerns european citizens. for these reasons, i support the adoption of the present report.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation aims to transpose into european law the measures of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean adopted in 2006 by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), to which the european union is a contracting party. in order to restore stocks, recovery plans provide for a progressive reduction in the level of total allowable catches, a limitation of fishing in certain areas and during certain periods, and measures on sport and recreational fishing. the proposal contains technical measures on transfer and retention operations of live bluefin tuna and measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate bluefin tuna quantities. the purpose of applying these iccat recommendations is to have uniform action at european union level with a view to the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks. the report provides for the use of artisanal stock conservation tools and techniques to this end, through the implementation of the recovery plan. i therefore voted in favour of the multiannual plan for the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and for the fisheries exploiting those stocks is intended to establish a framework for the management of the many species in those stocks. given that herring, cod and sprat in the baltic sea account for more than 94% of the catches in recent years, it is necessary to provide for rules to allow for the recognition of interactions between the species concerned. even if there was a management plan for cod stocks in the baltic sea, it is not sufficiently adapted to the new conditions, especially as herring and sprat stocks are not included in any management plan. this requires a multi-species management approach, taking into account sustainable and responsible exploitation and ensuring the stability of fishing opportunities. given the importance of cod, herring and sprat for the baltic sea ecosystem and the strong influence of biological interactions and environmental effects on the baltic sea stocks, i believe that a multiannual plan is needed for the proper management of these stocks, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ as a contracting party to the united nations convention on the law of the sea of 10 december 1982, the european union promotes a prudent and ecosystem-based approach to the regulation of fisheries and aquaculture. therefore, to ensure the socio-economic and environmental sustainability of the policies covered by the multiannual plan, permanent, effective and transparent collaboration between the co-legislators and the european commission is necessary. in order to minimise the negative effects of fishing activities on the marine ecosystem, technical support measures should be introduced, the selectivity of gear and practices improved, conservation reference levels established and a global fisheries plan drawn up. i voted in favour of this report, wanting to express the importance of institutional collaboration, consultation with experts and specialised bodies in order to create sustainable fisheries policies.
in writing. ‒ multiannual plans are fundamental to reduce fishing mortality to rate which can maximise long-term sustainable yield. the current management regimes do not allow sufficient predictability concerning the proper conservation of the stocks, or concerning fishing opportunities for the fisherman. i therefore support changes in order to cover, in a single management plan, the three main fished species distributed in eight stocks in the baltic sea, namely two for cod, five for herring and one for sprat, with the aim to achieve and maintain maximum sustainable yield (msy) for these stocks. moreover, i support the proposal to set a target range of fishing mortality in line with the msy principle as from 2015, and a minimum level of the spawning stock biomass which fishing management measures should strive to conserve.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which is of great importance in ensuring that legislation is in place to identify the interactions between the species concerned, the influence of cod species on herring and sprat stocks and vice versa and for the exploitation of fisheries. the commission should include all fish stocks in the baltic sea in a single management plan. this plan would look much more closely at the problem of fish stocks in the baltic sea area with a view to an ecosystem approach to fisheries management.
in writing. ‒ the cfp is a set of rules for managing european fishing fleets and for conserving fish stocks. this is the first multiannual management plan under the reformed cfp. i have voted for this report that aims to ensure the sustainable exploitation of the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, while ensuring that management is based on the most up to date scientific information on interactions within and between the stocks and with other aspects of the ecosystem and environment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is extremely important that these multiannual plans for the various fish stocks come into force as soon as possible. the negotiation and adoption of this multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea was a very long and arduous process, due to disputes between the european parliament and the council over the powers held in this case. the adoption of multiannual plans for these fish stocks is the basic instrument used to achieve the objectives of sustainable fishing and the protection of fish stocks set out in the cfp. in this regard, the resolution of this situation by adopting this plan will help to adopt, within a reasonable time, future multiannual plans for the other eu seas, including the black sea.
in writing. ‒ i believe that a management plan is needed for several species in the baltic sea and i welcome the commission's proposal to revise the regulation in this respect. the multi-species approach is much more effective than the single-species approach and the plan should provide for the sustainable and balanced exploitation of these stocks and guarantee the stability of fishing opportunities and, of course, the sources of income of fishermen. the multiannual plans should also ensure that the management of cod and herring stocks is based on the latest scientific advice on the state of the stocks concerned, the interactions between species and other aspects related to the ecosystem and fishing activities. i also support the commission's position that the regulation should include rules on by-catches of flatfish. flatfish such as baltic flounder, flounder, helical and helical-net may constitute significant by-catches during cod fishing and do not expose cod, herring and sprat to any major risk.
in writing. ‒ the baltic sea fisheries provide an important input to the eu-wide fisheries sector. within this almost enclosed body of water, no less than 94% of catches are cod, herring and sprat, just accidentally flatfish and other species. in this context, the commission has considered since 2008 that an integrated management of the catches of the three main species is needed in order not to affect the sustainable development of the marine ecosystem concerned. scientific studies in recent years have shown that fish stocks among the three species are interdependent, the cod being predatory on the other two. in these circumstances, the commission proposed a common regulation for the management of these stocks in the baltic sea, which includes maximum allowable stocks for each of the three species, but also for flatfish such as hake. the document also includes a multiannual approach, encourages small-scale artisanal fishing and provides for periodic reviews every five years for more flexibility. i consider this to be an important document for the marine ecosystem in the baltic sea under the new common fisheries policy and therefore support its adoption.
in writing. ‒ in october 2014, the commission proposed a multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. this plan is the first to be proposed, based on the principles of the 2013 reform of the common fisheries policy. a multiannual management plan should ensure the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks and marine ecosystems. in accordance with the principle laid down in article 2 of the basic regulation on the common fisheries policy, exploitation must allow the populations of species to be restored and maintained at levels above those which allow maximum sustainable yield to be achieved. multiannual management plans for these stocks which are interdependent aim to keep the size of stocks within biologically safe limits. those plans shall provide for a maximum catch and a series of technical measures, taking into account the characteristics of each stock and the economic impact of the measures on the fisheries exploiting those stocks. i therefore voted in favour of the multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks.
in writing. ‒ this initiative concerns jurisdiction and applicable law, as well as the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters, by establishing which court has jurisdiction to rule on applications in matrimonial matters. this proposal comes against the background of the increased mobility of persons, which generates an increase in the number of couples made up of citizens of different member states living in a member state other than their member state of origin. the various studies have revealed a number of difficulties faced by these transnational couples, difficulties caused by certain incompatibilities between the applicable rules governing the property effects of marriage, both those of substantive law and private international law. however, the approach to the proposal in question is not common to all member states, and the reason is that the provisions are insufficient to create a homogeneous framework, which takes into account all the situations that may arise in this sector, which is why i chose to abstain from the final vote on this report.
in writing. ‒ matrimonial law is the system of legal rules governing the property rights and obligations of spouses, both in their relations with each other and with third parties. this regulation clearly determines the court with jurisdiction to rule on applications in matrimonial property regimes. if a member state does not approve the marriage in question, the courts of that state shall be given the opportunity to refer the case to the courts of another state of the union, which shall recognise the marriage in question. i support this report on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters, as i consider that the regulation meets the requirements of the european parliament as regards both the circulation and enforceability of authentic instruments and judicial transactions. the agreement is clearly beneficial for the union and is also an important step for international couples in the eu, providing them with new means of transmitting basic legal information.
in writing. ‒ the disappearance of internal european borders has led to increased mobility, both for tourist and professional purposes, with a significant impact on the number of couples of different nationalities. however, these transnational couples face a number of practical and legal difficulties, in particular in relation to matrimonial regimes and the property consequences of the end of a marriage. i believe that the legal security of european citizens can be guaranteed by adopting common rules in the context of property regimes, containing specific provisions on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments on the property regimes of international couples. i voted in favour of this report, reiterating the need for the rules on jurisdiction and related procedures to be consistent in order to ensure legal certainty and predictability for citizens.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the regulation is to establish a clear legal framework in the european union for determining jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of matrimonial property regimes. due to the free movement of people in the eu there has been a significant increase in the numbers of international couples or couples that need to deal with cross-border issues. these couples are currently facing legal problems in dealing with property, both inside their marriage, and when dividing property in case of divorce. matters already covered by existing eu regulations, such as maintenance obligations, especially between spouses, and matters arising from the law of succession, are excluded from the scope of the regulation. the regulation aims at providing clear instructions that will help international couples choose the law that is applicable to them, the jurisdiction of the courts and also in terms of the recognition and enforcement of decisions adopted in other member states. the regulation does not affect the existence or validity of marriage under national law or the recognition in one member state of a marriage concluded in another member state. i supported the report in the vote in plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because the regulation will be a very useful tool for international couples in the eu. the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law is thus protected given that the regulation excludes from its scope, in particular, matters relating to the capacity of partners, the existence, validity or recognition of a partnership, maintenance obligations and the succession of a deceased partner. it is also without prejudice to the substance of the law of the member states as regards registered partnerships or their property effects. the property effects of registered partnerships proposed in the regulation are clearly in the interest of the union and of international couples, helping to eliminate many cases of confusion and legal difficulties.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report with direct and positive effects on international couples and on the european union on matrimonial property regimes. by applying this regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters, legal confusion and difficulties will be eliminated.
in writing. ‒ due to the free movement of people in the eu there has been a significant increase in the numbers of families that need to deal with cross-border issues. these families are currently facing legal problems in dealing with property, both inside their marriage, and when dividing property in case of divorce. i have voted for this report that aims to establish a clear legal framework in the european union for determining jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of matrimonial property regimes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims to simplify the legal rules on matrimonial property regimes in the member states of the european union as regards international couples. the report voted today introduces a new regulation with clear provisions on the transfer of property rights in the event of divorce or death of one of the partners in the matrimonial institution. the regulation voted today also introduces a law of universal application, which ensures flexibility in the application of third country law. this regulation therefore puts an end to the fractionation of the law applicable to the matrimonial property regime of the eu couple, a subject of major importance for a very large number of romanians in such situations. through this initiative, the council and the european parliament are helping to clarify the jurisdiction between national and european courts to rule on property law cases in eu matrimonial property regimes.
in writing. ‒ the overall aim of this regulation is clear legal framework in the european union for determining jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of matrimonial property regimes. this is a necessary procedure in light of the fact that the free movement of people has led to a significant increase in the numbers of international couples. these couples have to deal with a number of cross-border issues, and are facing legal problems in dealing with property and when dividing it in case of divorce. therefore, the present regulation will provide clear instructions which will help international couples by allowing them to choose the law that is applicable to them, the jurisdiction of the courts and also as regards the recognition and enforcement of decisions adopted in other member states.
in writing. ‒ this initiative concerns jurisdiction and applicable law, as well as the recognition and enforcement of judgments on the property consequences of registered partnerships, by determining which court has jurisdiction to rule on claims on the property consequences of registered partnerships. this proposal comes against the background of increased mobility of persons, which is generating an increase in the number of couples made up of citizens of different member states living in a member state other than their member state of origin. the various studies have revealed a number of difficulties faced by these transnational couples, difficulties arising from certain incompatibilities between the applicable rules governing the matrimonial property regime, both those of substantive law and private international law. however, the approach to the proposal in question is not common to all member states, and the reason is that the provisions are insufficient to create a homogeneous framework that takes into account all situations that may arise in this sector, which is why i chose to abstain from the final vote on this report.
in writing. ‒ in contemporary society, although marriage is the most common form of couple, we are seeing new forms of union, including registered partnerships. it involves the formal registration in the public register of the union of two persons in a stable relationship. this proposal for a regulation on the property consequences of registered partnerships is of major interest to the eu as it clarifies a number of confusions in the application of previous legislation on the law applicable to international couples. we live in a mobile world, and recognizing the rights of international partners, no matter where they are, will put an end to the legal regime of fractionation of couples' assets. the major achievement of this proposal for a council report, which i support, is the unity of the applicable law, according to which the property rights of registered partnerships apply to all property held in the partnership, wherever it may be. the regulation allows for the choice of the law applicable to the property consequences of registered partnerships, but this choice is limited by the requirement to be a national of the member state concerned or to have his habitual residence there. in addition, this regulation respects the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law and is without prejudice to the substance of the law of the member states on registered partnerships or their property effects.
in writing. ‒ the possibility of free travel within the union and the mobility of the labour force have led to an increase in the number of couples with different nationalities. alongside marriage, registered partnerships provide rights and obligations to couples who decide to formalise their relationship with the authorities of the state of residence. however, this form of formalisation of the relationship is not recognised in all member states and there are major differences between the laws of the states which allow registered partnerships. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of property consequences of registered partnerships because i consider it an important step in facilitating the legal and administrative procedures faced by a large number of international couples.
in writing. ‒ i find it extremely important to establish a clear legal framework in the european union for determining jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of matrimonial property regimes. due to the free movement of people in the eu there has been a significant increase in the numbers of international couples or couples that need to deal with cross-border issues. these couples are currently facing legal problems in dealing with property, both inside their marriage, and when dividing property in case of divorce. parliament adopted its position on these regulations during the last mandate, and it is very regretful the fact that the council took such a long time to take a position. i welcome the enhanced cooperation and hope that other member states will decide to join, as this regulation will make life of european international couples much easier and offer them legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because the property effects of registered partnerships concern international couples, but also the principle of unity within the union, as it will reduce confusion and legal obstacles. this will facilitate access to basic legal information for international couples, although obligations relating to the existence, validity or recognition of partnerships and obligations relating to maintenance obligations or the succession of a deceased partner will remain the responsibility of member states. in this context, the legal regime of the couple's property will be clarified and well defined. this will allow data subjects to choose the law applicable to the property consequences of registered partnerships, but will be limited by the requirement of citizenship or residence in a particular member state.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, whose proposal for a regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments has a beneficial and positive effect on the property consequences of registered partnerships and on the european union. it is hoped that this vote will enable parliament to give its favourable opinion on this proposal without any substantial changes at this stage.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on a proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of property consequences of registered partnerships. the personal opinion was favourable, as this regulation will remove many confusions and legal difficulties in regulating the legal aspects of international couples in the european union. in this respect, the report voted today clearly establishes the court with jurisdiction to rule on claims relating to the property effects of registered partnerships. this regulation will also provide flexibility in the legal regulation of the status quo for international couples in the eu, giving them the possibility to refer their case to another court.
in writing. ‒ the overall aim of this regulation is to create a clear legal framework in the eu for determining the jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of the property consequences of registered partnership. this is a necessary procedure in light of the fact that the free movement of people has led to a significant increase in the numbers of international couples. thse couples have to deal with a number of cross-border issues, and are facing legal problems in dealing with property and when dividing it following separation. therefore, the present regulation will provide clear instructions which will help international couples by allowing them to choose the law that is applicable to them, the jurisdiction of the courts and also as regards the recognition and enforcement of decisions adopted in other member states.
in writing. ‒ the democratic republic of congo is in an alarming situation. the military and humanitarian crisis caused the death of about 5 million people. children have been attacked, women have been abused, a number of territories in eastern congo have been occupied by armed groups. various actors estimate that over 7 million people require assistance and support services. the humanitarian crisis is intensifying, with hundreds of thousands of congolese being forced to flee the country. the vulnerability of the congolese has reached a maximum in the context of the military crisis, and they need immediate support. i cannot but welcome the efforts of the congolese authorities to combat this crisis, but the improvements must be much more visible. immediate action is needed against violations of human rights and freedoms, urgent and political solutions are needed to resolve the crisis in the east of the republic of congo in order to establish public safety and security and consolidate peace, which is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ over the past 20 years, more than 6 million people have lost their lives in the civil conflict in eastern democratic republic of congo, and the situation continues to deteriorate despite the efforts of international organisations. the causes of this persistent climate of violence are diverse, including the lack of state institutions that could allow for dialogue and increased interethnic cooperation, conflict between paramilitary groups and the army, or the struggle of organized crime groups to gain control of numerous natural resources and borders to facilitate illicit trafficking. the deterioration of living conditions and the lack of progress in respecting human rights, together with the state of insecurity and uncertainty to which the citizens of that state are subject, indicate the need to increase the importance given to this conflict. i strongly condemn the massacres in the east of the democratic republic of congo, the recruitment and use of minors in armed conflict, the physical or sexual violence against children, women and men, the attacks on humanitarian workers and the silencing of the media. the european union's assistance must continue, in particular to develop state institutions and promote inclusive social dialogue, in the context of the organisation of the next presidential elections, which will play a major role in stabilising the political situation.
in writing. ‒ i am extremely concerned by the deteriorating security situation in the north-eastern part of the democratic republic of congo, by the numerous reports of massacres, recruitment and use of children by armed groups and widespread violence. i strongly support the call on the drc government and the the onu peacekeeping mission monusco to conduct an investigation on the failures of the congolese and monusco forces to protect civilians in the region of beni. a thorough, independent and transparent investigation to be launched by the international community into the massacres is urgently needed, in order to find out who is behind these attacks beside the allied democratic forces (adf). the neutralisation of all armed groups, safety for all citizens and stability in the territories of beni, lubero and butembo has to be our priority. perpetrators of human rights violations, war crimes, crimes against humanity and sexual violence must be reported, identified, prosecuted and punished in accordance with national and international criminal law.
in writing. ‒ the security situation in the democratic republic of the congo continues to deteriorate in the north-eastern part of the country, where dozens of armed groups remain active, with numerous reports of massacres, of recruitment and use of children by armed groups, and of widespread sexual and gender-based violence. i have voted for this motion for a resolution that calls for all parties to the conflict to put an immediate end to the violence, lay down their arms, release all children from their ranks and promote dialogue towards a peaceful and sustainable resolution of the conflict.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the worrying situation in the congo. recently, there has been an escalation of violence, which has led to a deterioration of the humanitarian situation in the democratic republic of congo. the humanitarian crisis is caused in particular by the armed conflicts in the eastern provinces of the country, which have lasted for over 20 years. unfortunately, too many lives are being lost in this endless conflict, and today, through this vote, i want to express my solidarity with the people of the drc. i call on the eu and its member states to maintain their assistance measures to the people of the drc in order to improve the living conditions of the most vulnerable segments of the population, in particular of internally displaced persons. i also want to condemn any attack against humanitarian personnel, as well as the denial of access for the purpose of saving lives or distributing humanitarian aid.
in writing. ‒ the european union attaches great importance to relations with african states in order to support the strengthening of democracy, economic development and social conditions in this part of the world. in this respect, a very good relationship has been developed with the democratic republic of congo, a country affected by military and civil conflicts in recent decades. currently, in the east of the country, a number of armed rebel groups are operating, manifesting themselves violently through the massacre of civilians and the abduction of humanitarian activists, promoting ethnic cleansing, illegal diamond trafficking, the secession of certain regions. the eu has been actively involved in humanitarian assistance to the population of the region and in supporting the country's armed forces through the un stabilisation mission in the drc (monusco). however, efforts made so far have not led to a remedy of the situation on the spot. at the same time, the government administration has undertaken a series of reprehensible measures against the leaders of the political opposition, which are likely to discredit the democratic system among the local populations. the present resolutions support a greater involvement of the eu institutions, in cooperation with the congolese authorities, in the resolution of internal problems and in the strengthening of democracy and the rule of law in the drc. i support the adoption of these necessary documents.
in writing. ‒ education and training are very important because they help people to acquire the knowledge and skills they need to become competitive and innovative employees. it also plays an important role in shaping human beings with an open mind, empathy and curiosity, but also responsible citizens with a strong sense of identity, with a deep knowledge of their culture and heritage, who respect and know the common european values. it is worth noting that the recalibration of et2020 is achieved both by reflecting the paris declaration of the minister of education of 17 march 2015 and by placing a very high importance on the objectives related to employability and the promotion of social cohesion, equality, non-discrimination and civic skills. i voted in favour of the report on the measures taken as a result of the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training (et2020) because i believe that the best possible cooperation at european level is needed in education.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the vet 2020 strategy is to support member states in developing education and training systems to enable all european citizens to acquire and develop the skills and competences necessary for employment and lifelong learning, covering all levels and contexts, namely formal, non-formal and informal. i would stress that one of the most effective ways of combating inequality and poverty is to strengthen education; i therefore note that the effectiveness and operational aspects of et2020 need to be strengthened and call for increased attention to the quality of education, starting from kindergarten and then throughout life, which will allow young people to adapt easily to the changing social and economic environment. the union needs to respond as quickly as possible to the current challenges, therefore we need urgent measures at national and european level in the framework of et2020 for adult asylum seekers who have recently arrived in europe. education is key to integration, and participation in training and lifelong learning programmes is an opportunity for newly arrived immigrants.
in writing. ‒ through european cooperation in education and training, member states have the opportunity to promote a range of education policies that favour the equitable distribution of knowledge among the population, reducing socioeconomic disparities and increasing social inclusion. i believe that access to quality education and training programmes is a right that must be guaranteed to all european citizens. without losing sight of the importance of acquiring practical skills for professional integration, it is essential that vocational education and training systems allow for the acquisition of transversal civic, social and intercultural skills that are beneficial to the development of creativity and critical thinking. by promoting democratic values and principles and by increasing investment in education, research and innovation, a truly inclusive system can also be created, significantly reducing the chances of extremist and radical currents emerging. i voted in favour of this report, wanting to reiterate the importance of non-discriminatory access to education and training, the transmission of social, civic and ethical principles and values, support for teaching staff and increased investment in this area. i therefore wish to encourage cooperation and the exchange of good practice, inspired by the different european traditions, with a view to undertaking ambitious, coordinated and effective policy action at european level.
in writing. ‒ i believe that communication strategies between school and parents and character building and other personal development programmes, implemented in the learning environment, in cooperation with families and other relevant social partners, can contribute to a bottom-up social convergence, to the promotion of active citizenship and european values. i also believe that an encouraging family environment is essential for children to acquire the right basic skills and highlights the value of parent training, which can be effective in tackling educational poverty.
in writing. ‒ the et2020 education and training strategic framework has been revisited by the council and parliament in order to strengthen its effectiveness, reorder the priority areas of action and increase its added value. the et2020 stocktaking exercise underlines the need to achieve the long-term goals while working on issues of country-specific relevance: low rates of adult learning, early school leaving, social inclusion, the gender gap, teacher training, etc. as the s&d group, we have included the need for maximum focus on social inclusion in order to reach the et2020 targets and improve the inclusiveness and the quality of education and training systems in a lifelong learning perspective, and we are calling for better governance and cooperation in this area. digital skills, high-quality early childhood education and inclusive education, to ensure equal access and opportunities for all, including access to mobility opportunities especially for vet and more vulnerable groups are all important. a specific chapter is included on migration and education, calling for the proper integration of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers in education and training systems. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which provides for the correct and effective use of the framework for action taken as a result of the strategic climate for european cooperation in education and training (et2020). education makes a huge contribution to the formation of the free, creative and knowledgeable european adult. vocational education and training are at the heart of acquired vocational skills. it must be encouraged both through effective programmes such as erasmus+ and by contributing to the added value of human potential, of future responsible european citizens with a strong sense of identity, with a thorough knowledge of their culture and heritage.
in writing. ‒ education and training 2020 (et2020) is the framework for cooperation in education and training. it is a forum for exchanges of best practice, mutual learning and the gathering and dissemination of information and evidence of what works, as well as advice and support for policy reforms. i voted for this report, which will put in place at national and european levels, including within the et2020 framework, education and training measures for adult asylum seekers who have recently arrived in europe.
in writing. ‒ i support the conclusions presented in this report, reflecting the findings of the follow-up to the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training (et2020). ensuring the quality of education and training, understood as encompassing formal, non-formal and informal systems, is now more necessary than ever in a context of high youth unemployment and further challenges. the follow-up to et2020 indicates that significant problems persist with regard to quality, accessibility and socio-economic discrimination in education and training. better coordination, both at european and at national level, needs to be achieved. this should include measures such as the extension of the work cycle from three to five years, the establishment of a new generation of et2020 working groups, a strengthening of the steering role of informal bodies within et2020, and the creation of an informal coordination body.
in writing. ‒ social inclusion has a key role to play in achieving the et2020 objectives. improving the quality of education and training systems is necessary to ensure opportunities for all, especially for vulnerable groups. we need all actors to be involved in the long-term learning/training process. good governance and close cooperation between member states are key elements in achieving these objectives.
in writing. ‒ european cooperation in education and training is voluntary, but a strategic framework sets the objectives to be achieved by 2020. this framework structures communication in the field of education between member states at the level of the european union. in this context, the report in question sets out a detailed work programme and benchmarks approved in successive documents between 2001 and 2003. i believe that vocational education and training should not only be about meeting labour market needs but should be a value in itself, as education has an important role in the development of civic and ethical virtues. for this reason, i support by my vote the recommendations set out in the report.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energy needs a new approach to make it the main pillar of the eu's energy model. it is a fundamental responsibility to combat climate change, it is a historic duty that must be fulfilled. the transition to a sustainable production model is a social priority that cannot be solved by the market alone, and democratic participation and regulation are necessary elements to avoid serious environmental and social externalities, which do not allow us to let energy oligopolies define europe's energy future. the eu has a legal instrument to help achieve this through the renewable energy directive. by adopting this directive, europe has initiated a process of transformation of the energy mix in the member states, a legal instrument which has allowed the establishment of a favourable framework for the development of the renewable energy sector and has contributed to the development of a diversified and varied sector. i voted in favour of the renewable energy progress report because this renewable energy source is needed for all eu member states, both to make progress on bioenergy and to combat climate change in the eu and beyond.
in writing. ‒ the shift towards renewable energies is of the utmost importance for the european union’s energy model. we need to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels in order to combat climate change effectively. with this, we must ensure the creation of quality jobs and the development of necessary technologies in order to ensure a successful and smooth energy transition. the adoption of the renewables directive has provided a legal instrument to create a varied and diversified sector, through binding targets and clear rules on supervision and monitoring. this has allowed many of the member states to work more effectively to achieve the targets set for 2020. since reducing greenhouse gas emissions also depends on achieving the goals in renewable energy, it is important that the measures adopted improve support mechanisms for renewable energy sources to ensure that consumers benefit from the technological advances. thus, i voted for the resolution on the renewable energy progress report to ensure that we will reach the targets set for 2020 and those of the cop 21 paris agreement.
in writing. ‒ technological advances in the production and storage of energy from renewable sources, the awareness of the need to reduce the impact on the environment in order to achieve sustainable development, and the need to increase the autonomy of member states in a period when energy is used in constraint policies indicate the importance of the widespread use of these resources. in this context, i believe that the european union and the member states need to set more ambitious climate and energy targets, exceeding the european council's target of 27% of energy from renewable sources in energy consumption by 2030. i voted in favour of this report, wanting to underline the importance of diversifying energy sources in order to build a true european energy union. responsible, effective and transparent monitoring of the implementation of existing european legislation, encouraging public investment and democratic control over the energy sector will make it possible to eliminate energy oligopolies and ensure an autonomous, sustainable and efficient energy model.
in writing. ‒ i believe that it is important to exchange best practices on national renewable energy policies in order to promote their adoption within a more convergent european model, fostering increased cooperation and coordination between member states.
in writing. ‒ continued investment in renewables requires ambitious leadership and commitment and a long-term, stable and reliable policy framework consistent with the climate commitments made by the eu in paris. in order to achieve our goals, the commission has to ensure full implementation of the 2020 renewable energy directive and put forward an ambitious post-2020 legislative framework. the fact that the european council decided to abandon the binding national targets and set a relatively low target of 27% for 2030, binding purely at european level, is highly disappointing. i support an eu that is on track to meet its 2020 targets thanks to the use of binding national targets. i will not accept getting rid of these targets and i will not accept the european council’s low 2030 target.
in writing. ‒ my country, romania, is in first place in the percentage of green energy in total energy produced, but consumers have had a high cost and it is not normal to transfer all the pressure to the final consumer. i did not support this report because it does not contain clear provisions on how to protect consumers from the increase in the price of green energy, it does not clearly provide for the involvement of the efsi in research for modern technologies for efficiency and decarbonisation. they also disagree with the fact that no account was taken of country-specific conditions and subsidiarity requirements in the energy mix.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which encourages the development of renewable energy at european level, which, by supporting the legal framework at european union level, would encourage public investment, democratic control and facilitate the collective and democratic management of this sector. the aim is to ensure a fully sovereign and effective strategic model by 2050.
in writing. ‒ by 2030, half of our electricity will be renewable. by 2035, electricity will be carbon-free. renewable sources produce alternatives to fossil fuels and aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. these sources contribute to diversifying energy supply and reducing dependence on volatile and unreliable fossil fuel markets, in particular oil and gas. the development of renewable energy (wind, solar, hydroelectric, ocean, geothermal, biomass and biofuels) is a priority at eu level. the report provides recommendations specific to each member state and may thus help more than 5 countries to achieve the targets proposed at union level. the old framework for promoting renewable energy - for example the promotion of biofuels in transport - also had a strong negative impact on food production. we need to have global coordination and planning of logistics and urban policies for them to become truly sustainable.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on renewable energy because a stable regulatory framework is needed in the long term. the transition to a sustainable energy system must include efforts in energy efficiency, renewable energy, the optimal use of europe's energy resources and smart infrastructure. the development of renewable energy should coincide with the development of a functioning internal market for electricity, ensuring a level playing field for all market participants. renewable energy needs to involve more stakeholders and consumers in the energy system. the commission should include in future interim reports on renewable energy an assessment of the impact of renewable energy sources on costs and prices, in particular household prices. the production of energy from renewable sources should be linked to the need to ensure the continuity of conventional energy production, as a prerequisite for sustainability, security of supply and competitiveness. the establishment of the energy mix of the member states should remain a national competence, as the energy mix remains highly diversified. finally, incentives for the development of indigenous energy sources, such as hydroelectricity, as a renewable energy source, remain a priority.
in writing. ‒ the renewable energy progress report assesses the member states’ efforts in the promotion and use of renewable energy. in the run-up to the review of the renewable energy directive and associated instruments, which will take place later this year, parliament took the opportunity to show its support for this legal mechanism that has an enormous potential to drive substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. although we acknowledge the growth driven by the development of renewable energy in various sectors, some constructive criticisms are nonetheless in order, to make the framework sustainable to the fullest degree. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution that seeks to orientate policy towards a cost-efficient and clean energy model for 2050.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energies calls for a new approach that entails making them the main pillar of the european union’s energy model. i voted for this report, which looks at progress towards meeting the eu’s 2020 20% renewable energy target, and also looks forward to the post-2020 framework.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union must continue and strengthen its policy of developing the renewable energy industry, a policy which is close to achieving its 2020 targets. due to technological advances in recent years, advances in the process of generation and storage, the costs of producing energy from renewable sources have decreased significantly. this now allows this energy to be increasingly competitive with fossil energy. i welcome the proposal in the report to step up cooperation between the european commission and the member states to improve energy performance from renewable sources, energy that consumes few natural resources, with the same qualities, and, not least, energy that reduces pollution and greenhouse gases.
in writing. ‒ renewable energy contributes to increased energy independence and reduced greenhouse gases. some good progress has been made. however, the 2030 targets need to be ambitious enough to send a strong signal for investment in renewable energy projects which are sustainable both economically and environmentally. sustainability criteria for biomass will be especially important in the coming years.
in writing. ‒ global warming has brought to the fore the need to develop the renewable energy sector. the european union and its member states have formally supported this process over the past decades, becoming the main promoters of renewable energy worldwide. however, the transition to the sustainable energy production model involves a significant regulatory effort, in particular at social, environmental and competitiveness levels. the first step was taken with the adoption of directive 2009/28/ec on renewable energy, which contributed to the development and diversification of the sector at european level. however, more ambitious political momentum is needed to achieve the targets set for 2020 and beyond. regulation of the use of biofuels in transport is now needed to avoid a negative impact on the food industry, a stable investment framework, the creation of new quality jobs in the field and the maintenance of binding targets at national level. without the latter, it will be impossible to make the progress needed to achieve the 2030 targets. i therefore support the adoption of the present form of this report.
in writing. ‒ the report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive contains several positive points, such as the importance of energy efficiency for achieving climate objectives, the need for better monitoring and clarification of the definition of smes and state aid rules. excessive reporting requirements are criticised and a stronger focus on energy efficiency instead of energy saving is called for. however, there are a number of important provisions, such as the 40% energy efficiency target for 2030, which in my view are neither reasonable nor tangible. i therefore voted against this report, considering that we need much more feasible targets.
in writing. ‒ greenhouse gas emissions have steadily reduced by increasing the share of renewable energy sources in energy consumption. the energy efficiency directive aims to encourage member states to invest in energy efficient technologies. while the scheme may aid in starting the transition towards a more sustainable energy system, the directive is poorly implemented, hindering its full potential. the unambitious target of 27% for improving energy efficiency in 2030 can only be justified by an extremely unrealistic high discount rate. in light of the paris climate change agreement, there should be a 2030 target that better reflects the level of cost-effective energy efficiency potential. this high discount rate overlooks the role of public bodies in driving energy efficiency improvements. there should be new innovative and smart solutions to better utilise renewable energy and to reduce energy consumption. for these reasons, i voted against the resolution on the implementation report of the energy efficiency directive. in devising energy efficiency plans, energy audits based on reducing energy consumption must be conducted to address energy poverty. there needs to be a more comprehensive approach to improving energy efficiency.
in writing. ‒ increased energy efficiency and energy saving are key factors for, among others, environmental and climate protection, strengthening economic competitiveness and job creation. the fact that the eu is not on track to meet its 2020 energy efficiency target due to poor implementation of the eed, excessive flexibility and too many loopholes is extremely disappointing. the commission projects on which we are on track reach 17.6% instead of 20% for 2020. we must keep calling on the commission to propose a revised text eliminating loopholes and taking into account a target for 2030 of 40%. the 2030 target should be significantly higher and more ambitious than the one set by the european council, which is only 27%. finally, i believe that the energy efficiency directive should prioritise measures to alleviate energy poverty.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the important role of energy efficiency in meeting the european union's target of increasing production by 20% and reducing co2 emissions by 20% by 2020. this directive represents an opportunity to optimise and increase energy consumption efficiently in a way that is sustainable for the economy.
in writing. ‒ this report has shed some light on a series of problems regarding cost reductions achieved through energy savings. i supported this motion for a resolution that calls upon the commission to generate clever solutions to problems such as increased energy prices for households and small businesses or complex reporting obligations. in view of a coherent climate and energy policy, the commission needs to make additional efforts to detect any ambiguities, inconsistencies or inadequacies between eu-wide rules on climate protection, legislation linked with energy efficiency and national approaches to energy policy.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this implementation report that looks at how the energy efficiency directive (agreed in 2012) is being implemented by the member states, and the progress to reaching the 2020 20% energy efficiency target, as well as looking forward to the 2030 framework and target.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i am convinced that the efficient use of energy is a matter of common interest for all the member states of the european union and has as its objective a common goal: reducing energy dependence on various other countries. we are also facing, and i speak for all member states, extreme climate events that can no longer be ignored. building on this, the report adopted today promotes the efficient use of energy and calls on the european commission, together with the member states, to strengthen and promote new technologies that reduce energy losses, to encourage energy renovation programmes for buildings and, not least, the use of energy from renewable sources.
in writing. ‒ much more work is needed on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive. energy dependency and energy poverty remain huge challenges, both of which can be partly addressed by improved energy efficiency. i applaud the work of my s&d colleagues on this report and their efforts to provide an analysis of the current situation with an important focus on energy poverty.
in writing. ‒ the european union has undertaken a comprehensive greenhouse gas mitigation process over the past three decades to slow down global warming. thus, between 1990 and 2014, greenhouse gas emissions fell by 23%, while eu gdp increased by 46%. by 2020, the eu's targets include a 20% reduction in carbon dioxide emissions, a 20% increase in the share of renewable energy in total energy consumption and a 20% increase in energy efficiency. however, at present the commission estimates that only 17,6% of the energy efficiency target will be reached, which seriously jeopardises the achievement of the 40% target for 2030. the reasons for this include red tape in energy reporting, high levels of energy prices for smes and households and special provisions at national level. in this context, there is a need to clarify the european framework for energy efficiency, as well as a series of measures to boost the replacement of polluting energy with renewable energy at member state level, outside the framework already created by ets certificates. i therefore support the present form of the report.
in writing. britain has voted to leave the eu. we need to start negotiations to leave the union as soon as possible. it's the decision of the british people. i regret this decision, but i respect it and it must be enforced as such. the confusion caused by the delay in triggering article 50 on withdrawal from the bloc is fuelling populist tendencies. confusion is a negative element, which can cause problems both in the uk and in the eu. i think what is needed now is political will and unity. the eu's founding principles must remain sound. free movement cannot be called into question. the 27 member states must speak with one voice. i do not think we can now talk about member states with more integration speeds or member states which are the core of the union. that is why i shall vote against the european parliament's resolution on the uk referendum.
