in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the decision of the united kingdom to leave the eu following the referendum of 23 june 2016. the european parliament stresses that the will of the british people must be fully respected, starting with the immediate activation of article 50 of the treaty on european union (teu), and that negotiations must begin immediately after the formal notification. any new relationship between the united kingdom and the eu cannot be established before the conclusion of the withdrawal agreement. in view of the critical historical moment for the eu, the interests and expectations of the citizens of the union must be put back at the centre of the debate and the european project must be relaunched. the eu must deliver stability, social justice, sustainability, growth and job creation, overcome persistent economic and social uncertainties, protect citizens and address the challenge of migration. in particular, the development and democratisation of economic and monetary union and the area of freedom, security and justice, as well as the strengthening of the common foreign and security policy, are required. reforms must lead to a union that meets citizens' expectations.
in writing. ‒ the resolution was adopted by 395 votes to 200, with 71 abstentions. i was one of the deputies who abstained. i could not vote for it because the resolution, while calling for reforms within the union, is limited to vague statements. in my opinion, the reforms must be radical and must be started now! any delay or delay will only aggravate the crisis in which the union finds itself. also, although the enf group, of which i am a member, submitted several amendments to the text of the resolution, none of them was adopted. i am referring in particular to the amendment which requires that no group of states can take decisions on behalf of other states, thus violating the principle of equality between member states. on the other hand, i could not vote against, because i am convinced that the uk must respect the will of its citizens and start the process of leaving the eu as soon as possible.

mr. president, this report is about reducing pollution and a cleaner environment. 15% of total nox and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the european union are emitted by machinery used in agriculture or industry, such as the railway industry or even the shipping industry and other industries. the report we voted on today imposes limits on emissions, even from the approval of the engines of these vehicles. we are now finally aligning european legislation with american and japanese laws and regulations, which are much stricter in this area. emergency equipment, such as lifeboats, is exempted from this regulation for a time. it is also important to say that once this agreement comes into force, companies will have 20 years to replace polluting engines. it's a lot, it's a little, i don't know. they have time to do that, and we're not forcing them to invest large amounts of money now. but we should move faster.
in writing. ‒ the proposal on emission limits for non-road mobile equipment contributes to the competitiveness of the european industrial sector by simplifying existing vehicle type-approval legislation, improving transparency and reducing administrative burden. this is expected to reduce the pressure on member states to take additional regulatory measures that could affect the internal market. it also aims to remove barriers to external trade through harmonised rules and by reducing regulatory barriers resulting from divergent emissions requirements. taking into account that one of the objectives of this proposal is to protect human health and the environment and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market for engines for non-road mobile equipment, i have chosen to express my support for this report.
in writing. ‒ several eu urban areas do not meet air quality standards – and the problem is growing as more people move to cities. non-road mobile machinery emits 15% of all nox and 5% of all particulate matter in the eu. studies have shown that these ultra-fine particles are carcinogenic. there must be stricter standards for more engine power ranges, combustion types and fuels to eliminate loopholes in the legislation and to negate the environmental and health damage they do. member states should have the power to prohibit the use of combustion engines for reasons of health and safety, particularly in regions of poor air quality. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation to simplify the current legal framework and address the health concern generated by studies on ultra-fine particles. through this, and by improving the general conditions for enforcement, member states can protect the health and safety of persons working in the vicinity of machinery, by prohibiting the use of combustion engines.
in writing. ‒ i support the non-road mobile machinery proposal, which aims to regulate harmful emissions from engines installed in so-called non-road mobile machinery (nrmm) – a term covering a wide variety of machinery such as construction machines, inland water vessels, trains, chainsaws and generator sets. emissions from nrmm engines represent a significant part of the eu’s total emissions of nox and pm: 15% of total nox emissions and 5% of total pm emissions. this is thus an important piece of source-level air-quality legislation to ensure member states meet their national air quality targets. establishing stricter limits on nrmm emissions is an essential component of the eu’s air-quality policy framework and will help member states achieve the required emission reductions, as proposed in the necd and the ambient air quality directive. the share of total nox emissions in the eu accounted for by nrmm engines is predicted to grow to 19% in 2020. at the same time, whilst emissions standards for road vehicles have become more stringent, equivalent measures for nrmm have lagged behind. this is why i believe a new legislative framework addressing these sectors is key in order to achieve the union’s air-quality objectives.
in writing. ‒ new data shows that non-road mobile machinery engines contribute significantly to air pollution and are accountable for 15% of the nitrogen oxide and 5% of the particulate matter emissions in the eu, while their share of total emissions in the eu 15 is predicted to grow to 19% in 2020. taking this into consideration, a new legislative framework addressing these sectors is key in order to achieve the union’s air quality objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report, which will generally improve air quality following the public health concern created by studies indicating that ultra-fine particles are a carcinogenic substance. the report will strike a reasonable balance between health and environmental concerns and the competitiveness of eu manufacturing industry, with the jobs and know-how it entails.
in writing. ‒ poor air quality is the number one environmental cause of premature death in the eu. it causes millions of premature deaths each year worldwide. it has been rightly described as an ‘invisible killer’ - causing heart attacks, strokes, lung cancer, and respiratory disease. we have passed legislation in this parliament to reduce air pollution from major sources, such as road traffic and industrial installations. these legal limits deliver real reductions in pollution and help member states reach their national air quality targets. but the investment needed to improve air quality cannot be made by one or two sectors. cleaning up our air means higher standards in all sectors, including non-road mobile machinery. if the short-term economic costs are shared, the long-term health and social benefits will be much greater. this legislation is another important step in cleaning up our air, to improve our environment and ensure people live longer, healthier lives.
in writing. ‒ reducing pollutant emissions is one of the european union's key environmental policy objectives. a significant part of these emissions comes from internal combustion engines for non-road mobile equipment. this category includes construction equipment, river vessels, trains, dredges and electricity generators. in order to achieve the eu air quality targets, certain limits need to be respected at member state level. the commission's proposal to this end aims to introduce new emission limits to reflect technological progress, to extend the objectives towards harmonising domestic and international markets, to simplify administrative procedures and market surveillance, and to provide transitional periods to enable manufacturers of such engines to adapt their models to the new requirements. transition periods are mainly concerned with emission limits for inland waterway vessels and the obligation to replace transport fleets in urban areas; therefore, generous time limits have been set, which go as far as 20 years. i believe that these are necessary regulations, which take account of the progress made in limiting road pollution and which are aimed at improving the living conditions of european citizens. for that reason, i support the current report.

in writing. ‒ the refugee crisis is currently one of the main challenges facing the european union's structures. the different approaches of the member states have led to the aggravation of the crisis due to discriminatory and protectionist tendencies. at european level, however, this crisis could provide a new opportunity for eu development in all areas if the focus of approaches is shifted from the defensive temptation of member states to an inclusive approach. this new approach envisages the adoption of integrationist labour market policies within the union, in order to support legal migration channels and to ensure respect for fundamental rights and non-discrimination. at the same time, access to education and training, housing, healthcare, social protection, recognition of qualifications and family reunification must be guaranteed. the processing of applications for international protection, in particular with regard to vulnerable groups (women, children, persons with disabilities) but also highly skilled persons, needs to be accelerated and undeclared work and exploitation, including with the help of civil society, must be combated. the hostile attitude of society towards refugees serves no one and therefore populist forms of exploiting the fears of citizens of member states should be abandoned and strongly condemned. the document presented here is a correct approach to the problem and has my support.
in writing. ‒ i support the need to implement all recommendations on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate responsibility, which were addressed by parliament to the european commission in 2010. stronger action is needed at european level in this sector, taking into account that the eu has the capacity to make a positive contribution to human rights and sustainable development worldwide through its trade policy. at the same time, the link between trade and human rights on the one hand and social and environmental standards on the other has become an integral part of the eu's trade and economic relations. i believe that the eu should use its trade policy to set high global standards in human and social rights, consumer protection and environmental protection, which is why i support this report and vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the eu’s trade strategy should be a tool for the promotion of democratic values in third countries. enhanced trade agreements and trade preference programmes could be used to promote human rights, eliminate forced and child labour, ensure food security and the rights to health, sustainable development, high safety and environmental standards, and economic opportunities. it is important for the eu to build cooperation at a multilateral level. there needs to be a more effective cooperation and regular dialogue between the wto and the relevant un agencies and wto trade policy review mechanisms need to be reformed to include the social, environmental and hr dimensions. therefore, i voted in favour of this report that will set human rights, environmental and social standards at both a unilateral and bilateral level. member states should actively promote responsible business conduct among eu companies operating abroad. by accounting for the impact of trade and investment agreements on vulnerable people and by using trade policy to encourage eu partner countries to adopt higher social and environmental standards, the eu will set a global standard to protect human rights, society and the environment.
in writing. ‒ this is an own-initiative report on implementation of the 2010 recommendations of parliament on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate responsibility, which among other things, calls on the commission to urge for a reform of wto governance, incorporate a gender-sensitive approach, include effective hr clauses in trade agreements, and further involve the ep in decision-making. i support the call for ambitious trade and sustainable development chapters in all trade agreements; for binding corporate social and responsibility standards, focusing on ‘enforcement’ mechanisms; to see civil society organisations and social partners formally involved in the monitoring process; and to support a gender-sensitive approach to trade. social, environmental and human rights standards in trade agreements have become of major concern to citizens. this report has raised concerns about the level of ambition the eu has to uphold these. we want to see legally binding and enforceable standards to hold corporations and governments to account, taking on board the important views of civil society.
in writing. ‒ i believe it is important to see legally binding and enforceable standards to hold corporations and governments to account, taking on board the important views of civil society.
in writing. ‒ the report places sustainable development at the heart of eu trade policy and reaffirms the role of the european parliament in making sure that the goals of the eu in this area remain ambitious and are systematically achieved. the report contains specific recommendations for further measures that could be pursued by the eu at multilateral/wto level, in bilateral trade agreements and unilaterally through the system of trade preferences for third countries. it also calls for systematically addressing eu trade and investment agreements issues like gender equality, tax avoidance or corporate social responsibility. i therefore supported this report that ensures that the european parliament remains engaged in promoting the necessary link between trade and sustainable development and sets the basis for the eu to maintain its leadership in the area of human rights, environmental and social standards.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that reiterates the fact that all religious, racial, ethnic and political groups should be allowed to develop in a single society valuing the diversity among both men and women. this approach should be integrated in eu policies, ensuring a better coherence with regard to development, effective policy assessment and coordination between development aid and trade policy.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased to support this report on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate responsibility. binding corporate social responsibility standards and greater involvement of civil society organisations will deliver better employment conditions and give more credibility to international trade deals. trade policy should bring social and environmental benefits, higher standards for consumers and better conditions for workers. the paragraphs on reform of wto governance, sustainability impact assessments, gender mainstreaming and greater democratic accountability are especially welcome.
in writing. ‒ the european union has a duty to set high corporate social and responsibility standards and the alliance of socialists & democrats has always pushed for ambitious trade and sustainable development chapters in all trade agreements. our group wants to hold corporations and governments accountable and this can only be done through binding and enforceable standards. i support this resolution as it reflects a good compromise on all the main areas. furthermore, this report incorporates notions of gender mainstreaming in all policies, which is a significant achievement and a great step in the right direction.
mr. president, the international trade scene is changing rapidly. the economic importance of the european union has declined, in 2050 it will represent only 15% of world gdp. economic power is moving east. japan will become the world's largest economy by 2025 - that's what economists are predicting. what do we need in the european union to move forward? we need, first of all, innovation, investment in research. without investment in research, nothing will change. industries, new industries, need to re-create themselves, reinvent themselves, but only after they have solutions that only research can provide. so the first thing we have to start from, if we want to grow economically and be competitive, is to invest in research and innovation and then put it into practice.
in writing. ‒ the eu is now the richest economy in the world. unfortunately, according to forecasts by experts, by 2050 the eu28 will account for only 15% of global gdp, down from 23.7% in 2013, so the centre of wealth generation will shift eastwards to the asia-pacific region. in view of this deterioration, i believe that a comprehensive and forward-looking trade and investment strategy is urgently needed to provide a boost to economic and trade activities. i support the need for a trade policy that responds to citizens' concerns and at the same time we need more transparency, commitment and accountability to all parties involved. i voted in favour of this report, considering that the eu's trade policy is of major geopolitical and economic importance for europe to shape globalisation, strengthen international standards and improve access to foreign markets.
in writing. ‒ trade negations have brought public attention to european trade policy. while many eu citizens believe globalisation will result in job losses, the contribution of foreign trade to the development of the european economy is important. as wealth shifts eastward, the economic importance of the eu in the world trade scene will decline. it is important for the eu to devise an effective, comprehensive and forward-looking trade and investment strategy. therefore, i voted in favour of this report so that there will be increased transparency and openness at all stages of trade negations and greater coherence between the eu’s commercial objectives and other aspects of its external policy on trade for development. this will enhance synergies between trade and internal market policies. the opening-up of trade will also lead to higher productivity, increased external competitiveness and brings significant consumer benefits. this future strategy for trade and investment will be a powerful means to strengthen sustainable development, promote human rights, labour and social standards and environmental sustainability worldwide.
in writing. ‒ the report contains parliament’s reaction to the commission’s ‘trade for all’ communication on its future trade policy. it welcomes the communication as a significant shift towards value-based trade in line with our group’s position but insists that the commission must deliver on its promises. the report reaffirms parliament’s previous recommendations on the ttip and tisa negotiations and its opposition to granting market economy status to china. since it is a horizontal report it does not prejudge any final position by our group on any particular trade agreement or the proposed investment court system. instead it refers to ongoing debates. the report emphasises the need to account for the needs of smes and the manufacturing sector in trade policy which must be in line with a re-industrialisation strategy and smes. it deplores the council’s inactivity on the reform of trade defence instruments. i believe europe needs to be open to trade in the interest of jobs and growth. but that openness needs to be flanked with the right international rules and domestic safety nets to ensure ordinary people can benefit from trade. i support the call on the commission to deliver on its promises on value-based trade and demand that the ttip transparency initiative is extended to all ongoing trade negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i encourage trade, not as an end in itself, but as a means to achieve prosperity and equality, to promote business opportunities, social progress and cultural understanding, and to increase jobs and raise living standards without increasing public spending. on another note, i believe that the new generation of trade policies must address concerns about transparency and participation, welfare and jobs at the enterprise level in a globalised and interconnected economy. it should provide for measures to combat prosperity and ensure a fairer distribution of trade revenues, addressing issues such as digital trade and the key role of smes in developing a sustainable economy.
in writing. ‒ europe needs to be open to trade in the interest of jobs and growth. we need commitments based on international standards, country-by-country reporting obligations and an automatic exchange of information. we also need the right international rules and domestic safety nets to ensure ordinary people can benefit from trade.
in writing. ‒ the report, adopted on 5 july as a reaction to commission’s communication ‘trade for all’ reaffirms the main themes of the european parliament’s stance on trade, notably the mainstream idea that eu trade should contribute to growth and jobs, promote sustainable development and be consistent with other eu policy objectives. i supported this approach by voting in favour of the report. i welcome in particular the emphasis on specific needs of smes, on the role of recognising professional qualifications in promoting new market opportunities as well as on digital trade and on the need to cooperate with trade partners to fight against corruption, tax fraud and tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ on 14 october 2015 the commission proposed the new trade and investment strategy for the eu ‘trade for all - towards a more responsible trade and investment policy’. its goal is to make trade more effective by constantly updating trade policy in order to continue delivering economic opportunities. i have voted for this report that will quickly increase trade liberalisation, further integrating the eu into the global value chains.
in writing. trade policy must contribute to ensuring a transparent production process throughout the value chain and compliance with fundamental social, safety and environmental standards. eu trade policy needs to keep pace with digital and technological trends, as cloud computing, mobile internet services, smart energy networks and online communication platforms are radically transforming the business environment. although services account for 70% of gdp in the eu and will provide 90% of future jobs, the eu's manufacturing industry must be a key component in reindustrialising europe. the strategy for reindustrialising europe must place greater emphasis on the role of this sector in the eu's common trade policy. we urge the commission to work with trading partners to ensure that their markets are more open to eu companies, especially in the fields of transport, telecommunications and public procurement, since their foreign companies still enjoy broad access to the eu's internal market. i voted for the report on an innovative and forward-looking new trade and investment strategy.
in writing. ‒ having the purchasing power of the world’s largest single market gives us the leverage to promote standards and principles to ensure that international trade benefits everyone. trade policy should create opportunities for all businesses, especially small and medium sized enterprises, and not just the large multinationals. negotiations should focus on ensuring that environmental, labour and consumer protection standards are improved rather than undermined. i especially welcome the amendments tabled to this report by my political group on environmental protection, renewable energy, labour standards and gender equality. i urge the commission to adopt these priorities in its ongoing and future trade negotiations.
in writing. ‒ the european union is one of the world's leading promoters of free trade. at the same time, however, the european institutions are the main guarantors of the interests of european citizens. when the latter are threatened by international trade, it is the role of the union to propose fair multilateral arrangements to allow free trade in the interests of its citizens. this report seeks to propose a new approach to trading activities at union level, in response to the commission communication of november 2015 entitled 'trade for all'. the main proposals are for more transparency, commitment and accountability to stakeholders, and the design of trade agreements to strengthen the development of human rights, social and labour standards, gender equality and environmental protection worldwide. at the same time, greater attention must be paid to the interests of smes in order to develop a fair policy of reindustrialisation and sensitive agricultural sectors and to combat illegal migration, as well as forced labour and modern forms of slavery. the union's trade policy must also be more closely linked to development policy. this is an important document which will help to increase the fairness of the union's trade policies, which is why i support its adoption.
in writing. ‒ we voted on the own-initiative report on an innovative and forward-looking new trade and investment strategy. i welcome the rapporteur's approach and the fact that she has tried to build a comprehensive report in terms of the objectives the eu should pursue in its trade and investment policy. the report focuses on a transparent trade policy and a stronger voice for citizens, a forward-looking trade policy that takes account of the specific needs of smes, or on creating new market opportunities for european service providers and the recognition of professional qualifications: a key element of the eu's trade strategy. welcomes the request to the commission to monitor, evaluate and follow up existing agreements, and the request to promote global trade through a multilateral approach in the wto.
mr. president, the profits of human trafficking have reached 150 billion dollars. less than 1% of these cases end up in a criminal prosecution and we have a final court decision. that means that less than 1% of cases can be confiscated or victims can be saved. women and girls constitute 79% of the victims of sexual exploitation. men constitute 83% of the victims of forced labour. now let's talk about the children: the director of europol said that in europe, more than 10 000 children, refugees and migrants have disappeared. i voted for this report because states must pay particular attention, particular importance and this must be a priority to register refugees, to follow them, precisely so that they are not stolen, not subjected to human trafficking. in particular, minors, who are a disadvantaged and vulnerable group, are at high risk of exploitation and as such are in the first place to be protected.
in writing. ‒ trafficking in human beings is one of the most serious forms of human rights abuse, profoundly and in the long term violating the dignity, integrity and rights of the victim. one of the obstacles to combating trafficking in human beings is the inadequate application of the legal framework at national level, as well as the lack of an appropriate legal framework in third countries. we need european and global action, bearing in mind that this is a problem that transcends borders and is therefore extremely difficult to solve at national level. an estimated 53.8 million people worldwide are trapped in modern slavery, which means that human trafficking is endemic and affects all regions of the world. we cannot afford to be indifferent to this data, we need to react and combat this phenomenon which is constantly expanding. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the fight against all forms of human rights abuse today also concerns trafficking in human beings, one of the most serious acts that profoundly violates the dignity and integrity of human beings. most often, vulnerable persons are victims, through threats or force, of exploitation, whether sexual, reproductive, forced labour, slavery or slavery-like practices. in addition, trafficking in human beings also masks an overwhelming gender problem, as according to the eurostat report for 2015, over 80% of the victims are women. this phenomenon is present everywhere in the world, both in rich states (the destination of many sexual victims, in begging or in illicit transplants) and in developing states (the country of origin of many victims and exploitation through modern slavery). this international criminal activity is a highly developed and profitable business, which seriously violates human dignity. i believe that states should make efforts and cooperate closely to change traffic from a low-risk, high-profit business to a high-risk, low-profit business. the eu's external role in combating trafficking in human beings is crucial and this report strengthens legislation in this regard.
in writing. ‒ the report describes the global trends in trafficking of human beings; it also underlines that the trafficking is a highly lucrative business and that the proceeds from this criminal activity are largely re-injected into the global economy and financial system. the rapporteur reports on the different forms of exploitation, the victim’s rights including the right to remedy, the cooperation against trafficking in human beings at regional and international level and the eu policy in its external relations. moreover, the report makes a clear link between trafficking in migrants and trafficking in human beings. i supported the report in the plenary.
in writing. ‒ the report talks about different forms of exploitation, the victim’s rights including the right to remedy, the cooperation against trafficking in human beings at regional and international level and the eu policy in its external relations. one major problem underlined in the report is that the level of international co-operation is insufficient on cases of trafficking in human beings, particularly where countries of origin and countries of transit are involved. the report indicates that the eu should develop a regional approach, concentrating on the so-called ‘trafficking routes’ and should offer responses which are adapted to the type of exploitation in the different regions.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that denounces and rejects human trafficking. the report stresses that human trafficking is a modern kind of slavery, a serious and transnational crime of global nature, calling for measures aimed to fight its root causes through robust laws against as well as improved cooperation between countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that human rights are universal and must be defended worldwide. in this regard, as stated in the document adopted today, the fight against trafficking in human beings must be a priority for the european union and its partners. i welcome the proposal in the report to step up cooperation between the european union, the member states and third countries to investigate and combat trafficking networks. last but not least, i appreciate that the report encourages the european commission and the member states to adopt legislation on organ transplantation requiring the provenance of these organs to be known, in order to prevent and stop illegal procurement practices.
in writing. ‒ an estimated 35.8 million people worldwide are trapped in modern slavery, and that is a shameful number. recently, 10,000 migrant children have been reported missing and presumably ended up in prostitution rings. a few blocks from the european parliament, on brussels' famous avenue louise, illegal prostitution has been running for years, unfettered. it is unacceptable that this is ignored by the belgian authorities. at the same time, websites promoting child pornography are tolerated in europe. this issue has been shrouded in secrecy for too long and we can no longer accept this phenomenon in silence! international cooperation in trafficking cases is insufficient, especially when it comes to countries of origin and transit, which is a major impediment to effectively combating trafficking in human beings. action is needed now to save human lives, now, not tomorrow!
in writing. ‒ when we talk about trafficking in human beings, there is always some financial gain in the network of criminal organisations involved in trafficking in human beings. in the current migration process, there is also a huge financial benefit for traffickers, who are often more organized than state authorities and who send migrants seeking a better life to more developed regions in exchange for large sums of money compared to eastern european wages and savings. unfortunately, the suspicion that the authorities of certain third countries are cooperating with these criminal organisations in order to prevent large groups of migrants from remaining on their territory and crossing into europe has not been dispelled. in these circumstances, it is indeed difficult to explain to european citizens that while we are talking about action against trafficking in human beings, we are also working closely with those states that support and facilitate this process. so i think that breaking the business model of human traffickers can be achieved with one tool, consistently protecting the external borders.
in writing. ‒ human trafficking is one of the most abhorrent practices that still persists in the contemporary world. unfortunately, there is a significant level of funds involved in this area and then they enter the international financial system and the global economy. despite measures taken by the world's states, this type of trafficking manages to be predominantly cross-border, affecting a large part of developing countries. at the same time, human trafficking also involves a number of migrants who try to make their way to developed countries but are exploited by traffickers. in these circumstances, the european union has a duty to act to strengthen international cooperation in order to combat this phenomenon of organised crime and to protect the victims resulting from this process. the current report identifies problems in this area and considers that eu policy to combat trafficking in human beings must be an integral part of the union's external policy. only in this way can the union gain the necessary credibility at global level as a relevant actor in stopping this type of phenomenon. i support the adoption of this important document for the future.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on combating trafficking in human beings in the context of the eu's external relations. the rapporteur calls on the eu and its member states to adopt a human rights-based and victim-centred approach and to place victims and vulnerable populations at the centre of all efforts to combat, prevent and protect victims of trafficking in human beings. the report also shows that trafficking in human beings, as a form of organised crime, occurs at both external and internal borders, thus requiring strong national legislation against trafficking in human beings as well as cooperation between countries. the same document denounces human trafficking as a highly profitable business, with the proceeds of this criminal activity being largely reintroduced into the global economy and financial system.

vice-president of the commission. – madam president, many thanks to all those who have taken part in a very serious debate today. i have listened very carefully and i want to start from the recognition that came from many of you that we have a new budget for a reason, and the reason is that in the eu we have invented one of the best achievements of the 20th century, the convergence engine that enables us to lift up regions and countries that are falling behind and, in so doing, to benefit everybody. we do that with the internal market, but of course the budget is the fuel for this convergence engine. for it to work we have to make sure that we spend our money carefully so that we can get the highest impact. let me sum up some of the key messages that i have got from the debate today. first, there is a very clear recognition that the world is changing, but our budget has not been designed to offer the necessary flexibility. we have to use the mid-term review to see how we can do better in terms of aligning the budget with the priorities in a fast-moving world. secondly, we recognise that, when it comes to that alignment, there are certain priorities that we have to concentrate on, as otherwise our citizens would not forgive us: how can we get more jobs, especially for our young people; how can we get more innovation to generate smes that push europe forward in competitive terms; how can we get a more hopeful, youthful europe, without which, i think, we would all be very depressed. i have listened to the conversation here and it is a bit depressing, if we are to be very honest with ourselves, so we have to concentrate on ways of using the budget to lift up our europe, especially the young people of europe. secondly, how do we deal with the migration crisis? it is going to be with us. it moves from one place to another, but in a world that is, unfortunately, so severely undermined by conflicts and violent extremism, given the geography which we have in europe there are no walls that can be built to stop the flow of people. of course we have to protect our borders better. we also have to find more equitable, fairer, and more dignified ways to accommodate the migrants flowing into europe. thirdly, there is a very clear desire for our budget also to play the role of flag-bearer in addressing great global challenges such as climate action. if we are not strong on that front we would be undermined all because of the extreme weather that comes with unmitigated climate change. and the good news is that we have achieved over 20%: 20.3% of the budget is to be spent on climate action. of course, we have to do more. the same applies to our role internationally when it comes to dealing with conflicts and the stabilisation of fragile countries. so in your next very clear message you turn to us and say look, we have all these demands. prioritise. we will need your help to prioritise. given the limitations of the budget, not everything can be funded on an equal footing. there are old priorities and new priorities. we will have to be very disciplined in aligning our budget with them. looking to the future, we will have to modernise the budget significantly, and modernisation is not only on the expenditure side. i want to thank mr arthuis for reminding us that we have to sort it out and be more systematic. there also has to be modernisation on the revenue side. obviously the monti group is there to help us, and we have to have the guts to come up with proposals that give us a modern budget. last but not least, the budget also has to be modern in terms of the rules and procedures that we apply for the use of money and it has to be simplified. in the past every effort to simplify things would start out with great ambition, and then we would all come along, – including, with all due respect, members of parliament – and add our bells and whistles so that by the time we were done, things, instead of being simple, had been made more complex. we have a unique opportunity. in the next six months we need to dedicate ourselves to making best use of this opportunity to have a modern budget that serves us to the utmost. i look forward to our cooperation in these next months.

in writing. ‒ i support the nis directive, which represents the first eu-wide legislation on cyber-security. its main objective is to improve security in the eu online environment and to strengthen cooperation among member states and european institutions in this field, overcoming the current fragmentation. the nis directive will improve cybersecurity capabilities in member states, improve their cooperation in this field and require different operators of essential services in important sectors of society, as well as providers of key digital services, to take appropriate security measures and report incidents to the national authorities. i welcome the agreement reached on 7 december 2015 with the council and i believe it will deliver important benefits for citizens, consumers and businesses.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this recommendation regarding measures for a high common level of security of network and information systems across the eu.
in writing. ‒ the directive on measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security in the union aims to improve online security in the eu and to strengthen cooperation between member states and the european institutions in this area. the directive lays down obligations for all member states with regard to the prevention, management and response to risks and incidents affecting network and information systems. it establishes a cooperation mechanism between member states to ensure uniform application of this directive throughout the union and, where necessary, coordinated, efficient and effective management and response to risks and incidents affecting network and information systems. it also lays down security requirements for market operators. the resilience and stability of networks and information systems are essential for the proper functioning of the internal market and this directive plays a major role in this regard.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it concludes the process of adopting the directive on measures for a common level of security of network and information systems in the european union. in the context of the development of the digital market and the increasing number of cyber attacks, i believe it is essential that the eu, through joint action by member states, enhances the security of its digital information and critical infrastructures such as energy and transport. this directive requires member states to improve their level of preparedness and cooperation to ensure a secure digital environment in which eu values and citizens' rights are respected and protected, including in the digital area. i believe that, in the context of romania's digital development, the security of these networks is essential to increase the confidence of users of the various online platforms that they are protected and their data is safe.
in writing. ‒ the security of the member states is a prerogative that has remained the preserve of national institutions, but the coordination of strategies can also be achieved at european level. a key component of european security is currently ensuring a high level of cybersecurity. following lengthy negotiations at institutional level, the commission has arrived at an optimal formulation of a directive for a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union. this is the first eu-wide legislative measure on cybersecurity, aimed at strengthening security in the european online environment and cooperation between member states and european institutions in this area, to overcome the current fragmented approach. the adoption of this directive will support the regulation of the information space in accordance with common standards and mechanisms. this is a significant step forward in this very vulnerable area which urgently needs to be secured for the benefit of european citizens, consumers and economic operators. i consider this to be an important step forward and i support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european union directive on network and information security aims to enhance cooperation on cybersecurity in the member states and to establish harmonised rules at european level to eliminate the current differences between national systems. this requires the establishment of national cooperation strategies and plans, the establishment of competent authorities in the field of network and information security and cyber-emergency response teams at national level. furthermore, they must provide for cooperation and coordination arrangements with other member states. providers of basic services such as energy, transport, financial markets, health and even the food supply chain, or those providing digital services such as search engines, will be required to take measures to improve their ability to withstand cyber-attacks and to notify serious cases of network and information security breaches, taking immediate action to ensure information security. i therefore voted in favour of the report on a high common level of network and information security in the european union.

in writing. ‒ respect for the rights of european consumers is one of the priorities that the european institutions must take into account. in these circumstances, it is very important that the labels of products offered on the market in the member states comply with certain regulations established at european level. one of these regulations concerns energy efficiency labelling. the commission has had a directive on this since 2010, but it has been outdated by technological advances in recent years and needs to be revised. what is essential is to provide citizens with information on the environmental impact of the product and its life cycle. the energy classes currently defined on the a to g scale need to be redefined to take account of innovations in the field. this will, however, only be possible after a longer conversion period of at least 5 years. this will also allow the development of a new database of products on the european market, capable of competing with databases already existing in other parts of the world. i think that this is a necessary revision, which is why i support the adoption of this report.

in writing. ‒ protecting the eu’s borders means strengthening frontex and enhancing its mandate, taking ambitious steps towards the establishment of a european border and coast guard. this will strengthen the eu’s ability to deploy resources quickly when a crisis occurs. the eu cannot ignore the reality of the challenge faced today in member states managing the union’s external borders. the external border remains the most important single point for establishing the stability of asylum and migration policy as a whole. it is a strong external border which allows us to free up our internal borders through the schengen area, and to guarantee free movement of people. therefore, we must work more closely together to manage our external borders.
in writing. ‒ the schengen area comprises 26 countries that have abolished their border controls and implies free movement of citizens, one of the greatest visible achievements of european integration. because of the migrant crisis, considered by some countries as a threat to internal security, eight of them have reintroduced border controls. these are belgium, denmark, germany, hungary, austria, slovenia, sweden and norway, followed by france and malta to apply the same tactic. i voted in favour of this legislative resolution which addresses the need to ensure proper control of the schengen external border in order to ensure a high level of security, while at the same time not restricting the free movement of citizens within the european union. the adoption of this resolution, which is an emergency, also aims to strengthen external border control and return to a situation without border controls in the schengen area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the extension of the tasks and capacity of frontex is a necessary step towards the implementation of integrated border management at union level. member states need better coordination to be able to carry out rescue and return operations for irregularly staying migrants, as well as increased operational and technical assistance through joint operations and rapid border interventions. cooperation and coordination of the activities of the new border and coast guard agency with europol, eurojust and eurosur will become essential to support and strengthen the actions of the member states. preventing and combating crossborder organised crime, disrupting trafficking networks, and cooperation between national investigating and prosecuting authorities are objectives which, if pursued at european level, can be much more effective. last but not least, the new agency should monitor the level of security at all external borders and contribute to addressing the lack of harmonisation of union standards on border security. without a clear definition and uninterrupted application of common criteria for securing borders, the eu will not be able to ensure a high and uniform level of security and, consequently, an effective implementation of migration policy.
in writing. ‒ the schengen area, as an area of 26 countries without internal border control in which persons may move freely, is rightly considered by many as among the biggest and most visible achievements of european integration. i have voted for this report that will ensure the proper control of the schengen external border as a precondition to manage migration effectively, insuring a high level of security while safeguarding the free movement of persons within the eu.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to abstain from voting today on the report on the establishment of the european border and coast guard, as i consider it unfair that non-schengen states are being asked to get involved in this structure. of course, this structure could help to make the eu's borders more efficient and secure, but i cannot support a project that, once again, requires romania to be involved on an equal footing with the schengen countries, without our country being accepted in this area.
in writing. ‒ the intensification of migration to the eu member states has raised a number of issues in the management of the union's external and internal borders. a number of member states have called for the temporary suspension of the provisions of the schengen agreement on grounds of internal security, due to the permeability of the eu's external borders. the management of the external border is currently ensured by the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders (frontex), but in the current circumstances, ensuring the security of the union's maritime borders requires the development of a new and more efficient framework. the establishment of the european border and coast guard (ebcg), with the assistance of similar authorities in the member states, would implement the concept of european integrated border management, acting as a preventive mechanism to avoid ineffective external border control, by deploying liaison officers in the member states, following the establishment of a reserve of 1 500 border guards, and by establishing a stronger role of the agency in the field of return and enhanced cooperation with third countries. this european effort will not be possible, however, without the political commitment of all member states and without the appropriate allocation of resources from the community budget. i support the current report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european border and coast guard. the schengen area is considered one of the greatest and most visible achievements of european integration. as eight schengen states - belgium, denmark, germany, hungary, austria, slovenia, sweden and norway - have now reintroduced border controls under pressure from the wave of migrants, it is imperative to address the identified weaknesses and to find effective solutions leading to the preservation of free movement within the schengen area. the proposal on european border and coast guard addresses the need to ensure adequate control at the external border of the schengen area as a precondition for effective migration management, in order to ensure a high level of security in the union while safeguarding the free movement of persons within its territory.
in writing. ‒ this initiative proposes enhanced cooperation between the european maritime safety agency, the european border and coast guard agency and the european fisheries control agency to support authorities performing coast guard functions at national and union level and, where appropriate, at international level through a series of concrete measures. it is intended to share information by aggregating and analysing data available in ship reporting systems and other computer systems hosted by or accessible to the agencies, in accordance with their legal bases and without prejudice to the ownership of data by member states. furthermore, another measure is the provision of state-of-the-art surveillance and communication services, capacity building through the development of guidelines, recommendations and best practices and capacity sharing. i voted in favour of this initiative because i believe that european cooperation in the field of coast guard is necessary, and that there is a need for greater coordination between european agencies, so that there is cohesion between the services provided and at the same time a high level of safety is ensured.
in writing. ‒ the european maritime safety agency, in cooperation with the european border and coast guard agency and the european fisheries control agency, supports authorities performing coast guard functions at both national and union level by providing surveillance and communication services, through staff exchange and, not least, through information exchange. i voted for better functioning of maritime surveillance and for better solving the problems arising from this environment.

in writing. ‒ the european maritime safety agency is one of the eu’s decentralised agencies. based in lisbon, the agency provides technical assistance and support to the commission and member states in the development and implementation of eu legislation on maritime safety, pollution by ships and maritime security. i have voted for this report that will modify regulation no 1406/2002 for establishing a european maritime safety agency with the purpose of ensuring a high, uniform and effective level of maritime safety and prevention of pollution by ships.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it concludes the process of changing the legislation with a view to developing systems of cooperation between this agency, the european fisheries control agency and the european border and coast guard. i believe that the exchange of information and data between the three agencies, each with its own procedures and technologies for monitoring coastal areas, will help to identify and manage crisis situations more promptly and effectively.
in writing. ‒ the european union's maritime activity is one of the most important transport sectors on our continent. for this reason, ensuring security and safety in this area is one of the priorities of the european institutions. to this end, the commission has proposed a legislative package to strengthen the protection of the union's external maritime borders by establishing the european border and coast guard (ebcg), the european maritime safety agency (emsa) and by revising the role of the community fisheries control agency (efca). the proposal aims at cooperation between the three entities and similar national authorities of the member states, through the exchange of maritime information, surveillance and communication services based on the latest information technologies, including gps, the development of guides to good practice and recommendations, support for training and exchange of experience of specialised staff at national level, pooling of planning and implementation capacities. i consider this to be a key document in this area and support the commission's proposal and the report as proposed by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe).
in writing. ‒ this initiative proposes enhanced cooperation between the european fisheries control agency, the european border and coast guard agency and the european maritime safety agency to support authorities carrying out coast guard functions at national and union level and, where appropriate, at international level through a series of concrete measures. it is intended to share information by aggregating and analysing data available in ship reporting systems and other computer systems hosted by or accessible to the agencies, in accordance with their legal bases and without prejudice to the ownership of data by member states. furthermore, another measure is the provision of state-of-the-art surveillance and communication services, capacity building through the development of guidelines, recommendations and best practices and capacity sharing. i voted in favour of this initiative because i believe that european cooperation in the field of coast guard is necessary, and that there is a need for greater coordination between european agencies, so that there is cohesion between the services provided and, at the same time, a high level of safety is ensured.
in writing. ‒ national authorities performing coast guard functions are responsible for a wide range of tasks in diverse areas such as safety, security, rescue at sea, border control, customs control, environmental protection and law enforcement in general. at european level, there are currently 316 such national authorities. these numerous authorities work together through 70 different structures. for this reason, the current system of cooperation is lagging behind and lacking in clarity. i voted for strengthening the capacity to respond to the maritime threats and risks facing the european union by improving cooperation between european agencies, but also with all civil and military actors.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the adoption of this report enables the three agencies to coordinate their operations at sea and exchange information useful for their actions, pooling their action capacities and exchanging surveillance information for the benefit of maritime safety and security.
in writing. ‒ national authorities that carry out coastguard functions are responsible for a large number of tasks in areas as wide-ranging as maritime safety, security, search and rescue, border controls, customs checks, environmental protection and law enforcement in general. under this proposal, maritime surveillance, prevention and control operations will be coordinated at eu level in order to improve maritime awareness and support operations that are consistent and cost-effective. i welcome the proposal, which seeks to bring the powers and responsibilities of the european fisheries control agency into line with those of the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency as regards cooperation on coastguard functions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which involves aligning the tasks of the three agencies, the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency, on the cooperation of coast guard functions. the objective of this proposal is to strengthen the capacity to respond to the maritime threats and risks facing the european union and to improve cooperation between european agencies.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that aims to enable the three european agencies (european fisheries control agency, european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency) who are dealing with disasters at sea to coordinate their operations at sea and share information with regards to their activities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it supports the conclusions of the negotiations between the european parliament and the council on the way in which the european fisheries control agency operates and is involved in cooperation with the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard. the expertise of the fisheries control agency, together with the constant data and information it collects through vessel and catch monitoring systems, will help to identify possible irregularities or crisis situations falling within the remit of the other agencies. at the same time, cooperation with other structures and more effective coordination between civil and military authorities with coast guard responsibilities will help the european fisheries control agency to combat iuu fishing and ensure the correct application of the cfp principles and rules.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 768/2005 establishing a community fisheries control agency. the report calls on the three european agencies dealing with disasters at sea, among other things, to coordinate their operations and exchange information. the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency should be able to cooperate by pooling their capabilities and exchanging surveillance information for the benefit of maritime safety and security. the aim of this proposal is to strengthen the capacity to respond to the maritime threats and risks facing the european union, in particular by improving cooperation between european agencies, but also with all civil and military actors. cooperation would avoid duplication of effort, ensuring that european agencies act in a coherent and effective manner to develop synergies.
in writing. fisheries are governed by precise rules at eu level, which give coherence to community policy in this area. an important element in this regard is ensuring maritime security and safety, which involves in particular rescue at sea, border control, customs control and environmental protection. unfortunately, the existence of a high degree of fragmentation between the various national maritime authorities makes it impossible to have a policy with a minimum of coherence at european level. in order to strengthen cooperation and interoperability between national institutions, the commission proposed to review the competence of the european fisheries control agency (efca) to include cooperation on coast guard tasks. cooperation will include, through coordinated action with the european maritime safety agency (emsa) and the european border and coast guard (ebcg), systematic exchanges of relevant information, the provision of surveillance and communication services, awareness-raising on maritime security and safety issues, rescue at sea, fisheries and border control, and the conduct of multidimensional operations. the coordination of the resources of the three entities will be beneficial for the most efficient action in the field of maritime safety, including the implementation of the fishing activity under appropriate conditions. i support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the importance of strengthening the independence of the secretariat of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office has been underlined on several occasions, as early as 2013. i voted to close the loopholes in the european anti-fraud office's rules of procedure, allowing it to work more efficiently.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this proposal is to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee’s secretariat, thus providing for a more effective functioning of the supervisory committee. under the new proposed regulation, the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be provided by the commission, and no longer by olaf (article 15(8)). the budgetary appropriations for the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be moved from the budget line and the establishment plan of olaf to that of the commission (article 18). the proposed modification will thus not have any financial implications on the european budget. i agree with the proposal of the commission and the adoption of the fast-track procedure, therefore i am in favour of the mandate. there is a longstanding misunderstanding between olaf and the sc. the purpose of the separation of the two was to improve the working relations. we need efficient working relations between olaf and the sc for the protection of the eu’s financial interests
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat. the proposal for a regulation aims to ensure that the secretariat of the supervisory committee is provided by the commission, and not by olaf, without this having a financial impact on the european budget.
in writing. ‒ the task force ‘anti-fraud coordination unit (the modern day olaf) was created in 1988 as part of the secretariat-general of the european commission. the task force worked alongside national anti-fraud departments and provided the coordination and assistance needed to tackle transnational organised fraud. i have voted for this report that aims to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee’s secretariat, providing for a more effective functioning of the supervisory committee.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i believe that the fight against fraud at european level requires coordinated and intensified action by the member states and the european institutions. this is also why the report adopted today gives more independence to the secretariat of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office to eliminate conflicts of interest, thus giving it a more efficient functioning, and this will facilitate the fight against tax evasion and fraud on european territory.
in writing. ‒ the european anti-fraud office (olaf) is one of the important entities of the union for the supervision of good financial conduct at the level of the european institutions. in this respect, ensuring the independence of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat is crucial for the proper functioning of the entity, as is the efficiency of the functioning of the supervisory committee. there have been problems lately with the coherence of the relationship between olaf and the supervisory committee (sc) and this needed to be changed. the proposal resulting from the consultations between the commission, the council and parliament includes clarifying those issues by providing the secretariat of the sc directly by the commission and not by olaf, with the necessary budgetary changes. at the same time, the tasks of the data protection officer (dpo) of olaf will continue to include data processing activities by the secretariat, and the same confidentiality rules as in the past will continue to apply to secretariat staff. i consider that these are changes necessary for the proper functioning of olaf and for the protection of the financial interests of the union. for these reasons, i support the adoption of the report in its current form.

in writing. ‒ the recent challenges facing the union led to the request for the post-election revision clause of the multiannual financial framework (mff). since the adoption of the mff, the union has faced a number of challenges that were not foreseen initially, which requires an adjustment of the mff to reflect the new political and budgetary priorities of the union. there are now institutional concerns that were not anticipated at the time of the adoption of the mff. the refugee crisis, internal security issues, the agricultural crisis, the payments crisis facing the eu budget, the persistently high level of unemployment, especially among young people, and poverty and social exclusion are pressing issues that are significantly altering the priorities and the budget of the union. as a member of the committee on agriculture and rural development, i cannot help but stress the problems in the common agricultural policy, which requires more flexible financial resources and, at the same time, the provision of flexible instruments for farmers, in order to ensure an economically viable agricultural sector. i voted in favour of this initiative because i believe that the multiannual financial framework needs to be adapted to the current challenges facing the union in order to identify the best solutions anchored in the current reality.

in writing. ‒ the multiannual financial framework (mff) lays down the maximum annual amounts (‘ceilings’) which the eu may spend in different political fields (‘headings’) over a period of at least five years. i have voted for this report regarding the revision proposal for the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework with a special focus on employment, growth and competitiveness.

in writing. ‒ the multiannual financial framework (mff) allows the european union to plan for the implementation of its policies, programmes and projects over a seven-year period. the current mff (2014-2020) was adopted in 2013 and did not include a number of challenges currently facing the union that were not originally envisaged. a mid-term review is therefore needed, resulting from the institutional negotiation at european level, in accordance with the treaty of lisbon. the current report expresses parliament's position on the revision of the mff, following consultation of 14 specialised committees. the review is therefore intended to take into account the refugee and migration crisis, low levels of investment, high levels of youth unemployment, the need to strengthen internal security, crises in the agricultural sector, environmental issues, economic, social and territorial cohesion, increased pressure on development and neighbourhood policies, gender mainstreaming and payment arrears. in this respect, it is recommended to apply flexibility mechanisms, subject to the guarantee of the eu's fundamental right, use extraordinary revenue, support measures following international agreements on climate change, reform of the own resources system, budgetary unity and greater involvement of parliament in decision-making. i support the adoption of this important document.
in writing. ‒ the commission should present a mandatory evaluation of the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020 which would normally be accompanied by a legislative proposal to revise this framework. in this report, parliament sets out its own analysis of the current framework and stresses that it should provide more flexibility for the eu to react appropriately to unexpected crises. the challenges facing the eu in recent times, such as the migration and refugee crisis, terrorism and internal security issues, have had extremely important budgetary consequences since the adoption of the mff in 2013. in this respect, a mid-term review is absolutely necessary for the eu to address a number of issues and achieve its policy objectives. to that end, the changes resulting from the mid-term review of the multiannual framework should be implemented swiftly and included in the 2017 budget. the report also proposes the creation of a permanent eu reserve in the european budget for crisis situations and stresses the need for reform of the own resources system based on principles such as simplification, fairness and transparency. the commission has also received comments from the sampled union producers.

in writing. ‒ tax evasion is a problem with serious implications for the european union and the member states, directly affecting the union budget. combating tax evasion and tax avoidance must be a priority for each member state in order to restore tax justice. the support of member states is important in efforts to combat tax evasion, and they should themselves adopt legislative proposals to combat tax avoidance. as regards the existing codes of conduct for the tax advisory sector, they need to be strengthened in order to avoid situations of conflict of interest. national parliaments should also step up their cooperation to ensure adequate control and coherence of tax systems, strengthening their work on tax matters. i voted in favour of the report on tax rulings and other measures similar or having similar effects because i believe that it is necessary to ensure the fairness of tax systems and the guarantee of the payment of taxes, and that it is important to create effective tools to combat tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ the european commission estimates tax evasion and fraud at €1 trillion a year, while the oecd estimates that lost revenues globally are between 4% and 10% of total corporate tax revenues. almost a third of businesses' cross-border investments are channelled through offshore financial arrangements. parliament held a meeting with representatives of the governments of andorra, liechtenstein, monaco, guernsey and jersey, following which they committed to implementing the automatic exchange of information by 2017. we voted for a first step towards eradicating tax evasion by encouraging communication between national parliaments and supporting the work of the european commission in investigating all cases.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament is the representative forum of european citizens. in this capacity, parliament undertook a substantial inquiry, following the 'panama papers' and 'luxleaks' scandals, to determine the extent of tax evasion within the union, including how some of the revenues of european taxpayers end up in 'tax havens' around the world. in this regard, the special committee on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect (taxe) was set up in 2015 and its mandate was extended by the establishment of the taxe 2 special committee. the work of the last committee resulted in the present report, which contains the conclusions reached on a number of issues less addressed by the first committee, such as tax havens, the role of intermediaries, tax and banking advisers, whistleblower protection, harmful tax measures, patents for inventions, etc. issues related to the publication of beneficial ownership registers of companies, withholding tax, non-cooperative jurisdictions, publication of country reports, reform of the code of conduct, increased transparency and the publication of a blacklist of tax havens were also addressed. i think it is a very useful document for combating tax evasion and i support its adoption.
