in writing. ‒ the energy challenges facing europe include the dependence on oil and gas imports that has increased in recent years, the lack of diversification, high energy prices influenced by state-imposed energy taxes, the increase in global energy demand, as well as the integration and interconnection of energy markets and market distortions caused by different support systems. meeting the eu's climate change objectives requires a package of measures, which involves, in addition to the use of renewable energy, assessing the benefits of low-carbon technologies compared to high-carbon technologies. i voted in favour of the report on a new organization of the energy market, considering that the european commission's proposal for an energy policy involving both centralised and decentralised structures is correct and viable in the current international context.
in writing. ‒ the future of the energy market in eu countries is one of the current topics at european level. moreover, it was one of the catalysts from the outset of the founding act of the european union, an act directly linked to the management of energy resources. due to outdated infrastructure, poorly integrated markets and uncoordinated policies, consumers, households and businesses do not benefit from a wider choice or lower electricity prices. on 15 july 2015, the european commission published a set of guidelines and objectives to regulate and unify the european energy market. all measures must be checked in terms of instruments, legal basis, implementation and possibilities for europeanisation of electricity supply. i support the ep motion for a resolution on the report 'towards a new organisation of the energy market'. i believe it is time to complete the single energy market in europe for a secure, environmentally sustainable and affordable energy supply. predictable energy prices and security of supply will raise household living standards.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report comes ahead of the expected electricity market design legislation to be proposed by the end of 2016. part of the energy union, it concerns the rules for the electricity market and particularly trading, transmission and distribution of electricity. a new market design is needed to take into account the changing nature of our electricity supply, moving away from traditional, centralised, base-load power generation towards a system based more on variable renewables and flexibility, often produced at a more local level. thus the energy markets need to adapt. we need to ensure a market design that is fit for the future, and one which works for consumers and industry, ensuring affordable energy. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ we need to ensure a market design which works for consumers and industry alike, ensuring affordable energy. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european future electricity market has three political objectives: the creation of an eu-wide electricity market providing clear price signals for new investments; provision of a european dimension to security of electricity supply; strengthening of regional cooperation on energy policy, in particular when there is investment in new energy production facilities, for interconnectors and funding rules, and for the integration of renewables into the european single market. i have voted for this report that will ensure that energy policy objectives of security of supply, environmental impact and value for money can be achieved.
in writing. ‒ the new energy union strategy provides new benefits for energy consumers, gives them a much wider range of options in participating in energy markets and ensures better consumer protection. the full implementation of the third energy package in all member states is one of the most important steps towards a european energy market. we demand that the electricity supply and system services be allocated in accordance with market economy principles. such a public tender, whether national or cross-border, should be technologically neutral and should also allow the participation of energy storage operators. i stress the need to speed up the authorisation of energy infrastructure projects at all decision-making levels. as the commission's proposals for a new energy market organisation concern exclusively the electricity sector, we invite the commission to consider revising the concept of the natural gas market to respond to the challenges in the gas sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and therefore voted in favour of the new energy union strategy, because we must all be aware of the importance of such a union for the european market and for consumers who will ultimately have a wider range of choices. at the same time, the report emphasises a practical aspect: long-term planning of infrastructure development, reiterating the importance of renewable technologies in order to ensure the sustainability of this market.
in writing. ‒ the increasing diversity of energy sources and the full integration of renewable energy into power grids require a new energy market design. this will allow the eu to reduce dependence on centralised power generation and increase the use of many more localised sources of energy. this vital transition will increase our energy independence. i welcome the s&d’s approach to capacity mechanisms to ensure consumers get good value for money and to reduce the number of people living in energy poverty.
in writing. ‒ the european union is currently facing a number of energy challenges, including dependence on oil and gas imports, lack of diversification, high energy prices influenced by state-imposed energy taxes, rising global energy demand, security risks for producing and transit countries, tackling climate change, slow progress on energy efficiency, increasing the share of energy from renewable sources, the integration and interconnection of energy markets and market distortions caused by different support systems. in this regard, the commission considered that better integration and coordination of energy markets is required, by creating an eu-wide electricity market, creating a genuine european dimension for the security of energy supply and strengthening regional cooperation in the field of interconnections and support systems, as well as with a view to integrating energy from renewable sources. however, the current situation is characterised by the predominance of national decision-making, which emphasises the need for consultation in the sub-areas of price-setting in the event of shortages, the extension of regulatory oversight at european level, increased interconnection, the use of energy from renewable sources, the subsidiarity of the european market organisation, price liberalisation. it's a step forward to improve the situation.
in writing. ‒ following the communication of the european commission of july 2015 on a new energy market organisation, this report highlights the need to reorganise the energy market and improve the regulatory framework in order to increase the use of renewable energy and fill existing gaps in legislation at cross-border level. the report argues that the organisation of the energy market should be based on market-specific principles, as this could help to stimulate investment, guaranteeing market access for smes, and thus achieving a stable, integrated and smart energy system. in this context, the report recommends that the commission, in its work on the new energy market organisation, seek to ensure a level playing field between european electricity producers and those in third countries, with the aim of providing european consumers with sustainable and affordable electricity. the report stresses the importance of supporting stable and cost-effective renewables for long-term investments that are adjustable in the short term and can be adapted to national needs. the report therefore calls on the member states to encourage their use, given their essential role in the energy market. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the new energy market organisation.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the own-initiative report on a new energy market organisation. the rapporteur believes that the european commission's proposal for an energy policy involving both centralised and decentralised structures is in principle correct. i welcome his view that the desired market organisation must therefore be designed in such a way that transformation processes can take place without distorting markets and leading to bad investments.
in writing. ‒ many european buildings are currently facing the problem of energy loss due to their inadequate insulation and old and inefficient heating systems. at the same time, energy poverty affects almost 11% of the eu population. the eu's policy tools and capabilities are not yet sufficiently developed to drive the transformation of the heating and cooling sector, to make the most of its potential and to develop solutions to reduce demand. it is estimated that the amount of heat energy produced by industrial processes and dissipated in the atmosphere or water, instead of being used productively, is sufficient to fully cover the heating needs of residential and commercial buildings in the union. i welcome the initiative of the committee on industry, research and energy to initiate this report, considering that the correct application of the measures to develop a comprehensive and integrated strategy for heating and cooling offers both businesses and consumers in the eu a number of significant opportunities in terms of reducing overall energy costs for industry, boosting competitiveness and ensuring a reduction in costs borne by consumers, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the issue of heating and cooling has profound effects in a wide range of areas. it is essential to make real progress in revolutionizing the heating and cooling sector as part of a wider reform of the energy system. the main way to combat energy poverty is to reduce heating prices, ensuring that energy efficiency will increase significantly. the strategy to increase the efficiency and sustainability of heating and cooling aims to address a complex issue: the distribution of elements referring to heating in several directives and legislative instruments such as the energy performance of buildings directive, the renewable energy directive and the energy efficiency directive. i support the european parliament's motion for a resolution on an eu strategy for heating and cooling. i stress the importance of more extensive scientific research into the development of innovative technological solutions to ensure energy-efficient household appliances and all heating and cooling systems. an important source of heat, which has not been used sufficiently, is solar radiation, which, with the help of panels that heat water or generate electricity, can be exploited to the maximum.
in writing. ‒ gradual warming of the climate causes cooling that generates energy losses in buildings without adequate thermal insulation. i voted to set aside at least 25% of the european energy efficiency and renewable energy fund for the purpose of thermal renovation of properties. this objective should be a priority, especially as the problem of heating and cooling is increasingly a problem in the member states. the use of appropriate architectural solutions, insulation and reversible heat pumps, and the replacement of outdated thermal power plants with high-efficiency ones are concrete solutions to alleviate the thermal discomfort of the citizens of the member states affected by these climate changes.
in writing. ‒ given that energy efficiency policies should focus on the most cost-effective ways to improve the performance of buildings by reducing heat demand and/or connecting buildings to high-efficiency alternatives, i consider it important to undertake extensive scientific research to develop innovative technological solutions to propose energy-efficient household appliances and heating and cooling systems that run on energy from renewable sources.
in writing. ‒ heating and cooling accounts for roughly half of the eu’s final energy demand – which is why it is so important to reduce demand and make the sector more efficient, in order to reduce dependence on energy imports, reduce emissions, and bring down costs to consumers, especially those at risk of energy poverty. the report is in response to a commission communication on the heating and cooling strategy. heating and cooling refers to heating and cooling of buildings both in the residential and industrial sectors. it will feed into some of the upcoming legislative initiatives on energy efficiency, in particular the revised energy performance of buildings directive to be proposed in the autumn. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because the issue of heating and cooling is increasingly being raised by eu member states. i support finding and using innovative and appropriate architectural solutions, such as thermal insulation of buildings. cooling is a growing concern directly linked to the gradual warming of the climate. therefore, i consider that under the energy efficiency directive, member states should develop state building renovation plans with a view to making buildings energy efficient, not least by providing incentives for the renovation of buildings owned by individuals, and that these plans should also include specific measures for the most vulnerable groups, in order to contribute to the fight against energy poverty.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on an eu strategy for heating and cooling of buildings in the residential and industrial sectors. this will improve the performance and energy efficiency of the revised buildings to be proposed in the autumn.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on an eu strategy for heating and cooling, in which i reiterated the importance of developing eu systems that provide incentives for the energy-efficient rehabilitation of public buildings, private and social housing, and for the construction of green buildings. in the same report, we stressed the need to use structural funds to modernise the building system, particularly in the form of preferential loans, which would facilitate much-needed modernisation of existing buildings, especially in the less developed parts of the eu. the amount of heat produced from industrial and commercial processes lost to air or water could fully cover the heat demand in european residential buildings. the eu needs to find a viable technological solution and legal framework to recover this energy loss. member states should speed up the implementation of the energy efficiency directive, as stimulating energy efficiency in buildings is a key element that would help to alleviate energy poverty in households. state building renovation plans should provide for support measures for people living in the most deprived areas and for vulnerable groups facing energy poverty.

in writing. ‒ heating and cooling systems account for about half of the eu's energy consumption. in this context, it is very important that the european institutions contribute to making the field more efficient, both for industrial and household consumers. in particular, the energy efficiency of buildings is addressed by means of thermal insulation of older buildings, upgrading and even replacing old thermal power stations, and upgrading heating and cooling equipment (including boilers and air conditioners). this process is already underway in many member states, but coordination of efforts at european level is needed to avoid gaps between regions and to avoid the vulnerability of certain social groups. national resources are insufficient and individual investment by citizens is unthinkable. to address these problems, a substantial increase in european funding is needed, covering the thermal renovation of residential lots and the construction of innovative installations, as well as an increase in the use of renewable energy (in particular solar energy). this is an absolutely necessary initiative, which i support wholeheartedly.
in writing. ‒ heating and cooling account for the largest share of energy consumption at european level. in this regard, this report underlines the need for a specific long-term strategy with renewable energy at its core. the report thus highlights the major role played by new technologies based on water, air, solar energy, geothermal energy, etc. and calls on member states to provide incentives for the promotion and adoption of these technologies. in this context, it is considered that upgrading outdated and inefficient heating systems, better use of heat by district heating systems and a thorough renovation of buildings are some of the key elements that can enable a safer and more sustainable approach to heat supply. the commission therefore proposes an attractive financing system, favouring the use of new technologies for heating households based on renewable energy. furthermore, the report underlines the importance of scientific research to develop innovative technical solutions for energy-efficient and renewable heating devices and systems. i therefore voted in favour of the report entitled 'the eu's strategy for heating and cooling'.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament is concerned with creating the best possible living conditions for european citizens. recently, however, it has become increasingly difficult to reconcile career and family life at european level. this has a negative impact on demographic trends, contributing to the rapid ageing of the european population. to counteract these effects, this document proposes to review european legislation to achieve a balance between career and personal life, in particular with regard to maternity and paternity leave, flexible working schedules, and increased participation of parents with children in the labour market. these measures require additional investment in social services, in particular in the care of children, the elderly and the disabled, the creation of quality jobs, equal treatment in the labour market. these measures will increase the frequency of paternity leave, allowing equal participation of parents in child-rearing, encourage carers of the elderly, children or the disabled, encourage the reintegration of mothers into the labour market and ensure free access for children to education, health, care, food and housing. i believe that these measures are beneficial to raising the standard of living of european citizens as a whole and i support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the eu is currently facing an alarming demographic situation, caused by the steady decline in birth rates in most member states. in the face of this finding, the report indicates that establishing policies for reconciling family and working life can help to strengthen economic growth, competitiveness, gender equality, reduce the risk of poverty and, moreover, increase the birth rate in the eu. it stresses that work-life balance should be a fundamental right for all, not just young parents, and encourages member states to promote social protection models at the level of enterprises, in the public and private sectors, that respect this right. the proposed measures also include: promoting a family-friendly working environment, work-life balance plans, re-entry programmes, employee-employer communication interfaces, and incentives for businesses, in particular to ensure that citizens are not economically penalised for having children. i therefore voted in favour of the report which proposes to create conditions in the labour market which are favourable to work-life balance.
mr president, i would first of all like to condemn in the strongest terms the attempted coup d'état that took place in july in turkey. the fact that this attempt to take power by force has failed is something to be welcomed. because, obviously, in a democratic state, violence can never take the place of the vote in any form. no one knows, however, if this is the end of the attempts to take power in turkey, other than democratically. beyond that, i would like to express my serious concern at the way this failed coup d'état has been used to settle a number of political scores. of course, those who tried to take power by force must be brought to justice. but nothing justifies using this pretext to eliminate political opposition, to hunt down teachers, journalists, ordinary turkish citizens described as terrorists. turkey must respect freedom of expression and association. i think it should be clear to our turkish friends that we will not waive any of the conditions for visa liberalisation. turkish citizens will have the right to travel freely in the union when all 72 criteria are met by the authorities.
mr president, i have to confess that i heard some of my colleagues speaking realpolitik, a lot of it in a quite cynical way, but saying very little, if anything, on principles and values. turkey is a candidate country and it has to guarantee high standards on human rights, freedom of expression and the rule of law. turkey took steps towards democracy and secularism many decades ago and has strengthened its position as a credible and powerful actor on the international scene. but this also implies external and internal obligations and responsibilities towards all its citizens – i repeat all its citizens – and international partners. otherwise we must realise here today that, after the failure of the coup d'état, which we all condemned, turkey has chosen lately to undermine its commitments. since the coup attempt, the turkish government has overseen a vast purge. more than 100 000 people have been dismissed or suspended from their jobs and many others have been detained. therefore i call on turkey to respect the right to justice and to a fair trial for all its citizens and for the foreigners living in turkey. turkey is facing a wide range of threats, including terrorism, in relation to which cooperation between europe and turkey is fundamental. finally, another very important aspect is that turkey is a key actor in finding a political solution for syria in the fight against isis and in the management of the syrian crisis and refugee flow. i urge turkey to play a constructive role and to change its behaviour for good.
in writing. turkey's internal stability is of paramount importance to both the european union and nato, we have no interest in chaos and instability in the country, and any attempt to overthrow the democratically elected government by force is to be condemned at all times. however, this claim is independent of the current migration situation. we cannot change our attitude towards turkey based on whether the turkish government is turning a blind eye to illegal migration on its shores or taking a hard line on human traffickers. similarly, the enforcement of human rights should not be judged in light of turkey's role as an important ally in the coalition against the islamic state. a few months ago, after the eu-turkey summit, i said that it was unthinkable to speed up turkey's accession negotiations, that there could be no special treatment for turks, and that this would undermine the credibility of the whole enlargement process. i can only confirm this today: we must take a firm stand on turkish affairs, we must not behave as if turkey were doing a service to europe which we are returning with a visa-free regime. this kind of discourse suggests to european citizens that the eu is powerless without turkey on this issue, which i am convinced is not the case.

madam president, back in the 2000s, central and eastern european countries joined a european union based on an open market economy with free competition, and on a single market with four freedoms, opening up their economies to fierce competition from companies that had far more capital and far more technological advantage than theirs. what we see today, however, are attempts by old member states to introduce a pick-and-choose variety of competition and single market, depending on what suits perceived interests or populist political approaches better. this happens, be it through attempts to restrict the rules on the posting of workers or be it through the fabrication of an ill-defined notion with highly negative connotations, which is how, today, we are talking about social dumping, instead of enforcing existing single market regulation. in a fight that is about neutralising less-developed countries’ main competitive advantage – lower wages – the next logical step would be to set higher tariffs on goods imported from there. i do not think that is the direction in which the european union should be heading.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating my colleague, mr guillaume balas, on his report. i think we all agree that we need, at this point, better protection of workers, their rights and their safety in all member states. equally important, in my view, is that this report should leave no doubt as to its objectives. i believe that the benefits of the european single market and freedom of movement in europe are clear and have been felt in the east and at least as much in the west of the european union. it is a reality that i ask you never to forget! i would therefore like to encourage and support, on this occasion as well, all constructive good faith initiatives which contribute to strengthening this founding principle of our union and which, at the same time, take into account the rights and protection of european workers, regardless of the member state in which they work.
in writing. the report on social dumping highlights that europe faces significant differences in the application of workers' rights. from the perspective of the transport sector, these differences distort the internal market and endanger the safety of passengers. the solution to creating common rules, but also to ensuring that they are implemented, is to have a body with clear responsibilities and the legitimacy to coordinate action at european level. this is why the european union needs a european road transport agency. this would ensure that member states do not impose unilateral restrictive measures that punish firms in low-gdp countries. at the same time, better coordination will help us tackle legislative gaps and stop some firms abusing the freedoms offered by the european single market. there are still a few things to be clarified. first, we must avoid labelling and create a level playing field for all participants in the european market. a constructive approach will require all stakeholders to mobilise to create a single legislative framework, which does not allow for a race to the bottom of social rights to the detriment of the most vulnerable or consumers.
in writing. the european parliament's motion for a resolution on social dumping is welcome, given that inequalities in europe are increasing, thus undermining the achievement of the europe 2020 poverty and employment targets. this means taking a strong eu stance against what we call 'social dumping', which gives it a role model on the world stage, by obliging third countries to respect fundamental human rights, international labour law and social standards, and limiting the effects of social dumping worldwide. we agree that there is no universally accepted definition of the concept, but social dumping, in its various forms, has not only economic, social, financial and budgetary effects but also environmental effects, which are not specified in this proposal. the free movement of persons is indispensable to the achievement of the objectives of economic, social and territorial cohesion, but it would be desirable that the situation of workers from developing member states accused of social dumping in developed eu member states be clearly regulated, rather than merely taking note of the commission's proposal to revise directive 96/71/ec.
in writing. today's debate was needed more than ever. europe is in a deep image crisis and this is giving rise to extremism. citizens of the different european countries see europe through the lens of their lives. i thank giani pittella for having mentioned in his speech the need for romania, bulgaria and croatia to be in schengen. this is why measures are needed to increase social cohesion, safety and quality of life. mr juncker, the commission is often seen as the 'service-guilty' by citizens who cannot send their children to school, by young people who are out of work, by pensioners who cannot live on low pensions, by smes that are crushed by multinationals. the misunderstanding of the commission's role also stems from the faulty communication. you are right, europe needs to be explained better! as parliamentarians, we want to support the commission. help us support you! be more transparent! take parliament's resolutions into account and focus on social cohesion investments. the efsi has not achieved its objective and therefore you need to change the spending rules, taking into account also underdeveloped regions with a reduced administrative capacity to write projects. let's stay united through projects for people. only then will we be a power in the world.
in writing. on 24 june, with the uk referendum, the european union entered a crucial stage for its future. let me be clear: i do not want the dismemberment of europe and the isolation of our countries in a cave nationalism. on the contrary, i want to save what can be saved in a europe of nations that are united and cooperative in all areas. i expected that, in the meantime, there would be an avalanche of proposals to reform the union and debate them. apart from the proposal put forward by president schulz, which i welcome, i have seen nothing but closed-door meetings between various heads of state, after which only vague statements were made publicly. unfortunately, political leaders are overlooking the fact that brexit and euroscepticism in general were generated by the fracture between the political system and the citizens. the state of the union is worse now than it was on june 23rd! that's because nothing was done! continuing to ignore people's grievances is not a solution to get europe out of the crisis! to continue to exist, the european union needs a profound structural reform!

in writing. ‒ due to its geographical and cultural proximity and, in particular, its political and economic importance, the eu and the 28 member states are switzerland's most important partner. the eu has closer links with switzerland than with any other state outside the european economic area (eea), through a wide range of agreements. while switzerland is the eu's fourth largest trading partner after the united states, china and russia, the eu is switzerland's largest trading partner. over one million eu citizens live in switzerland, and another 230 000 cross the border daily to go to work. approximately 430 000 swiss citizens live in the eu. with the accession of romania, bulgaria and croatia to the eu, the internal market has expanded even further, reaching almost 505 million citizens and becoming even more important for our swiss partner. in view of the extremely important bilateral relations between the eu and switzerland, i considered this protocol to be important and therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the protocol on the free movement of persons was signed in 2000 by switzerland and the european union of 15 member states, and is due to enter into force in 2002. following each of the enlargements of the union, in 2004 (accession of the 10 new member states to the eu) and 2007 (accession of romania and bulgaria), the eu-switzerland agreement was amended, entering into force as protocol ii. with the accession of croatia to the european union in 2013, protocol iii between the eu and switzerland was initiated, extending the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. i voted in favour of this draft legislative resolution of the european parliament because i agree with the text adopted by the committee on employment and social affairs.
in writing. ‒ switzerland is the eu's fourth largest trading partner after the united states, china and russia, and the eu is its largest economic partner. over one million eu citizens live in switzerland, and another 230 000 cross the border daily to go to work. approximately 430 000 swiss citizens live in the eu. the objective of that agreement was to establish rules between the union and switzerland equivalent to those laid down in the acquis communautaire, allowing entry, residence, work, establishment as a worker, studies, introducing the right to social security and granting living, employment and working conditions identical to those guaranteed to its own nationals. we voted for a larger internal market, in which free movement is an essential element, but also for the economic and cultural benefits that can be derived from it.
in writing. ‒ given that switzerland is the european union's fourth largest trading partner after the united states, china and russia, and that the internal market has expanded even further since the accession of romania, bulgaria and croatia to the eu, and is becoming even more important for the swiss partner, i support the rapporteur's position to support this protocol to the agreement and recommend its approval.
in writing. ‒ it is beyond doubt that both croatia and switzerland will benefit politically, culturally and economically from the signature of protocol iii. free movement is a crucial element and can hence not be separated from internal market participation. i therefore voted in favour of the protocol.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on protocol iii extending the agreement between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the swiss confederation, of the other, on the free movement of persons in croatia. this agreement was initiated upon the accession of croatia in 2013 and comprises a transitional period of 7 years, with a safeguard clause for switzerland for a further three years. during this period, switzerland may restrict the access of its citizens to the labour market, with the restrictions to be accepted by a swiss-eu joint committee during the last 2 years of this period. the free movement of persons is the driving force behind the development of the european community at all levels.
in writing. ‒ the free movement of persons given to the citizens of the european union and switzerland to live and work in each other’s territories is regulated by this protocol. i voted for this report that will take into consideration the accession of croatia.
in writing. ‒ the first set of bilateral agreements between the eu and switzerland entered into force in june 2002, including the agreement on the free movement of persons. they were subsequently amended by protocols i and ii. protocol iii was initiated with the accession of croatia to the european union in 2013 and signed recently. it provides for a transitional period of seven years. there is no doubt that, from a political, economic and cultural point of view, both croatia and switzerland will benefit from the signing of this protocol. free movement is an essential element and therefore cannot be separated from participation in the internal market.
in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit for growth and employment (tss) was established by decision 2003/174/ec, which formalised the practice of organising informal high-level meetings, starting in 1997, within the framework of the european employment strategy. this decision has been proposed to institutionalise the practice of high-level consultation between the eu institutions and the eu social partners. the proposal meant the abolition of the former standing committee on employment, which was set up in 1970 and reformed in 1999. i voted in favour of this proposal, which will allow the social partners at european level to contribute, in the context of social dialogue, to the various components of the union's strategy for growth and jobs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of approving the draft council decision on a high-level social tripartite meeting for growth and employment and repealing decision 2003/174/ec.
in writing. ‒ as co-legislator, it is essential that parliament, represented by the chair of the committee on employment and social affairs (empl) is invited to the tripartite social summit (tss) for growth and employment on a regular basis. the ppe rapporteur, mr sógor, the shadows and the empl coordinators proposed that consent be given to the council position only on the condition that the chair of the empl committee is invited to the tss on a regular basis. respective assurances should be given by the council and the commission prior to the plenary vote. in the meantime parliament received a letter from the council and the commission confirming that the empl chair will be invited to the tss also in the future, thereby satisfying parliament’s demands. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to strengthen the social dialogue between the european union institutions and the european social partners for job creation and the development of social inclusion, and to lessen the adverse impact of the migration and refugee crisis on labour markets.

in writing. ‒ article 3 of the treaty states that one of the objectives of the european union is to develop a highly competitive social market economy, aiming at full employment and social progress. in defining and implementing its policies and actions, the union must take into account the social dimension of those policies and actions, in particular the requirements of promoting a high level of employment, ensuring adequate social protection, combating social exclusion, and the requirements of a high level of education, vocational training and protection of human health. the union has established a tripartite social summit for development and employment, recognised as an integral component of the social dialogue at eu level. it will enable the social partners at european level to contribute, in the context of their social dialogue, to the various components of the union's strategy for growth and jobs. the summit shall be composed of representatives at the highest level of the president of the european council, the presidency of the council and the two successive presidencies, the commission and the social partners. the summit shall meet at least twice a year, before the spring and autumn sessions of the european council respectively.
in writing. ‒ eu—level social dialogue plays an essential role in the smooth functioning of our social market economy; it has benefits for employers and workers alike, as well as for the economy and society as a whole. this is why i am grateful that this house adopted my report on the tripartite social summit for growth and employment. in the current process of strengthening economic governance – if we want to ensure real ownership of policies and to ensure effective implementation of our decisions – it is critical to involve the social partners in policy debates and decision-making processes. beside the macroeconomic dialogue, the tripartite social summit is one of the key opportunities for improving the involvement of the social partners in the coordination of economic and employment policies at eu level. this is why it is of utmost importance that the social partners have the possibility to negotiate with eu leaders at the highest levels within a stable consultation framework. this is an essential condition to ensure a coherent, fair and efficient decision—making process.
in writing. ‒ growth and employment are two closely related and interdependent concepts. aware of this, the european institutions have initiated consultations with the social partners in the trilateral format employers trade unions institutions, to boost the eu's economic development. in this format, the european union was represented by the commission and the council as decision-making forums. however, in the context of the provisions of the lisbon treaty, the role of the european parliament as the main forum for the representation of european citizens must be respected. the council's position was adopted, but before parliament had expressed its position, which does not exactly reflect the normal procedure. it was therefore a compromise decision that the chair of the committee on employment and social affairs (empl) should participate in these consultations. it is a welcome formula, which acknowledges, even in part, the importance of the european parliament's participation in this dialogue. i believe that this is a step forward which can contribute to the success of the high-level social tripartite meeting so necessary in the current european context.

in writing. ‒ inland waterways are an increasingly important mode of transport within the european union, mainly due to the low cost of freight transport and the low potential for pollution. however, there are a number of obstacles to operating these transport routes to their full capacity. these include the lack of harmonisation of national regulations and of the various river sections. to this end, the european commission has proposed common technical standards for river vessels used by the various member states. the proposal aims to ensure a high level of safety and efficiency, the rapid adaptation of standards to scientific and technical progress and the periodic review of regulations. the infrastructure for alternative fuels, including liquefied gas, is also planned. an important component of the institutional negotiations was the parliament's prerogative to take decisions on updating technical standards in the field of inland waterways. this is an important achievement, which is why i support the adoption of this recommendation in its current form.
mr president, in the next ten years, the african, pacific and caribbean countries will liberalise 80% of their trade with the european union. this is possible on the basis of a partnership agreement concluded in 2012. the agreement, however, is not complete and it is not perfect. the union must be more ambitious and continue negotiations to include services, investment, intellectual property, public procurement or sustainable development. this is in the interest of these countries, in africa, in the caribbean, in the pacific, and it's even more important now that we're facing the refugee crisis. diversifying the economies of these countries will lead to economic and political stability, to the safety of their citizens and to the stability of everyone: both those regions and europe.
in writing. ‒ in 2000, when the cotonou partnership agreement was concluded, there was a need for fundamental changes to the long-standing non-reciprocal trade preferences that had governed economic and political relations between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states and the european union for almost 40 years. the main reason for this was that the impact of these unilateral preferences had been disappointing: firstly, the share of acp trade in the eu market was continuously declining and most countries were not able to use these preferences to diversify their economic structures. while this development-oriented regional trade agreement currently only includes provisions on trade in goods, development cooperation and trade and provisions on sustainable development, it allows for the negotiation of additional provisions on services, investment, intellectual property, public procurement and enhanced provisions on sustainable development. i voted in favour of this report, considering it essential to promote trade and development between the eu and sadc epa states.

in writing. ‒ the european union supports free trade worldwide, which is expressed through the conclusion of economic partnership agreements with various countries and regions of the world. these include the southern african development and cooperation (sadc) region, which includes countries that already have a strong cooperation relationship with the eu, such as south africa, but also others that aspire to this status, such as botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia and swaziland. the current agreement, signed in june 2015, gives all these countries free, duty-free access to the european market, encouraging their sustainable development. unfortunately, the agreement also does not contain formal mechanisms to monitor its implementation, although such mechanisms are included in eu agreements. in this regard, the role of civil society is essential to monitor the achievement of the objectives of the agreement, in particular in the area of ensuring fundamental rights and labour standards. fortunately, the agreement can be revised after five years, which is a reason for optimism. however, it would be useful to include some verification mechanisms in the agreement as early as possible. in any event, this is an important step forward for the protection of products of protected origin, and not only. i support the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the fishing industry has grown considerably. this growth, however, hasn’t come without a cost – in terms of working conditions and occupational safety – to full and part-time workers in the fishing sector. people in the fishing sector often face harsh or difficult working conditions: they may spend long periods at sea and are frequently exposed to unpredictable and dangerous conditions. adopting these international labour standards for what is one of the world’s most dangerous professions is extremely important to protect workers and provide them with decent working conditions. i therefore voted in favour of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ in 2007 during the 96th international labour conference the work in fishing convention was adopted ensuring that fishermen get decent working conditions on board fishing vessels. i have voted for this motion for a resolution that highlights the fact that the agreement provides only minimum requirements, thus allowing member states and their social partners to adopt specific measures favourable to workers in particular areas.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it supports the agreement on the implementation of the labour convention in the fisheries sector, a document concluded between the social partners. the special characteristics of work carried out on board fishing vessels require increased protection for workers in this field. in this respect, i support the text of this motion for a resolution, which calls for the adoption of the council directive without delay, stressing that both the social partners' agreement and the commission proposal only address minimum requirements, leaving member states free to adopt measures more favourable to workers in this field.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the fisheries economic sector has experienced significant growth, which has led to the creation of a significant number of jobs. over 100 000 people are currently employed in the fisheries sector across the eu. however, their work is subject to difficult, high-risk circumstances at sea. the rate of accidents and injuries in this field is 15 times higher than the average in other fields. the commission has therefore proposed to regulate this sector in order to improve the working conditions of those employed in fishing. in 2007, a directive was adopted to implement the international labour organisation's fisheries labour convention. consultations were subsequently organised with the social partners, in this case the general confederation of agricultural cooperatives of the european union (cogeca), the european transport workers' federation (etf) and the association of national fisheries organisation of the european union (europêche). following these consultations, the implementing agreement was adopted in 2013 and has so far only been ratified by france. the current recommendation aims to boost the ratification process and the necessary practical application of those standards. i support the adoption of the document.
in writing. ‒ recent events in poland concerning disputes related to the composition and functioning of the constitutional tribunal have raised concerns regarding the guarantees of respect for the rule of law. there have been a number of discussions with the polish authorities, but the issues threatening the rule of law have not been fully resolved, which leads the commission to consider that there is a systemic threat to democracy in poland. in this regard, the european commission has made concrete recommendations to the polish authorities on how to address its problems under the emergency regime. there are also concerns about respect for freedom of expression and freedom and pluralism of the media. all this leads the european institutions to intervene in order to resolve the problems created in a satisfactory way, bearing in mind that the principle of separation of powers and the independence of the judiciary are at the heart of the democratic system and must not be undermined. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the resolution tabled by the ppe group, together with the s&d, alde, gue/ngl and the greens/efa.
in writing. ‒ recent events in poland, referring here to the disputes over the composition and functioning of the constitutional court in that country, as well as the worrying aspect of the non-publication of some judgments of that court, call into question the guarantees of respect for the rule of law. it should be stressed at the outset that the principle of separation of powers in the state and the principle of the independence of the judiciary are at the heart of the democratic system and must not be undermined in any way. the polish government has not only made no progress in resolving the constitutional crisis, but also raises a number of concerns regarding respect for freedom of expression and freedom and pluralism of the media. the commission has also received comments from the polish authorities on the implementation of the new law on the media, which is expected to be adopted in the near future. i therefore vote in favour of this resolution to invite the polish government to cooperate with the commission in accordance with the principle of sincere cooperation in order to find a compromise that would resolve the current constitutional crisis and to rapidly identify concrete solutions to the systemic threats to the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ it is clear that procedural safeguards and material conditions set in the police act for implementing secret surveillance are not sufficient to prevent its excessive use and unjustified interference with privacy and data protection of individuals. the issues that threaten the rule of law in poland have not been satisfactorily resolved and i therefore believe there is a systematic threat to the rule of law in poland. this is why i welcome the fact that, on 27 july 2016, the commission activated the second stage of the rule of law framework by making concrete recommendations to the polish authorities on how to address its concerns. we are not prepared to accept political decisions which go against the fundamental values of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against the motion for a resolution regarding the recent development in poland and their impact on fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ the debate over the last few months on the worrying political developments in poland has been of the utmost interest to the european institutions. the constitutional tribunal has been entrusted with the task of ensuring the independence of the judiciary and the rule of law, and has been entrusted with the task of ensuring the independence of the judiciary. attempts to introduce a ban on abortion, to amend the public media law, the police law, the attorney general law and the code of criminal procedure are measures that can only make us more aware of the defence of the fundamental values of the union. the dialogue between the european and polish national institutions has not produced any notable results, although the venice commission itself has issued critical opinions on the new national legislation. in these circumstances, in july the commission activated the second phase of the rule of law monitoring framework, making new recommendations to the polish authorities. i believe it is time for the european parliament to send a signal in defence of the fundamental rights of european citizens in all member states. this resolution is only a first step in that direction, but it is a self-imposed measure. i support the adoption of the present resolution, so that polish democracy can be saved.

in writing. ‒ the peaceful democratic transition process in tunisia represents a successful example in the arab world and its consolidation is paramount for the stability of the entire region and, as a direct consequence, for the security of europe. however, tunisia currently faces a difficult socio-economic situation but also security challenges mostly deriving from the situation in libya. furthermore, tourism, which represents a key element of the tunisian economy, is severely affected by these circumstances and by the terrorist attacks which have targeted the country. consequently the eu and its member states must remain committed to working with the people of tunisia and their government to promote common interests, including in trade, investment, tourism, culture and security. the report in question is a good and balanced text, divided into four parts: political reforms and institutions; economic and social development; security and defence; and mobility, research, education and culture. the report reemphasises the need to support tunisia and calls for many actions such as the launch of a programme in support of the reform of the judicial sector and the rule of law and the increase of eu aid to tunisia through the european neighbourhood instrument. i support this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, given the provisions on the harmonisation of social policies at eu level, as well as those on the creation of protectionist measures in the member states and the introduction of limitations and barriers to the free movement of services and workers. i can agree with provisions relating to efforts to ensure that all workers are protected and have access to fair working conditions, but i cannot agree with measures that undermine member states' competences, especially in terms of wage setting, social security, the tax system and specific labour market reforms.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i believe that the particular situation of some new member states, which switched to a market economy in 1990, has not been taken into account. a definition of social dumping is attempted as a wide range of abusive practices which allow, inter alia, the development of unfair competition by illegally minimising operating and personnel costs. in a unitary economic environment, this definition would be correct and would not raise any objection. however, there is a gap in economic development between the old and new member states, which also largely explains the low operating costs in those countries, as well as lower staff costs. i believe that the rapporteur should have taken this into account and given a complete picture of the state of the european economy. of course, i agree to fight social dumping, because it often consists of illegal practices such as undeclared work or abusive practices. however, for an economy as complex and diverse as the european union's, i believe that the economic level of some eastern european member states should not be confused with social dumping.
in writing. ‒ the phenomenon of social dumping arises from practices of unfair economic and social competition and represents a ‘race to the bottom’ in relation to social conditions in europe, damaging high level of social protection in the eu. increased competition between economic operators encourages them to reduce spending related to labour costs; this is leading to a weakening of the social standards in force in the various member states of the union, is gradually undermining all the rights enjoyed by european employees and, finally, is reducing the financial resources necessary for the various social protection systems. this asymmetry between economic freedoms and social rights is fuelling the feeling that europe weakens both individuals and communities, instead of protecting them. thus, the proliferation of abusive practices and unfair social competition weakens adherence to the principle of the internal market and undermines confidence in the construction of europe. these phenomena encourage protectionist tendencies by the member states and unilateral decision-taking by them in the social field. through this report we show that we are very aware of the gravity of this issue and that we engage in fighting against social dumping practices and in ensuring that all workers in europe enjoy high levels of social protection and rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to support the building of a united social europe. i support the joint effort to combat social dumping and to ensure a high level of social protection and equal rights for all workers in europe. social dumping is the result of unfair economic and social competition practices and represents a high degree of distortion of social protection in the eu. this unfair competition undermines the rights of european workers by reducing labour costs, social standards and, by implication, the cost of living.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report on social dumping in the eu that will ensure social convergence in the union and strengthen controls and inspections both at national and european level, in application of the existing legislation. the report emphasises the fragility of social protection availability for employees.
in writing. ‒ one of the basic principles of eu policies is social cohesion, which means a constant and ongoing convergence of wages and social security protection guaranteed to all workers, whether local or remote. significant differences in working conditions and wages persist across the union, with differences in pay levels being the main reason why workers leave their country of origin. it is crucial to ensure a level playing field and fair competition throughout the eu, and to eliminate social dumping. labour inspectorates and/or social partners play a key role in ensuring respect for workers' rights, defining decent pay in accordance with member states' laws and practices, and providing advice and guidance to employers. the rules on secondment should be clear, proportionate and justified and we stress the need to respect the host country's collective agreements and industrial relations systems.
in writing. ‒ increased competition between economic operators has at times led to a race to the bottom as regards social conditions for european workers. the proliferation of abusive practices and unfair social competition is constantly weakening the principle of the internal market and ultimately undermines the construction of the european project. moreover, in trying to defend their own market, some member states have introduced protectionist measures which have further distorted the market. to respond to all these issues, the present report has aimed to bring some clarity with regard to the practice of social dumping, with the final aim of ensuring social rights in a harmonious manner across europe. it calls for control and inspections to be strengthened, at both national and eu level, and calls for the establishment of a legal framework for the protection of all european workers. in the field of transport, a key achievement is the request for the creation of a european road agency, a body which could ensure the coordination of all transport policies, including social aspects, between national authorities and eu institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the adoption of the report on social dumping in the eu because i am deeply convinced of the importance of the four fundamental freedoms of the common market and the need to avoid discrimination of any kind when we are talking about the future of these freedoms. the report seriously confuses concepts such as undeclared work, freedom of movement of workers, freedom of movement of services and abuses the notion of social dumping, using this vague and insufficiently defined term to justify potential harmful consequences for citizens of eu member states.
in writing. ‒ it is important that information for consumers about investment products is comparable in order to promote a level playing field in the market, regardless of the type of financial intermediary that produces or markets them. the lack of detailed guidance in the delegated regulation on key information documents for insurance-based structured individual investment products (priips) has been identified as a gap relating to the 'intelligibility alert', which gives rise to a serious risk of inconsistent application of this element. i consider that there is a risk that the rules laid down by the delegated regulation in its unamended form would run counter to the spirit and purpose of the legislation, which is to provide clear, comparable and intelligible information to retail investors, which is why i voted in favour of the report, namely in favour of the european commission presenting a new delegated act.
in writing. ‒ commission delegated regulation of 30 june 2016 supplementing regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 of the european parliament and of the council on key information documents for insurance-based structured individual investment products (priips) contains shortcomings in the methodology for calculating future performance scenarios, such as the removal of credit risk from the calculation of the risk category for insurance products that would mislead investors and result in the loss of money by investors. the delegated act, as adopted by the commission, cannot enter into force and therefore the commission is invited to present a new delegated act taking into account the above-mentioned calculation methodology and eliminating the risk that the rules laid down by the delegated regulation would be in contradiction with the spirit and purpose of the legislation.
in writing. ‒ the regulation on key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (priips) introduces a key information document or kid (a simple document giving key facts to investors in a clear, comparable and understandable manner) covering not only collective investment schemes but also other ‘packaged’ investment products offered by banks or insurance companies. i consider that revision and improvement of the delegated act is necessary. i support a stronger wording on better information on performance scenarios, in order to avoid misleading the retail investor with over-optimistic scenarios, and the need for a detailed comprehension alert addressed to the investor regarding very risky products.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i believe it is important that information provided to consumers about investment products is comparable, in order to ensure a level playing field in the market. it is also important that investors are provided with information that is 'fair, clear and not misleading', in particular with regard to the transparency of the risk details for products that cause losses periodically during the recommended minimum holding period. the establishment of regulatory technical standards on the presentation or the manner in which key information documents are reviewed and amended, as well as the conditions for their provision, is essential for the establishment of detailed guidance and for the consistent application of this element in the key information document, in particular in the context of the single market.
in writing. ‒ i believe that better information on investment products can really help retail investors and avoid another financial crisis. the regulation on key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (priips) introduced a key information document or kid which is a simple document giving key facts to investors in a clear, comparable and understandable manner, covering not only collective investment schemes but also other investment products offered by banks or insurance companies. in the current environment, i believe that we should do everything possible to reach an agreement on rules for the information of non-professional investors. i believe in openness and transparency. the regulation should enter into force with an improved content on 1 january 2017 as it was planned.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this motion for a resolution regarding key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products.
in writing. ‒ european citizens must be at the heart of the concerns of decision-makers at the level of the european institutions. this is also the case for structured and insurance-based individual investment products (priips), where customer information is of paramount importance. unfortunately, the level of regulation so far has not proved sufficient, failing to ensure a level playing field in the market, removing credit risk from the calculation of the risk category for insurance products, excluding multiple option products and omitting performance scenarios. therefore, further standardisation of this area is necessary in order to provide documents with essential information on these products. the commission proposal for a regulation concerns the presentation, content and review of these documents, as well as the conditions for fulfilling the requirement to provide such documents. however, the proposal fails to address the existing problems. in conclusion, the european parliament's motion for a resolution proposes to postpone the date of application of the regulation in order to ensure the smooth implementation of the requirements of the regulation and the entry into force of the regulatory technical standard. i support this resolution.

member of the commission. – madam president, thank you very much for this debate. thank you to so many members – giegold, lambert, gomes, cato scott, nunes, de masi, da vito, caputo, all of these colleagues, among others – for their support and encouragement, which are very much appreciated: the encouragement to do what we do, which is very basic – to enforce competition law and our state-aid rules so as to ensure fair competition. a lot of you mentioned small and medium sized businesses. these are businesses who pay their taxes. these are businesses who contribute by taking apprentices. these are businesses where you do not find the same statistics – as i am quite sure that my colleague pierre moscovici has presented to you – as you see with multinationals in terms of tax burden and taxes being paid. if taxes are not being paid by some, then they have to be paid by others and that is why it is not fair competition when some member states hand out selective benefits. a lot of you have been asking about the rule of law and the legal basis. this goes back to the very beginning, because our founding fathers saw very clearly that you cannot have fairness and fair competition if rich member states or decisive member states hand out selective benefits to some companies which are not available to others. the courts have said very clearly that state aid can come in many forms – it can be a very cheap piece of land, a very favourable loan, a bundle of cash in your hand, a tax benefit. but state aid it is, because it lowers your costs and lower costs are a thing which is not available to your competitors. secondly, the court has also said very clearly, talking about smes, stand-alone businesses and multinationals, that when multinationals do what they of course need to do, intra-holding trading, then there should be a resemblance to market conditions. because stand-alone companies, the small and medium-sized businesses who are on their own, they have to do their thing in the market. therefore the court has several times committed to the fact that we should be fair and transparent. this is also why, mr hayes, this cannot be a political decision. it is built on the rule of law, it is built on due process, and it will of course be tested by our courts because of the completely legitimate opportunity for ireland to appeal. but the court will hear nothing about party politics or emotions or gut feelings. they want the facts of the case, the court practice, how the case has been decided previously, and that of course will be tested. talking about what guidance we can give, we have too little case practice now to make great guidelines, but we have started to give guidance and to discuss in our high-level state-aid forum how to make sure that member states can work with this, because obviously it is the responsibility of the member states to make sure that national tax legislation, which is 100% a national issue, is upheld at the same time as what we have decided in common in eu state-aid rules. bernd lucke asked about why just now. well, actually this is a very good example of why we need transparency because this case was only opened because of hearings in the us senate. this was where data came out that enabled the commission to get concerned that something may not be as it ought to be, that there was a risk of state aid being handed out. mr kelly asked about retroactivity. no, this is exactly the way things are always dealt with. if a benefit is handed out as a selective benefit to a particular company, it has to be taken back. we do that with a 10-year perspective from the date we asked the first question. this tax ruling has been in place since 1998, but we do not go back the whole way. we do exactly as we used to do: maximum 10 years’ going back. it is not retroactivity. not a single rule has been changed. the only secrecy here was the tax rulings and that is why unpaid taxes have to be paid, just as well as other selective benefits will have to be repaid if they are seen to be illegal state aid. last but not least, state-aid control cannot change tax legislation. if tax legislation is to be changed, it is done by the front door. it is either in the national parliaments, as done in ireland a couple of years ago where the double irish was done away with; or it is by unanimity in the council of ministers, and we do that by the front door to propose to ministers to make things easier. i am talking about the common corporate consolidated tax base. not only will this make it more tricky for people to escape or to aggressively plan their taxation, but also it will make it much easier for small and medium-sized companies because they do not need to hire advisers in order to explain to them what they should be taxed on if they are active in more than one country, maybe just a few. sven giegold asked about resources. what we are doing right now is trying to empower member states to take as many state-aid decisions as possible themselves within the framework of the treaty. i think we are up to 80 or 90% now, which frees up resources for us to look at the more tricky cases where you have a true cross-border issue and where fair competition is at stake. i also, lastly, thank you for the encouragement to work within the oecd and the g20, because obviously this is a global matter. and obviously the highly qualified work done in the oecd to prevent base erosion and profit shifting is a cornerstone of what we can do in the future, because this is for all of us, and a global tax alliance is being formed in these years in order to ensure fair taxation, where everyone participates in paying their fair share, not more and not less, and where all the companies who pay their taxes to see that we have fair competition and that we are willing to work for it. thank you very much for a very qualified and encouraging debate.
