rapporteur. – mr president, i would like to start by thanking the shadow rapporteurs not only for their sound and constructive contribution to this report, but mainly for their genuine commitment and work for the protection of human rights and for combating discrimination. in 2000, i was part of a human rights organisation network that advocated for the adoption of anti-discrimination legislation at the eu level. when the two equality directives were adopted we considered it an historical moment, because discriminating against other human beings is one of the most despicable behaviours one could imagine. sixteen years later, i have the privilege as a member of this european parliament to evaluate how the employment equality directive has been implemented. in 2000, a duty was imposed on our member states to provide protection against discrimination in the areas of employment and occupational and vocational training. it comes as no surprise that, while some member states have gone beyond its requirement by extending protection against discrimination to other areas, including access to goods and services, others are still pretty far from implementing it at the minimum level. the report highlights the necessity of collecting equality data both at the level of member states and the european union in order to make it easier to prove the existence of discrimination and, particularly, indirect discrimination. there is quite a discrepancy between the levels of discrimination experienced and discrimination reported. awareness-raising, with the help of equality bodies and the social partners, is of utmost importance at all levels of society considering that the victims themselves still have difficulty in recognising discrimination, let alone fighting it. i cannot stress enough the role of equality bodies in awareness-raising and data election in helping the victims but also the employers to understand how to change their policies in line with equality requirements. the impartiality of such bodies must be ensured and their activity supported, including through adequate funding. i particularly want to emphasise the issue of multiple discrimination, which is often a consequence of the existence of fragmented rules and standards across member states. if it is difficult for the victims of one type of discrimination to understand the situation and act, we can easily imagine their difficulties when they face multiple discrimination. it is important to note that access to justice is still limited in many discrimination cases, and the report strongly recommends that the member states ensure that victims can obtain accessible legal advice and assistance at all stages of the legal process, including confidential counselling in person by equality bodies or appropriate intermediaries. legal redress is not only important for the victims, but it also has an educational impact on society because pursuing court cases and ensuring adequate representation are still problematic in some cases. we asked the member states to find ways to help victims including, for example, by means of court tax exemptions or reductions or legal aid and assistance from specialised ngos. in fact, it is important to recognise the legal standing of ngos with a legitimate interest in the relevant judicial or administrative procedures. sharing good practices among member states is a must. acknowledging the importance of fighting all forms of discrimination, i truly hope that this house will adopt this report with a large majority.
mr president, commissioner, i too would like to thank the rapporteur, renate weber, and the others who worked on the report. equal treatment in employment and employment should no longer be questioned by anyone from all points of view: gender, nationality, religion. moreover, the constitutions of the member states clearly provide for equal treatment. the problems arise when we have to apply them in practice. i wanted to take the floor to underline the importance of the report and to raise an alarm about the lack of equal treatment in the workplace or when applying for a job, particularly when it comes to people with disabilities or women in the hiring process. there are still cases of harassment at work or pressure to leave work. i believe in the need for equal treatment by respecting the values and competences of each person, which is why i support this report.
mr president in assessing the application of the relevant equal treatment directive, we cannot ignore the unjustified limitation of the scope of the legislation. discrimination on grounds of membership of a national minority is not part of the wording of the directive. i therefore welcome the call to the commission in the report to monitor all types of discrimination. it is time for the council to finally act on the adoption of a horizontal eu anti-discrimination directive to protect european citizens against discrimination outside the workplace. in my libe opinion, i also proposed that the prohibition of discrimination on grounds of membership of a national minority should be included in the legislative and control direction. discrimination is a daily experience for millions of eu citizens.
member of the commission. – mr president, this debate demonstrates how important it is to remain vigilant and continue fighting against all forms of discrimination, notably on the labour market. as i said, i hope, and the commission trusts, that the proposal for a horizontal directive will soon be adopted by the european council. the european directives have set up a comprehensive europe-wide legal framework against discrimination that has been transposed in all member states. in 2014, the commission reviewed their application and found that often there is a lack of awareness, sometimes a weak implementation and enforcement at national level. the commission has, therefore, further developed support to member states in order to facilitate the full implementation of those directives, in particular by ensuring that the investment priorities of the european structural funds such as the european social fund properly include the fight against discrimination in employment. as you know, with věra jourová we last year launched a new initiative to promote work-life balance, with the main objective to ensure that women are not obliged to choose between a family and a professional career. ms weber’s report and its recommendations will help the commission to further monitor and, where needed, improve the policy framework on equality on the labour market. i thank you for the report and this debate and i thank you for your attention.
rapporteur. – mr president, i would like to thank the commissioner and all the colleagues for their comments. the report highlights the need for adequate training for all relevant stakeholders: from employees of authorities of all kinds to law—enforcement bodies, judges, prosecutors and lawyers. however, i am now thinking that we, as public representatives, could also benefit from such training because i have a hard time understanding how the implementation of a fundamental right, which is provided for by article 10 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, could be a matter of subsidiarity. we have well-established european court of human rights jurisprudence on the restriction of the fundamental right to a certain extent, but more than that should not be accepted. moreover, i am wondering how we could accept the non-observance of court decisions: that contradicts everything i had learned and thought over the past 30 years about the meaning of the rule of law. i want to stress that, for me, adequate training not only refers to knowledge of legislation in court decisions but also includes training on understanding cultural differences and on acknowledging unconscious bias. since 2007, when i became a member of this parliament, together with many colleagues i have been advocating the adoption of a horizontal anti-discrimination directive outlawing discrimination in access to goods and services across the eu. nine years later, yes, i find it is a disgrace that this directive is still blocked in the council by a coalition of some member states. i cannot but welcome the optimism of commissioner thyssen that the directive will become a reality soon, so let us stay optimistic and let us hope.

in writing. the main objective of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is to act quickly and effectively to counter unforeseen difficulties in the labour market. the instrument has helped to mitigate the negative effects of restructuring by supporting the sectors most affected by the crisis. egf measures are temporary in nature but in the long term should pursue new job prospects, depending on the employment potential in the regions affected by the relocation or the reduction of the activity of certain industries. there are regions with a negative unemployment rate; therefore, i believe that egf measures should also include options such as support for the relocation of workers affected by unemployment to areas with high employment potential. last year, the restructuring of the steel company mechel turda in my region led to the dismissal of 1 000 workers, who received eur 3.6 million in egf support, but bureaucratic procedures led to delays and subsequent penalties for the romanian government. we should pay particular attention to monitoring the impact of globalisation, providing support to businesses to anticipate sectoral changes and to buy time for the re-professionalisation of workers at risk of redundancies.

in writing. ‒ postal services have undergone major changes since the full opening of the market in the postal services sector in 2008. the increase in the volume of online purchases has led to a recovery and an increase in the number of parcels transported by postal operators. quality postal services are an essential component of communication in the eu internal market. in 2011, the european postal sector recorded an annual turnover of eur 91 billion, representing 0,72% of the union's gdp. approximately 1,2 million people are employed by postal service providers. i voted for better working conditions, guaranteed to all workers in the postal services sector.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i support technological progress and the digitalisation of the postal services sector as a means of modernising and diversifying postal services. this has had a strong impact on working conditions and employment in this sector, especially in remote, rural and mountain areas, with very high growth in the parcel delivery sector due to the development of e-commerce. as a member of the tran committee, i believe that quality postal services are an essential component of communication in the eu internal market. the european union postal sector remains a key contributor to ensuring social, economic and territorial cohesion and to the development of the digital single market. the reliable and affordable delivery of parcels and packages is essential for the single market. other sectors such as e-commerce, publishing, mail order, insurance, banking and advertising are heavily dependent on the development of the postal infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ the volume of letter deliveries has decreased in recent years, and this has led to a decrease in the competitiveness of the market. i voted for the report, which calls for greater transparency regarding pricing conditions and performance in postal services.
in writing. ‒ key objectives of the liberalisation of european postal services have been achieved following the revision of postal services in 2008. postal services went through formidable changes after the full market opening of the sector in that year. the growth of e-commerce increased the business-to-consumer segment of the parcel and packets market so that, europe-wide, postal services account for 0.62% of the eu’s gdp. i voted for this report, which promotes and safeguards effective competition in the postal services sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it supports the implementation of the postal services directive, while making substantive additions. i consider it very important that, in the context of competition on this market, consumer rights are protected. in this regard, simplification of complaint handling procedures and dispute resolution mechanisms are very important. also, given the cross-border nature of these services, i believe that these procedures must protect the rights of consumers in all member states.
in writing. ‒ the review of the postal services directive has provided the opportunity to examine the current state of the postal services market, with a view to protect the rights of consumers while adopting the use of new technological developments. given the fact that postal services are a fundamental right for all eu citizens, but also taking into account the decline in letter volume over the past few years, the report has aimed to provide, first of all, a definition of universal service. an improved postal services system would contribute to the social cohesion and economic growth of the union, and would facilitate coordination between national regulatory authorities. the report also calls for improved transparency as regards public pricing conditions and asks for transparency checks where prices are not controlled by competition.
in writing. ‒ i voted on the report on the implementation of the postal services directive. welcomes the request of the rapporteur to the commission to facilitate and strengthen cooperation and coordination between national regulatory authorities to ensure greater efficiency and interoperability in cross-border deliveries and to oversee the regulatory activities of the nras - including the provision of universal service - with a view to ensuring a uniform approach in the application of european legislation and the harmonisation of the postal services market within the eu. it recalls that the universal service must evolve in line with the technical, economic and social context and the needs of users, and that the postal services directive gives member states the necessary flexibility to take account of local characteristics and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the provision of universal services.
in writing. small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps play an important role for the european economy in terms of employment and growth, accounting in 2014 for 67% of total employment, 71,4% of employment growth and 58% of value added in the eu non-financial corporate sector. in view of the above figures, sme financing should have a broader basis, thus ensuring optimal access to finance for smes at every stage of the development of an enterprise. due to differences between member states and between regions in terms of financing conditions and needs of smes, they face a number of challenges such as the amount and cost of available financing, economic volatility, slow economic growth and more. i have voted in favour of this report because i support the need for a diversified, well-regulated and stable financial services sector that offers a wide range of tailored and cost-effective financing options, thus best serving the financing needs of smes.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are a substantial part of the eu economy. access to finance for smes has been a greater constraint during the crisis than for larger enterprises, even though these enterprises are dependent on bank loans, which are their most important source of financing. it is important that smes have in-depth knowledge of complementary market-based sources of finance. we voted for a diversified, well-regulated and stable financial services sector that offers a wide range of cost-effective and tailor-made financing options. in view of the high rate of youth unemployment, encouraging the development of entrepreneurship among younger generations is a viable solution to address this crisis.
in writing. ‒ i believe that adequate training, support, access to finance and increasing the diversity of finance for businesses are essential, and that special training is needed to prepare young people for the green economy. we must not forget that preventing environmental damage and the transition to a low-carbon economy is a societal challenge that also offers new business opportunities for businesses that bring green products and services to the market.
in writing. ‒ i support this balanced and far-reaching report, due to the proposed measures that defend public and private investments, alternative financing tools and special attention to smes run by women and minorities. i agree that we should encourage smes to consider the whole eu as their home market and to use the potential of the single market for their financing needs. we need to ensure coordination, consistency and synergies between european instruments and programmes for smes such as the european structural and investment funds. it is also essential to promote a holistic approach to the dissemination of information on all eu funding opportunities by encouraging the member states, the eib and national promotional banks, in this context, to provide information on financing options and loan guarantee schemes. the report points out very well the financial problems suffered by smes and the situation of uncertainty experienced by suppliers generated by late payments by larger companies, public institutions and authorities, and thus i believe that the commission should, during the review of the late payment directive, assess the introduction of specific measures to simplify the payment procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i am co-chair of the sme intergroup of the european parliament and former minister delegate for smes, business and tourism in my country, but also because i have worked in the real economy as an sme, so i know the difficulties they face. the karas report thus calls on the commission to support smes in particular, as they have suffered considerable constraints in terms of financing compared to larger enterprises. as there is a great diversity among the types of european smes, diversity is also needed in terms of funding options and this initiative is a priority for the capital markets union. it is also essential that smes have better knowledge of the costs, benefits and risks associated with financing arrangements in order to create a culture of capital markets. a simple and harmonised financing system is needed, which ensures a level playing field for all enterprises and is the best way to ensure the development of smes.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the european parliament’s contribution to the capital markets union. it follows the work initiated by the commission with the green paper on retail financial services. the commission should pay particular attention to the specificities of smes and ensure that cross-border activities in the field of retail financial services lead to better access to finance. the report calls for measures defending public and private investments and alternative financing tools.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because smes are key players in the eu economy in terms of their share in employment and value added. according to the directorate-general for internal market industry, smes employ close to 90 million persons. bank loans constitute the main source of external funding for corporations in the majority of member states. companies in southern and eastern europe are most reliant on banks loans. the global financial crisis has left a large private-sector debt overhang, and high levels of non-performing loans (npls), in several european countries. smes across the eu thus face many difficulties in obtaining bank loans, as the result of differences in terms and conditions for loans or credit in the eu.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) represent a substantial part of the eu economy, making access to finance for smes an important topic on the policy agenda. i voted for this report, which aims to increase smes’ knowledge of complementary market-based funding sources and the use of new technologies in relation to new funding opportunities.
in writing. ‒ access to finance for smes is essential to the wellbeing of the european economy and to growth, as smes account for 67% of employment in europe. bank lending was and remains the most used source of sme finance, however, as the resolution rightly concludes, the financial crisis brought home the realisation that diversifying access to finance for smes is important to avoid over-dependence on the bank sector. the resolution suggests ways to diversify channels of funding for smes, highlighting conditions that would create a conducive environment for sme financing. removing structural barriers (i.e. reducing red tape and harmonising national legislation governing the sme sector across the eu), developing a capital markets union in the eu, encouraging a culture of crowd-funding, introducing innovative technology (fintech), and matching smes with investors are just a few of the concrete examples cited. to conclude, the resolution is very promising and i therefore vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i believe this is a balanced and far-reaching report which calls for measures to defend public and private investments, alternative financing tools and special attention to smes run by women and minorities. it is imperative for the commission to pay particular attention to the specificities of smes and ensure that cross-border activities in the field of retail financial services lead to better access to finance for smes. it is especially important to emphasise that financial education for smes is not only key to increasing bank lending. it is also key to expanding the use and acceptance of capital market solutions as well as to encouraging women and young people to start and expand their businesses, allowing for a better assessment of costs, benefits and the associated risks. encouraging women and young people is a very important aspect and one which has my strong support.
in writing. ‒ smes play a very important role in the european economy, accounting for 67% of total employment and making a major contribution to economic growth in the eu. the report underlines the need for a diversified strategy in legislation and initiatives to support smes and calls on the commission to create a series of programmes and tools to support enterprises in their start-up and development phases, taking into account their turnover and financing needs. moreover, these programmes should ensure equality between women and men entrepreneurs. member states are encouraged to reduce administrative barriers for smes and to create one-stop shops that centrise all legislative requirements for entrepreneurs. as regards the financing of these enterprises, bank loans are the main source and, in this regard, the report recommends that member states work with the financial sector to ensure full and equal access to bank loans for all smes. furthermore, by supporting the principle of diversified financing, the report proposes the possibility of private-to-private lending to facilitate access to new funds for entrepreneurs. i therefore voted in favour of the report on access to finance for smes.
in writing. the report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of sme finance in the capital markets union is a welcome initiative. we voted for the report which comes up with interesting solutions for european smes' access to sources of finance. one of these proposals concerns the possibility of introducing 'lending funds' schemes, which would make ecb money available to banks for the sole purpose of lending to smes.
madam president, please. the situation of smes requires a differentiated approach. regional differences between member states should be taken into account. the lack of skilled labour is already causing huge problems in the countries of central and eastern europe, due to the lack of development of vocational training systems and mass emigration. some countries have a significant proportion of their active population working abroad, typically in western european eu member states, reducing the structural labour shortages in these countries. the answer to this phenomenon is not to lock down, to reduce foreign labour by any administrative means, but to raise wages in the new member states. as long as there are eight to ten times the average wage differences between member states, we should not expect any change in labour migration between member states. migration will always be present, and labour-sending countries may face a number of problems - demographic imbalances, unsustainable pension systems, labour shortages - in the decades ahead.

madam president, i should like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, mr neuser, for his work in a spirit of compromise, which has resulted in a balanced and ambitious text. this report is an important contribution from parliament which i hope will be taken into account in the communication we expect on the future of acp-eu relations after 2020. as the permanent rapporteur on policy coherence for development (pcd), i am pleased to see that this concept has been highlighted in this report. the cpd has much to contribute, not only to the revision of the cotonou agreement but also to the implementation of the sustainable development goals. that is why i insisted that the report again calls for the establishment of permanent co-rapporteurs on the cpd within the acp-eu joint assembly. it is true that the acp-eu partnership has not achieved all its objectives and has disappointed in some respects, but i am convinced that we can improve these weak points while maintaining the current structure, which is a unique tool in the union's external relations. its legally binding nature contributes greatly to its effectiveness. in my view, the reform of the partnership must take account of our other foreign policy instruments, in particular the various road maps which will lead to the union's overall strategy. i regret that this strategy does not specifically mention the acp-eu partnership. if there is one point on which the reform of the cotonou agreement must concentrate all its efforts, it is on the strengthening of political dialogue. many african countries are currently facing serious political and electoral crises - the latest being gabon - and, in particular, the issue of presidential term limits: this is where political dialogue becomes relevant. it must be able to be used by both sides to prevent these crises and to act upstream.

the next item on the agenda is the debate on the commission statement on access to education for syrian children in lebanon (2016/2913 ((rsp)).
mr president, five years after the start of the conflict in syria, more than 250 000 children – approximately half of the nearly 500 000 school—age syrian children registered in lebanon – are out of school. this is totally unacceptable. the high number of refugee children out of school is an immediate crisis. education is a fundamental right under international law. all children in lebanon – including syrian refugees – have a legal right to free and compulsory primary education and access to secondary education without discrimination. education is also crucial for protecting children in situations of displacement, which can sometimes last for an entire childhood. despite these efforts, too many syrian children are still out of school. i believe lebanon needs more international financial support to respond to the educational needs of syrian refugees, including expanding and rehabilitating public schools, investing in quality education, fully including children with disabilities, training and hiring more teachers and subsidising school transportation.

the next item is the debate on the oral question with debate on the eu's global objectives and commitments on nutrition and food security in the world, addressed to the commission by mr enrique guerrero salom, on behalf of the committee on development (o-000099/2016 - b8-0717/2016) (2016/2705 ((rsp)).
mr president, i strongly support this report, which underlines the importance of the development of social safety nets. i would like to underline the importance of achieving sustainable development goal 2, which aims to end hunger and malnutrition by 2030, notably by increasing the productivity of smallholders’ farms, and achieving sustainable and climate resilient agriculture and food systems. currently 159 million children are stunted and 50 million are affected by wasting. malnutrition has a tremendous impact on their development and health and fuels the cycle of poverty. the level of investment remains inadequate. the commission nutrition action plan pledged to reduce stunting by 7 million children by 2025 and should honour its commitments, ensuring it addresses all forms of under-nutrition while also filling the huge current funding gap for nutrition—specific interventions.
in writing. we have been talking about malnutrition and hunger for decades, but despite the development aid allocated to sub-saharan countries, malnutrition and hunger still exist. unfortunately, even though the commission's action plan on nutrition has committed to reducing stunting in children by 7 million by 2025, out of a total commitment of 3.5 billion, only 400 million is allocated to nutrition-specific measures. in 2012, the world health assembly endorsed a set of six global nutrition targets for 2025, including a target to reduce stunting in children under five by 40%. however, investment in nutrition is still insufficient. the european commission should increase aid for nutrition and support the development of the agricultural sector in countries facing hunger.
mr president, illegal logging and deforestation is a huge problem in several eu member states. here again, we are witnessing the well-known phenomenon that while we have legislation to deal with the issue, the reality of everyday life is that corrupt systems have been built to continue uncontrolled logging on an industrial scale. entire forests are being destroyed, and in many cases the governmental authorities are turning a blind eye, leaving local forest owners helpless. it is an open secret that logging companies buy, process and sell illegally harvested timber with no regard for environmental or other considerations. breaking the law seems to have no consequences, and citizens expect the law to apply to everyone, even to companies that process millions of cubic meters of timber and provide hundreds of jobs.
in writing. forests cover significant areas of the planet and are important ecosystems both for humans and for the environment. in order to achieve the objectives of the 2020 strategy for forests, i believe that the strategy for forests and the forestry sector needs to be strengthened by: combating deforestation and forest degradation, promoting sustainable forest management as a means of protecting biodiversity, combating desertification and responding to climate change, while ensuring that forest ecosystems provide goods and services, contributing to sustainable development and poverty eradication. strong commitment, coherence and political support from all parties involved in the flegt action plan is needed to ensure that development and climate change policies place forests and the forestry sector at the heart of the green economy and highlight the benefits that forests can provide in a sustainable way, while ensuring their protection and combating illegal deforestation.

madam president, capital punishment, torture and cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment are incompatible with the principles and values governing the european union. the fact that some substances or products in the european union may be used for the execution of human beings by lethal injection is a reality and further measures are necessary to prevent human rights violations in this regard. in this context, it is important to ensure an appropriate mix of legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures of the european union to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of goods intended for torture, and to effectively control those with potentially lethal and inhumane uses. major emphasis and increased efforts should be directed towards export controls, but also towards the development of a specific list of goods to be controlled. however, efforts cannot be limited to eradicating torture by reducing the availability of equipment with which it can be abused, but also by promoting appropriate controls beyond its borders. in continuing these efforts, the european union should also seek to control other services that may contribute to the spread of products that can be used for torture or capital punishment, such as financial services, but especially marketing services. on the other hand, as regards technical assistance providers, they should be prohibited from providing instruction, advice, training or imparting knowledge or practical techniques which could assist in the commission of enforcement. the commission should also be able to monitor the implementation of the commitments of the member states, including their reporting and information exchange obligations, through a secure and encrypted system.

in writing. ‒ the commission adopted a proposal for a directive on provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and on judicial assistance in european arrest warrant proceedings, the implementation of which requires member states to trust each other's criminal justice systems, including the way in which the rights of suspects or accused persons are safeguarded. in practice, however, national practices differ and there are large differences between member states as regards the quality of legal aid provided, depending in particular on the fees paid to lawyers for legal aid. in cases where fees are too low, lawyers will not devote sufficient time and effort to providing high-quality free legal aid. i voted in favour of the report, considering that there should be a single judicial policy in all the member states and that this differentiation between the states and the approach to legal aid should be one and the same, regardless of the fees received by lawyers.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it represents a welcome step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. however, this level represents the limit of the right to free provisional legal aid offered to suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings who are deprived of liberty and of the right to free provisional legal aid for wanted persons subject to proceedings related to the european arrest warrant. it is important that suspects, accused persons or requested persons benefit from legal certainty as regards eligibility criteria. the right of defence or the right to translation should not depend on the country in which the proceedings are taking place, or on the nationality, gender or social class of the person. the eligibility criteria mentioned in the commission recommendation provide some clarification for the time being, but do not amount to full harmonisation. equity for citizens, regardless of the cost, must be balanced so that the citizens' rights of people in such situations are balanced.

in writing. ‒ judicial cooperation is one of the chapters where member states have much work to do to harmonise regulations and practices. the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides for the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions to be respected through mutual trust in the criminal justice systems of the member states. this principle also covers provisional judicial assistance for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and judicial assistance in european arrest warrant proceedings. in practice, national systems differ, which affects the respect of the right to free legal advice and assistance, especially for those who lack the necessary financial resources. the commission's proposal to regulate this area is therefore an important step, but not enough, towards ensuring a minimum level in all member states. it is limited to suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings who are deprived of their liberty and to wanted persons who are the subject of the european arrest warrant. the difference between lawyers' fees in the various member states, the quality of legal services provided by the office and the lack of regulation of the preference of the suspect or accused person are subjects to be covered by the commission directive. i support the adoption of this report.
madam president, this report finally outlaws the thriving business of trading in products that can be used for executions, torture, degrading treatment, and those who wish to engage in such activities will finally be able to answer to the law. for example, the regulation prohibits the use of single-use goods for torture or execution, and if it is a multi-functional goods, then there is an authorisation system precisely so that they cannot be used for execution or torture. and drugs need to be controlled precisely so that they can't be used for lethal injections -- that's the trade in these drugs. very briefly, this report will lead to the elimination of the death penalty and torture worldwide. i hope so.
in writing. ‒ eu export controls are foreign trade policy instruments serving a multitude of wider policy objectives. the regulation against torture (ec) no 1236/2005 is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights through the control of assets and activities used or likely to be used fraudulently to impose the death penalty, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. this regulation contributes to the eu's long-standing policy of abolishing the death penalty worldwide and preventing torture. it contributes to the achievement of the objectives by combining prohibitions with licensing requirements for trade in listed goods. i spoke in favour of this report, considering that the review of eu controls on trade in instruments of torture is extremely important in the current european context.
in writing. ‒ in europe, the death penalty has been abolished in its entirety, except in belarus, which has applied it as a sentence even this year. the retention of the death penalty is also one of the reasons why belarus is the only european country that is not a member of the council of europe. moreover, the abolition of the death penalty is a precondition for eu membership, as it is considered a cruel and inhumane practice. the european union challenges the death penalty, regardless of its motivation, whether it is one of deterrence of crime or punishment of war crimes (the last eu member state, latvia, abolishing the death penalty for all types of crime in 2012). in this context, the eu is continuing its long-standing policy of eliminating the death penalty in the world by regulating the prohibition of trade in 'single-use' goods and related technical assistance intended for torture and execution and a licensing system for 'multi-purpose' goods that could be misused for torture and executions by lethal injection. furthermore, i support this report as the eu needs to update the checklists regularly to include all relevant devices or technologies that appear on the market.
in writing. ‒ the torture regulation is the only instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights through the control of assets and activities fraudulently used to impose the death penalty, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. adequate synchronisation between eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures to prevent and prohibit the production, trade or use of goods intended for torture is important. ensuring compliance with controls by national authorities is a necessity when dealing with increasingly complex foreign trade transactions. i voted for a community approach to maintaining a level playing field by means of a system of regular reporting and review, consistent with export control regimes.
in writing. ‒ this is a much welcome example of the eu setting a global standard in eradicating torture. the updated rules will help eu authorities to react more quickly to new emerging trends in torture and inhumane treatment, namely by regulating their sale on line, etc. in recent years we have seen how a change in eu practices has led to the demise of the death penalty in many partner countries such as the us. this will be set to continue when the regulation comes into force. i welcome in particular the inclusion of a ‘catch-all clause’ in the ep position. with the new ‘urgency procedure’, customs authorities will be able to act just as fast in detaining torture goods. moreover, there will be an outright ban on displaying and selling torture goods at trade fairs, updated rules on banning advertising to include online sales of torture goods, and the transit of the prohibited products will be outlawed.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i believe it is essential to contribute to the abolition of the death penalty worldwide and to prevent torture. an important step is to strengthen the provisions on the transfer of goods, transit, technical assistance and commercial marketing, with a view to prohibiting trade in goods intended for torture and execution or 'multifunctional goods' that could be misused for torture and execution by lethal injection. increased efforts are needed at eu level and trade instruments are an element of a comprehensive approach to eradicating torture by prohibiting the transfer of elements that could lead to the facilitation or commission of executions, torture and other ill-treatment. it is also essential to ensure consistency of the european union's export controls on military goods, firearms and goods which could be used for torture and other inhuman or degrading treatment, without requiring duplication of controls. the list of prohibited products needs to be revised. i voted for this report because i believe that the economic and commercial development of the internal market must not facilitate torture through products created and marketed online or offline.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of strengthening the 2005 regulation banning trade in items that could be used for torture or executions in third countries, in order to address loopholes identified by civil society and make this ambitious piece of legislation (the first of its kind worldwide) even more effective. i welcome in particular the fact that the european parliament’s views on brokering and technical assistance, including advertising and promotion, transit through the union’s territory of such goods, and the review clause, have been included in the final version of the compromise agreed with the council and the commission.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that calls for human rights protection and for the eu’s policy of eliminating the death penalty worldwide or any other type of human torture.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, supporting the concern that the trade with certain goods could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. prohibiting such services is essential to protect public morals and to respect the principles of human dignity which underpin european values, as embodied in the treaty on european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. furthermore, it is necessary to prohibit brokers in the union from providing brokering services in relation to goods whose export and import are prohibited as such goods have no practical use other than for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. i am also in agreement with the prohibition of commercial marketing and promotion of any transit of goods listed in annex ii, regardless of the origin of such goods, unless such goods will be used for the exclusive purpose of public display in a museum, taking into consideration their historic significance.
in writing. ‒ the european union exports a wide range of goods worldwide. these include a number of products that can be used as instruments of torture and execution, for example by lethal injection. to this end, eu-wide control is required to avoid exported products being used in ways that contravene the 2005 european regulation against torture or for the death penalty, which the eu wants to be abolished worldwide. this is not possible at present due to the absence of multilateral export control regimes for these exports, in particular for military goods, dual-use goods, firearms, medical products. one solution could be to create a union general export authorisation for countries that have made commitments in accordance with protocol no 13 to the european convention on human rights or the second optional protocol to the international covenant on civil and political rights. it would contain specific product lists, providing greater clarity for exporters, and a series of controls, checks, sanctions, guidance and information from national authorities. the european parliament should be duly involved in this process. i support the adoption of this report.

in writing. ‒ cooperation between the european union and the people's republic of china has reached an impressive level in all areas in recent years. in addition to economic cooperation, another important area of strategic cooperation is public policy. this is an area of particular interest in the context of the increasing terrorist threats to contemporary society. in relation to china, an important component of cooperation is the fight against organised crime in the form of illegal immigration, trafficking in human beings and drugs, counterfeiting of the euro, infringement of intellectual property rights, corruption in sport, cyber attacks and money laundering. the current cooperation agreement excludes the exchange of personal data and relates in particular to exchanges of general situation reports, strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation and crime prevention procedures, training activities and certain criminal investigations. the adoption of this agreement completes the series of cooperation initiatives between europol and other structures of the main international actors, with the aim of making the prevention and fight against cross-border crime more effective. it is a necessary measure, which is why i support the adoption of this report.

in writing. ‒ over 80% of the least developed countries (ldcs) are from acp regions, which gives particular importance to the eu-acp partnership (the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states). since the signing of the cotonou agreement, there have been changes in the political and economic landscape of the acp group and within the european union, and the future of acp-eu relations should be based on a new reflection on the potential and future obstacles to cooperation between the two entities. the results with regard to the objectives of poverty eradication and integration of the acp countries into the world economy have so far been unconvincing, given that half of the acp member states are still among the least developed countries (ldcs) and that the acp member states together account for less than 5% of world trade and about 2% of world gdp. i voted in favour of this report, firmly believing that a new agreement, with the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals (sdgs) at its core, and the creation of robust monitoring mechanisms, is urgently needed.

in writing. ‒ the european union's relations with the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries have been consistently at a very good level over the past decades. the eu is the main source of development aid for these countries, which gives it a very important role in supporting their positive development. however, their position is still quite difficult, which requires a new agreement that puts the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals (sdgs) at the forefront. this new agreement should include a mechanism for periodic monitoring, accountability and peer review, knowledge-based policy planning, measures to eradicate poverty and inequality, policy coherence for development (cpd), protection of human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law, appropriate action in cases of serious corruption, political dialogue, strengthening of local and regional authorities, support for minorities, youth and women, and the private sector of the economy. to this end, it is envisaged to set up new cooperation institutions, in addition to the acp-eu council, such as the joint parliamentary assembly (jpa), the jpa bureau, the jpa commission. they will better manage funding through the various european instruments involved and through economic partnership agreements (epas). i support this report.

member of the commission. – mr president, the commission believes that sound financial reporting is vital for the efficient functioning of its capital markets. investors and other users of financial information must be able to rely on it. we do not develop the standards ourselves but use those developed by the international accounting standards board. it is for this reason that we have a rigorous endorsement process to test each standard to determine whether it should be adopted into eu law. the scrutiny period by parliament is an important part of this process. international reporting standard 9 is an important standard for financial services companies and governs the accounting for most assets and liabilities on bank balance sheets. it is for this reason that we are here today. the financial crisis showed that financial accounting has economic consequences. the g20 called on the standards board to develop a new approach to accounting for losses on lending so as to avoid reporting too little, too late and the new standard achieves this fundamental change. we assess whether a standard will be conducive to the european public good. for this reason we asked the european financial reporting advisory group, our adviser on the reporting standard, to consider a number of areas of concern in developing its endorsement advice. your question reflects some of these areas. first, we wanted to understand its effects on long—term investment. the european financial reporting advisory group did not expect that reporting standard 9 would lead to significant changes in long—term investment strategies, a finding that we recently confirmed. nevertheless, we will continue to monitor this area carefully and will work with the advisory group and the standards board to assess whether a change in the standard would be necessary. secondly, the european financial reporting advisory group identified a limitation in the standard for insurance entities. these will face a huge challenge in their accounting for their liabilities relating to their insurance contracts, which will come on board in 2020 or 2021. however, reporting standard 9, which covers the accounting for investments backing those liabilities, is effective from 2018. this misalignment of dates could give rise to volatility in reported results, as well as leading to higher costs in implementing the two standards. we therefore support a deferral of standard 9 for the insurance industry. the international accounting standards board has developed an optional temporary deferral solution which we will propose for endorsement as it will bring relief to most large pure insurance groups in the eu. the solution also includes a form of relief for bank insurers who will not qualify for a full deferral. most member states and the european supervisory authorities support this solution. nevertheless, we are currently considering whether it is satisfactory for europe as a whole. we are assessing whether the lack of a full deferral could create a significant competitive disadvantage for bank insurers compared to pure insurance groups. if we were to conclude that such risk exists, we would extend the scope of the standards board deferral to the bank insurers, taking into consideration that this is a temporary measure. however, we have not yet arrived at this conclusion. thirdly, based on the advice of the european financial reporting advisory group, which drew on input from the european central bank and the european supervisory authorities, we believe that reporting standard 9 should be an improvement over its predecessor in the area of financial stability. the commission, together with the european banking association and the basel committee, is assessing the need for a transitional phasing—in of the prudential capital effects arising from the new impairment model in reporting standard 9 so as to prevent a sudden impact on capital ratios when the standard is first applied. i should like to thank you and, in particular, the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the international financial reporting standard permanent team under the chairmanship of mr stolojan for the detailed and careful consideration of this standard. in conclusion, we strongly believe that international financial reporting standard 9 should be endorsed, but our work on the standard will not stop with its endorsement. we will be vigilant to avoid any unintended consequences.
on behalf of the epp group. mr president, this standard, the financial instruments, has given us a lot of headache here in the european parliament. we had many hearings, we had many letters from interested people in the banking, insurance industry. what we know very well is that the current standard has allowed banks to report hundreds of billions of dollars or euros of losses with a long delay. we have come to the conclusion in this parliament, in the econ working group, that the proposed standard, the new standard is better than the old one, even if it is not perfect. we therefore support the process of adopting the standard in the european union. we are convinced that it will allow banks in particular to apply an earlier loss recognition policy. at the same time, this resolution to be voted on in the european parliament on thursday shows a number of concerns that exist among parliamentarians, but also among those who are going to apply this international financial reporting standard. i thank the european commission and all my colleagues for the work they have done on this standard.

first vice-president of the commission. – mr president, let me dwell on one issue that was raised by most speakers, which is the issue of migration. it is clear to me that the european union as such cannot survive a situation of uncontrolled mass immigration into europe. it is equally clear to me that the european union cannot survive in a situation where we take leave of our fundamental values, refusing international protection to people fleeing atrocities such as in aleppo, on the grounds that they are migrants and not refugees, which is a false ground. so these are the two guiding principles i would like to apply to our migration policy. if we want to have controlled migration, and if we want to stick to our fundamental values, which is providing shelter to people fleeing from war and persecution which, i might add, is a fundamental christian value to those who seem to use christian values to keep out refugees, then we desperately need a comprehensive approach to the migration issue. we cannot pick and choose. we need to do everything, everywhere, at the same time, which means to do better at protecting our international borders, to do better at redistributing migrants who have arrived according to agreements we have reached, to make sure we also apply resettlement in those areas where refugees are now, and cannot be sustainably housed, to have agreements with third countries so that we provide for development there and that we provide for the right conditions so that economic migrants or people who seek an economic future in europe but have no right to international protection can be returned to those countries. this is a comprehensive approach and we cannot pick and choose, one or the other. those who say flexible solidarity means you can pick and choose are wrong. we need to do it all. we do not need to do everything in the same measure everywhere, but everything will have to be done by all of us. i insist on this also because i was in lampedusa a couple of days ago. and here today i want to salute the incredible efforts of the italian navy, of the people of all the international organisations involved, of the italian coastguard, who daily save hundreds, if not thousands, of people from drowning. and still we have not prevented people from drowning in the mediterranean, in incredible numbers in the southern mediterranean, and also here only a sustainable policy will help us solve this problem. fences and walls will not solve the problem. those who believe that fences and walls will solve the problem are simply fleeing from reality. just imagine that africa and the next generation will have anywhere between 3 and 6 billion people. if we do not help africa develop itself, if we did not make sure that girls can go to school, and that women do not feel they have to have nine children to survive, if we do not provide for that, no high fence, no barbed wire, no walls will stop people from coming to europe. either we help them develop themselves or we will be subject to mass immigration into europe. that, my colleagues, is something we need to do jointly, and we need to start doing it now. finally, i want to pay tribute to václav havel. i have strong memories of a speech he made in prague, and i was present there, where he recalled his memories of fighting for freedom, fighting against walls, fighting against fences, fighting against barbed wire. he said in that speech that he grew up and lived in a society where east and west were moral categories, where east and west defined a difference in values, and he was so happy that now he was president of a country and a society where east and west were reduced to mere geographical qualifications. please let us stay true to the ideas and idealism of václav havel, and please let us make sure that, in our european union, east and west remain purely geographical denominations.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is one of the main instruments for promoting children's rights. the convention establishes a system of cooperation between central authorities aimed at resolving cases of international child abduction. these cases arise mainly in situations where the parents come from different countries, countries that have not consolidated a cooperation partnership. the commission should be able to assess the impact of the measures on the situation of the child in the member state concerned. the hague convention thus aims to resolve such disputes at international level by providing for a system ensuring the immediate return of illegally displaced or retained children. the accession of the republic of peru to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an action that i consider appropriate given the considerable number of union citizens of peruvian origin who will be able to be protected against child abduction. i spoke in favour of the accession of the republic of peru to the hague convention, as i consider it essential that the prevention of child abduction remains a priority for the european union and third states.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, adopted in 1980, is an international instrument of cooperation, enabling signatory states to settle cross-border cases of child custody. the convention clarifies the applicable national law in cases when there is a conflict of competence between two or more national legal systems. the scope regards civil aspects, so it concerns mostly situations of separated parents or other persons having legal rights over the child. given that the scope of the convention is protecting children finding themselves in legal uncertainty, the aim is to have it ratified by as many states as possible. all eu member states have ratified. this report aims at giving austria and romania the authorisation to accept the accession of peru to the convention, which will allow the entering into force of the convention between peru and the entire eu. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ this report aims at giving austria and romania the authorisation to accept the accession of peru to the convention, which will allow the entering into force of the convention between peru and the entire eu. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ peru recently joined the convention on child abduction, but romania and austria have not yet accepted this. but i think romania and austria should do so, because only then will the convention be able to apply in relations between the eu as a whole and this south american country. the convention adopted in the hague on 25 october 1980, which defines the legal framework of the united nations on parental child abduction, is a very important instrument for the regulation of this crime. ratified by all eu member states as well as other countries around the world (93 in total), the document clarifies situations where the courts of two different countries dealing with a case (where the parents are of different nationalities) consider each other to have jurisdiction and, consequently, grant custody in parallel to the parent in that country. the convention shed light on these cases by establishing that the court of the child's country of residence has jurisdiction. as an immediate consequence, if the child is with the parent who does not reside in the same state as the child, then the child must be brought to the country where the parent who has the same residence as the child is. the european union has exclusive competence in these cases, as confirmed by the european court of justice.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention has as its primary objective the cases of international abduction of children due to the separation of the parents who have different citizenship from each other. i have voted for this report that will grant the accession of peru to the convention in order to ensure eu’s protection to the children in that specific part.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an important agreement to help avoid legal uncertainty in cases of cross border child custody. in those cases where custody of children is contested, a quick and fair resolution is in the interests of the child. delays, confusion and uncertainty, not to mention expensive legal bills, should be avoided as far as possible. i welcome the addition of these new countries to this convention, which is a vital form of cooperation in our increasingly interconnected world.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important document, adopted internationally in 1980 and ratified by all eu member states, which established cooperation between signatory states in this sensitive area. this situation arises in particular from divorces of transnational couples and creates difficulties at the level of national states in the care of minor children. the convention governs the settlement of such cases and provides for the application of the law of the child's state of residence and the immediate return of abducted children. as the eu has exclusive external competence in this area, member states should be authorised to accept the accession of third states to the convention. this is the case with the accession of the republic of peru, which has had a number of internal conflicts in the past but has successfully overcome that period. the council now has to authorise two member states, austria and romania, to accept this accession, which will allow the convention to enter into force between peru and the whole eu. this is an important step in favour of eu citizens of peruvian origin, which is why i support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction aims to address cases of international child abduction. in 2014, at the request of the european commission, the court of justice of the european union was consulted on the competence of the union with regard to the acceptance of the accession of a third state to the 1980 convention. the opinion of the court of justice in october 2014 confirmed the existence of the exclusive competence of the union to accept the accession of a third state to the 1980 convention. in may 2001, peru deposited its instrument of accession to the 1980 convention, but following its accession to the convention, a council decision is required to authorise the last two eu member states that have not yet accepted accession, austria and romania. this will allow the effective entry into force of the convention between peru and the whole of the european union. the european parliament's report supports the accession of that state to the convention and proposes approval without amendments so that the children concerned are guaranteed the protection granted throughout the union.
