on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – madam president, thank you for this opportunity to address the issues of nuclear security and non-proliferation. the vice-president/high representative is in the dominican republic at a very important conference for latin america. i will begin my remarks by saying that first of all, the risk of terrorists releasing nuclear or radiological materials needs to be taken into account in our overall efforts to prevent terrorist attacks. responsibility for ensuring nuclear security lies with national governments, but international cooperation in this area is and will remain crucial. the eu is strongly committed to ensuring the highest level of nuclear security, both in europe and worldwide. i have said before, during our debate on belarus, what we are doing, and we are very much concerned about what is happening in this field. the commitment of the eu to nuclear security and the progress achieved in recent years are described in detail in a joint staff working document issued on 9 march 2016 entitled ‘eu efforts to strengthen nuclear security’. allow me now to briefly highlight some of the eu policies and actions. as regards the legislative framework, the euratom treaty continues to be the basis of the eu’s activity on nuclear issues. through euratom, the eu operates an effective regional nuclear safeguard system, which includes nuclear material accountancy, verification through onsite inspections, regular reporting, and technical and scientific support for the eu member states. all this in close cooperation, of course, with the international atomic energy agency. the eu can claim major credit for promoting the entry into force, in may this year, of the crucial 2005 amendment to the convention on the physical protection of nuclear material. all 28 eu member states, as well as euratom, have ratified the amendment and the european external action service has conducted diplomatic outreach on behalf of its entry into force. the european union will continue to help states to fully implement the provisions of the amended convention and the atomic energy agency to promote universal adherence to it. in the area of combatting illicit trafficking of nuclear and radiological materials, the eu has supported the effective implementation worldwide of un security council resolution 1540 through financing and capacity building. we have established a network of chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear centres of excellence, which today counts 54 partner countries in eight regions of the world, with about 50 projects funded and around 300 people trained. it is funded under the instrument contributing to stability and peace, in accordance with the eu cbrn action plan of 2010. the eu supports the central role of the international atomic energy [agency], and international cooperation for improving the level of nuclear security worldwide, and is looking forward to the international conference on nuclear security being organised from 5 to 9 december 2016 in vienna. turning now to nuclear non-proliferation, the new eu global strategy, unveiled in june this year, confirmed that the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems remains a growing threat to europe and the wider world. the european union will strongly support the expanding membership, universalisation, full implementation and the enforcement of multilateral disarmament, non-proliferation and arms control treaties and regimes. we will use every means at our disposal to assist in resolving the proliferation crisis as we successfully did on the iranian nuclear programme. more specifically, i would like to mention two major treaties, the nuclear non-proliferation treaty and the comprehensive nuclear test ban treaty, as well as a couple of regional issues. the european union and its member states agree on the importance of upholding and strengthening the authority and integrity of the npt which has contributed to international peace, security and stability for more than 40 years. we call for the implementation of all obligations and commitments assumed under the treaty or undertaken during the previous review conferences. the european union has been and remains a strong supporter of the ctbt and its organisation and is working towards the entry into force of the treaty. of course, all 28 member states have ratified this treaty, and together with all the member states in this 20th anniversary year of the treaty’s opening for signature, the european union is conducting a number of actions promoting the treaty and its organisation, based on an action plan adopted at the beginning of the year. the european union welcomes the recent un security council resolution 2310 which urges all states that have either not signed or ratified this treaty to do so without further delay as it is an important step forward towards the entry into force of the treaty. i warmly welcome the act that in june this year parliament’s committee on foreign affairs (afet) held an exchange of views on this treaty, with the reporter. madam president, this is the second report on artemis and eniac. in the spring, we postponed the discharge because the court of auditors issued a qualified opinion. as you know, the two joint ventures no longer exist at this time, they are merged into one, ecsel, which will continue to operate. the reason given by the court of auditors was that, due to the different regulations of these two joint ventures, it was not possible to calculate an error rate that was valid from the point of view of the european union rules, because the calculation of the error rate is made according to the national rules. in my opinion, this argument was not the best one to consider. i therefore postponed the discharge and instead asked the national auditors to certify whether the activities of the two joint undertakings were financially sound or not. and we have received such official documents from all the courts of account in the states that have worked with these two joint ventures, so we can now grant this discharge without any emotion, because there are documents to prove that the activity was financially correct. at e for energy it's a different situation. the international iter organisation presented an action plan for the next period, which was rejected by the commission and an external expert assessment was requested. that's why i've postponed the budget discharge - to see the outcome of this evaluation. this evaluation was carried out, the result was positive, the action plan was very little corrected, it was approved by the council of the iter international organisation and in this way we were able to propose the granting of discharge to the european union's home agency of this international organisation. i think iter is a project that we need to continue to pursue and support, because it can bring very great benefits to society as a whole even though it may require a little more money.

madam president, the european year of volunteering 2011 represented a major political opportunity to highlight the added value of volunteering in europe. volunteering is one of the most visible expressions of solidarity, which promotes and facilitates social inclusion, builds social capital and produces a transformative effect on society. i believe it should be further strengthened through a legal framework, regulating a support mechanism and establishing appropriate organisational structures. member states that still need to define a legal environment for volunteers should do so as quickly as possible through the use of recommendations in the policy agenda for volunteering in europe and the european charter on the rights and responsibilities of volunteers. moreover, i support the call on the commission to facilitate the development of a more coordinated european volunteering policy, with a view to establishing a single contact point in the commission which would interconnect the individual initiatives and programmes, and improve access to volunteering programmes.
european voluntary service offers the opportunity to experience a form of social action which is unfortunately increasingly lacking in our time. voluntary contribution to the solution of social problems, support for the needy, was considered a natural form of social participation decades ago, whereas today it is considered in many cases a deviant social pattern. community involvement, free work for the community, is strengthening the very fabric of europe that has been weakened, made vulnerable and almost forgotten. volunteering, active citizenship, or as we call it in szeklerland, the kalákák, is much more important than we might think. volunteering is a way of investing in the future, especially in your own small community. it expresses confidence in the future of your community, willingness to do things for it, and the capacity for sacrifice. it is therefore important that as many european citizens as possible experience volunteering, and it is therefore very important that the european voluntary service is strengthened.

commissioner, the common agricultural policy should lead to an increase in the number of people in employment, but we are seeing the opposite. in many countries, villages are depopulated, land is uncultivated, animal farms are closed because farmers are no longer motivated. unfortunately, we are importing toxic and poor quality products for european citizens because we have no trade defence policies towards third markets - as mr juncker admitted just yesterday. the common agricultural policy must be linked to other economic policies. to increase agricultural employment in rural areas, we need to have infrastructure development projects, we need to have markets, we need to have fair competition. the european commission must open up third markets for the sale of products. how can we have animal husbandry when milk sells for less than a litre of water, when producers cannot sell their products? the cohesion fund should be directed to the less developed areas. that is why i welcome the report, but it must not remain on paper.
the circumstances affecting the lives of farmers vary widely across member states and should therefore be taken into account when planning the future of the cap beyond 2020. while the average european farmer has 12 hectares of land, in romania, for example, the figure is only 3.6. if you look at the average size of the individual farmers, the average farm size, it's only two hectares. this figure is 56 hectares in germany, 54 in france, 79 in italy and 90 in the united kingdom. the disparities are therefore enormous, not to mention other aspects such as the existence of distribution networks, the creditworthiness of farmers or the technological possibilities available to them. the european farming model is based on food security and the balanced and sustainable development of rural areas. however, the achievement of these objectives is at risk in some member states.

areas and recognises the fundamental importance of agriculture, forestry and their related sectors for the economic and social development of viable rural areas and communities. the associated value chains of the agriculture and forestry sectors are engines of rural growth, providing jobs and livelihoods to tens of millions of europeans. the eu’s rural development policy plays a very important role in securing and creating jobs and growth in rural areas through investments in farm competitiveness, diversifying farm businesses, promoting innovative approaches, or fostering knowledge transfer. the unemployment rate in rural areas has shown a positive trend in recent years, with 2015 values already at the level of 2009. nonetheless, we can and must do more. for example, we need to significantly improve access to fast or ultra-fast broadband to allow rural areas to seize the opportunities of the digital society, like e-commerce. commissioner hogan is particularly focused on the mobilise rural potentials. integrated and participatory local development strategies based on approaches like leader have proved their value and will be important to ensure dynamic rural areas as well trade means jobs. for every one billion euros of additional exports, 14 000 extra jobs are created across the eu, and more than 30 million jobs. one in seven of all jobs in the eu now depend on exports to the rest of the world. the eu is also the world’s biggest importer of agri-food products. it is closely involved in global value chains and needs to rely on stable trade relations and functioning global markets. the agri-food sector is the largest provider of employment in the eu, with 44 million people employed. many of the challenges quite rightly identified in the report can be ways to boost jobs, growth and investment in rural areas for the benefit, not only of our rural communities, but for the european economy as a whole.

in writing. ‒ the institutions of the european union are obliged to operate in a transparent manner with the funds entrusted to them, being accountable to the citizens of the union. following its audit work, the court of auditors considered that the funds allocated to the two institutions, the european council and the council, had been spent in accordance with the existing needs, and no significant errors had been identified in the payments for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies concerned. however, i cannot but express my regret that the recommendations made by parliament regarding the separation of the budget of the european council and the council have not been implemented. i believe that there is still a need for close cooperation between parliament and the council for an effective budgetary control exercise. i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014, section ii - european council and council, as i consider that the two institutions have managed the funds in a fair manner and in line with real needs.
in writing. ‒ discharge was refused, as it has been for several years now. parliament and the council continue to hold different legal views on the discharge procedure. the council does not recognise parliament’s authority but sees itself on the same level, as one of two arms of the eu budgetary authority. parliament’s interpretation of article 319 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union clearly distinguishes the two institutions’ roles – parliament being the authority which gives the discharge, whereas the council gives a recommendation on whether to grant discharge.
in writing. ‒ each year the european parliament takes a decision, under the form of a recommendation by the parliament from the council, regarding the discharge for budget implementation through which it releases the commission from its responsibility on managing the given budget for a specific year by marking the end of its execution. i have voted for this report on the eu general budget for the european council and council 2014 discharge.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by which the european parliament refuses to grant the secretary-general of the council discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014. the resolution annexed to the report states that the ep regrets that the european council and the council do not provide parliament with their annual activity report and considers this inadmissible and detrimental to the reputation of the eu institutions. it also regrets that the budget of the european council and that of the council have not yet been separated, as recommended by parliament in its recent discharge resolutions. the european parliament considers that the lack of cooperation of the european council and the council with the discharge authority sends a negative signal to the citizens of the union.

in writing. ‒ international security and stability are threatened by deteriorating relations between nuclear powers such as the united states and russia, as demonstrated by russia's suspension of the 2000 plutonium management and disposal agreement and ongoing tensions between india and pakistan. the deteriorating security environment around the european union raises the question of the re-emergence of nuclear weapons as a means of active deterrence, as well as of possible nuclear proliferation, which runs counter to the principles of the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons, which underpin global efforts to prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons, to promote the safe and secure use of civilian nuclear energy and to pursue the goal of a world without nuclear weapons. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on nuclear security and non-proliferation because i believe that every effort must be made to ensure a stable security environment.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the agreement reached on this resolution but i would like to express my deep concern for the many nuclear threats that are arising in different parts of the world. north korea continues to reject un security resolutions and to conduct nuclear test. this is not tolerable and has to be condemned by all means. russia has deployed short-range missiles to kaliningrad and, possible, in crimea. this deteriorated situation is extremely dangerous for the security of the euro atlantic area, especially in the black sea region. the fact that they believe they have the right to deploy nuclear weapons in these two areas represents a serious global threat and the european union should have to respond accordingly, in cooperation with nato.
in writing. ‒ it is important to uphold international peace, security and stability. this is crucial specifically in today’s deteriorating security environment from both a geopolitical and geostrategic perspective.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this motion for a resolution, which supports the nuclear non-proliferation treaty which entered into force in 1970 through efforts to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and promote the safe and secure use of nuclear energy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i consider that the changes in the security environment around the world in general and around the eu in particular are worrying, leaving the possibility that nuclear weapons could once again become an argument for intimidation and negotiation. it is a worrying prospect for the future if it starts to be dominated again by debates about the nuclear capability of states and not focused on diplomatic approaches. the possibility of nuclear technology falling into the hands of terrorist groups or being held by states that do not respect any of the existing international agreements on the subject, are not reliable partners and behave unpredictably should also not be overlooked.
in writing. ‒ we are currently witnessing a considerable deterioration of the global security environment, not just the eu, generated by different regional and global actors, despite the eu's efforts in this area. moreover, international peace, security and stability are seriously affected, including by the deterioration of relations between nuclear-weapon states. as such, it is necessary to strengthen the core non-proliferation and disarmament objectives of the three pillars of the npt (non-proliferation, disarmament and cooperation) for the peaceful uses of nuclear energy. in this regard, the presentation of the eu's comprehensive strategy in this area is welcome, given that the eu has committed itself, through the strategy against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction adopted by the european council on 12 december 2003, to using all the tools at its disposal to prevent, deter, halt and, if possible, eliminate proliferation programmes of global concern. clearly, for the eu to become the world's driving force in strengthening and continuing multilateral disarmament and nuclear non-proliferation agreements, the 2003 eu strategy against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction needs to be updated and expanded.
in writing. ‒ nuclear security has been a topic of debate since the early stages of the cold war and continues to be a topic of great interest today. in this period, we are witnessing the deterioration of the european security environment, with old nuclear arms limitation treaties being denounced by some of the signatories, and international actors, state and non-state actors, resorting to the development and even the spread of these types of weapons with devastating impact on all humanity. in this context, it is precisely the more or less conventional nuclear threats that are endangering european and world peace that are being addressed. in these circumstances, the s&d group, in line with its political tradition at european level, is clearly in favour of curbing these dangerous trends and defending peace, security and stability on the european continent. the european parliament, as the guarantor of the security of the citizens it directly represents, must take a stand and condemn these deplorable acts, which serve no one's interests in the medium and long term. i support this resolution, which is of course necessary.
in writing. ‒ the european year of volunteering 2011 represented a major political opportunity to highlight the added value of volunteering in europe. volunteering is one of the most visible expressions of solidarity, which promotes and facilitates social inclusion, builds social capital and produces a transformative effect on society. i believe it should be further strengthened through a legal framework, regulating support mechanisms and establishing appropriate organisational structures. member states that still need to define a legal environment for volunteers should do so through the use the recommendations in the policy agenda for volunteering in europe and the european charter on the rights and responsibilities of volunteers. moreover, i support the call on the commission to facilitate the development of a more coordinated european volunteering policy with a view to establishing a single contact point in the commission, which would interconnect the individual initiatives and programmes and improve access to volunteering programmes.
in writing. ‒ a culture of volunteering is beneficial for society as it addresses civic and social concerns and contributes to a vibrant civil society, and in turn a healthy democracy. volunteering is above all a free choice, through which individuals can building solidarity with communities. it also has benefits at the communal level, in terms of building social capital and transforming society. therefore, i support this resolution’s call to create a legal framework that identifies the rights and responsibilities of volunteers and volunteering. such a framework will help protect volunteers and embed volunteering as a norm in society. this resolution as ultimately volunteering is the responsibility of the population. volunteering is a matter of human kind and calls for deeper investments should come primarily from citizens themselves. caring, sharing, helping and getting involved are much more than a choice, they are our duties as citizens, and they must be driven by our hearts and minds, from our human and financial resources.
in writing. ‒ the european voluntary services (evs) helps young people travel abroad to participate in volunteering projects whilst experiencing different cultures, making new friends and helping others learn new skills. i have voted for this motion for a resolution regarding the evs, which that recognises the expression of solidarity, freedom and responsibility that it offers.
in writing. ‒ i support this motion for a resolution on the creation of the european voluntary service because i believe that encouraging this type of civic service is actually an opportunity to develop human links that help social inclusion, understanding and acceptance of cultural differences between citizens. i believe that this form of informal learning plays a major role in developing open and tolerant societies, ready for the new challenges we face. in this respect, i support the idea that volunteering, which is practised by so many people across the european union, should be recognised as a learning and development activity and supported through specific programmes by both the european commission and the member states.
in writing. ‒ volunteering has a value and importance as one of the most visible expressions of solidarity, which promotes and facilitates social inclusion, builds social capital and produces a transformative effect on society. volunteering contributes both to the development of a thriving civil society, which can offer creative and innovative solutions to common challenges, and to economic growth, and as such it deserves to be measured in a specific, targeted way in terms of both economic and social capital. i supported this report as i believe in the importance of providing a legal framework which identifies a volunteering status, with rights and responsibilities for volunteers and volunteering. moreover, i think it is a great idea for member states to establish adequately funded national voluntary service schemes and to improve access to quality information on volunteering opportunities at national and local level.
investing in young people means investing in the human capital of today and tomorrow. it's basically an investment in our future. with europe's ageing population, the future of young people is an urgent priority for us. we have to act accordingly and not just talk about it, as we have been talking about for a long time, but put into practice public policies, strategies, concrete plans that give them jobs, that take them out of the social passivity that has led to a kind of exclusion. there are over 8 million young people in europe today who are unemployed. the highest rates are in greece and spain, but there are many everywhere. moreover, this exclusion, lack of jobs and so on and lack of concrete measures for them also caused them to vote less than in other generations. i support this report because the union needs a policy that encourages the participation of young people first and foremost in the economy, so they need to enter entrepreneurship, which will further lead to their re-entry into society, which means social contribution, inventiveness, imagination, progress and taking the union forward.
in writing. ‒ the evaluation of the eu youth strategy 2013-2015 found that there are positive trends in education indicators, as a result of which early school leaving is declining, but youth unemployment has also declined in most member states. to build on these positive results, the youth policy 2010-2018 proposes eight areas of action to support young people and improve their quality of life. these are: education and training, employment and entrepreneurship, health and quality of life, participation, volunteering, social inclusion, youth in the world, creativity and culture. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that young people are europe's most important resource and that the european institutions need to invest in them, continuing the union's youth strategy and continuing to respond actively to the challenges faced by young people.
in writing. ‒ one of europe's main assets, and one of the guarantors of the eu's future, is the human and social capital of young people. the european union has the role of coordinating, guiding and supporting member states' policies for young people. the renewed framework for european cooperation in the field of the eu youth strategy covers the period 2010-2018 and defines eight areas of action: education and training, employment and entrepreneurship, health and quality of life, participation, volunteering, social inclusion, youth in the world, creativity and culture. there are positive trends in school dropout. the percentage for the 18-24 age group decreased from 13.9% in 2010 to 11.1% in 2014. the youth unemployment rate has dropped from 24% in february 2013 to 20% in november 2015, but things are not resolved. in total, there are 13.7 million young europeans who are neither in employment nor in education, and some 27 million young people are still at risk of poverty and social exclusion. i voted for the further development of youth projects and their support through the tools available to the eu.
in writing. ‒ i strongly believe young people and youth organisations should be systematically involved in youth policy-making. european young people are facing today many different challenges such as youth unemployment, poverty and social exclusion. there is a need to channel investments into inclusive education with regards to ensure equal access and opportunities for all young people, including those having different socio-economic backgrounds as well as vulnerable and disadvantaged groups such as refugees, migrants and asylum-seekers. we should fight for a better recognition of the learning outcomes of skills acquired through non-formal and informal learning not only because they equip young people with the right set of competences and knowledge, but also because they contribute to the personal development and growth of learners in order to make them proactive, responsible and open-minded citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it gives an objective assessment of the eu youth strategy 2013-2015 and very rightly underlines the importance of its continuation and development in the period ahead. i consider the continuation of the eu youth strategy a priority and i am convinced that investments in supporting young people, whether in education, finance or personal development, will ensure the development of our societies and economies in the future.
in writing. ‒ i would like to highlight one aspect of the situation of young people in the european union which has a very damaging impact on the societies of eastern europe: the emigration of young people from the countries of central and eastern europe. according to a study by the international monetary fund, since 1990 some 20 million young people have left these states and settled in western europe, losing about 16 percent of their population in romania and bulgaria. the problem is compounded by the fact that three quarters of those leaving the region were of working age, and 80 percent of those leaving romania were of this age. while these young people are useful members of western european societies through their work, they are sorely missed in their home countries, both economically and demographically. and emigration continues today, with temporary foreign employment often turning into permanent displacement. i am convinced that the only way to reverse these trends is to bring the economies of the countries of central and eastern europe up to speed, and the solution is to maintain and even strengthen the eu's cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ the importance of the eu youth strategy is enhanced by the consideration of human and social capital as the foundation for the development of human society in general, given that the resource of competence, creativity and entrepreneurship is provided by young european citizens. starting from identifying the causes of youth unemployment and investing in education (formal, non-formal and informal), vocational training, health and employment, facilitating the transition to the labour market through coordinated local, regional, national, community (european) programmes, using the potential offered by new technologies and involving all national and european actors from all markets in the fulfilment of the two objectives of the youth strategy 2016-2018, we are offering the european union opportunities for sustainable development through proactive and responsible young europeans.
in writing. ‒ this report gives an overview of the european youth situation, the challenges that youth face in europe, such as unemployment, social inclusion and poverty, and some recommendations in order to improve the current state of affairs. moreover, the report identified targeted groups who are more likely to be unemployed and marginalised: young people with poor qualifications, neets and those with special needs, disadvantaged and lower socioeconomic backgrounds such as ethnic minorities, refugees, migrants and asylum seekers. the recommendations include investing in accessible quality education, improving cross-sectorial cooperation at all levels and notably between the different eu strategies that affect young people, drafting a new eu youth cooperation framework after 2018, investing in quality and secure jobs and in mobility schemes, especially in erasmus. i fully support this report, as i believe that the most important solution to the challenges that youth face in the european union is to invest in education and to involve youth in policymaking that will affect their future.
in writing. ‒ rural areas account for 77% of the territory of the european union and many jobs in these regions depend on agriculture and the agri-food industry. together, these industries account for 6% of the eu's gdp, comprise 15 million businesses and generate some 46 million jobs. in recent years, we have seen a drastic reduction in the number of farmers and a continuous decline in their income. between 2005 and 2014, the volume of agricultural labour decreased by almost a quarter. i voted for the development of the necessary instruments to modernise and ensure the competitiveness of economic sectors in rural areas in a sustainable and environmentally sound way. the development prospects of this sector are huge and the economies of the member states stand to gain from it.
in writing. ‒ i strongly believe we need to make best use of the cap to counter the downward trend in agricultural and non-agricultural jobs over many decades in rural areas. diversification on farms, ensuring sustainable business development, and ensuring maximum opportunity and involvement of young farmers, women and other stakeholders in rural development are all key to building resilience in rural communities. ensuring basic services and connectivity all help retain people in the countryside and tackle depopulation and decline. ensuring cap tools are fit for these purposes is a continuing task for policy makers and all who put them in place and use them on the ground. finally, i welcome the strong focus on diversification, environmental aspects, organic and quality food systems, short food supply chains, and fairness in the supply chain for primary producers.
in writing. ‒ the cap is a good opportunity to re—launch the agricultural sector in europe, which has been spiralling downwards. the cap could bring in farm diversification, more opportunities and involvement for young farmers and a plan for sustainable business development.
in writing. ‒ in 1962 the common agricultural policy (cap) was introduced, implementing a system of agricultural subsidies and other programmes. i have voted for this report regarding the improvement of cap for the creation of new jobs in the rural areas that calls on member states to offer young farmers long-term prospects to address the issue of rural depopulation, stresses that a large part of cap direct payments are going to big farms and encourages the member states to step up their support for small and medium-sized farms.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report on the cap and how it can create quality jobs in rural areas, as it is a very important topic for romania as well. it is essential that the cap supports farmers and ranchers, but at the same time, a step forward is needed to increase support for job-creating investment. the problem of labour market supply in rural areas is one that we face in all member states, and romania is no exception. in a context where the area of agricultural areas is in constant competition with development and protected areas, i believe that the cap must support more the sustainable development of agriculture, always with a view to creating quality jobs.
in writing. ‒ the rural area of the eu member states has been one of the hardest hit by the financial and economic crisis of recent years. it also created a false impression that in the future the rural area will not be as important, forgetting that it generates most of the food of the urban population. the common agricultural policy (cap) is designed to prevent this negative trend and to ensure the sustainable development of the areas concerned. in this context, the first pillar of the cap can help support high-employment sectors by helping to maintain rural producers. at the same time, coupled payments could be supplemented, with the introduction of a maximum ceiling of eur 150 000, in particular to support young entrepreneurs and women entrepreneurs. the second pillar of the cap can support rural development and job creation, including by encouraging rural tourism and other areas related to agriculture. this could avoid the current depopulation of rural areas, which would become more attractive to young entrepreneurs and better connected to the dynamics of the european economy. i support this laudable initiative.

vice-president of the commission. – madam president, on behalf of the commission and, in particular, my colleague commissioner bulc, i would like to welcome this initiative. this report is indeed timely. we are convinced it will give further momentum to our maritime year 2017. the issues the report raises are very much the ones we want to work on. we want to ensure safe, secure and sustainable maritime transport that serves the internal market, connects europe globally and keeps the eu maritime cluster competitive. waterborne passenger transport is part of this story with the role it plays in people’s daily lives, for their leisure and for the employment it provides to many europeans. so we welcome the fact that the report looks into passenger transport and leisure activities. however, in some cases there are differences that should be recognised, for example, when it comes to financial assistance to transport operators linked to public service obligations, which is not generally available to cruise services. regarding environmental aspects, limits on the sulphur content of shipping emissions were included in eu legislation in 2012 with effect from 1 january 2015. the international maritime organisation recently confirmed the global sulphur cap, as of 2020, in line with eu legislation. in 2013 the commission set up the european sustainable shipping forum, bringing together stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of environmental legislation in the maritime sector. in this framework a green shipping guarantee programme was developed and launched by the commission in cooperation with the european investment bank this year. this programme is aimed at providing guarantees to accelerate investments in clean maritime technologies and to help the industry to go beyond the current eu environmental legislation. a first framework agreement with national financial institutions was recently signed, to be followed by others later this year. the total financial envelope of eur 750 million approved for the green shipping guarantee programme is provided by the connecting europe facility and the european fund for strategic investment. clean and sustainable shipping will be further promoted with the effective implementation of the directive on the development of alternative fuels infrastructure, ensuring the necessary standardisation and setting up of the basic fuel supply infrastructure between 2025 with eu financial support. the european maritime safety agency will assist with the drafting of technical guidance to port authorities and administrations for liquefied natural gas bunkering. the ten-t guidelines and their main financing instrument, the connecting europe facility, supports the promotion of green shipping. in this context, over eur 185 million were allocated in 2014 and 2015 for studies, pilot actions and infrastructure projects to support new technologies and innovation in processes. with regard to transport provided by ferries, integration with other means of transport, including integrated ticketing, is indeed important and, through the its directive, technical and functional specifications are being developed. this will include timetables, as well as information, for passengers with reduced mobility. the commission notes parliament’s interest in extending passenger rights to multimodal journeys, in line with the principles enshrined in the current passenger rights regulations, among others the waterborne passengers’ rights regulation. the commission is currently looking into possible initiatives in this field. in may 2016 the commission submitted its report on the operation of the waterborne passengers’ rights regulation. stakeholders and national authorities expressed their satisfaction with the regulation, but also agreed that further coordinated action, such as information campaigns to inform citizens about their rights, and cooperation between authorities to ensure the uniform application of the regulation, is needed to improve the regulation’s effectiveness. the commission welcomes the interest of parliament in the question of the international governance of inland waterway transport. this issue is relevant both for passenger and freight transport and, in the context of the commission’s naiades ii programme, important steps of streamlining and regulatory convergence have already been taken through the creation, in the framework of the ccnr, of the european committee for drawing up standards in the field of inland navigation. the commission would also support the call to have more statistical data on passenger numbers, but it must be underlined that eurostat can only collect data on the basis of legislation. harmonised rules for accident statistics exist and a detailed report is published every year. unfortunately this is not the case for inland waterways. finally, the commission fully agrees that ports play an important role in the performance of waterborne passenger transport and has already, since 2013, proposed a comprehensive ports policy. this includes measures to improve the efficiency of ports. we therefore count on your vote in favour of the ports regulation, which the council and commission expect to go to the plenary without much delay. we also count on your support in promoting good use of the eu’s instruments for finance and investments, notably the connecting europe facility and efsi. the commission believes that ports cannot develop in isolation from their neighbourhoods and thus encourages initiatives that improve the relationship between ports and port cities. let me also use this opportunity to thank parliament for its support in relation to issues on securing our external sea borders and the decisions on european coastguard cooperation.
in writing. the success of european transport policies will depend to a large extent on how well the european union can redirect transport flows across all existing modes, as well as on the quality of the services provided. in the context of growing demand and a growing concern for reducing emissions, water transport can be the solution to sustainable and safe transport, giving a new impetus to economic development in riparian and coastal areas. in view of this, member states and the commission should pay greater attention to passenger transport by water, starting with the rehabilitation of the necessary infrastructure and ending with rigorous training of staff in this sector. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on the environment and climate change, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on climate change and its impact on the environment. the european executive should therefore work more closely with the member states to attract european funds, especially those for smes and cohesion policies, in order to develop a transport strategy that is appropriate to the needs of each region, but also in relation to the priorities of the ten-t network.
the rapporteur. madam president, i am very pleased that our parliament will vote tomorrow on the text which i initiated and drafted in the committee on development. we will thus have the opportunity to present our position before the high-level meeting of the global partnership for effective development cooperation, to be held in nairobi next week. this meeting is of crucial importance for the topic of development effectiveness as it is the first such meeting after the adoption of the 2030 agenda. we believe it is essential that the european union takes a strong stand in nairobi, emphasizing with determination the need to build on the development effectiveness acquis and to strengthen existing cooperation cases. the four principles of development effectiveness, namely ownership of development strategies, results orientation, inclusive partnership, transparency and mutual accountability, are indeed, as acknowledged in the draft nairobi outcome document, the driving forces for achieving the sustainable development goals (sdgs). action now is needed to make our development cooperation as effective as possible in achieving these ambitious goals and making the best use of public and private resources for development. official development assistance, while particularly suitable in certain contexts, cannot do everything, especially in the current economic context. it should complement countries' efforts to mobilise national resources and help catalyse private investment and additional public resources. nevertheless, we must insist on meeting the commitment to allocate 0.7% of gdp to development - and we are still far from it - and on making further efforts in terms of the quality of the aid provided. on issues such as aid unbundling or alignment with national priorities, progress must be accelerated. since we are talking about the mobilisation of resources for development, i must particularly emphasise the role of the private sector. i believe that it is an important partner in achieving the sdgs and, like other development actors, it must commit to align itself with the principle of development effectiveness. beyond the private sector, the nairobi meeting should also be an opportunity to reaffirm the importance of inclusiveness and partnerships with all actors to achieve the sdgs. we need synergies between the various development actors to achieve this and realise the full potential of these partnerships. the global partnership for effective development cooperation has an important role to play in this regard. it is essential to strengthen it, including in terms of monitoring, in order to position it well in the overall architecture for the implementation of the 2030 agenda. the european union, which has been a pioneer in the effectiveness of development aid, must continue to play a leading role on these issues as well as on the involvement of civil society, national parliaments and other stakeholders, south-south cooperation, gender equality and women's empowerment. responsibility for development outcomes is shared, and with agenda 2030 we have an additional requirement that stems from the overall philosophy of leaving no one behind. finally, there is a whole series of ideas which we have developed in this report, but which i think are missing from the draft final document from nairobi. i think we should stress this point. the effectiveness of development cannot be guaranteed without peace, respect for human rights and the rule of law. we therefore call for increased support for improving transparency, good governance and the rule of law in developing countries. they are as essential to achieving the sdgs as the other more technical requirements of the global agenda for development effectiveness.
madam president, the european union is the world's largest donor, with almost 55% of the funds allocated worldwide. however, we are facing a number of difficulties: whether we are talking about the medium- and long-term impact of development assistance funds, whether we are talking about the insufficiency of joint projects between member states, or whether we are talking about the financing, sometimes, of the same projects by several member states or from several budget lines. all these problems, however, can be solved with a series of practical solutions. to increase the efficiency of development assistance funds, we need to regulate the allocation of assistance at european level. we need to develop comprehensive programmes to monitor and support beneficiaries both during and after the projects. we need to increase transparency in the allocation and spending of funds, but we also need to establish a public reporting system for european funding and projects. because ultimately, what we have to do is to find a way in which we can coordinate all the projects developed by the european union and the member states. the problem of efficiency can be solved if we want it and fight for it.
madam president, at present, more than half of the world's development aid is provided by the eu and its member states. however, the success of development policies depends on the effectiveness of international development cooperation and cooperation on sustainable development. we must see that international mechanisms, while showing a strong commitment and in many cases being the only help in a given situation, can only show very limited results. the slow decline in global inequality cannot offset the environmental changes, the water shortage problem, and the partly resulting migration, some of the consequences of the population explosion. the developed world can only demonstrate its commitment to the goals by pursuing a more determined and ambitious development policy and by correcting international trade mechanisms.
madam president, respect for human rights is regulated both at european level and at the level of each member state. however, there are serious violations of citizens' rights in many member states. and unfortunately, this seriously and sometimes irreparably affects people's lives and dignity. the case of mariana rarinca, a citizen of my country, is well known and therefore i consider this example to be eloquent for my argument. ms rarinca, the complainant in relation to the president of the csm in romania, was charged. she was arrested 191 days before her trial. this lady's ordeal lasted for years, and finally, after she was acquitted, she was sentenced again. the rarinca case is a typical case where the ordinary citizen fights with the institutions for justice and fails to win. it is serious in this case that both the csm and the presidential institution failed to comply with the legal provision on the period of fifteen days allowed to a citizen to lodge a complaint. i believe that we must, from here, at european level, supervise the institutions of a state governed by the rule of law so that they act separately, non-discriminatorily, with respect for human rights. and i also believe that the lack of accountability of the judiciary in some countries' legislation leads to abuse and suffering, but also to the spending of huge sums from the budget for compensation to citizens who, in the end, find justice in the european institutions.
madam president, there are many voices in european public opinion who believe that romania's fight against corruption is an example for many other countries. i personally think that a big change has taken place in romania and the cleansing of the public can be a huge positive for this process. but we cannot ignore the excesses of the system. a hungarian catholic school operating in a building returned to the catholic church under romanian restitution laws is currently being investigated by the corruption prosecutor's office because of suspicions of irregularities in the licensing process. if this has happened, it must be corrected, but it is unacceptable to accuse of corruption officials who only implemented the laws and question the good faith of the school principal, and create uncertainty among parents and children. the legality of schools operating on reclaimed church property is increasingly being questioned in romania, with fears that the authorities are driven by the intention to reverse the entire restitution process.
madam president, one of the objectives of the european union is to stimulate research at european level. but unfortunately, the way it implements its programmes creates new pay discrimination between researchers in eastern and western europe. despite the fact that funds are won through competitions at european level, there are huge differences between the pay grids applied under the main research and innovation programme horizon 2020. i therefore ask the european commission: how is it possible that an expert of type a in a european project can earn about 70 euros (300 lei), while the income of the romanian researcher in the same project is ten times lower, being reduced to only about seven euros? i therefore support the initiative of the babeș bolyai university in cluj-napoca and the polytechnic university of bucharest and strongly urge the european commission to restore a uniform salary for all european researchers. equal work, equal pay. as a member of the european parliament and a romanian academic, i cannot accept such discrimination and i will fight to restore justice.

mr president, commissioner, i will begin my speech with two key words: social responsibility. if europe's policy is not subordinated to this need, we will have no chance of remaining a united europe, we will not be able to compete in the global market. mr stiglitz explains scientifically that the 3% deficit threshold and the 60% public debt are taken out of thin air. there is no calculation to prove that 3% is the optimal threshold. i've worked in industry, and i know what deficit is, i know what investment is. when you make investments you need to increase the deficit. but it's important to make smart, operational investments that will cover your deficit in the next step. that's the key to solving it, securing jobs, quality of life. we need to boost smes, rural development and agriculture. commissioner, there is also a need for financial responsibility. tax evasion and all evasion from payments to the budget shall be monitored. but we need institutions to support the euro, because otherwise we cannot coordinate 19 countries with the same currency.

in writing. ‒ efforts to restore cod stocks in eu waters cannot be effective unless there is cooperation from all stakeholders and they take their responsibilities to reduce fishing mortality and the negative impact on the community in those fishing areas. in this regard, member states should give priority to the development and promotion of measures and (financial) incentives to avoid unwanted catches and the use of selective fishing gear, with the financial support of the european maritime and fisheries fund. member states should also make efforts to identify (through the stecf process) gear characteristics that result in the reduction or elimination of cod by-catches and to transfer the knowledge gained to other member states so that cod stocks can be restored. it is clear that in justifying a long-term plan for the recovery of cod stocks, account must be taken of the fact that fully documented fishing activities have produced results and that variants of these can be developed with beneficial effects on cod stocks and related fisheries.
