in writing. ‒ even though women’s rights and gender equality are enshrined in the constitutions and legal systems of all six eastern partnership countries (armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, moldova and ukraine), social and economic discrimination and gender stereotypes remain important and prevent greater inclusion of women in the labour market and participation in political decision-making processes. also violence against women and the lack of sexual and reproductive health and rights remains a problem. the eu needs to impose more actively gender equality and gender mainstreaming through the many useful instruments of its neighbourhood policy.
in writing. ‒ as rapporteur for the social affairs committee of the euronest parliamentary assembly delegation on the report on women's rights in the eastern partnership countries, i voted for this report because we need to get involved in improving the situation of women's labour market in these countries. first, we need to focus on gender equality as a shared value from the eu-eastern partnership perspective. secondly, concrete eu-eea cooperation in this area is a priority to achieve the desired results. most of the challenges are of the same nature for the eu and its eastern neighbours, but a political boost can help to promote women's rights and gender equality within the political priorities of the eastern partnership. all countries within the eea have developed strategies, programmes or action plans to improve the situation of women. the eu should help partners implement commitments in line with these strategies and national objectives, and provide expertise for the adjustment of labour legislation on gender equality and the improvement of women's participation in the labour market and decision-making.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the eu needs to impose gender equality and gender mainstreaming more actively through the many useful instruments of its neighbourhood policy. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in order to open the pathway to discussions of trade, human rights, economic strategy and travel agreements, amongst other issues, with armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, moldova and ukraine, the eu inaugurated the european partnership on 7 may 2009. i have voted for this report that highlights the barriers to women’s empowerment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this ambitious report, which analyses the situation of women in the eastern partnership countries and proposes solutions for improvement, and i welcome it as respecting, promoting and guaranteeing gender equality is part of the european union's wishes. the report correctly notes that violence against women is still significant in many of the eastern partnership countries and takes multiple forms such as physical, emotional, threats or sexual abuse. i appreciate that the report adopted today calls on partner countries to promote women's political participation, to respect the principle of gender equality in pay and promotion at work. i also consider it beneficial for all eastern partnership countries to ratify the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence as soon as possible and for national authorities to develop, in partnership with the eu, strategies to combat violence against women and to strictly monitor their implementation.
in writing. ‒ in general, the situation of women in europe is not adequate to their role and importance in ensuring the sustainable development of society. the european institute for gender equality also points out that the european union is only halfway to a gender-equal society. in this context, it is clear that women's rights in the eea states are also not respected, with gender equality remaining a horizontal priority in the european neighbourhood policy (enp) and the european neighbourhood instrument (eni). in order to ensure respect for women's rights and to improve their social and economic situation in those countries, there must be general political stability and the necessary framework for respect for human rights in general. specific measures to improve the situation of women in the eea states, included in national action plans, resulting from cooperation with international organisations and civil society actors, are thus urgently needed. moreover, the eea states should promote and support women's socio-economic and political participation and leadership, taking into account that they have a high level of integration in the labour market, playing an important role in conflict resolution and peacebuilding.
in writing. the report covers the situation of women's rights in six eastern partnership countries covered by the european neighbourhood policy (enp). although women's rights and gender equality are enshrined in the constitutions and legal systems in all these countries (armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, moldova and ukraine), social, economic discrimination and gender stereotypes remain important issues. the eu needs to be more active in promoting gender equality and gender mainstreaming through the many useful instruments of its neighbourhood policy. i therefore support the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the own-initiative report on women's rights in the eastern partnership countries. the report draws attention to the fact that women are predominantly active in low-wage sectors in all the eastern partnership countries, despite their higher education level. the report calls for women's involvement in economic policy-making and policy implementation, the promotion of business programmes aimed at the integration and promotion of women in firms and enterprises, and the implementation of local development projects aimed at women's economic empowerment. the report also calls on the eastern partnership countries to allocate more resources to combating all forms of violence against women, including amending legal instruments and providing assistance to victims of violence.

as you know, we discuss our annual human rights reports twice a year, but if i look at the long list of debates we have had together in this chamber over the last year, human rights have been at the madam president, farmers throughout the european union are complaining that their incomes are falling and that the areas they are working on are shrinking sharply. during this time, production costs have increased considerably, driving up prices, with a heavy impact on both agricultural producers and consumers. in these circumstances, price volatility is particularly severe in the agricultural sector, which is vulnerable to fluctuations in domestic and external markets, global consumption trends and climate change. agricultural producers have difficulty managing these effects and national public authorities unfortunately do not make use of effective tools to correct imbalances in the markets. we therefore believe that the process of setting up and developing producer organisations and associations in the agricultural sectors needs to be strengthened in order to create their own production, processing, storage and marketing capacities. the negotiating power for medium and long-term contracts must also be increased, as must the facilitation of supply to supermarkets in what we call the short supply chain. at eu level, it is important to set up a forecasting unit to forecast production by sector and market absorption capacities so that farmers can effectively match demand with supply. the development of mutual funds in agriculture and of production insurance instruments is a real support for farmers in preventing price volatility and combating losses in this sector.
in writing. it is becoming increasingly clear that the instruments under the second pillar of the cap are not sufficient to combat the volatility of agricultural prices. as regards the current cap instruments, the latest available data show that they have been used by 12 member states to counter price volatility. in total, eur 2.7 billion of public expenditure was allocated (of which eur 1.7 billion came from rural development funds). unfortunately, although they have increased compared to the funds allocated to the previous cap system, these expenditures still represent only 0,4% of cap expenditure and less than 2% of expenditure under the second pillar. the european commission should, in the future cap reform, pay particular attention to market instruments and ensure stable and decent incomes for farmers.

in writing. ‒ the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council replacing the lists of insolvency practitioners and insolvency proceedings in annexes a and b to regulation (eu) 2015/848 on insolvency proceedings. annex a lists the insolvency proceedings, while annex b is intended to specify the insolvency practitioners. regulation (eu) 2015/848 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 may 2015 on insolvency proceedings (recast) ((1)) entered into force on 26 june 2015 and was to apply from 26 june the following year. i have spoken in favour of this draft as i consider it to be an essential instrument in ensuring judicial cooperation in civil matters at european union level and this initiative will ensure that the scope of the reformed regulation is adapted, taking into account coherence with existing policy provisions and other union policies.
in writing. ‒ this regulation includes as annexes lists of insolvency proceedings and insolvency practitioners relevant to its application. annex a to regulation (eu) 2015/848 lists the insolvency proceedings referred to in point (4) of article 2 of the regulation. annex b lists the insolvency practitioners referred to in point (5) of article 2. in december 2015, poland notified the commission on a substantial reform of its domestic law on restructuring, which would take effect as of 1 january 2016, and requested a modification of the lists set out in annexes a and b to the regulation accordingly. according to article 1(1), to point (4) of article 2 and to recital (9) of the regulation, national proceedings qualify as ‘insolvency proceedings’ in the context of the regulation only if they are listed in annex a thereto. the annexes to the regulation can be amended only by a regulation to be adopted following the ordinary legislative procedure under the legal base on which the original regulation was adopted, namely article 81 tfeu. therefore, i agree with the proposal of the commission and of the rapporteur. the proposal contains no substantive change to the regulation, except changes of purely technical nature.
in writing. ‒ across the eu companies and individuals are increasingly establishing business or economic interests in eu countries other than where they conduct their core activities. in case they become insolvent, there may be direct implications for the good functioning of the internal market. i have voted for this report that will replace the list of insolvency proceeding and insolvency practitioners.
in writing. ‒ in december 2015, poland notified the european commission on a substantial reform of its domestic law on restructuring, which was to take effect as of 1 january 2016, and requested a modification of the lists set out in the annex lists of insolvency proceedings and insolvency practitioners. the annexes to the regulation can be amended only by a regulation to be adopted following the ordinary legislative procedure. after examining the request from poland, the commission submitted a proposal to the european parliament and to the council to ensure that the scope of the recast regulation will be adjusted to the actual legal framework of the polish insolvency legislation by the time of its application. i support this report, as the commission’s proposal was of a purely technical nature.

in writing. ‒ the 1966 agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on reciprocal access to fishing in the skagerrak and kattegat and the 1980 bilateral fisheries agreement between the european union and norway provide for reciprocal access between the three countries to fish up to 4 nautical miles from their baselines in the skagerrak and kattegat. the existing agreement has been considered as being inconsistent with the current provisions of the law of the sea, given the more recent developments in international fisheries law and in particular with the introduction of the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea. norway has therefore expressed concern about the control provisions, but also about the conservation and management principles, which no longer correspond to current needs. the present project thus aims to support historical fishing rights in this area and at the same time to ensure an efficient and sustainable fish stock management system, which is why i voted in favour of this initiative.
in writing. ‒ there has been an agreement between denmark, norway and sweden since 1966 on reciprocal access to fishing in the skagerrak and kattegat. in view of the more recent developments in international fisheries law, norway considered that the existing agreement is not in line with the current provisions of the law of the sea. it is particularly concerned with the control provisions. this new agreement maintains the exclusive access granted to each other by vessels from denmark, norway and sweden, while ensuring effective conservation and management measures in the fisheries sector. we voted to respect the historic right to fish in these waters, even though only two of these countries have become eu member states.
in writing. ‒ the new agreement maintains the exclusive access granted to vessels from denmark, norway and sweden to each other’s waters outside four nautical miles from the baselines. it ensures continued reciprocal access for the two member states and norway to the respective waters of the other parties in the skagerrak area, whilst at the same time ensuring sound conservation and management measures for fisheries in the area. furthermore, it allows for control measures in harmony with the principles of normal coastal state jurisdiction, as is already the case for fisheries in the north sea. i fully support this agreement, which is in conformity with the 1980 bilateral fisheries agreement, with unclos and with the objectives of the cfp. it ensures that fishing vessels from denmark, norway and sweden operating in the area comply with the relevant laws, regulations and control and enforcement measures for the conservation and sustainable use of the living resources in the skagerrak.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to ensure reciprocal access to the skagerrak for vessels from denmark, norway and sweden for the conservation and sustainable use of living resources. the report emphasises that access to the internal market for any third country must be based on reciprocity and that, in the case of norway, any customs duties on food products, including fishery products from the eu, must be in accordance with the agreement on the european economic area.
in writing. ‒ on 7 august 1967, an agreement on reciprocal fishing access in the skagerrak area between denmark, norway and sweden entered into force. following denmark’s and sweden’s accession to the eu, the commission became responsible for the management of this agreement on behalf of these two member states. i have voted for this recommendation regarding the renewal of this agreement.
in writing. the european union institutions have taken over the role of regulating fishing areas on behalf of the member states following the application of the provisions of the common fisheries policy. such an area is also the skagerrak and kattegat straits between the north sea and the baltic sea. in that area there is a historical tradition of joint fishing between danish, swedish and norwegian fishermen, which led to the adoption of the 1966 agreement between the three countries on reciprocal access to fishing up to 4 nautical miles from the baselines, following the principle of the high seas. the denunciation of this agreement by norway in 2012, on the basis of the un convention on the law of the sea and the un fish stocks agreement, led to the launch of formal negotiations between the commission and the norwegian state to establish a replacement agreement. the new agreement was initialled in october 2013 and signed in january 2015 and provides for reciprocal access for vessels of the three countries to the skagerrak area, ensuring effective conservation and management measures in the fisheries sector, but also control measures in line with the principles of normal coastal jurisdiction. i support the adoption of the current parliament recommendation, which lays the foundations for the normalisation of the fishing situation in the area.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund plays a key role in supporting workers affected by structural changes in world trade practices. in the present case, the european adjustment fund was requested by spain to facilitate the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant following the bankruptcy and closure of bosal sa. the factors triggering these redundancies occurred against the background of the decrease in vehicle production in the european union. therefore, bosal took a number of actions to reduce its costs and adapt its production capacity, but these proved to be insufficient. by mobilising this fund, workers will benefit from various active labour market measures such as: vocational guidance services, job search facilitation, integrated training, job search and training allowances. i voted in favour of this request because i believe it is necessary to support workers who have been made redundant for external reasons through various forms of facilitating their reintegration into the labour market.

madam president, rail transport in europe has changed, railway companies can provide services throughout the union. the high-speed rail network has expanded very rapidly to the benefit of economies and, of course, to the benefit of citizens. fifty years ago, the alternative was between air and rail, but today, fortunately, we have a variety of options for rail transport. the 1969 infrastructure management regulation has become incompatible with union law. i therefore support a liberalised market in which all companies use and are obliged to apply the same rules, but in a competitive environment. it is also necessary to have fair competition between railway undertakings, precisely to facilitate the entry of new firms into the rail transport market.
in writing. ‒ i strongly welcome the establishment of a single european railway area and the opening of the domestic rail passenger market to competition. it is clear that there is still need for a transitional period regarding the compensations paid for level crossing facilities due to the fact that some member states still use this regulation as a basis for level crossing facilities compensations. in future, member states may continue to pay compensation for the costs of those facilities. they may, nevertheless, need time to amend their national law and administrative provisions to take account of the repeal of regulation. concerning the domestic passenger transport services by rail (pso) regulation, i believe there is a need to strengthen the social protection in the new regulation, and that we must keep fighting for transport workers rights and jobs protection.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against the recommendation on the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of this recommendation for the adoption of the regulation on the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings and the repeal of the old one, as it needed to be adapted to the new realities on the eu market. the provisions of the old regulation were in contradiction with the new legislation adopted by the fourth railway package, as it allowed member states to subsidize certain costs specific to rail transport for a number of 40 companies. in the absence of repeal of these provisions, the allocation of these subsidies will favour certain companies and railway companies will have an advantage over other means of transport, which is contrary to eu legislation.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal for the repeal of regulation 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings will allow member states to compensate railway undertakings for the payment of obligations that undertakings of other transport modes do not have to support. this will take place gradually, which is necessary due the fact that some countries still use this regulation as a basis for level crossing facilities compensations. in the future, member states may continue to pay compensation for the costs of those facilities and may need time to amend their national law and administrative provisions to take account of the repeal of regulation 1192/69.
madam president, as i said, rail transport is no longer limited to the member states, but ensures the connectivity of the union. regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 concerns the award of public service contracts for rail transport. it is necessary to ensure effective community rules for the award of such contracts and for public procurement procedures in the field of transport. we have all heard many times about rigged auctions, contracts given to certain companies, and this practice must stop. all railway undertakings must comply with the same quality and social standards imposed by the national authorities. so member states must make efforts to ensure transparency in public procurement, few, clear and transparent rules. in these conditions, corruption or fraud is very difficult to intervene, and the costs of these contracts are much reduced, to the benefit of the citizen.

in writing. ‒ agricultural markets are subject to successive shocks in the two market components (demand and supply), the structural elements of agriculture and the price of agricultural products, with agricultural supply being affected by climate change and related phenomena (drought, flooding), the effects of pests, structural factors, environmental and animal protection policies, trade policies, etc. as such, farmers face an increase in production costs, combined with an increase in their indebtedness, which has led to a decrease in agricultural production and rural employment. moreover, the increase in the global population, which is largely undernourished, contributes to the increase in the phenomenon of price volatility in agriculture. moreover, agricultural markets, where demand meets supply, are inherently unstable, making the eu's mission to ensure food security and help european farmers and vegetable producers compete in the world market all the more difficult. but the eu has not only the risk management tools of the cap, but also the possibility of building a coherent agricultural policy with specific strategic instruments at european and national level.
in writing. ‒ the european union's common agricultural policy (cap) was designed as an effective instrument to support this sector, which is so necessary to ensure food security for european consumers. unfortunately, the agricultural market has been characterised in recent years by increasing instability and increased price volatility due to a rapid succession of changes in demand, supply and prices. the current cap, although it includes a number of provisions designed to ensure the stabilisation of agricultural incomes, fails to manage the current situation and producers are increasingly vulnerable, while the rest of the production chain is not affected. in these circumstances, reform of the cap is needed, by introducing increased support for producers and organisations in the field, greater transparency of contracts and improved tools for monitoring agricultural markets and prices. in order to protect farmers' incomes, risk management, crisis prevention and management tools are also needed to be included in countercyclical measures. european farmers must be protected against unfair trading practices to the same extent as consumers. it is an important report for european agriculture and i support its adoption.

member of the commission. – mr president, honourable members of the parliament, the last-minute addition of this point in the plenary agenda was a very welcome one to me. the agreement on the reinforced suspension mechanism goes beyond the importance of the mechanism itself. let me start by expressing my thanks to our rapporteur, mr agustín díaz de mera, for his excellent work. i know it was not an easy job. you did it. without his commitment it would not have been possible to reach an agreement before the end of the year. i also want to express my thanks to the council presidency, which brokered the deal in the council. both institutions made decisive steps towards each other at the last minute, which made the agreement possible. the commission also made some concessions for the sake of an overall agreement – for example, by accepting some elements of automaticity introduced by the council. we also committed to taking into consideration the categories proposed by the member states and to ensuring that these categories are sufficiently large to address in a proportionate way the circumstances. the commission has made declarations in that respect to coreper. overall we have jointly succeeded in making the suspension mechanism a more effective instrument for our common visa policy. it will enable the european union to react quickly in situations of strong migratory pressures or high security risks by suspending the visa exemption for certain third-country nationals. the final outcome allows for a flexible approach and a proportionate reaction to the circumstances encountered. very importantly, it also allows for a dialogue with the third country concerned to remedy the situation that led to the suspension. by adopting this strengthened suspension mechanism we will be able to pursue our visa liberalisation strategy based on stronger safeguards. i am pleased to know that the trilogue on visa liberalisation for georgia has been successful, and i am looking forward to the same outcome for ukraine. these two countries have concluded a series of reforms to implement their so-called visa liberalisation road map, and it is now for us to deliver and grant to their citizens visa-free travel to europe. our common priority now is to accelerate the procedures for the entry into force of the suspension mechanism as well as for the adoption of the visa liberalisation proposals for georgia and ukraine. we have delivered on the commitments made to our partners. the correct implementation of visa-free travel for georgia and ukraine will only be beneficial mutually, enhancing the cultural and economic exchanges and strengthening mobility between these countries and the european member states. it is an important and symbolic achievement, bringing people and nations closer. i hope that it will become a reality early in spring thanks to the agreement on the suspension mechanism that we are discussing today.
on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i also congratulate our colleague augustin diaz de mera, who amended the regulation very well and under pressure, with late-night negotiations - i participated in them as rapporteur for my group. the visa waiver suspension mechanism is currently not adequate and that is why we have basically changed the regulation as regards the suspension process and we will vote on this tomorrow. it's very important to understand that the credibility of the european union is at stake, which grants visa-free travel to some countries and then obviously expects those countries to continue the progress and the criteria that they met at the time of the visa-free travel. if they step back, it's not normal for them to continue to benefit from visa exemption. it is also our credibility in the eyes of european citizens, who see that we have exempted citizens of certain countries from visas, but then they see that they are breaking public order, they see that they are not coming with good and clean intentions to the territory of the union and are creating problems. that's why it's very good for credibility. what we are changing, very briefly, is: the deadlines for requesting visa waiver suspension have been shortened, also the grounds for requesting visa waiver suspension have been increased and one of them is new, namely non-compliance with the obligation to readmit migrants where such agreements exist. a new mechanism has also been introduced to verify whether the criteria that existed when a particular state was exempted from visa requirements still apply and whether there has been no regression. everyone will be more responsible, both the member states and the union.

mr president, the visa suspension mechanism for third countries whose nationals require visas to enter the european union is much more flexible after the adoption of this regulation. we also have a new surveillance system, which the commission can trigger immediately and in a very short time. the grounds for visa suspension have been extended and i will mention some of the new grounds introduced now by this vote: the rapid and significant increase in the number of people staying illegally in the territory of the european union, also the unfounded asylum applications from the citizens of these countries who have been granted visa exemption, the imminent risks and threats to public order and internal security of the respective member states.
in writing. ‒ visa policy is a fundamental issue for the european union, with repercussions on both external action and internal security. its importance is so great that its treatment is clearly regulated as a competence shared between the co-legislators by means of the ordinary legislative procedure. the amendment to regulation (ec) no 539/2001 adopted by the european parliament and the council on 11 december 2013 introduced substantive elements such as the 'suspension mechanism', the amendment of which is the subject of this report, without forgetting the amendment of the reciprocity mechanism, as a way of counteracting this first element. i voted in favour of this report, taking into account the evolution of the political and migration situation, in particular in view of the successive visa liberalisation procedures, which lead to a review of the suspension mechanism in order to make it more flexible.

in writing. ‒ the european union's visa policy reflects its relations with third countries and the agreements signed to exempt their nationals from visas, at least in the short term. in certain situations, however, unforeseeable events generating a large flow of migrants seeking to reach the eu territory for the purpose of seeking asylum or readmission generate the need for special measures by member states and european institutions to strengthen internal security. the visa waiver is a visa waiver for citizens of the union who are not nationals of the member states and who are not entitled to stay in the territory of the member states. these measures are to be temporary, for a period of 9 months, with the possibility of extension for 18 months if the situation persists or of interruption if the necessary conditions, mainly respect for human rights, are fulfilled. the commission will work with the member states and the third state concerned to remedy that situation. the european parliament will be able to be involved in this procedure and to express its position. it is an obvious step forward, which meets the requirements of some of the member states and will generate more security for european citizens. i support the adoption of this report.

in writing. ‒ the single eu aviation market has been developed through dramatic changes in the economic and regulatory landscape of air transport in europe to the benefit of consumers and business. the creation of the single eu aviation market has also had implications for the eu's external aviation relations, leading to the development of the eu's external aviation policy. closer international relations will not only provide access to new markets, but also allow the eu to ensure high standards of safety and security in international air transport as well as to work with others more effectively to address the impact of aviation on the environment and to safeguard fair competition in an increasingly globalised and liberalised aviation market.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of this motion for a resolution regarding international aviation agreements proposed in the aviation strategy for europe which is an initiative to generate growth for european business, foster innovation and let passenger profit from safer, cleaner and cheaper flight while offering more connections.
in writing. ‒ in the past 30 years the european union has created the world’s largest and most successful single aviation market, which developed through dramatic changes in the economic and regulatory landscape. however, today the european union is not only focusing on the internal aviation market, but also on a harmonised external aviation policy, that would benefit the eu economy and its citizens. i salute this report, although i would like to stress that these agreements should not only focus on economic gains, but also on air safety standards for crew and passengers, and the rights of employees.
